entry.title: When a Verified World Model Still Loses: Play-Adequacy vs Prediction-Accuracy in LLM-Synthesized Code World Models

author.name: Javier Aguilar Mart\'in

entry.summary: The paper argues that high transition accuracy is the wrong adequacy criterion for LLM-synthesized code world models used in planning, showing a model can be over 98% state-accurate yet lose systematically because the rare errors are exactly the pivotal dynamics. It introduces the verified-vs-correct gap and quantifies play cost.

entry.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs

author.name: Jimmy T. H. Smith, Tarek Dakhran, Alberto Cabrera, Simon S. Lee, Paul Pak, Aditya Tadimeti, Tim Seyde, Maxime Labonne, Alexander Amini, Mathias Lechner

entry.summary: The paper introduces an in-place tokenizer expansion recipe for pre-trained LLMs that upgrades a model's tokenizer to reduce fragmentation for later-added languages, which is especially costly for compact on-device models where embedding matrices are a large share of parameters. It addresses latency, compute, and energy penalties for underserved languages.

entry.title: Token Time Continuous Diffusion for Language Modeling

author.name: Parikshit Bansal, Sujay Sanghavi

entry.summary: Token Time Continuous Diffusion introduces a diffusion language model that operates in continuous space, deterministically mapping Gaussian noise to a final token canvas without further sampling, and adds per-token times so some tokens denoise faster than others. This aims to avoid the inaccuracy of discrete-space parallel token sampling at high speedups.

entry.title: Multi-Head Latent Control: A Unified Interface for LLM Agent Decision Making

author.name: Amirhosein Ghasemabadi, Ruichen Chen, Bahador Rashidi, Di Niu

entry.summary: Multi-Head Latent Control introduces lightweight heads that read an LLM's latent generation process to make agentic control decisions, such as whether to proceed, defer to a stronger model, request information, call tools, or abstain. It replaces input-side routing with latent-signal-based control.

entry.title: Controlled Reformulation Testing for Logical Consistency in Large Language Models

author.name: Alexander Gu, Alan Chen

entry.summary: CRTBench presents 350 question families (1,750 questions) to test logical invariance under controlled reformulations like contrapositive rewriting, double negation, and passive voice. It documents a large accuracy-consistency gap, with a non-reasoning model at 98.9 percent accuracy but only 60.3 percent family consistency versus a reasoning model at 96.9 percent consistency.

entry.title: D-cut: Adaptive Verification Depth Pruning for Batched Speculative Decoding

author.name: Tianyu Liu, Yuhao Shen, Rui Cen, Junhan Shi, Jiebin Zhang, Guangshuo Qin, Hong Liu, Song Liu, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu

entry.summary: D-Cut is an adaptive verification-depth pruning method for batched speculative decoding that jointly selects draft tokens across a batch to concentrate the verification budget on tokens most likely accepted. It targets throughput loss when long drafts waste computation under high concurrency.

entry.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions

author.name: Yasheng Sun, Zezi Zeng, Yifan Yang, Chong Luo, Wenyi Wang, Ziwei Liu, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: SciDiagramEdit is a benchmark and skill-evolution framework that learns to edit scientific figures from natural paper revisions, operating on the figure's editable vector source so users can inspect and co-edit individual elements. It addresses natural-language-instructed editing of dense scientific infographics.

entry.title: MEMORA: Embodied Action Memory from Egocentric Videos for Reasoning and Planning

author.name: Zihao Yu, Xiu Yuan, Chongjie Zhang

entry.summary: MEMORA formalizes Embodied Action Memory as forming, maintaining, and using persistent experience from egocentric videos, implemented via a formation-consolidation-retrieval lifecycle with four typed memory stores (environment, entity, activity, inferred knowledge). It targets long-horizon robot planning that draws on remembered places, object states, and procedures.

entry.title: Instrument Effects in Language-Model Honesty Evaluation: An Auditable Single-System Demonstration

author.name: Justin Bronder (Corabo Inc.)

entry.summary: This paper tests the measurement instrument rather than the model in honesty evaluation, building a text-adventure world where the game engine (not the model) knows ground truth and scores the model's completion/unreachable/undecidable verdicts. It shows that instrument choices, such as expanding a two-verdict to a three-verdict grammar, substantially change measured behavior.

entry.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language

author.name: Mingfei Chen, Zijun Cui, Ruoke Zhang, Hyeonggon Ryu, Eli Shlizerman

entry.summary: SceneBind is an omni-modal representation binding semantics and 3D spatial structure across vision, audio, and language, encoding scenes as global semantic embeddings plus object-centric semantic-spatial slots. It also proposes a matching scheme integrating global and object-level alignment for cross-modal retrieval.

entry.title: Open-AoE: An Open Egocentric Manipulation Dataset and Toolchain for Embodied Learning

author.name: Zishuo Li, Bowen Yang, Changtao Miao, Kai Zhu, Hao Chen, Qingze Guan, Zhengxing Wu, Wanke Zhan, Yang Sun, Zhiyi Huang, Zitong Shan, Zhenchao Jin, Jiadong Hong, Taowen Wang, Yushi Feng, You Liu, Yibo Wang, Yifan Yang, Zhaowen Zhou, Man Luo, Hao Cheng, Bo Zhang, Jianshu Li, Jiansheng Cai, Guocai Yao, Jize Zhang, Chenhao Lin, Renjing Xu, Lequan Yu, Chao Shen, Chunhua Shen, Zhe Li

entry.summary: Open-AoE is an open egocentric manipulation dataset and toolchain with about 2,000 hours of natural-environment video from 500+ contributors and 400+ smartphones, providing text annotations, MANO hand poses, camera trajectories, and atomic action labels plus a full processing pipeline. It targets scalable supervision for embodied learning.

entry.title: Stochastic Filtering for Quorum Sensing in Robot Swarms under Anonymous Communication

author.name: Fabio Oddi, Andreagiovanni Reina, Vito Trianni

entry.summary: Proposes a stochastic filtering protocol inspired by k-priority sampling to reduce double-counting bias in quorum estimation for robot swarms using anonymous communication. It improves collective quorum-level estimates while preserving scalability.

entry.title: Communication-Efficient Relative Pose Estimation with Vision Foundation Models for Ephemeral Collaborative Perception

author.name: Qihang Li, Jo-Hao Huang, Jiewen Liu, Suyoung Kang, Hao Zhang, Peng Gao

entry.summary: Introduces CERPE, a communication-efficient relative pose estimation framework using vision foundation models for short-lived multi-robot encounters with limited bandwidth and intermittent visual overlap. It avoids reliance on global reference frames or sustained view overlap.

entry.title: MIND-CAVs: Multi-Intelligence Negotiation and Decision System for CAVs based on Intent-Driven Autonomy

author.name: Mainak Mondal, Yihang Feng, Yangchao Luo, Han Song

entry.summary: MIND-CAVs proposes a multi-intelligence negotiation and decision framework for connected autonomous vehicles that communicates high-level maneuver intentions and uses edge computing for decision arbitration rather than just content delivery. It targets globally consistent, intent-aware coordination across vehicles.

entry.title: Chat2Scenic: An Iterative RAG-Based Framework for Scenario Generation in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yuan Gao, Wenting Miao, Mattia Piccinini, Haoyu Wang, Qunying Song, Johannes Betz

entry.summary: Chat2Scenic is an iterative retrieval-augmented framework with a chatbot interface that generates executable autonomous-driving test scenario scripts in a domain-specific language from regulatory descriptions, supporting interactive refinement. It aims to improve compilation success and scalability over retrieval-assemble and full-script-generation baselines.

entry.title: PiVoT: A Variational Solution for Real-time Large-scale Multi-object Detection and Tracking under Heavy Clutter

author.name: Runze Gan, Qing Li, Simon J. Godsill, Mike E. Davies, James R. Hopgood

entry.summary: PiVoT is a fast, clutter-resilient variational multi-object tracker that performs end-to-end detection and tracking of a large, time-varying number of objects from noisy positional and Doppler point clouds without external clustering, jointly inferring states, shapes, existence, data association, and measurement rates. It targets real-time large-scale radar tracking under heavy clutter.

entry.title: Adapting Generalist Vehicle Models for High-Speed MPC Across Terrains

author.name: Rwik Rana, Jesse Quattrociocchi, Christian Ellis, Nathan Tsoi, Garrett Warnell, Joydeep Biswas

entry.summary: OptCar is a recipe for specializing generalist forward-kinodynamic prediction models to a target vehicle for high-speed off-road MPC while preserving cross-terrain generalization, using a history-conditioned adaptation. It addresses overfitting when adapting foundation dynamics models to specific platforms.

entry.title: OmniaBench: Benchmarking General AI Agents Across Diverse Scenarios

author.name: Chengyu Shen, Yujie Fu, Gangtao Xin, Yanheng Hou, Wenlong Fei, Guojie Zhu, Jiawei Li, Hongcheng Gao, Runming He, Zhen Hao Wong, Meiyi Qiang, Hao Liang, Zhao Cao, Hao Jiang, Chong Chen, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: OmniaBench is a benchmark for evaluating general AI agents across diverse scenarios with explicit state spaces, deriving a hierarchical taxonomy spanning consumer, business, and enterprise settings from app stores, product docs, and web sources. It aims to systematically characterize agent capabilities beyond narrow tool ecosystems.

entry.title: Linear representations of grammaticality in neural language models

author.name: Jane Li, Najoung Kim

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether neural language models encode grammaticality as a linear representation, moving beyond probability-based tests that entangle grammaticality with likelihood, frequency, and plausibility. It probes internal representations for genuine grammatical knowledge.

entry.title: MemoHarness: Agent Harnesses That Learn from Experience

author.name: Yue Huang, Wenjie Wang, Han Bao, Yuchen Ma, Xiaonan Luo, Yi Nian, Haomin Zhuang, Zheyuan Liu, Yue Zhao, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: MemoHarness is an adaptive agent-harness optimization framework that decomposes the harness into six editable control dimensions and stores per-case diagnoses plus distilled global patterns in a dual-layer experience bank, adapting the harness per test case via retrieved experience. It moves beyond a single global harness reused for all cases.

entry.title: G$^2$SR: Geometric Methods for Fast and Memory-Efficient Gaussian-based Surface Reconstruction

author.name: Dasong Gao, Vivienne Sze, Sertac Karaman

entry.summary: G2SR introduces geometry-driven methods for fast, memory-efficient few-view Gaussian surface reconstruction suited to mobile robots. It aims to avoid floater artifacts and heavy transformer compute while staying accurate.

entry.title: Uni-AdaVD: Universal Concept Erasure for Visual Generation via Orthogonal Value Decomposition

author.name: Qifan Zhou, Yuan Wang, Yanbin Hao, Xiang Wang, Kuien Liu, Richang Hong, Meng Wang

entry.summary: Uni-AdaVD is a universal inference-time concept-erasure framework for visual generative models that treats attention value space as a unified intervention space via orthogonal value decomposition. It aims to remove undesirable concepts while preserving other content.

entry.title: VideoSEMA: a scalable and efficient Mamba-like attention for video understanding

author.name: Nhat Thanh Tran, Fanghui Xue andShuai Zhang, Jiancheng Lyu, Yunling Zheng, Yingyong Qi, Jack Xin

entry.summary: VideoSEMA is a split space-time video classification model combining a Mamba-like efficient attention block in space with softmax temporal attention, with a proof that under rank conditions it equals full space-time attention. It outperforms heavier transformer and Mamba models on K400 and SSv2.

entry.title: Introspective Attention Modulation for Safe Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Basim Azam, Hossein Rahmani, Naveed Akhtar

entry.summary: Proposes an inference-time introspective attention-modulation method for safe text-to-image generation that rebalances attention activations to steer away from unsafe concepts while preserving alignment, claiming robustness to fine-tuning-based bypasses. It targets intrinsic safety without external guardrails.

entry.title: Stigmergic Graph Memory: An Environment-Aware Approach for Many-to-Many Multi-Agent Pickup and Delivery

author.name: Aditya Dutta, Joon-Seok Kim

entry.summary: Introduces Stigmergic Graph Memory, a bounded, decaying memory layer that records recent execution signals on warehouse graph nodes and edges to rank feasible endpoints and route preferences for many-to-many multi-agent pickup and delivery. It informs endpoint selection with recent traffic without altering collision constraints or planner validity.

entry.title: SPINE: Bridging the Cyber-Physical Gap with Agentic AI

author.name: Minkyu Ham, Dongho Kim, Chan Lee, Jiayi Wang, Min Jun Kim, Yixi Zhang, Guo Ye, Jihai Zhao, Soyeon Park, Han Liu

entry.summary: SPINE is an agentic multi-agent framework that automates calibration and debugging for deploying bimanual robots, using a profile builder and a diagnosis-repair-validation debugger loop. It targets the deployment bottleneck of embodied AI by reducing the robotics expertise needed to get teleoperation working.

entry.title: Networked Intelligence: Active Shared Context Graphs for Human-AI Team Science

author.name: Sutanay Choudhury, Jeffrey J. Czajka, Lummy M. O. Monteiro, Erin Bredeweg, Jason McDermott, Katherine Wolf, Alex Beliaev, Josh Elmore, Paul Piehowski, Kylee Tate, Yuqian Gao, Aivett Bilbao, Kelly Stratton, Scott Baker, Jaydeep P. Bardhan, Kristin Burnum Johnson, Chris Oehmen, Robert Rallo

entry.summary: Mycelium introduces networked intelligence through active shared context graphs so that hypotheses produced by one human or agent can reach other people, agents, or instruments that can act on them. It reframes AI-for-science from scaling a single reasoner to scaling connections across a team.

entry.title: SAFETY SENTRY: Context-Aware Human Intervention via EXECUTE-ASK-REFUSE Routing

author.name: Tianyu Chen, Chujia Hu, Wenjie Wang

entry.summary: Safety Sentry reframes agent action safety from a binary safe/unsafe label to a per-instance three-way routing decision over execute, ask, and refuse, distinguishing intrinsic harm from context-appropriateness. The lightweight guard model reduces routine interruptions that erode user attention to real alerts.

entry.title: STOCKTAKE: Measuring the Gap Between Perception and Action in LLM Agents with a Fair Oracle

author.name: Sagar Deb, Ashwanth Krishnan

entry.summary: STOCKTAKE is a 26-week supply-chain replenishment benchmark built as a factored partially observable MDP with a computable fair oracle, designed to separate an agent's perception failures from action failures (the knowing-doing gap). It provides an exact Bayes filter reference policy the agent never has privileged access to.

entry.title: Compaction as Epistemic Failure: How Agentic LLM Tools Fabricate Confirmed Results from Killed Processes

author.name: Hiroki Tamba

entry.summary: This paper documents a failure mode in an agentic coding tool where partial output from timed-out commands is recorded in compaction summaries as confirmed results, propagating false positives across sessions. It attributes this to conflating information appearing in the terminal with information durably persisted.

entry.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Monoculture

author.name: Gordon Burtch

entry.summary: This study examines whether AI coding assistants homogenize software artifacts, using Kaggle submissions from 2019 to mid-2026. It documents widespread convergence toward the seed value 42 and analyzes broader homogenization at submission and abstraction levels.

entry.title: Baselines Before Architecture: Evaluating Coding Agents for Autonomous Penetration Testing

author.name: Ananda Dhakal, Krish Neupane, Aarjan Chaudhary

entry.summary: This controlled study on the 104-task XBOW penetration-testing benchmark uses default coding CLI agents as plain baselines with a fixed model, budget, and scoring to isolate how much reported gains come from security harnesses versus the underlying model. It compares default scaffolds against published security-specific systems.

entry.title: EMAGN: Efficient Multi-Attention Graph Network via Learned Clustering for Scalable Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Mingxing Xu, Rakesh Chowdary Machineni, Ke Liu, Xi Cheng, Chengqi Lu, Xin Hu, Lyuhao Chen, Xiangyu Li, Junwei You, Oliver Gao

entry.summary: EMAGN linearizes spatial attention for traffic forecasting using learned clustering matrices inspired by fast Gaussian filtering, cutting complexity from quadratic to near-linear while preserving dynamic attention flexibility. It aims to make attention-based spatiotemporal forecasting scalable.

entry.title: GeoAnchor: Collaborative Reasoning via Latent Decomposition for 3D Spatial Understanding

author.name: Hao Li, Han Fang, Zixin Pan, Xin Wei, Hongbo Sun, Jinglin Xu, Zhiyu Lin, Ye Yuan, Zhongjiang He, Yu Yu, Hao Sun

entry.summary: GeoAnchor is an interleaved text-latent reasoning framework that decomposes 3D spatial information into position, direction, and other complementary latent components to improve MLLM spatial understanding from 2D images. It addresses the fidelity gap of pure symbolic text tokens for continuous geometry.

entry.title: Generalized Neural Distributional Regression

author.name: Natan Hilario da Silva, Vicente Garibay Cancho, Adriano Kamimura Suzuki

entry.summary: GNDR embeds deep networks into the parameter space of classical probability distributions and uses a two-step semi-parametric estimation to recover analytical Fisher Information for rigorous uncertainty quantification. It provides observation-specific confidence bands and tolerance intervals via the delta method.

entry.title: ToolAnchor: Anchoring Counterfactual Context to Boost Agentic Tool-use Capability

author.name: Weiting Liu, Jieyi Bi, Wanqi Zhou, Jianfeng Feng, Yining Ma, Ai Han, Wenlian Lu

entry.summary: ToolAnchor identifies behavioral inertia as the reason tool-augmented agents fail to adopt new tools, and injects counterfactual anchor contexts at critical decision points to break that inertia. Teacher models are used to hypothesize anchors and scale the approach for toolset expansion.

entry.title: Inference-Time Concept Suppression and Video-Centric Evaluation for Text-to-Video Models

author.name: Wenxuan Chen, Wenjie Feng

entry.summary: SIRUS is a training-free inference-time framework for removing a target concept from text-to-video generators by localizing prompt evidence and suppressing target expression during sampling while preserving non-target content and temporal structure. The paper also introduces a video-oriented evaluation framework for T2V unlearning.

entry.title: Never Too Late for Force: Accelerating VLA Post-Training with Reactive Force Injection

author.name: Yi Wang, Wendi Chen, Zimo Wen, Han Xue, Xueqi Li, Wenye Yu, Zhijie Chen, Hao Yang, Jun Lv, Chuan Wen, Cewu Lu

entry.summary: LIFT is a force-aware post-training framework that grafts a reactive action expert beside a pretrained vision-language-action policy, injecting 6D end-effector force through causal force memory to add contact reactivity while preserving general manipulation knowledge. It addresses failures when manipulation enters occluded or force-sensitive contact states.

entry.title: Beyond scalar losses: calibrating segmentation models via gradient vector field surgery

author.name: Laurin Lux, Alexander H. Berger, Moritz Knolle, Daniel R\"uckert, Johannes C. Paetzold

entry.summary: The paper offers a gradient-level explanation for why region-based losses like Dice cause overconfident, miscalibrated segmentation models, and proposes a gradient vector field surgery that rescales the loss derivative to improve calibration. It targets clinical adoption where miscalibration hinders tasks like tumor margin definition.

entry.title: Steering Robustness into World Action Models via Mechanistic Interpretability and Optimal Control

author.name: Jihoon Hong, Julian Skifstad, Qiyue Dai, Alice Chan, Glen Chou

entry.summary: This work uses mechanistic interpretability to study how robustness-relevant perturbations are represented in World Action Model activation spaces, finding low-dimensional linear separability in some architectures, and leverages contrastive directions and optimal control for training-free steering. It introduces a World-Action Linear Quadratic Regulator for feedback steering.

entry.title: MeanFlowNFT: Bringing Forward-Process RL to Average-Velocity Generators

author.name: Yushi Huang, Xiangxin Zhou, Jun Zhang, Liefeng Bo, Tianyu Pang

entry.summary: MeanFlowNFT brings forward-process reinforcement learning to MeanFlow generators, which sample with average velocities, by using the MeanFlow identity to bridge the gap with DiffusionNFT's instantaneous-velocity optimization. It aligns fast few-step MeanFlow generators with human preferences and task objectives.

entry.title: Latent Communication Between Language Model Agents: Channels, Alignment, and the Limits of Text

author.name: Markus Wenzel

entry.summary: The paper hypothesizes that LLM agents communicating in clear text lose information their internal world models could otherwise convey, and quantifies this loss using sparse autoencoder feature analysis across three communication channels. It reports that an SAE-sparse channel retains high probe accuracy at large compression, suggesting text limits inter-agent communication.

entry.title: Polestar: Drift-Aware Cache Calibration and Token Commitment for Efficient Inference of Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Mingyu Lee, Akshat Ramachandran, Souvik Kundu, Tushar Krishna

entry.summary: Polestar is a training-free inference framework for diffusion LLMs that uses token representation drift as a unified signal to both calibrate stale KV-cache positions and commit tokens for safer parallel decoding. It addresses the twin efficiency challenges of KV-cache reuse under bidirectional attention and quality loss from static confidence thresholds.

entry.title: Grokipedia vs Wikipedia: An LLM-Based Audit of Political Neutrality along Ideologies

author.name: Filippos Vlahos, Guillaume Bied, Tijl De Bie

entry.summary: This large-scale audit compares political neutrality of Grokipedia (written by Grok) against Wikipedia across 1,394 article pairs on nine ideology dimensions, using four LLM judges and controlling for judges' own biases. It asks whether an LLM-written encyclopedia is truly more neutral or simply embeds a different ideology.

entry.title: AdaTurn: Budget-Aware Test-Time Scaling for Active Visual Perception Agents

author.name: Susan Liang, Chao Huang, Filippos Bellos, Jing Bi, Jason J Corso, Chenliang Xu

entry.summary: AdaTurn is a budget-aware test-time scaling framework that conditions active visual perception agents on allowed turn limits to avoid catastrophic truncation under tight budgets. It explicitly trains boundary behavior for variable rollout budgets.

entry.title: GlobalForge: Towards Robust AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Manni Cui, Ruiqi Liu, Dianyuan Zou, Ziheng Qin, Jingrui Xu, ZiAn Wang, Jianglan Wei, Han Zhou, Yu Liu, Yan Wang, Shu Wu

entry.summary: GlobalForge improves robustness of AI-generated image detection by shifting the discriminative cue from fragile local artifacts to robust global structure, using a local information bottleneck and global structural reasoning. It targets detector fragility after JPEG compression and blur.

entry.title: FlashDecoder: Real-Time Latent-to-Pixel Streaming Decoder with Transformers

author.name: Minguk Kang, Suha Kwak

entry.summary: FlashDecoder is a memory-efficient pure-transformer video decoder that maps latents to pixels frame-by-frame using a rolling KV cache for constant-latency streaming, replacing slow 3D convolutional decoders. It supports training up to 1080p with bounded memory.

entry.title: Beyond Single Expert: Harmonizing Diverse Visual Priors in MLLMs for Spatial Understanding

author.name: Xiao Lin, Xiaohu Huang, Kai Han

entry.summary: ViPS is a multi-model prior framework that harmonizes complementary spatial priors from diverse vision foundation models into MLLMs, using an efficient prior proxy to boost spatial understanding across tasks. It shows different foundation models help different spatial tasks.

entry.title: Symbal: Detecting Systematic Misalignments in Model-Generated Captions

author.name: Maya Varma, Jean-Benoit Delbrouck, Sophie Ostmeier, Akshay Chaudhari, Curtis Langlotz

entry.summary: Symbal detects systematic misalignments in MLLM-generated image captions, where recurring errors correlate with specific visual features, using a dual-stage setup with off-the-shelf foundation models and natural-language summaries. It targets automated detection of these correlated captioning errors.

entry.title: Hierarchical Denoising For Multi-Step Visual Reasoning

author.name: Zezhong Qian, Xiaowei Chi, Chak-Wing Mak, Tianze Zhou, Ruibin Yuan, Yuhan Rui, Hengzhe Sun, Zhuoqun Wu, Yuming Li, Siyuan Qian, Sirui Han, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: HDR (Hierarchical Denoising for Visual Reasoning) organizes video latents into a tree-structured hierarchy for coarse-to-fine multi-step reasoning within causal video generation, seeking logical consistency and low-latency streaming. It bridges streaming autoregressive efficiency and bidirectional global revision.

entry.title: ESAR: Event-Based Synthetic Aperture Reconstruction

author.name: Harbir Antil, Daniel Blauvelt, David Sayre

entry.summary: Formulates monocular event-camera imaging as a synthetic-aperture inverse problem, reconstructing a static log-radiance field via a geometric relation and a linearized temporal-differencing model over binned event counts. It offers a principled reconstruction approach for asynchronous event data.

entry.title: Adaptive Control of Motor-Position-Controlled Flexible Joint Robots with Uncertain Joint Stiffness

author.name: Annika Kirner, Grazia Zambella, Igor Kovacevic, Hannes H\"oppner, Jee-Hwan Ryu, Christian Ott

entry.summary: Presents an adaptive control approach for flexible-joint robots with position-controlled actuators that online-estimates the uncertain nonlinear torque-deflection relation of each joint via an implicit control law. It improves model-based control when stiffness models drift with wear and operating conditions.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for the Full Strawberry Harvesting Process: Obstacle Separation, Detachment, and Placement

author.name: Changyou Miao, Teng Li, Ya Xiong

entry.summary: Develops a reinforcement learning framework with heuristic phase coordination for the full strawberry harvesting pipeline of obstacle separation, fruit detachment, and placement, using a shared interaction-aware policy and hierarchical Cartesian impedance control. It tackles contact-rich manipulation among deformable, occluding plant structures.

entry.title: Hybrid Rigid-Soft Robotic Gripper with Shape Adaptation, Uniform Force Distribution, and Self-Locking Capabilities

author.name: Xi Chen, Yun Wang, Lichao Yang, Haitao Li, Ya Xiong

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid rigid-soft robotic gripper integrating membrane-based pneumatic actuators with 3D-printed dual ratchet-pawl mechanisms to achieve shape adaptation, uniform force distribution, and energy-free self-locking. It targets the trade-off between compliant grasping and high load capacity in agricultural automation.

entry.title: Assessing Physical Frailty and Fall-Risk Indicators with Social Robots: An in situ Evaluation with Older Adults

author.name: Aniol Civit, Antonio Andriella, Alba Mart\'inez, Joan Ars, Aida Ribera, Cristian Barru\'e, Guillem Aleny\`a

entry.summary: Describes a robotic framework using a behaviour-tree architecture and vision-based skeleton tracking to guide older adults through standardized frailty and fall-risk tests, capturing clinical scores plus additional biomechanical frailty metrics. It was evaluated in situ with older adults to provide deeper functional insight.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Adaptive Cooling for Deterministic MPPI via Entropy Feedback

author.name: Shuqi Wang, Wenrong Sun, Tao Han, Yue Gao, Xiang Yin

entry.summary: Proposes an information-theoretic adaptive cooling framework for deterministic Model Predictive Path Integral control that uses the Shannon entropy of importance weights as online feedback to regulate the temperature toward zero. It replaces predefined open-loop cooling schedules to improve efficiency and robustness.

entry.title: Training On Interpretability Probes Is Bad In Proportion To How Contingent The Features They Rely On Are

author.name: jdp

entry.summary: Argues that the harm of training against interpretability probes is proportional to how contingent or non-essential the features they rely on are, contrasting fragile linear/SAE probes against methods capturing deep cognitive structure like natural latents. It offers heuristics for when training against interpreted features is robust versus counterproductive.

entry.title: Anatomically Faithful but Temporally Blind: Auditing Attribution for Left-Ventricular Ejection-Fraction Estimation from Echocardiography

author.name: Hyunkyung Han, Min Jung Kim

entry.summary: Audits whether attribution methods for deep echocardiography models estimating ejection fraction are faithful both spatially and temporally, fine-tuning a VideoMAE transformer and an R(2+1)D CNN. It finds explanations may localize anatomy correctly yet fail to identify the decisive end-systolic and end-diastolic frames.

entry.title: Multimodal Assessment of Pancreatic Cancer Resectability Using Deep Learning

author.name: Vincent Ochs, Christoph Kuemmerli, Florentin Bieder, Julia Wolleb, Joel L. Lavanchy, Julia Ruppel, Jan Liechti, Stephanie Taha-Mehlitz, Christian Andreas Nebiker, Beat Mueller, Giuseppe Kito Fusai, Joerg-Matthias Pollok, Anas Taha, Philippe C. Cattin, Sebastian Staubli

entry.summary: Introduces a fully automated multimodal deep-learning framework that jointly analyzes 3D contrast-enhanced CT and structured clinical data to classify pancreatic cancer into three NCCN resectability categories, using a Swin-UNETR backbone with auxiliary anatomical segmentation. It addresses high inter-expert variability in resectability assessment.

entry.title: How Well Does AI-Generated Feedback Work? Intrinsic and Extrinsic Evaluation across more than 20,000 EFL Essay Drafts

author.name: Steven Coyne, Diana Galvan-Sosa, Ryan Spring, Machi Shimmei, Michael Zock, Keisuke Sakaguchi, Kentaro Inui

entry.summary: A large-scale study of LLM-generated written corrective feedback in an EFL writing course, deploying systems with nearly 2,000 students and over 20,000 drafts, evaluated both intrinsically by teachers and extrinsically via student engagement. It highlights that pedagogically sound feedback needs learner-centered extrinsic evaluation, not just factuality.

entry.title: Rubrics on Trial: Evolving Rubrics from a Single Query via Synthetic Pairwise Evidence

author.name: Haocheng Yang, Licheng Pan, Xiaoxi Li, Zhichao Chen, Zhiheng Zhang, Yuan Lu, Haoxuan Li, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Rubrics on Trial is a query-only framework that evolves an evaluation rubric set from empty without human annotations or model training, deriving supervision solely from synthetic rubric-conditioned response pairs. It checks whether generated rubrics actually discriminate answer quality rather than rewarding optional style.

entry.title: SD-MAR: Multi-image Analytical Reasoning via Synthetic Data and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shiyu Yuan, Sourav Sanjukta Bhabesh, Zhe Wang, Dmitriy Bespalov, Wesley Rose, Huzefa Rangwala

entry.summary: SD-MAR is a framework using synthetic data and reinforcement learning to train and evaluate vision-language models on multi-image analytical reasoning tasks such as comparison, change detection, and multi-step inference. It targets an underexplored capability gap in existing multimodal benchmarks.

entry.title: Moment-Resolved Readout and Reservoir Diversity in Nonequilibrium Langevin Computing

author.name: JiZheng Duan, MingYang Zhao, YanWei Chen, Lei Yang

entry.summary: Extends thermodynamic (Langevin-dynamics) computing from mean-only readout to moment-resolved readout, constructing response vectors from higher-order polynomial moments of fluctuating reservoir states. It explores richer physical computation via thermal fluctuations.

entry.title: Curvature-Constrained and Constant-Speed Distributed Simultaneous Arrival Control for Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Zhouru Xiao, Yang Lu, Weijia Yao, Min Liu, Yaonan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a distributed switching control method based on maximum consensus for multi-robot simultaneous arrival under trajectory-curvature and constant-speed constraints, exploiting geometric properties. It targets fixed-wing-UAV-like systems needing coordinated arrival at a target point.

entry.title: Tamed Stochastic Gradient Hamiltonian Monte Carlo

author.name: Zhuoran Wang, Ying Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a tamed stochastic gradient Hamiltonian Monte Carlo algorithm for sampling and stochastic optimization with superlinearly growing gradients, establishing a non-asymptotic Wasserstein-2 error bound and an excess-risk estimate. It is illustrated on a newsvendor and a Conditional Value-at-Risk minimization problem.

entry.title: Refusal Is Redundantly Distributed, Not Localized: A Per-Layer Ablation Study on Llama-3.1-8B

author.name: hdhurve

entry.summary: This post replicates and extends earlier refusal-direction interpretability work by applying per-layer difference-in-means ablations to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, finding that refusal behavior is redundantly distributed across layers rather than localized to a single one. It argues that safety guardrail training produces a surface-level, linearly accessible feature rather than a deep capability change, which has implications for how robust alignment interventions really are.

entry.title: Set-shifting Behavioral Test for Harnessed Agents

author.name: Ziwei Ye

entry.summary: This benchmark borrows the set-shifting paradigm from cognitive psychology to test how LLM agents adapt when a reliable tool silently changes reliability mid-session. It finds agents quickly settle into recurring routines and adapt poorly after hidden reliability shifts.

entry.title: Automatic Ordinary Differential Equations Discovery For Biological Systems Using Large Language Model Powered Agentic System

author.name: David Krongauz, Arad Zulti, Eran Segal, Teddy Lazebnik

entry.summary: MEDA is an LLM- and symbolic-regression-powered agentic system that automatically discovers ordinary differential equations for biological systems, incorporating domain priors and automating parts of the research workflow. It targets biological mechanistic modeling, an area underexplored by prior equation-discovery work.

entry.title: AgentCompass: A Unified Evaluation Infrastructure for Agent Capabilities

author.name: Kai Chen, Zichen Ding, Jiaye Ge, Shufan Jiang, Mo Li, Qingqiu Li, Zehao Li, Zonglin Li, Tiaohao Liang, Shudong Liu, Zerun Ma, Zixing Shang, Wenhui Tian, Zun Wang, Liwei Wu, Zhenyu Wu, Jun Xu, Bowen Yang, Dingbo Yuan, Qi Zhang, Songyang Zhang, Peiheng Zhou, Dongsheng Zhu

entry.summary: AgentCompass is an open-source, extensible evaluation infrastructure that decouples the agent evaluation process into Benchmark, Harness, and Environment components to reduce fragmentation and redundant engineering. It adds a fault-tolerant asynchronous runtime and trajectory analysis tools.

entry.title: Experience Memory Graph: One-Shot Error Correction for Agents

author.name: Wenjun Wang, Yuchen Fang, Fengrui Liu, Zibo Liang, Kai Zheng

entry.summary: Experience Memory Graph reformulates agent failure recovery as a graph-matching problem, converting failed and successful exploration trajectories into a graph so agents can perform one-shot error correction without brittle prompt-based reflection. It aims to cut the API cost and time of iterative retry loops.

entry.title: Final Authority in AI Governance: Frontier-Provider Sovereignty and Action-Centered Deployer Governance

author.name: Zexun Wang

entry.summary: Safe-Psych is a sequential psychiatry benchmark built from over 1,000 real clinical notes segmented to simulate incremental evidence disclosure, with psychiatrist-derived labels of DIAGNOSE, CLARIFY, or ABSTAIN at each stage. It evaluates whether LLMs appropriately seek clarification or abstain under evolving diagnostic uncertainty.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Sequential Decision Rules for Event-Triggered LLM Invocation in Streaming Systems

author.name: Zhaohui Wang

entry.summary: This paper casts the decision of when to invoke an expensive LLM in a streaming pipeline as a risk-based sequential stopping problem, proving results including a minimum inter-event bound, optimality of threshold policies, approximate SPRT guarantees, and sublinear regret bounds under stationary and changepoint streams. It provides formal treatment of fast-model-to-LLM triggering.

entry.title: Inference Economics of Enterprise Coding Agents: A Case Study of Cloud vs. On-Premise LLMs

author.name: Sheng-Wei Peng, Yi-Hsun Lin, Yi-Pei Lee

entry.summary: This longitudinal single-developer case study compares an API-based frontier coding-agent configuration against an on-premise quantized open-weights configuration over two 28-day periods on a production monorepo. It finds prompt caching with a very high hit rate cut realized API cost sharply, informing cloud-versus-on-premise inference economics.

entry.title: WaterMoE: Expert-Routing-based Watermarking for High Fidelity and Efficiency

author.name: Z Sun, Q Jiang, S Sheng, L Xiang

entry.summary: WaterMoE proposes expert-routing-based watermarking for LLMs after benchmarking nine existing methods and finding most degrade quality or add prohibitive overhead, especially on restricted tasks. It aims for high fidelity and low-latency deployment via routing.

entry.title: TSSM: Triaxial State Space Model for Global Station Weather Forecasting with Temporal-Variable-Historical Modeling

author.name: Songru Yang, Zili Liu, Tao Han, Ben Fei, Fenghua Ling, Lei Bai, Chang Liu, Xiangyang Ji, Zhenwei Shi, Zhengxia Zou

entry.summary: TSSM is a triaxial state space model for global station weather forecasting that adds a temporal-variable-historical paradigm, incorporating period-aligned historical data to capture long-term periodic patterns beyond the lookback window. It targets improved accuracy on extreme events and reduced error accumulation.

entry.title: CoDiffGRN: Rethinking Gene Regulatory Network Inference via the BEELINE-KGC Benchmark and Co-evolutionary Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Jiaze Song, Runhao Zhao, Minghao Xu, Bin Cui, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: CoDiffGRN reformulates gene regulatory network inference as an inductive, ranking-centric graph-completion problem and introduces a benchmark with inductive gene-holdout splits and knowledge grounding, plus a co-evolutionary discrete-diffusion model. It targets researchers' real need for a small set of high-confidence interactions involving unseen genes.

entry.title: Adaptive Filtering of the KV Cache: Diagnosing and Correcting Structural-Role Bias in LLM Inference

author.name: Soumil Mandal

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses a structural-role bias in attention-based KV cache eviction, showing that on schema-dense inputs like nested JSON delimiter and structural key tokens accumulate far more attention energy and are over-retained relative to answer-carrying value tokens, collapsing exact-match accuracy at tight budgets. It proposes adaptive filtering to correct the bias.

entry.title: Efficient Text-to-Audio Generation via Pruning

author.name: Arshdeep Singh, Yi Yuan, Yun Chen, Wenwu Wang, Mark D. Plumbley

entry.summary: Applies filter pruning with norm-based criteria and light finetuning to the U-Net backbone of AudioLDM, removing up to 83% of parameters and 39% of MACs while recovering perceptual quality. It targets efficient deployment of diffusion text-to-audio models.

entry.title: Is the Statistical Advantage Worth the Cost? An Empirical Comparison of KANs and MLPs for Structured Data Classification

author.name: Matthew Steven P. Toledo, Justine Raphael H. Jacinto, Vivekjeet Singh Chambal, Rodolfo C. Camaclang III, Jamlech Iram N. Gojo Cruz, Reginald Neil C. Recario

entry.summary: Empirically benchmarks Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks against MLPs on twelve tabular classification datasets under standardized settings, finding KANs statistically outperform MLPs in binary and multiclass tasks. It weighs the accuracy advantage against computational cost.

entry.title: Traffic-Aware Randomized Smoothing for LLM-Based Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Zhenpeng Li

entry.summary: Traffic-Aware Randomized Smoothing certifies robustness of LLM-based network intrusion detectors by injecting Gaussian noise only into the attacker-controllable feature subspace during finetuning and certification. It identifies that standard randomized smoothing yields weak certified accuracy on clean-trained LLM-IDS.

entry.title: Unleashing Multimodal Large Language Models for Training-free HOI Detection in the Wild

author.name: Ting Lei, Jialin Liu, Zhu Xu, Yuxin Peng, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free human-object interaction detection method that exploits the multimodal reasoning of MLLMs rather than only extracting discriminative representations via prompting, aiming to generalize to open-world and compositional interactions. It disentangles interaction understanding from dataset-specific supervision.

entry.title: Music-to-Dance Generation via Atomic Movements

author.name: Xinhao Cai, Yixuan Sun, Minghang Zheng, Qingchao Chen, Xin Jin, Song-chun Zhu, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a structure-aware music-to-dance generation framework that models choreography as sequences of interpretable atomic movements, built by segmenting and clustering dance data and labeling clusters with an LLM. It aims to make generated dances more structurally coherent and controllable than continuous-signal approaches.

entry.title: Rethinking Penetration Testing for AI-Enabled Systems: From Resource Compromise to Behavioral Objective Violation

author.name: Mohammad Allahbakhsh, Mohammad Hassan Bahari, Moslem Attar-Raouf

entry.summary: Reframes penetration testing for AI-enabled systems from resource compromise toward objective-driven behavioral evaluation, noting adversaries can alter behavior via prompts, retrieved content, sensors, training data, memory, or tools without breaching infrastructure. It defines AI-enabled systems as those where learned models materially influence outcomes.

entry.title: Deep-learning Causal Retrieval Optimization for Efficient e-commerce Distribution in Pinterest

author.name: Junpeng Hou, XianXing Zhang, Sai Xiao, Derek Cheng, Darren Reger, Olafur Gudmundsson, Mehdi Ben Ayed, Zhiqing Rao, Huizhong Duan

entry.summary: Pinterest deploys a production causal decision system that triggers shopping candidate generators only when commerce content helps rather than distracts, using a deep multi-task model with doubly-robust uplift learning and randomized logging for counterfactual coverage. It personalizes and contextualizes triggering policies at scale.

entry.title: NexForge: Scaling Executable Agent Tasks via Requirement-First Synthesis

author.name: Jiarong Zhao, Zhikai Lei, Zhiheng Xi, Rui Zheng, Hang Yan, Jie Zhou, Qin Chen, Liang He

entry.summary: NexForge is a requirement-first framework that compiles free-form capability requirements into executable agent training data, using research-based demand discovery and distribution-aware task compilation instead of substrate-first pipelines tied to fixed tools. It aims to make agent training data reflect real-world demand.

entry.title: The Steering Budget: Examples beat Knobs

author.name: Raj Kumar Rajendran

entry.summary: This paper argues that the ceiling on steering generative models with knobs (prompts, guidance scales, tags) is a budget fixed by the training data, and that a large movable range can only be reached by showing concrete examples rather than turning knobs. It offers a way to predict this budget in advance.

entry.title: DiMaS: Distribution Matching for Steering Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Pegah Khayatan, Sara Meziane, Jayneel Parekh, Matthieu Cord

entry.summary: DiMaS is a distribution-matching steering strategy for flow-matching vision-language-action models that transports between representation distributions rather than shifting along a fixed linear direction, which the authors show fails in VLAs. It enables fine-grained behavioral control of how a robot performs tasks.

entry.title: NeuralChaos: Optimal Adapted Approximation of Square Integrable Predictable Processes

author.name: Anastasis Kratsios, Giulia Livieri, Philipp Schmocker

entry.summary: NeuralChaos is a neural operator architecture that approximates square-integrable predictable stochastic processes using only finitely many evaluations of the driving Brownian motion while preserving predictability. It aims to overcome the dictionary and iterated-integral costs of traditional Wiener-chaos expansions.

entry.title: MamaBench: Benchmarking LLM Robustness in Maternal and Child Health Diagnosis through Counterfactual Clinical Perturbation

author.name: Thanni Adewuyi, Anuoluwa Sotome, Samuel Okoko, Angel Ezendu, Oluwafunke Akinbuwa, Oluwaseun Odunsi, Oluwasegun Oguntuase, Oluwadarasimi Oguntuase, Ifeoma Nwabueze, Abiodun Adereni

entry.summary: MamaBench is a counterfactual benchmark for maternal and paediatric AI with 434 expert-authored clinical narratives in 217 pairs, measuring a Bias Trap Rate for whether models fail counterfactuals after succeeding on base cases. It also proposes an evidence-anchored retrieval method to improve robustness.

entry.title: Smarter and Cheaper at Once: Byte-Exact KV-Cache Grafting Turns a Frozen Small Model into a Verified-Knowledge Flywheel

author.name: Sietse Schelpe

entry.summary: The paper deposits verified knowledge as a byte-exact key-value cache artifact that can later be grafted into a fresh inference context of a frozen small model, producing bit-exact identical logits without changing weights. It verifies exactness across two model scales and GPU targets.

entry.title: Full-data accuracy with fewer labels for training and fine-tuning machine-learning force fields

author.name: Sheng Bi, Yi-Ze Wang, Jun Cheng

entry.summary: This work presents an active-learning workflow using last-layer-projection regression as a cheap per-configuration uncertainty estimator to build compact training sets that recover full-data accuracy for machine-learning force fields. It avoids the impractical committee approach for foundation MLFFs.

entry.title: Stop Thinking, Start Looking: Efficient Post-Training for Multimodal Document Question Answering via Reasoning-Free Alignment

author.name: Harikrishnan P M, Goutham Vignesh, Ganesh Parab, Saisubramaniam Gopalakrishnan, Vishal Vaddina, Varun V, Rohit Agrawal

entry.summary: Perception-RFT applies Group Relative Policy Optimization to multimodal document question answering, bypassing verbose intermediate reasoning tokens to directly align visual features with structured grounding outputs. It questions whether explicit reasoning traces are necessary and reduces inference token cost.

entry.title: Optimal Self-Distillation for Rectified Flow via Linear Probing

author.name: Saptarshi Roy, Debepsita Mukherjee, Pratik Patil

entry.summary: The paper studies optimal self-distillation for rectified flow, proving for linear rectified flow with ridge regularization an exact affine path identity and deriving the optimal mixing coefficient in closed form. It shows when a student trained on true and teacher velocities can provably improve a suboptimal teacher.

entry.title: Subjective Risk Decomposition: A New View for Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Raghad Alamri, Michele Caprio, Gavin Brown

entry.summary: The paper reframes uncertainty measures not as primitives requiring axioms but as consequences of decomposing a subjective risk based on a strictly proper loss, recovering classic epistemic and aleatoric terms and unifying many prior measures. It suggests deriving task-appropriate uncertainty measures from the modeling scenario and loss.

entry.title: Delocalization of bias in unadjusted Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and underdamped Langevin

author.name: Yifan Chen, Xiaoou Cheng, Jonathan Niles-Weed, Jonathan Weare

entry.summary: This theory paper extends the delocalization-of-bias phenomenon from overdamped Langevin to unadjusted Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and underdamped Langevin, showing that controlling the Wasserstein bias of any K-dimensional marginal needs only about square-root-K integration steps. It clarifies dimension dependence of bias in unadjusted samplers.

entry.title: Just Keep Prompting: Evaluating Repetitive Socratic Prompting in VLMs

author.name: Shayda Moezzi, Bishoy Galoaa, Lorena Genua, Taskin Padir, Sarah Ostadabbas

entry.summary: Just Keep Prompting is a multi-turn evaluation framework measuring vision-language model epistemic stability when users repeatedly challenge or contradict answers, using adversarial negation and Socratic strategies over up to 10 turns. It evaluates GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Qwen3-VL-30B on a STAR benchmark subset.

entry.title: The Severance Problem: LLMs are Unaware of the Person Beyond the Prompt

author.name: Dor Litvak, Liu Leqi

entry.summary: The Severance Problem argues personal AI assistants fail (sycophancy, overconfidence, hallucination) because models lack an explicit representation of the person beyond the provided context, especially what remains unknown. It frames this missing user-model as a fundamental limitation to address.

entry.title: Gold-Guided Programmatic Distillation for Financial Reasoning over Hybrid Tables and Text

author.name: Yun Dong, Erica Zhao, Elana Chen

entry.summary: This work distills numerical reasoning from a large teacher to a compact student over hybrid tabular-and-text financial data using execution-verified Python programs rather than free-form rationales, guided by gold derivations and filtered to programs that produce the gold answer. It aims for reliable supervision that avoids arithmetic errors in text rationales.

entry.title: MonteRET: AI Agent Enhancing Multimodal LLMs with Multi-granularity Knowledge Retrieval for Chest CT Report Generation

author.name: Yi Lin, Yihao Ding, Elana Benishay, Elefterios Trikantzopoulos, David Nauheim, Hanley Ong, Jiang Bian, Hua Xu, Yuzhe Yang, George Shih, Yifan Peng

entry.summary: MonteRET is a region-aware, retrieval-enhanced multimodal framework for chest CT report generation that combines global volume features with region-level anatomical representations, retrieves knowledge via predicted conditions and vision-language alignment, and refines reports with a rewriting agent. It was trained and evaluated on large public chest CT cohorts.

entry.title: MedFailBench: A Clinician-Built Open-Source Benchmark for Medical AI Safety Boundary Inspection

author.name: Goktug Ozkan

entry.summary: MedFailBench is a clinician-built synthetic benchmark and failure atlas that labels medical AI errors by severity (1-5) and safety-gate type (e.g., missed urgent escalation, unsafe remote dosing, evidence fabrication) rather than just correctness. The v0.2.1 release includes 44 clinician-reviewed cases, a taxonomy, and a live leaderboard.

entry.title: DCVC-MB: Neural B-Frame Video Compression using State Space Models

author.name: Arjun Arora, Calvin-Khang Ta, Carlos Restrepo-Galeano, Kruthi Murali, Naga Akhil E S, Arunkumar Mohananchettiar, Jay Shingala, Tong Shao, Peng Yin, Sean McCarthy

entry.summary: DCVC-MB is a neural B-frame video codec using state-space (Mamba-style) models for bidirectional temporal prediction, an IBP low-delay strategy, and an entropy-aware skipping mechanism to reduce coding time. It reports BD-rate reductions up to 8.98 percent on average over prior neural video codecs.

entry.title: VIABench: A Comprehensive Video Benchmark Collected from Blind Individuals for Visual Impairment Assistance

author.name: Yunfeng Liu, Yuandong Yang, Jiarui Han, Zhenpeng Huang, Yuqing Tang, Xiangyu Zeng, Gangshan Wu, Limin Wang

entry.summary: VIABench is a video benchmark built from first-person footage by visually impaired individuals to evaluate MLLMs on real blind-assistance tasks such as proactive reminders. It targets a practical accessibility gap in MLLM evaluation.

entry.title: FoMoVLA: Bridging Visual Foresight and Motion Guidance for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Wei Li, Peijin Jia, Yuan Ma, Xuefeng Jiang, Titong Jiang, Sheng Sun, Yujian Li, Xin Wen, Han Hong, Zhikang Liu, Bailin Li, Kun Zhan

entry.summary: FoMoVLA augments vision-language-action models with joint future feature foresight and sparse 2D point tracking, arguing these are complementary (goal state plus motion path). It adds explicit spatio-temporal supervision to otherwise reactive VLA policies.

entry.title: Benchmarking Face Recognition without Real Faces

author.name: Pawe{\l} Borsukiewicz, Daniele Lunghi, Wendk\^uuni C. Ou\'edraogo, Jacques Klein, Tegawend\'e F. Bissyand\'e

entry.summary: Investigates whether synthetic face datasets can replace real benchmarks for face recognition evaluation, testing 12 synthetic datasets against 7 real benchmarks with 24 pretrained models. It addresses the privacy gap left when training is synthetic but evaluation still uses real faces.

entry.title: MAGiSt3R: Multi-Agent Feed-forward 3D Reconstruction from Monocular RGB Videos

author.name: Ziren Gong, Xiaohan Li, Fabio Tosi, Ninghui Xu, Stefano Mattoccia, Jianfei Cai, Matteo Poggi

entry.summary: MAGiSt3R is a multi-agent feed-forward 3D reconstruction and camera-tracking framework for monocular RGB videos running near 10 FPS, using a 3R-family model with a MAGMA merging module plus pose-graph optimization to reduce drift. It reports superior accuracy versus state-of-the-art.

entry.title: Confidence-based Ranking with Adaptive Sampling for Noisy Black-Box Optimisation

author.name: Enrico Halim, Hemant Kumar Singh, Tapabrata Ray

entry.summary: Proposes a confidence-based ranking method with adaptive sampling to reduce the number of expensive evaluations needed for fitness estimation in noisy black-box optimization. It seeks a better balance than standard implicit and explicit averaging approaches.

entry.title: An Intelligent-Cloud Edge Multimodal Interaction System for Robots

author.name: Zihan Guo, Xiaoqi Li

entry.summary: Presents a cloud-edge multimodal robot interaction system pairing an enhanced YOLO gesture detector (with CBAM attention and DIoU loss) with coordinated LLM and VLM agents for scene understanding and task planning under limited onboard compute. It targets robust human-robot interaction in complex environments.

entry.title: Modeling and Validation of Quality of Control for Edge-Offloaded Collaborative Navigation

author.name: Neelabhro Roy, Mikael Hammarling, Victor Nan Fernandez-Ayala, Gourav Prateek Sharma, Mani H. Dhullipalla, Dimos V. Dimarogonas, James Gross

entry.summary: Extends a quality-of-control framework to model end-to-end wireless network effects on closed-loop performance for edge-offloaded collaborative navigation with dynamic collision avoidance, exploring how control parameters affect network latency and energy. It aims to avoid resource over-provisioning under stochastic delays.

entry.title: Human-Robot Interaction in GenAI Architectures via the Agent-Client Protocol

author.name: Jesus Moncada-Ramirez, Jose-Raul Ruiz-Sarmiento, Javier Gonzalez-Jimenez

entry.summary: Proposes adopting the Agent-Client Protocol, originally from coding agents, to standardize the human-robot interaction layer in GenAI/LLM-based robotic architectures, complementing the Model Context Protocol used for lower-level tool integration. It aims to reduce fragmentation in real-time human-in-the-loop robot collaboration.

entry.title: Goal-Oriented Semantic Communication for Distributed ISAC-Enabled Vehicle Coordination

author.name: Wenjie Liu, Yansha Deng

entry.summary: Investigates distributed integrated sensing and communication for vehicle coordination at unsignalized intersections, where roadside units jointly transmit sensing and command-and-control signals under a central base station using a goal-oriented semantic communication scheme. It aims to reduce redundant transmissions and stale state for reliable coordination.

entry.title: Precise sample covariance spectral norm error -- an RDT view

author.name: Mihailo Stojnic

entry.summary: Determines the precise limiting spectral-norm value of the sample covariance error for centered Gaussians using a Random Duality Theory framework, deriving explicit upper bounds and a novel bilinear-quadratic lower-bounding mechanism combined with a two-replica strategy. It moves beyond scaling characterizations to exact constants.

entry.title: Post Hoc Inference for Component Attribution in Multivariate Change-Point Detection

author.name: Dhia-Elhaq Ouerfelli, Sylvain Arlot, Kevin Bleakley, Patrick Pamphile

entry.summary: Develops post hoc statistical procedures to attribute a detected multivariate change-point to predefined coordinate blocks using nonparametric two-sample tests with Type I error control guarantees. It supports interpreting which components are responsible for a detected change.

entry.title: Oracle Agent Memory as an Enterprise Memory Substrate for Long-Horizon AI Agents

author.name: Richmond Alake, Cesare Bernardis, Paul Cayet, Luca Engel, Damien Hilloulin, Sungpack Hong, Allen Hosler, Nickolas Kavantzas, Ingo Kossyk, Son Le, Rhicheek Patra, Kartik Talamadupula, Valentin Venzin

entry.summary: This report describes Oracle Agent Memory, a database-native memory substrate for long-horizon agents that manages ingestion, extraction, consolidation, retrieval, and revision of durable state. It positions agent memory as a systems problem requiring lifecycle management under latency constraints.

entry.title: Can We Steer the Black-Box? Towards Controllability-Centric Evaluation of Recommender Systems with Collaborative Agents

author.name: Jiwen Zhou, Xiang Liu, Mingming Li, Pengbo Mo, Jiao Dai, Honglei Lv, Jizhong Han, Songlin Hu

entry.summary: CtrlBench-Rec is a collaborative multi-agent framework for evaluating recommender-system controllability across target content discovery, interest-profile shaping, and popularity-bias mitigation. It introduces steerability as a missing evaluation dimension for black-box recommenders.

entry.title: ScanFocus: A Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding

author.name: Kai Chen, Ming Dai, Wenxuan Cheng, Wankou Yang

entry.summary: ScanFocus is a coarse-to-fine framework for spatio-temporal video grounding that decouples global scanning from precise boundary focusing to recover high-frequency boundary cues lost under aggressive temporal downsampling. It improves object trajectory retrieval from language descriptions.

entry.title: Adversarial Prompting Framework for AI Safety Assessment

author.name: Yash Bhatnagar, Kunal Banerjee, Anirban Chatterjee

entry.summary: Implements an Adversarial Prompting Framework that systematically generates structured adversarial prompts at escalating sophistication levels, from direct harmful requests to encoding-based attacks, to assess GenAI model resilience. It provides a practical red-teaming safety-assessment tool.

entry.title: Privacy Leakage in Federated Learning in Radiology Reports: A Comparative Evaluation of Tokenizer-Driven Privacy Risks

author.name: Santhosh Parampottupadam, Andres Martinez, Dimitrios Bounias, Sinem Sav, Klaus Maier-Hein, Ralf Floca

entry.summary: Quantifies gradient-inversion privacy leakage in federated learning on radiology reports and compares three tokenizers under a fixed transformer architecture. It shows tokenizer design materially affects reconstructable sensitive information from shared gradients.

entry.title: GeoDetect: Geometric Adversarial Detection for VLPs

author.name: Afsaneh Hasanebrahimi, Hanxun Huang, Christopher Leckie, James Bailey, Sarah Erfani

entry.summary: GeoDetect studies the geometry of vision-language pretrained model embedding spaces, showing structured anisotropy under which adversarial examples exhibit greater geometric separation from clean examples, and uses this for adversarial detection. It extends single-modality detection insights to multimodal VLPs.

entry.title: ReportMedSAM: Guiding Segmentation Through Radiology Reports

author.name: Anghong Du, Theodoros N. Arvanitis, Colin Watts, Alejandro F. Frangi, Le Zhang

entry.summary: ReportMedSAM guides medical image segmentation directly from free-form radiology reports using a learnable concept bank and a frozen BiomedCLIP encoder, aligning organ-level concept embeddings with clinical corpora via contrastive learning. It aims to replace brittle rule-based phrase extraction for scalable, report-driven segmentation.

entry.title: The Misclassification of Autistic Writing as AI-Generated

author.name: Summer Chambers, Matthew C. Kelley

entry.summary: This study empirically tests the anecdotal claim that autistic writers' work is disproportionately flagged as AI-generated, comparing GPT-2 detector outputs on roughly 60,000 likely-autistic versus general Reddit posts. It examines whether detectors exhibit bias against a minority writing style.

entry.title: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Scientific Visualization Literacy

author.name: Patrick Phuoc Do, Chau M. Ta, Chaoli Wang

entry.summary: This work benchmarks six multimodal LLMs on a standardized scientific-visualization literacy assessment (49 items over 18 visualizations, 8 techniques, 11 task types) under a closed-world protocol, comparing against 485 human participants. It finds MLLM SciVis literacy is non-uniform, with Gemini strongest overall.

entry.title: MixCompress: Mixture of Experts for Variable Rate Learned Image Compression

author.name: Calvin-Khang Ta, Praneet Singh, Tong Shao, Peng Yin

entry.summary: MixCompress is a variable-rate learned image compression framework using sparsely gated mixture-of-experts routing to resolve feature entanglement between low-rate smoothing and high-frequency detail preservation across rate-distortion operating points. It replaces storing independent per-rate models with structural specialization.

entry.title: $K$-NeAS: Scalable Multi-Material CT Reconstruction Using Neural SDFs

author.name: Daksh K. Shah, Emmanouil Nikolakakis, Razvan V. Marinescu

entry.summary: K-NeAS is a scalable neural-SDF architecture for sparse-view multi-material CT reconstruction that replaces independent per-material networks with a shared latent backbone and removes rigid two-material constraints and manual attenuation bounds. It aims for automated multi-material surface reconstruction with lower radiation exposure.

entry.title: Emergent Region-Level Facial Correspondence in Frozen Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Izaldein Al-Zyoud, Abdulmotaleb El Saddik

entry.summary: This paper tests whether frozen DINOv3 features define a region-level facial coordinate system where facial parts remain distinguishable across identities and time without face-specific training, using patch embeddings and FaRL only as a labeling interface. It reports 83 percent region-level semantic accuracy on unconstrained cross-identity matching over real videos.

entry.title: Quantifying Training Membership Information in the Hyperspherical Embedding Geometry of Face Recognition Models

author.name: \"Unsal \"Ozt\"urk, S\'ebastien Marcel

entry.summary: Quantifies training-membership information leakage in the hyperspherical embedding geometry of face recognition models, computing cluster-geometry statistics across 180 models in a factorial design over backbone, loss, duration, and identity count. It links training factors to how member vs non-member clusters differ.

entry.title: HoloGeo: Mitigating Landmark Bias in Geo-localization via Evidence-Driven Reasoning

author.name: Pengcheng Zhou, Xuanyu Liu, Yanchen Yin, Bobo Li, Shengqiong Wu, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: HoloGeo mitigates landmark bias in VLM-based image geo-localization, introducing Bias Intensity and Bias Harmfulness metrics, the LandmarkBias-3K benchmark, and an evidence-driven reasoning framework backed by an annotated dataset. It aims to reduce reliance on spurious landmark correlations.

entry.title: Asymptotical Analysis of the $(1+(\lambda,\lambda))$ GA Escape Time from Local Optima on Jump Functions

author.name: Anton V. Eremeev, Valentin A. Topchii

entry.summary: Provides an asymptotic runtime analysis of the (1+(lambda,lambda)) genetic algorithm escaping local optima on Jump benchmark functions, using probability limit theorems to study escape time under tunable mutation, crossover, and population parameters. It advances theoretical understanding of evolutionary algorithm dynamics.

entry.title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable,Navigable, and Editable

author.name: Ruhan Wang, Yucheng Shi, Zongxia Li, Zhongzhi Li, Yue Yu, Junyao Yang, Kishan Panaganti, Haitao Mi, Dongruo Zhou, Leoweiliang

entry.summary: Harness Handbook addresses the behavior-to-code mapping problem in large agent harnesses, helping developers or coding agents locate all code implementing a target behavior before modification. It aims to make evolving agent harnesses readable, navigable, and editable.

entry.title: UESF-Bench: Benchmarking and Probing for Unified Embodied Seeking and Following

author.name: Kun Yu, Jianhua Yang, Yixiang Chen, Changwei Wang, Hongyuan Yu, Yan Huang, Fushuo Huo, Ya Jing, Zhumin Chen, Keji He

entry.summary: UESF-Bench unifies embodied seeking and following, requiring an agent to first find a language-described target and then persistently follow it in a dynamic environment, unlike prior benchmarks that assume the target is initially visible. It provides systematic evaluation and probing for this combined task.

entry.title: When Bots Join the Team: Bot Adoption and the Institutional Fabric of Open-Source Software Projects

author.name: Yongren Shi, Wenyi Gong

entry.summary: Studying 2,991 GitHub projects two years before and after their first bot adoption, this paper treats bots as team participants and measures repeated engagement, social memory, and role differentiation alongside conflict and output distinctiveness. It finds bot adoption is followed by stronger coordination signals.

entry.title: A Self-Evolving Agent for Longitudinal Personal Health Management

author.name: Haoran Li, Jiebi Deng, Tong Jin, Jinghong Han, Yuxin Wang, Zexin Wang, Qingyi Si, Weikang Gong, Xiahai Zhuang, Jia You, Wei Cheng, Jianfeng Feng, Hongcheng Guo

entry.summary: HealthClaw is an open-source self-evolving agent for longitudinal personal health management that separates shared safety rules and medical knowledge from private longitudinal memory, updating profiles, procedures, and episodic traces after each encounter. On a synthetic year-long benchmark it dramatically improves answer accuracy over current-query prompting.

entry.title: Deep Interaction: An Efficient Human-AI Interaction Method for Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Hefeng Zhou, Jinxuan Zhang, Jiong Lou, Yuxin Liu, Chaochao Lu, Jingjing Qu, Jie Li

entry.summary: Deep Interaction enables direct editing of a reasoning model's original chain-of-thought response so users can correct erroneous steps while preserving correct ones, then refines the edited reasoning, avoiding full regeneration or repeated flagging. It is an efficient human-intervention mechanism for large reasoning models.

entry.title: SingGuard-NSFA: Extensible Guardrails for Agentic AI via Generative Reasoning and Real-Time Classification

author.name: SingGuard Team

entry.summary: SingGuard-NSFA is a guardrail framework for agentic AI defending against prompt injection, sensitive-data extraction, malicious code, tool misuse, and resource exhaustion, organized by a CIA-triad-grounded NSFA taxonomy of 185 risk variants. It ships a large multilingual benchmark and a dual-mode detection approach combining generative reasoning and real-time classification.

entry.title: Efficient and Privacy Aware Edge Cloud Collaborative Inference for Large Language Models

author.name: Yi Li, Chen Li, Jiexiong Liu

entry.summary: This framework enables privacy-aware edge-cloud collaborative LLM inference built on endpoint-authenticated KV cache, with local devices handling preprocessing, embeddings, speculative decoding, and low-dimensional heads while the cloud performs authenticated decoder inference. It targets the latency-hardware-privacy trilemma of on-device LLMs.

entry.title: Audited Selective Verification for Risk-Controlled N-1 Thermal Contingency Screening under Deployment Shift

author.name: Jayakumar Manoharan

entry.summary: Introduces Audited Selective Verification, a risk-budgeted layer that lets a cheap surrogate skip most outage checks in power-grid N-1 contingency screening while an online audit and calibrated threshold certify a bound on missed thermal violations. It targets safe deployment of learned or optimization-based controllers under distribution shift.

entry.title: Symbiosis-Inspired Knowledge Distillation for Incremental Object Detection

author.name: Mingyue Zeng, De Cheng, Zhipeng Xu, Huaijie Wang, Nannan Wang, Xinbo Gao

entry.summary: SIKD proposes symbiosis-inspired knowledge distillation for incremental object detection, leveraging object co-occurrence and occlusion dependencies through shared representations rather than separating feature spaces. It aims to reduce catastrophic forgetting driven by ignoring spatial-semantic dependencies.

entry.title: Greedy Volume Maximization of Gradient Embeddings for Long-Tailed Frame-Level Bioacoustic Active Learning

author.name: Shiqi Zhang, Marius Fai{\ss}, Ariana Strandburg-Peshkin, Tuomas Virtanen

entry.summary: BADGE-Greedy-DPP is a deterministic active-learning batch selector that greedily adds the segment whose gradient embedding most enlarges the batch volume, with a submodular (1-1/e) optimality guarantee, for long-tailed frame-level bioacoustic annotation. It targets efficient labeling of rare sparse call types.

entry.title: GHR-VLM: Making Zero-Shot Transit Video Analytics Realizable with Grounded Hybrid Reasoning

author.name: Kaicong Huang, Weiheng Oh, Ruimin Ke

entry.summary: GHR-VLM is a grounded hybrid reasoning framework for zero-shot transit-bus video analytics using an edge-cloud design that converts long surveillance streams into compact passenger-centered spatiotemporal evidence to make VLM reasoning reliable and affordable. It avoids task-specific annotation while capturing fine-grained transit data.

entry.title: Beyond Color Geometry: Evaluating Human-Like Color Representations in Vision Models

author.name: Ayan Igali, Pakizar Shamoi

entry.summary: Evaluates whether vision models organize color the way humans do by comparing eleven Vision Transformer encoders against a fuzzy perceptual model of 86 graded human categories, measuring category boundaries, compactness, and graded alignment. It finds category-level similarity but diverging graded alignment across encoders.

entry.title: Certified Domain Consistency for Multi-Domain Retrieval: Label-Free Per-Domain Contamination Control with Conformal Risk Guarantees

author.name: Jayakumar Manoharan

entry.summary: Introduces C3R, a label-free control layer for multi-domain retrieval that certifies per-domain contamination budgets using risk-controlling prediction sets and abstains when a guarantee is infeasible. It targets the failure of standard conformal risk control to protect the worst-covered domains.

entry.title: Quantize with Confidence? An Empirical Study of Quantization for Code Generation

author.name: Saima Afrin, Md. Zahidul Haque, Antonio Mastropaolo

entry.summary: An empirical study evaluates six post-training quantization methods on Qwen2.5-Coder and CodeLlama across Python and Java benchmarks, assessing functional correctness alongside maintainability, reliability, and security of generated code. It targets local inference on resource-constrained hardware.

entry.title: Real-Time Detection of Charge Jumps in Superconducting Qubits with a Convolutional Neural Network

author.name: Daniel Gaytan-Villarreal, Peter Meiring, Daniel Baxter, Daniel Bowring, Grace Bratrud, Matteo Cremonesi, Giuseppe Di Guglielmo, Grace Wagner, Bowen Xiao

entry.summary: The paper presents an online convolutional neural network detector for charge jumps in superconducting qubits, based on a dilated causal CNN designed for in-the-loop deployment on quantum control hardware. It replaces offline detection with low-latency real-time detection trained on synthetic Ramsey tomography scans.

entry.title: Random Parameter Noise Does Not Make Exact ReLU Verification Easy

author.name: Mojtaba Soltanalian

entry.summary: This complexity-theory paper shows that adding clipped Gaussian noise to ReLU network weights does not make exact verification tractable, proving no sound-and-complete verifier runs in expected polynomial time under standard assumptions. The hardness holds even for tiny one-hidden-layer networks at a fixed noise level.

entry.title: ConFlow: Constraints-Guided Learning with Flow Matching for Motion Generation

author.name: Nutan Chen, Jianxiang Feng, Marvin Alles, Botond Cseke

entry.summary: ConFlow is a constraint-guided flow-matching framework that incorporates constraint information directly into the training objective via differentiable barrier or cost functions, rather than relying solely on inference-time guidance. It targets robot motion generation where task constraints are absent from the training data.

entry.title: One-Shot Generative Design for Disordered Metamaterials via Self-Organizing Neural Cellular Automata

author.name: Yujie Xiang, Liwei Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a one-shot generative design framework for disordered metamaterials using self-organizing neural cellular automata that grow complex microstructures through learned local interaction rules. It aims to overcome the data-hunger and poor generalization of prior generative approaches for irregular microstructures.

entry.title: SAGA: Schema-Aware Grounding for Agentic Text-to-SPARQL Generation

author.name: Yiming Zhang, Koji Tsuda

entry.summary: SAGA is an agentic text-to-SPARQL framework that improves knowledge-base grounding by systematically conditioning on entity types, property domains, and ranges rather than only lexical relevance during interactive query construction. It targets complex knowledge-base question answering via semantic parsing.

entry.title: Riesz-Kernel Stein Variational Gradient Descent: Renormalized Entropy and Long-Time Particle Limits

author.name: Trevor Teolis, Maarten V. de Hoop

entry.summary: This theory paper studies periodic Riesz-kernel Stein variational gradient descent with self-interaction removed and proves a many-particle, long-time sampling theorem showing convergence to the target distribution. It addresses the infinite self-interaction problem of singular Riesz kernels at finite particle counts.

entry.title: Domain Adaptation of Mismatched Proximal Denoiser for Plug-and-Play Image Reconstruction

author.name: Guixian Xu, Jinglai Li, Junqi Tang

entry.summary: The paper defines proximal mismatch as the discrepancy between a deployed denoiser and a target-domain proximal reference, and analyzes how this mismatch affects convergence of plug-and-play proximal gradient descent for image reconstruction. It also proposes domain adaptation to mitigate the mismatch.

entry.title: SMC-ES: Automated synthesis of formally verified control policies

author.name: Riccardo Curcio, Toni Mancini, Enrico Tronci

entry.summary: SMC-ES is a simulation-based methodology that automatically synthesizes control policies with formal statistical guarantees on performance, safety, and robustness, given a confidence parameter and allowable failure probability. It aims to bridge the gap between flexible learning-based controllers and formal safety guarantees.

entry.title: AlphaWiSE: Adaptive Weight Interpolation for Continual Multimodal Representation Learning

author.name: Sarthak Jain, Qiran Hu, Zhen Zhu, Yaoyao Liu

entry.summary: AlphaWiSE is a post-hoc weight-space interpolation method for continual multimodal learning that composes two frozen source checkpoints by fitting a single scalar coefficient per parameter tensor on a small exemplar memory. It avoids committing every retrieval direction to the same stability-plasticity trade-off in CLIP-style models.

entry.title: Concept-Guided Spatial Regularization for World Models in Atari Pong

author.name: Yukuan Lu, Zaishuo Xia, Weyl Lu, Yubei Chen

entry.summary: The paper studies five visual world-model agents (DreamerV3, DIAMOND, TWISTER, Simulus, STORM) in Atari Pong in isolation, freezing the learned models and running closed-loop rollout diagnostics that reveal failures like ball disappearance and incorrect dynamics. It then introduces concept-guided spatial regularization to improve them.

entry.title: Routing Ceilings Are Domain-Independent: Structural Prior Injection in Code Security Vulnerability Detection

author.name: Manuel Israel C\'azares

entry.summary: This paper tests whether the routing-ceiling phenomenon, where structural priors boost in-distribution performance but collapse below zero-shot out-of-distribution, is domain-independent by reproducing a math-reasoning design in code security vulnerability detection with three LLMs. It finds the same collapse, suggesting the effect is cross-domain.

entry.title: Show Me How You Reason and I'll Tell You Who You Are: Reasoning Graphs for Robust LLM Authorship Attribution

author.name: Zlata Kikteva, Artur Romazanov, Annette Hautli-Janisz, Ramon Ruiz-Dolz

entry.summary: This paper attributes LLM authorship by analyzing reasoning structures rather than surface linguistic features, using a graph neural network over reasoning graphs extracted by an argument-mining pipeline. It claims improved robustness to paraphrasing and better generalization than a Longformer baseline.

entry.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA

author.name: Sushant Gautam, Vajira Thambawita, Michael A. Riegler, P{\aa}l Halvorsen, Steven A. Hicks
