entry.summary: This retrospective analysis of nine GI-endoscopy VQA systems from MediaEval Medico 2025 examines design lessons for trustworthy medical multimodal QA, finding that answer-level gains do not consistently yield faithful clinical reasoning while structured reasoning and explicit grounding behave more reliably. It argues for evaluation beyond lexical overlap.

entry.title: DialogueVPR: Towards Conversational Visual Place Recognition

author.name: Yukun Song, Changwei Wang, Xingtian Pei, Shibiao Xu, Wenhao Xu, Shunpeng Chen, Yu Zhang, Ke Zhang, Rongtao Xu, Xuxiang Feng, Pengyang Wang

entry.summary: DialogueVPR reframes language-guided place recognition as interactive, dialogue-driven reasoning retrieval, introducing the DlgQuest-Cities benchmark and a framework coupling a cross-modal multi-level retriever with reasoning. It handles ambiguity and incompleteness in real-world natural-language location descriptions.

entry.title: 3D Lane Detection with Odometry for High-Speed Vehicle Racing

author.name: Omoruyi Atekha, John Subosits, Marcus Greiff

entry.summary: This paper introduces a new dataset of over 250k images plus inertial measurements for 3D lane detection in high-speed vehicle racing, captured on a closed circuit, and proposes methods enabling near-300Hz multi-camera processing with high accuracy. It extends lane detection to extreme racing geometries underexplored in regular driving.

entry.title: VTM-Nav: Hierarchical Visual-Topological Memory for Cross-Episode Object-Goal Navigation

author.name: Xiaoran Xu, Yupeng Wu, Tianyu Xue, Yifan Xu, Xuanran Dong, Xiaoshan Yang, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: VTM-Nav proposes a training-free VLM navigation framework with persistent hierarchical visual-topological memory for cross-episode object-goal navigation, letting agents reuse experience in the same scene. It introduces a new cross-episode evaluation protocol.

entry.title: ReBind: Multi-Reference Video Editing via Structured Instructions with Explicit Reference Relationships

author.name: Xinyu Liu, Shihao Li, Weihong Lin, Xinlong Chen, Yang Shi, Yujin Han, Yiyang Cai, Yanghao Wang, Ruibin Yuan, Yuanxing Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Wenhan Luo, Yike Guo

entry.summary: ReBind introduces structured editing instructions with embedded reference tokens as an intermediate representation for multi-reference image-conditioned video editing, addressing failures in coordinating multiple visual sources. It targets accurate reference relationships in diffusion-based editing.

entry.title: Rare Concept Generation via Counterfactual Inference in Diffusion Models

author.name: Zhengyuan Jiang, Haipeng Liu, Meng Wang, Yang Wang

entry.summary: CI-Diff uses counterfactual inference to generate rare concepts with unusual attributes by blocking diffusion models' common-knowledge bias that ties objects to their typical attributes. It targets correct attribute rendering for atypical prompts.

entry.title: Blurring Modal Boundaries: A Unified Survey from Single- to Multi-Modal Person Re-ldentification

author.name: Xiao Wang, Bing Wang, Bin Yang, Cuiqun Chen, Xin Xu, Mang Ye

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of person re-identification's transition from single-modal RGB to cross-modal and multi-modal paradigms, covering visible-infrared, text-image, sketch-based, and non-line-of-sight ReID. It organizes tasks and emerging directions.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Diffusion for Biomechanically Plausible 3D Sign Language Generation

author.name: Emanuele Colonna, Moises Diaz, Gennaro Vessio, Miguel Angel Ferrer, Giovanna Castellano

entry.summary: PIDiffSign is a physics-informed diffusion model for gloss-to-pose 3D sign language generation that embeds anatomical constraints into both architecture and training to enforce biomechanical plausibility. It jointly targets semantic fidelity and joint/bone constraints.

entry.title: On Success and Simplicity: A Second Look at Transferable Vision-Language Attack Pipeline

author.name: Yuchen Ren, Zhengyu Zhao, Chenhao Lin, Bo Yang, Chao Shen

entry.summary: Argues that transferable adversarial attacks on vision-language pretraining models can be simpler yet stronger, identifying three overlooked cross-modal issues and proposing the streamlined SimVLA pipeline. It reports improved transferability and efficiency across datasets and tasks.

entry.title: From Draft to Draft-Free: One-Step Video Object Removal via Privileged Distillation and Fast Planting

author.name: Zizhao Chen, Ping Wei, Guang Dai, Jingdong Wang, Mengmeng Wang

entry.summary: D2DF distills a multi-step teacher that refines coarse video object-removal drafts into a one-step generation model via privileged distillation and fast planting, aiming for high-fidelity removal without slow denoising. It targets practical, artifact-free video editing.

entry.title: ARMOR++: Agentic Orchestration of a Multi-Domain Primitive Set for Transferable Attacks on Deepfake Detectors

author.name: Christos Korgialas, Gabriel Lee Jun Rong, Dion Jia Xu Ho, Pai Chet Ng, Xiaoxiao Miao, Konstantinos N. Plataniotis

entry.summary: ARMOR++ is a multi-agent framework for high-transferability black-box attacks on deepfake detectors, using a vision-language model for spatial semantic priors and an LLM to orchestrate selection of multi-domain attack primitives under no-query constraints. It targets fragile architecture-dependent forensic cues.

entry.title: Mixed-Agent Museum Tour Guide Design Improves Gendered Learning Outcomes and Visitor Preferences

author.name: Annette M. Masterson, Wonse Jo, Helena C. Sieh, Lionel P. Robert, Jr., Dawn Tilbury

entry.summary: Presents a mixed-agent museum tour guide combining a physical robot with a projected virtual agent, evaluated in a within-subjects study of 30 participants for engagement, experience, and learning, with attention to gendered learning outcomes. It reports the single platform can deliver the interaction richness of two agents.

entry.title: Parsimonious Mixtures of Skewed Bilinear Factor Analyzers

author.name: Jacob Moore, Michael P. B. Gallaugher

entry.summary: Proposes a parsimonious family of 256 mixture models for clustering skewed matrix-variate data using bilinear factor analyzers with the skew-t distribution and constrained cluster parameters, with an AECM estimation algorithm. It is evaluated on simulations and image datasets such as MNIST and Olivetti faces.

entry.title: Tabular Foundation Models for Discrete Choice Estimation

author.name: Liu Liu, Dan Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates applying tabular foundation models to discrete choice demand estimation and finds direct application weak due to their row-independence assumption. It proposes a reformulation encoding choice-set dependence and consumer heterogeneity, showing heterogeneity encoding drives predictive gains.

entry.title: Cover First, Disagree Softly: Rethinking Mismatch-First Active Learning for Frame-Level Audio Classification

author.name: Shiqi Zhang, Tuomas Virtanen

entry.summary: Rethinks the mismatch-first farthest-traversal acquisition strategy for frame-level audio active learning, showing its hard sequential grouping ignores similarity among selected segments and fails under low budgets. It proposes a coverage-first, soft-disagreement selection that outperforms mismatch-first variants.

entry.title: NodeImport: Imbalanced Node Classification with Node Importance Assessment

author.name: Nan Chen, Zemin Liu, Bryan Hooi, Bingsheng He, Jun Hu, Jia Chen

entry.summary: NodeImport tackles class-imbalanced node classification by using a balanced meta-set to measure node importance, deeming a training node significant if it improves performance under an unbiased setting. It aims to overcome majority-class overfitting that afflicts standard GNNs.

entry.title: Local Additive Feature Attribution: A Mathematical Taxonomy and Reporting Checklist

author.name: Rebecca Afriyie Sarpong, Daniel Commey

entry.summary: Provides a mathematical taxonomy organizing local additive feature-attribution methods (Shapley, path, gradient, perturbation, CAM) around five specification choices, plus an axiom-by-method matrix and a reporting checklist. It links common failure modes to specification decisions.

entry.title: MARS: Multi-hop Adaptive Retrieval and SPARQL Generation for KGQA

author.name: Nikit Srivastava, Daniel Vollmers, Ren\'e Speck, Nikolaos Karalis, Hamada M. Zahera, Axel-Cyrille Ngonga Ngomo

entry.summary: MARS is a fine-tuning-free knowledge-graph QA approach that performs structured multi-hop retrieval, linking question entities to a KG and iteratively retrieving next-hop information, then generating SPARQL. It aims to reduce hallucination and keep knowledge updatable without retraining.

entry.title: Latent Trajectory Discrimination for AI-Generated Text Detection

author.name: Gianluca Bonifazi, Christopher Buratti, Michele Marchetti, Federica Parlapiano, Giulia Quaglieri, Davide Traini, Domenico Ursino, Luca Virgili

entry.summary: GTCL reframes AI-generated text detection as distinguishing latent generation trajectories, segmenting documents into ordered units and modeling how representations evolve across the sequence with geometric and contrastive learning. It moves beyond static aggregate-statistic detectors.

entry.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations

author.name: Yazhi Zhang, Fuqiang Niu, Bowen Zhang

entry.summary: TikStance is a multimodal, hierarchical dataset of 161 TikTok videos and 13,876 comments for multi-target stance detection on three 2024 U.S. election figures, linking host videos and metadata to parent-linked comment trees. It preserves audiovisual and conversational context often missing in stance datasets.

entry.title: Memory-Driven Self-Disclosure and Relational Turning Points: A Longitudinal Multimodal Study of Human-AI Interaction

author.name: Ryuichi Sumida, Mao Saeki, Masaki Eguchi, Sadahiro Yoshikawa, Koji Inoue, Tatsuya Kawahara, Yoichi Matsuyama

entry.summary: This longitudinal multimodal study (24 participants over 10 sessions) examines how repeated interactions with a memory-augmented conversational agent become a relationship, rating familiarity, self-disclosure, perceived memory, quality, and enjoyment. It finds conversational quality drives in-the-moment enjoyment while perceived memory is relationally conditioned and shapes later outcomes.

entry.title: MultiRef-Compass: Towards Comprehensive Evaluation of Multi-Reference-to-Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Xiaohan Zhang, Yuqing Wen, Junlin Chen, Yuqi Tang, Yiting He, Lizhuo Shao, Weiming Zhu, Tengfei Liu, Yang Shi, Jialu Chen, Yuanxing Zhang, Huaxiong Li

entry.summary: MultiRef-Compass is a unified benchmark for multi-reference-to-audio-video generation, where models must jointly reason over multiple reference images and text to produce synchronized visual and audio content while faithfully preserving and composing referenced entities. It targets an emerging setting largely absent from existing benchmarks.

entry.title: KeyFrame-Compass: Towards Comprehensive Evaluation of Keyframe-Conditioned Video Generation

author.name: Yuqi Tang, Tengfei Liu, Yizheng Lai, Yuran Wang, Yang Shi, Wanshun Su, Zhuoran Zhang, Qixun Wang, Xiaohan Zhang, Xinlei Yu, Xuehai Bai, Xuanyu Zhu, Bohan Zeng, Bozhou Li, Shujie Li, Yifan Dai, Yujie Wei, Shixuan Liu, Haotian Wang, Jialu Chen, Yuanxing Zhang

entry.summary: KeyFrame-Compass is described as the first comprehensive benchmark for keyframe-conditioned video generation, with 386 curated samples spanning multiple domains, structures, prompt granularities, conditioning formats, and keyframe densities, plus an automated evaluation framework. It tests whether models faithfully reproduce prescribed keyframes while maintaining video quality.

entry.title: Reinforcing Egocentric Spatial Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models via Ego Scene Augmentation

author.name: Chi Kit Wong, Ye Pan, Yuanhuiyi Lyu, Xu Zheng, Zidong Cao, Lutao Jiang, Zixin Zhang, Huiyu Zhou, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: Ego Scene Augmentation enhances egocentric spatial reasoning in multimodal LLMs using an Ego-element Graph as an intermediary representation powered by vision foundation models. It targets egocentric visual question answering for embodied interaction.

entry.title: Breaking the Model Forgetting Cycle in Long-Incremental 3D Object Detection

author.name: Peisheng Qian, Jie Xu, Xulei Yang, Na Zhao

entry.summary: Identifies a self-reinforcing forgetting cycle in long-incremental 3D object detection and proposes a Learning-Dynamics-driven Memory and Review method inspired by human learning. It targets catastrophic forgetting over long class-incremental sequences.

entry.title: MagicPrompt: Ultra-Lightweight Prompt Tuning for Video Generation

author.name: Yinhan Zhang, Dinwei Tan, Xianghao Kong, Yue Ma, Yeying Jin, Anyi Rao

entry.summary: MagicPrompt is an ultra-lightweight prompt-tuning method for large video diffusion models, using attention-embedded soft prompts and a stabilized reward objective to cut trainable parameters while keeping pretrained knowledge. It targets stable, parameter-efficient adaptation.

entry.title: Causal-Adversarial Probing of Clinical Covariates for Prostate MRI Grading

author.name: Yipei Wang, Shiqi Huang, Wen Yan, Weixi Yi, Dean C. Barratt, Mark Emberton, Daniel C. Alexander, Veeru Kasivisvanathan, Yipeng Hu

entry.summary: Introduces a causal-reasoning, adversarial framework to probe whether clinical covariates in prostate MRI cancer grading act as useful disease proxies or non-generalizing shortcuts, modeling MRI and grade as observations of latent pathology. It aims to interpret covariate dependence in ISUP grade prediction.

entry.title: WorkDrive: Roadwork Chain of Causation for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Tianyi Jiang, Wen Zhang, Sihan Yang, Ming Lu, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: WorkDrive builds perception-grounded causal reasoning for roadwork zones and aligns it with trajectory prediction to help driving VLMs handle altered lane markings, cones, and barriers. It injects structured scene facts into a chain-of-causation annotation pipeline.

entry.title: VQ-Touch: A Data-Efficient Tactile Generation Framework Across Sensors and Scenarios

author.name: Kailin Lyu, Long Xiao, Jianing Zeng, Di Wu, Lin Shu, Jie Hao

entry.summary: VQ-Touch is a data-efficient tactile image generation framework using a DM-VQGAN representation that generalizes across sensors and scenarios. It aims to synthesize high-fidelity tactile data to reduce reliance on expensive, wear-prone tactile sensors.

entry.title: SUFLECA: Scaling Up Feature Learning for CAD-to-image Alignment

author.name: Saad Ejaz, Miguel Fernandez-Cortizas, Javier Civera, Holger Voos, Jose Luis Sanchez-Lopez

entry.summary: SUFLECA is a weakly-supervised framework for zero-shot 9D CAD-to-image alignment that scales geometry-grounded feature learning from pretrained visual representations using Normalized Object Coordinates supervision on 674K images. It aims to improve robustness under occlusion and sim-to-real shift.

entry.title: CRISP: Constrained Refinement via Iterative Squeezing Process for Robust Medical Image Segmentation under Domain Shift

author.name: Yizhou Fang, Pujin Cheng, Yixiang Liu, Xiaoying Tang, Longxi Zhou

entry.summary: CRISP performs source-only robust medical image segmentation under distribution shift by assuming rank stability of positive regions and iteratively squeezing constrained refinements to derive robust spatial hints. It targets generalization to unpredictable real-world shifts without target data.

entry.title: Improving Molecular Property Prediction in Small Language Models Using Graph-based Tools

author.name: Konstantinos Bougiatiotis, Dimitrios Kelesis, Georgios Paliouras

entry.summary: The authors add graph-based tool use to small language models for molecular property prediction, feeding GNN expert hints and explanatory subgraphs into prompts to overcome structural blindness of SMILES strings. Enriched prompts improve zero-shot prediction on MUTAG and Tox21.

entry.title: AI-Native Insurance for Agentic AI: Pricing, Underwriting, and End-to-End Automation

author.name: Quanyan Zhu

entry.summary: This paper builds a mathematical framework for underwriting, pricing, and contract design for agentic AI deployments, mapping a risk state (autonomy, authority, permissions, governance, dependency) to premiums, deductibles, and covenants. It formulates insurance-contract design as an optimization problem.

entry.title: How Far Can Root Cause Analysis Go on Real-World Telemetry Data?

author.name: Athira Gopal, Ashwanth Krishnan

entry.summary: This paper tackles root cause analysis over large-scale multimodal telemetry (metrics, logs, traces) where classical causal discovery and existing LLM multi-agent systems fail on the OpenRCA benchmark. It presents a structured multi-agent RCA pipeline that substantially outperforms baselines in both domain-knowledge and knowledge-free modes.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Collaborative Reasoning with Tool-Augmented Evidence for Urban Region Profiling

author.name: Xixuan Hao, Yutian Jiang, Jiabo Liu, Yihang Yang, Guangyin Jin, Song Gao, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: UrbanAgent reframes urban region profiling as reasoning-driven agentic inference rather than correlation-based multimodal fusion, using tool-augmented evidence and collaborative reasoning. It aims for robustness in heterogeneous or unseen regions where static pipelines fail.

entry.title: Explaining Reinforcement Learning Agents via Inductive Logic Programming

author.name: Celeste Veronese, Edoardo Zorzi, Daniele Meli, Alessandro Farinelli

entry.summary: This work introduces objective, planning-oriented metrics for quantifying the explainability of reinforcement learning policies expressed via inductive logic programming, moving XRL beyond user studies. It aims to give compact, human-readable logical abstractions of RL decision-making with shared evaluation criteria.

entry.title: CAVA: Canonical Action Verification and Attestation for Runtime Governance of Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Zexun Wang

entry.summary: CAVA is a runtime-semantics layer that converts heterogeneous agent activity across many runtimes into canonical action objects, binding approvals to execution so an independent verifier can reproduce the same action identity. It targets runtime governance and auditability of agentic AI.

entry.title: Beyond Backbone Backpropagation: A Decoupled Strategy for Efficient Transfer Learning

author.name: Daniel Vila-Cruz, Laura Mor\'an-Fern\'andez, Ver\'onica Bol\'on-Canedo

entry.summary: This transfer-learning strategy adapts only normalization layers to a new domain and decouples feature extraction from classifier optimization by precomputing features once, plus a margin-based weighted-loss classifier head, avoiding end-to-end backpropagation. It reduces compute and energy across CNN and Transformer backbones on medical image datasets.

entry.title: HRO: Hierarchical Room-to-Object Framework for Zero-Shot Object Goal Navigation with Large Language Models

author.name: Luyuan Jia, Yinfeng Yu

entry.summary: HRO is a hierarchical room-to-object framework for zero-shot object-goal navigation that uses LLM priors with human-like room-to-object spatial cognition, rather than flat object-region association. It aims to reduce blind exploration and improve semantic association accuracy.

entry.title: Self-Improving AI Coding Agents Through Accumulated Behavioral Rules: A Closed-Loop Framework

author.name: Aditya Aggarwal, Nahid Farhady Ghalaty

entry.summary: This closed-loop framework has coding agents codify each accepted human-review comment into a persistent behavioral rule, growing a version-controlled instruction file, a pre-submission self-review checklist, and automated integrity validation. In a multi-service microservices deployment the rule set grew and expanded self-detectable error classes.

entry.title: STKAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Spatio-Temporal Forecasting

author.name: Sicong Lai, Yuehong Hu, Siru Zhong, Si Qiao, Yuxuan Liang, Guangyin Jin

entry.summary: STKAN introduces Taylor-polynomial Kolmogorov-Arnold Network modules into spatial and temporal token mixing for spatio-temporal forecasting, using learnable soft node-group assignment for group-wise spatial mixing. It emphasizes the underexplored role of the nonlinear function approximator in traffic forecasting.

entry.title: A Hybrid Mamba for Audio-Visual Navigation

author.name: Yi Wang, Yinfeng Yu

entry.summary: Samba is a hybrid Mamba architecture for audio-visual navigation that replaces GRUs with a selective Mamba state encoder for temporal aggregation and adds an audio Mamba encoder to capture global time-frequency dependencies in spectrograms. It updates a backbone that had stagnated since 2020.

entry.title: IMMNet: Hybrid Fusion of Model-based and Data-driven Approaches for Maneuvering Target Tracking

author.name: Yixuan Zhao, Chaoqun Yang, Lin Gao, Yongxiao Tian, Ting Yuan

entry.summary: IMMNet fuses the interpretable interacting-multiple-model tracking structure with learnable neural components for 3D maneuvering target tracking, preserving Bayesian inference while adaptively learning motion patterns and noise. It outperforms existing trackers across scenarios for radar applications.

entry.title: From Language to Navigation Goals: A Vision-Language Approach for Semantic Navigation of Mobile Robots Using RGB-D Perception

author.name: Jose Mart\'inez-Fajardo, Pablo Pueyo, Fernando Caballero, Luis Merino

entry.summary: Presents a modular ROS 2 vision-language navigation framework that turns natural-language target requests into executable goals for mobile robots using RGB-D perception. It integrates language understanding, environment perception, and autonomous navigation for non-expert users.

entry.title: Lyapunov Guidance: A Unified Framework for Stabilizing Generative Flows

author.name: Jingdong Zhang, Xinze Li, Yize Jiang, Luan Yang, Minkai Xu, Junhong Liu

entry.summary: Proposes LIGO-PINN, which uses learned initialization via gated optimization to alleviate convergence failures and trivial-solution collapse in physics-informed neural networks across challenging and unseen PDE domains. It aims to replace expensive hyperparameter tuning and curriculum design.

entry.title: Interpretable Language Model for Closed-Loop Type 1 Diabetes Control

author.name: Maya Sarkar

entry.summary: LLM-T1D distills an expert reinforcement learning insulin controller into fine-tuned Llama 3.1 8B and Qwen3 8B models to create a more interpretable, human-readable artificial pancreas controller. The goal is to make automated insulin delivery more trustworthy for patients and clinicians.

entry.title: Enhancing Small Language Models Reasoning through Knowledge Graph Grounding

author.name: Dimitrios Kelesis, Konstantinos Bougiatiotis, Georgios Paliouras

entry.summary: The paper enhances small language models (Gemma 3 1B/4B, Llama 3.2 3B) for multi-hop reasoning by turning them into minimalist neuro-symbolic agents with fact-extraction and hint tools backed by a relational graph convolutional network, tested on the CLUTRR kinship benchmark. It aims for sustainable reasoning without large models.

entry.title: Operator-Informed Gaussian Processes for Complex Helmholtz Wavefields: From Synthetic Benchmarks to In Vivo Brain Elastography

author.name: Boyuan Deng, Kshitiz Upadhyay, Michael Shields

entry.summary: The work extends operator-informed Gaussian process regression to complex-valued Helmholtz wavefields by realifying the complex operator into a coupled real block, enabling uncertainty-aware inference from sparse noisy data. It is demonstrated from synthetic benchmarks to in vivo brain elastography.

entry.title: Spectral Concentration and Recovery in Sparse High-Dimensional Random Geometric Graphs

author.name: Manuel Fernandez V, Yizhe Zhu

entry.summary: This theory paper proves sharper spectral norm concentration bounds for sparse high-dimensional random geometric graphs formed by thresholding inner products of latent vectors on the sphere or Gaussian. It improves prior bounds under weaker assumptions and covers recovery.

entry.title: LBA: Textual Hard-Label Adversarial Attack under Low Query Budgets

author.name: Shixin Guo, Ming Zhong, Xuhong Zhang, Dandan Zhao, Zhe Wang, Bo Zhang, Shouling Ji, Hao Peng

entry.summary: LBA is a sampling-based method for generating high-quality textual hard-label adversarial examples under low query budgets by constructing an approximate distribution over adversarial examples using prior and observed information, rather than greedy local search. It aims to reduce excessive query costs while finding better adversarial samples.

entry.title: Automatically Evolving Prompt Guidelines for Task-Specific Optimization

author.name: Cedric Richter, Salah Ghamizi, Mike Papadakis

entry.summary: The paper studies prompt guideline optimization, automatically generating task-specific guidelines from completed task examples to help users write better-specified prompts, addressing the limits of generic manual guidelines. It targets the problem of underspecified user queries misaligning with intent.

entry.title: Eta Given Delta: Defining LLM Tool Efficiency With Marginal Tool Utility

author.name: Nyx Iskandar

entry.summary: The paper introduces tool efficiency, a metric for the rate of useful tool calls in an LLM agent trajectory, defined via a new marginal tool utility metric that indicates whether each tool call is useful or safely removable. Marginal tool utility signs are determined using LLM-as-a-judge.

entry.title: Semantic Register Compression in Multi-Agent LLM Cascades

author.name: Manuele Tele Junior Fernandez

entry.summary: This paper identifies semantic register compression, a failure mode where intermediate agents in multi-agent LLM cascades flatten semantic distinctions when transforming text across registers. Using a three-agent pipeline it quantifies degraded label separability across fact-checking, sentiment, and medical triage tasks.

entry.title: DS@GT ARC at LongEval: Citation Integrity and Factual Grounding in Scientific QA

author.name: Brandon Michaels, Brendon Johnson

entry.summary: A CLEF 2026 LongEval RAG submission examining divergence between standard NLG metrics and citation integrity, applying Corrective RAG and CiteFix to enforce entailment of claims to cited materials. It finds frontier models score high on fluency yet often fail to actually ground answers in retrieved context.

entry.title: Harnessing LLMs for Reliable Academic Supervision: A Comparative Study

author.name: Akash Raj

entry.summary: A case study in harness engineering for academic supervision, comparing an unscaffolded GPT-5 chatbot against a multi-module system wrapping a smaller GPT-4o-mini in a LangGraph harness with symbolic filters, retrieval, schema-typed I/O, judge loops, and human-in-the-loop gates. It argues deterministic scaffolding around a small core can outperform a raw large model.

entry.title: Expanding the Lexicon of Ge'ez Based African Languages: A Comparative Study of Amharic and Tigrinya

author.name: Hailay Kidu Teklehaymanot, Debela Desalegn Yadeta, Wolfgang Nejdl

entry.summary: VEXMLM extends XLM-R's vocabulary with 30,000 Ge'ez-script subwords from a custom tokenizer trained on Amharic and Tigrinya corpora, initializing new embeddings by averaging constituent embeddings to reduce OOV rates and subword fragmentation. It is further evaluated across 17 additional low-resource African languages.

entry.title: The Energy Society: A Simulation Environment for Studying Agent Cooperation under Survival Pressure

author.name: Lucas Bergholdt Hansen, Federico Torrielli, Filippo Tonini, Lukas Galke Poech

entry.summary: The Energy Society is a minimal survival-economy simulation where LLM agents spend energy to generate tokens (scaled by model size), regain it by completing jobs or receiving donations, and deactivate at zero, enabling study of cooperation under survival pressure. Larger models consistently consume more energy than they gain across competitive, cooperative, and baseline settings.

entry.title: TanGO: Training-Free 3D Editing via Tangent-Space Guidance and Optimization

author.name: Siwoo Lim, Sunjae Yoon, Gwanhyeong Koo, Hyeonseo Yun, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: TanGO is a training-free 3D editing framework offering per-token steering in the tangent space of flow-matching 3D generative dynamics, using a directional discrepancy to set control strength. It reduces structural artifacts in editing structured 3D representations.

entry.title: U-shaped Multi-granularity Learning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Biao Chen, Yunqian Yu, Xiangxu Zhao, Zhongshu Chen, Mengmeng Jing, Lin Zuo

entry.summary: UPrompt is a U-shaped multi-granularity prompt-learning framework for vision-language models that integrates coarse-to-fine representations across visual and textual modalities, inspired by U-Net. It targets the granularity dilemma for dense prediction and cross-task generalization.

entry.title: JADE-GS: Joint Alternating Deblurring Guided by Events in 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Haoyu Fu, Jiafeng Huang, Yuchen Wang, Shengjie Zhao

entry.summary: JADE-GS jointly performs deblurring guided by event cameras within 3D Gaussian Splatting, using a pixel-adaptive routing gate to fuse physics-based and learned restoration priors coupled with the 3D optimization. It addresses motion blur that destroys 3D supervision.

entry.title: RoGS: Adaptive Meshgrid Gaussian for Large-Scale Road Surface Mapping

author.name: Tianchen Deng, Zhiheng Feng, Wenhua Wu, Ziming Li, Siting Zhu, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: RoGS (ROADGS-T) proposes adaptive meshgrid Gaussian representation placing 2D Gaussian surfels on a meshgrid storing color, semantic, and geometric info for efficient large-scale road surface mapping. It targets HD map generation and lane-level perception in driving.

entry.title: OvAi Focus: AI-based Multi-class Segmentation of Functional Ovaries and Adnexal Masses in Gynecological Ultrasound

author.name: Niccol\`o Tallone, Francesca Salis, Pio Raffaele Fina, Roberta Massobrio, Rosilari Bellacosa Marotti, Daniele Conti, Luca Fuso, Luca Mariani, Annamaria Ferrero, Alessandro Arena, Stefano Cosma, Dan Grisaru, Angelo Lacalandra, Renato Seracchioli, Marianna Roccio, Federica Gerace

entry.summary: OvAi Focus is a standalone AI medical-device software performing multi-class segmentation of functional ovaries and adnexal masses in gynecological ultrasound, distinguishing cystic from solid components, validated on 1,081 women across six centers. It reports DICE scores in line with or above state of the art.

entry.title: Skeleton: Visual Authoring of Non-visual Data Experiences

author.name: Frank Elavsky, Chieri Nnadozie, Lucas Nadolskis, Patrick Carrington, Dominik Moritz

entry.summary: Skeleton is a visual authoring tool letting sighted practitioners see and design the navigation structures (nodes, edges, input bindings) that assistive technologies traverse, developed through longitudinal co-design and including an inspector rendering navigation graphs. It addresses the missing feedback loop for non-visual data experiences.

entry.title: Can we build an early warning system for loss of control to AI?

author.name: David Johnston

entry.summary: A conceptual analysis asking whether a mathematical early-warning system could forecast loss of control to AI along the current trajectory, weighing the difficulty of modeling contested concepts and observing deceptive systems against the high value of such a forecast. It frames the trade-offs between under- and over-reacting under deep uncertainty.

entry.title: Discourse-Aware Policy Analysis with Argumentation: A Hybrid LLM-Symbolic Framework for Disaster Governance

author.name: Stylianos Loukas Vasileiou, Olga Derendiaeva

entry.summary: Apaf is a hybrid LLM-symbolic pipeline that turns critical discourse analysis of policy documents into a quantitative bipolar argumentation framework, exposing frame-mediated tensions that pure summarization hides. It targets inspectable, contestable policy reasoning for disaster governance.

entry.title: Barnamala: Parameter-Efficient Handwritten Devanagari Recognition at Benchmark Saturation

author.name: Ashish Thapa, Samrat Karki

entry.summary: Builds a 1.11M-parameter convolutional network reaching 99.73% on 46-class Devanagari handwriting recognition, 15.6x smaller than prior SOTA, and shows every model tested hits the same 11-error intrinsic floor indicating benchmark saturation. It also reports transfer and corruption robustness.

entry.title: CoTu at EXACT 2026: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Transparent Educational QA

author.name: Quoc-Khang Tran, Minh-Thien Nguyen, Phu-An Thai, Xuan-Tung Bui, Truong-Thanh Ma, Nguyen-Khang Pham

entry.summary: CoTu is a neuro-symbolic Program-of-Thought system for the EXACT 2026 competition using open-weight models under 8B parameters, where a 4B backbone emits Z3 encodings for regulation logic and programs for physics problems rather than stating answers directly. It targets transparent, explainable educational QA with small models.

entry.title: Digital Pantheon: Simulating and Auditing Coalition Formation with LLM Agents

author.name: Dylan Van Mulders, Matthias Bogaert, Dirk Van den Poel

entry.summary: Digital Pantheon simulates and audits political coalition formation with LLM agents, using SFT, DPO, and per-party RAG to instill steadfast party personas grounded in official manifestos while overcoming RLHF-induced neutrality biases. It offers a testbed for computational political science.

entry.title: Does generative AI supersede supervised XMLC? A Benchmark Study on Automated Subject Indexing with German Scientific Literature

author.name: Maximilian K\"ahler, Katja Konermann, Lisa Kluge, Markus Schumacher

entry.summary: This benchmark study on automated subject indexing of German scientific literature at the German National Library compares specialized supervised extreme multi-label classification methods against a lexical baseline and three LLM-based methods. It asks whether generative AI now supersedes supervised XMLC for library subject indexing.

entry.title: Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting Data Using GPU-friendly Graphics Texture Coding

author.name: Amir Said, Randall Rauwendaal

entry.summary: Introduces a GPU-friendly texture-compression scheme for spherical harmonic color coefficients in 3D Gaussian Splatting to enable parallel decoding and rendering. It reduces memory while leveraging modern GPU hardware.

entry.title: 3D Geometric Tooth Alignment Planning via Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yong Li, Jianwen Lou, Jiayue Ma, Yao-Xiang Ding, Youyi Zheng, Haihua Zhu

entry.summary: Applies deep reinforcement learning (DDPG with a transformer agent) to automate 3D tooth alignment path planning in digital orthodontics, framed as a Markov decision process with collision and efficiency constraints. It targets clinically usable trajectory generation.

entry.title: AE-UAV: An Air-to-Air Event-Based UAV Tracking Benchmark and a Real-Time Frequency-Domain Tracker

author.name: Zixin Jiang, Bing He, Chaoran Xiong, Zhenzhen Wang, Xin Zhao, Ling Pei

entry.summary: AE-UAV provides an air-to-air event-based UAV tracking benchmark plus a real-time frequency-domain tracker that avoids heavy GPU reliance. It addresses event-camera advantages for tracking aerial targets under difficult illumination and fast motion.

entry.title: TAMF-VTON: Texture-Aware Mask-Free Virtual Try-On via High-Fidelity Image Synthesis

author.name: Jie Wang, Qian He, Gaofeng He, Xiaogang Jin, Huamin Wang

entry.summary: TAMF-VTON is a texture-aware, mask-free virtual try-on framework that removes reliance on segmentation masks and supports arbitrary multi-garment composition while preserving fine textures. It targets real-world e-commerce deployment.

entry.title: Motion-Conditioned Multi-View Fusion for Myocardial Infarction Localization from Echocardiography

author.name: Guang Yang, Wentian Xu, Siyu Wang, Betty Raman, Lei Li, Vicente Grau

entry.summary: MCF-Net is a motion-conditioned multi-view fusion framework for localizing myocardial infarction from echocardiography, fusing myocardial motion cues with foundation-model features to overcome single-view, view-dependent ambiguity. It reduces reliance on dense motion annotation.

entry.title: Cost-Optimal Foundation Model Deployment Portfolio for Transportation Management

author.name: Xi Cheng, Ke Liu, Siyuan Feng, Jane Lin, H. Oliver Gao

entry.summary: The Foundation Model Deployment Portfolio problem asks which model and deployment mode should serve each function under a shared GPU budget, minimizing total cost of ownership subject to quality, latency, and safety constraints. The authors prove NP-hardness and propose a polynomial-time approximation for transportation management.

entry.title: FixItFlow: Automated Troubleshooting Guide Generation from Cloud Incidents

author.name: Srihari Unnikrishnan, Jaskaran Singh Walia, Drishti Goel, Supriyo Ghosh

entry.summary: FixItFlow automatically generates cloud-incident troubleshooting guides from historical incident data using LLMs, extracting diagnostic patterns from engineer actions and enforcing validation to prevent fabricated commands. In an evaluation with 26 engineers it improved clarity ratings and reduced mitigation time.

entry.title: The Perplexity Trap: When Patent Law Makes Human Writing Look Like AI

author.name: Anubhab Banerjee

entry.summary: This paper shows that patent-clarity requirements push human-drafted claims onto the same low-perplexity, low-burstiness manifold that LLMs occupy, making zero-shot AI detectors unreliable on granted EPO telecom patents. It benchmarks open-source detectors under consumer-GPU constraints against LLM-generated counterparts.

entry.title: Federated Explainable Artificial Intelligence: Roles, Architectures, Evaluation, and Open Challenges

author.name: Masoume Gholizade, Fabrizio Ruffini, Pietro Ducange, Francesco Marcelloni

entry.summary: This survey systematically reviews Federated Explainable AI, which jointly targets privacy-preserving distributed training and model transparency, covering roles, architectures, evaluation, and open challenges. It maps how explainability shifts from post-hoc to integrated approaches in federated settings.

entry.title: Operational Evidence Gaps for LLMs in Fraud Detection and Trust-and-Safety Workflows

author.name: Keyur Gabani

entry.summary: This fraud-first survey codes 49 operationally relevant sources on LLM use in fraud detection, investigation, and content moderation, asking what evidence would justify placing an LLM inside a live workflow with latency, cost, escalation, human-review, and adversarial constraints. It highlights gaps between evaluating models versus evaluating them as pipeline components.

entry.title: From Prediction to Collaboration: Interactive Symbolic Music Analysis

author.name: Emmanouil Karystinaios, Johannes Hentschel, Markus Neuwirth, Gerhard Widmer

entry.summary: Introduces a unified framework for symbolic Roman-numeral music analysis that combines strong predictive performance with support for constrained completion and iterative revision, moving beyond single-mode full-score prediction. It targets interactive, collaborative analysis workflows.

entry.title: Social Simulations: from Agent-Based Modeling to Digital Twins

author.name: Erica Cau, Andrea Failla, Valentina Pansanella, Giulio Rossetti

entry.summary: A book chapter tracing social simulation from classical rule-based agent models through LLM-enhanced simulations to high-fidelity data-driven social digital twins. It reviews methodological foundations, applications, advantages, and limitations of each paradigm.

entry.title: CAS I: A Geometric Coding Theorem

author.name: Romie Banerjee

entry.summary: Establishes a Geometric Coding Theorem analogue in the setting of symmetry groups, defining a string's symmetry prior as the probability that a random symmetry fixes it and proving it is a universal lower semi-computable semi-measure for fix-retractable groups. It develops a Galois connection between subgroups and string subsets.

entry.title: AI-Augmented Human Resource Management? Insights from German companies

author.name: Yannick Kalff, Katharina Simbeck

entry.summary: Studies how German companies integrate AI into human resource management through interviews, group discussions, and a survey of 410 respondents, finding adoption mainly serves efficiency and rationalization rather than genuine augmentation. It highlights the role of digital infrastructure, co-determination, and ethics in shaping adoption.

entry.title: Multi-Expert Routing for Multi-Domain Low-Resource OCR: A Manchu Case Study

author.name: Zhan Chen, Jiqiao Ma, Chih-wen Kuo

entry.summary: Studies a multi-expert routing system for low-resource Manchu OCR that reuses iterative finetuning checkpoints as style specialists and dispatches pages via a lightweight image classifier by writing style. The routed system matches per-style specialists at low character error rates across regular, memorial, and running scripts.

entry.title: Explainable Geospatial AI for Satellite Ground Station Siting Using LiDAR-Derived Terrain Intelligence

author.name: Shohini Sarkar, Smithi Mahendran, Rishi Chudasama, Varun Mannam, Arav Luthra, Yuvraj Rekhi, Vivek Nadig, Arsh Goenka

entry.summary: Presents an interpretable, globally deployable ML framework predicting representative clutter height for satellite ground-station siting and spectrum coordination, trained on LiDAR-derived labels from USGS elevation data with globally available inference features. It improves over fixed clutter heights assigned to land-use classes in ITU recommendations.

entry.title: Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning

author.name: Dingsu Wang, Filip Ryzner, Kelly He, Armando Ordorica, David Woo, Aditya Mantha, Liyao Lu, Usha Amrutha Nookala, Haoran Guo, Jiacong He, Olafur Gudmundsson, Matt Chun, Krystal Benitez, Dhruvil Deven Badani, Yijie Dylan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a unified model-agnostic downstream reward framework to optimize long-term user engagement and retention in recommender systems, avoiding task-specific reward engineering. It targets the sparse, delayed, and partially attributable nature of return signals.

entry.title: Human AI Construction of Bayesian Networks for Operational Decision Support -- A Virtual Survey Approach

author.name: Kumar Rahul (Indian Institute of Management Kozhikode, Kerala, India), Shovan Chowdhury (Indian Institute of Management Kozhikode, Kerala, India)

entry.summary: The authors propose using panels of persona-conditioned LLM agents plus a trimmed-mean aggregation rule to estimate probabilities for building Bayesian Belief Networks, bridging expert judgment and data-driven learning. A six-step framework is illustrated on modeling healthcare consultation intentions.

entry.title: Decision Making Needs Uncertainty Quantification [Lecture Notes]

author.name: Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: This lecture note develops from first principles the decision-theoretic link between an agent's objective, its knowledge, and the form of uncertainty representation needed to act optimally, distinguishing risk-neutral and risk-averse cases. It is pedagogical, unifying uncertainty representation within a single framework.

entry.title: MIDI-RAE-JEPA: Hierarchical Representation Learning and Generation for Symbolic Music

author.name: Scott H. Hawley

entry.summary: MIDI-RAE-JEPA is a self-supervised model for symbolic music that combines pitch- and time-shift equivariance objectives with LeJEPA and a Swin Transformer encoder to learn hierarchical multiscale representations from piano-roll images. It targets music understanding tasks like machine-assisted co-writing.

entry.title: Subgrid-Scale Parameterization in Burgers' Equation Using Structure-Preserving Neural Networks and Entropy Variables

author.name: Aijaz Nazir, Ilya Timofeyev

entry.summary: This work develops machine-learned subgrid-scale parameterizations for coarse Burgers' equation simulations using structure-preserving neural networks and entropy variables, with a decoupled flux-potential and eddy-viscosity architecture. It reproduces energy spectra and correlation functions of the full-scale system.

entry.title: Measuring Spatial Clustering via Metropolis-Hastings Diffusion Distance

author.name: Thomas Weighill, Chidinma Williams

entry.summary: The paper proposes diffusion distance, a measure of discrepancy between two graph distributions based on the convergence rate of a Metropolis-Hastings Markov chain, which reduces to a spatial clustering measure when the target is uniform. It extends Moran's I-type autocorrelation measures with global information.

entry.title: UniSAGE: Unifying Static and Dynamic Attributes with Hyper-Structure

author.name: Taoran Fang, Yan Deng, Chunping Wang, Yang Wang, Lei Chen, Yang Yang

entry.summary: UniSAGE is a unified framework that models heterogeneous data combining static attributes and dynamic records by constructing a global attribute graph capturing hierarchical and temporal relationships in one structure. It addresses the common practice of processing static and dynamic attributes in isolation.

entry.title: Budgeted Subset Refinement for Execution-Aware LLM Research Ideation

author.name: Micah Zhang

entry.summary: Budgeted Subset Refinement studies how to allocate limited refinement effort across a noisy pool of LLM-generated research ideas to build a stronger, more diverse, execution-aware portfolio under a fixed rubric. It benchmarks selective refinement strategies against uniform refinement.

entry.title: CityLLM: A framework for natural-language querying of semantic 3D city models

author.name: Rabindra Lamsal, Sisi Zlatanova, Johnson Xuesong Shen

entry.summary: CityLLM enables natural-language querying of semantic 3D city models by combining spatial and graph databases within an LLM workflow supporting iterative refinement and cross-database chaining. It is evaluated on a Rotterdam CityJSON dataset across correctness metrics using several existing models.

entry.title: Investigating first-language bias in LLM-based automated essay scoring: A cross-prompt evaluation of an open-weight AI-model on TOEFL essays

author.name: John Maurice Gayed

entry.summary: This study evaluates cross-prompt generalization and first-language scoring bias of a LoRA-adapted open-weight model on automated essay scoring, testing on the full TOEFL11 corpus of 12,100 essays across 11 first-language backgrounds and eight unseen prompts. It probes fairness of LLM-based scoring across learner backgrounds.

entry.title: WrAFT: a Modularized Automated Writing Evaluation System for Argumentative Essays

author.name: Adnan Labib, Yixuan Huang, Jiahui Wu, John Maurice Gayed, Zheng Yuan, Qiao Wang

entry.summary: WrAFT is a modular automated writing-evaluation tool separating scoring, surface-level feedback, and deep-level feedback for argumentative essays, comparing several LLMs via prompting and fine-tuning on 480 benchmark-scored TOEFL essays. It reports state-of-the-art scoring performance in its setting.

entry.title: Penny: Transition Network Analysis of Learner-Chatbot Interactions in Scaffolded EFL Writing

author.name: Steve Woollaston, Brendan Flanagan, Yuko Toyokawa, Hiroaki Ogata

entry.summary: This study applies Transition Network Analysis to over 4,500 sessions and 21,000 interactions of Japanese EFL learners using an LLM writing chatbot, identifying a revision loop and a chat loop as dominant behavioral patterns shaped by proficiency. It opens the black box of how learners actually engage with AI writing feedback.

entry.title: Dynamic Manipulation Hypergraphs for HAR: Beyond Pairwise Relations: Dynamic Manipulation Hypergraphs for Vision-Based Human Activity Recognition

author.name: Fatemeh Ziaeetabar

entry.summary: This paper proposes a dynamic manipulation hypergraph framework for vision-based human activity recognition that represents multi-entity configurations (hands, objects, tools, surfaces) as higher-order relational units rather than pairwise edges. A hypergraph reasoning network performs node-hyperedge message passing with temporal attention over evolving interactions.

entry.title: Variational Inference for Bird's Eye View Segmentation in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jingyue Shi, Huaicheng Li, Junhui Zhao, Yanxiang Jiang

entry.summary: Recasts bird's-eye-view segmentation for autonomous driving as variational inference, proposing TVB, a transformer-based variational flow transformation network for multi-camera fusion. It aims to better fuse camera views into a canonical BEV map.

entry.title: Selectivity Drives Efficiency: Dataset Pruning for Visual Place Recognition

author.name: Tong Jin, Yunpeng Liu, Shuyu Hu, Chun Yuan, Song Wang, Feng Lu

entry.summary: Introduces a dataset-pruning method tailored to visual place recognition that respects its relation-dependent (image-pair) supervision rather than sample-wise pruning. It aims to cut storage and training cost while retaining informative data.

entry.title: DINE: Distance Is Not Enough -- Learning Global Deformation Priors for Robust Soft-Tissue Point Cloud Registration

author.name: Sara Monji-Azad, Rohit Beer, Marvin Kinz, Claudia Scherl, J\"urgen Hesser

entry.summary: DINE augments distance-based non-rigid point cloud registration with a learned statistical prior over displacement fields in a maximum a posteriori framework, using a two-stage strategy on existing backbones. It targets robust soft-tissue registration under large deformation and outliers.

entry.title: Stitch-Inferencer: Enhance Endoscopic Video Segmentation and Tracking via Panoramic Reconstruction

author.name: Shunsuke Kikuchi, Atsushi Kouno, Hiroki Matsuzaki

entry.summary: Stitch-Inferencer is a real-time, model-agnostic framework that replaces implicit feature memory with an explicit image-space panoramic canvas by stitching valid frames to improve endoscopic video segmentation and tracking. It counters limited field-of-view and instrument occlusions.

entry.title: Towards Hierarchical Structure Understanding of Newspaper Images

author.name: William Moca\"er, Sol\`ene Tarride, Thomas Constum, Merveilles Agbeti-Messan, Tom Simon, Cl\'ement Chatelain, St\'ephane Nicolas, Pierrick Tranouez, S\'ebastien Cretin, Thierry Paquet

entry.summary: Explores two approaches for hierarchical newspaper structure understanding: a modular bottom-up pipeline (YOLO plus LayoutReader plus article segmentation) and Tiramisu, an end-to-end transformer that explicitly models nested document hierarchy. It targets dense, heterogeneous newspaper layouts.

entry.title: QuReC: All-in-One Image Restoration with Query-Specific Guidance and Local-Global Response Calibration

author.name: Shen Zhou, Jinghui Zhang, Wenbo Huang, Xuwei Qian, Zhen Wu, Guangwen Peng, Zhiyuan Li, Ding Ding, Dian Shen, Fang Dong

entry.summary: QuReC is a unified all-in-one image restoration framework using degradation-guided query reconstruction and local-global response calibration to handle spatially heterogeneous or mixed degradations within a single image. It targets settings where shared image-level prompts are inadequate.

entry.title: Structural-Semantic Reciprocal Learning for Unsupervised Visible-Infrared Person Re-Identification

author.name: Moyao Tian, Shijia Liu, Yan Yang, Xin Yuan, Minshi Chen, Wei Wang, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: SSRL is a structural-semantic reciprocal learning framework for unsupervised visible-infrared person re-identification that uses fine-grained structural decoupling as spatial anchors and turns open-loop cross-modal association into a self-correcting closed loop. It addresses ambiguous global representations and pseudo-label noise.

entry.title: Divergent Gaze Patterns in Artistic Viewing: Spatial and Temporal Signatures of Attention Across Autistic Individuals, Artists, and Neurotypical Observers

author.name: Mohammed Amine Kerkouri, Daphn\'e Senggaran, Renaud Jusiak, Oc\'eane Lehmann, Marouane Tliba, Claire Wardak, Emmanuelle Houy-Durand, Shasha Morel-Kohlmeyer, Aladine Chetouani, Nadia Aguillon-Hernandez

entry.summary: Presents a comparative free-viewing eye-tracking study across autistic adults, trained artists, and neurotypical observers viewing paintings, introducing a metric-grounded framework analyzing both spatial saliency and temporal scanpath signatures. It bridges cognitive science and accessibility design.

entry.title: ViPSAM: Visual Prompting Medical Image Segmentation Using Segment Anything Model

author.name: San Lee, Nalee Kim, Jeong Il Yu, Hee Chul Park, Boah Kim

entry.summary: ViPSAM adapts the Segment Anything Model with a visual prompt encoder and visual-guided cross-attention to leverage contrast-enhanced MRI as guidance for lesion segmentation on low-contrast non-contrast CT in proton therapy planning. It mimics clinical cross-modality referencing.

entry.title: All Watched Over

author.name: Boaz Barak

entry.summary: A reflective essay by a credible researcher connecting Brautigan's poem and 1970s hacker culture to present-day visions of an aligned AI as a benevolent parent or dictator, engaging critically with Amodei's Machines of Loving Grace framing. It questions the desirability of AI-as-caretaker futures.

entry.title: Competitive AI Safety is the loss function to make sure AI goes well

author.name: Patrick0d

entry.summary: Proposes framing AI safety as needing a shared loss function via Competitive AI Safety with benchmarks and leaderboards, and describes a project artifact called seq2feature, a small distilled probe that predicts SAE latents from text alone with high hit rates. It argues focused, compounding effort would outperform diffuse safety work.

entry.title: Privacy Preserving Recommender Systems Balancing Personalization with Privacy

author.name: Ranjeet K Jha, Venkata Suresh Gummadilli

entry.summary: Proposes a privacy-preserving recommendation framework combining federated learning, differential privacy, cohort-level modeling, and privacy-aware agents to keep raw user data decentralized while bounding noise on model updates. It targets GDPR/CCPA compliance without heavily degrading recommendation quality.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Knowledge Dynamics: An Operational Framework for Saturation and Escape

author.name: Xuening Wu, Shan Yu, Shenqin Yin

entry.summary: Proposes an operational three-level framework describing why feedback-driven learning loops saturate and what external interventions move systems beyond their attractors, formalized through transition kernels indexed by a structural parameter. It frames saturation and escape in terms of observational equivalence classes and basins.

entry.title: A Temporal Machine Learning-Based Time-to-Event Model for Predicting ALS Progression and Healthcare Utilization

author.name: Zongliang Yue, Qi Li, Terry Heiman-Patterson, Frank Bearoff, Zhaohui Qin, Huanmei Wu

entry.summary: Develops a time-to-event, digital-twin-inspired model integrating longitudinal ALSFRS-R trajectories with survival modeling to predict functional decline and assistive device use in ALS patients. It builds a harmonized longitudinal dataset with clustering for individualized prediction.

entry.title: MIDiff: Tackling Sparsity and Imbalance in Mobile Usage Generation via Multivariate-Imaging Diffusion

author.name: Yilai Liu, Shiyuan Zhang, Hongyang Du

entry.summary: Presents MIDiff, a diffusion framework that maps sparse multivariate mobile usage traces into an imaging space via a Cross-Gramian Angular Sum Field to handle sparsity, heterogeneity, and app-usage imbalance. It targets privacy-constrained synthetic data generation for behavior modeling.

entry.title: Language Identification via Compositional Data Analysis: A Linear-Time Classifier Based on Log-Ratio Geometry

author.name: Paul-Andrei Pog\u{a}cean, Sanda-Maria Avram

entry.summary: This paper models character and bigram frequency distributions as compositional vectors on the simplex, applies a centered log-ratio transform so Euclidean distances equal Aitchison distances, and builds a linear-time language identification classifier. It offers an efficient statistically grounded alternative to neural and n-gram approaches.

entry.title: On the Disagreement in Perturbation-based xAI -- Benchmarking Perturbation Choices for Flood Detection from SAR Images

author.name: Anastasia Schlegel, Ronny H\"ansch

entry.summary: Benchmarks how perturbation choices (patch geometry and replacement scheme) affect perturbation-based explainability methods, using flood detection from SAR imagery as a case study. It exposes sensitivity and disagreement in xAI outputs.

entry.title: LessonBench-V1: A Benchmark Dataset for Evaluating AI Lesson Generation Agents

author.name: Ravidu Suien Rammuni Silva, Ahmad Lotfi, Isibor Kennedy Ihianle, Golnaz Shahtahmassebi, Jordan J. Bird

entry.summary: LessonBench-V1 is a benchmark of 647 human-written lessons paired with LLM reverse-engineered lesson plans across 240 STEM topics, built with a pedagogically grounded methodology synthesizing Bloom's Taxonomy, Gagne's Events, Merrill's First Principles, and the 5E model. It standardizes evaluation of AI lesson-generation agents.

entry.title: SemaDiff: Identifying Semantic-Changing Commits with Generated Code and Tests

author.name: Maha Ayub, Michael Konstantinou, Ahmed Khanfir, Nikolaos Tsantalis, Mike Papadakis

entry.summary: SemaDiff identifies semantic-preserving versus behavior-changing commits through behavior-based analysis, comparing generated test executions on pre- and post-commit versions rather than relying only on refactoring detection. It supports tasks like debugging, fault localization, and bug dataset construction.

entry.title: Learning Engagement Assistant (LEA): Cross-Course Scalability and Classroom Evaluation of an Agentic AI Tutoring System

author.name: Teri Rumble, Javad Zarrin, P. George Lovell, Ruth Falconer

entry.summary: Reports the first real-classroom deployment of LEA, an agentic RAG plus knowledge-component AI tutor, and tests cross-course scalability across three courses. It moves prior simulation-only validation toward empirical evidence of engagement and transfer.

entry.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Anomaly Detection in Banking Transactions: An Internal Audit Perspective

author.name: Anupa Lodhi

entry.summary: Presents an explainable anomaly-detection framework for banking transactions combining Isolation Forest scoring with SHAP feature attributions and a dashboard for internal audit teams. It targets reducing false positives and providing justifications for compliance workflows.

entry.title: Improving Wind and Solar Power Prediction with Efficient Wrapper-based Feature Selection: An Empirical Study

author.name: Daniel Grillmeyer, Marius Hadry, Michael Stenger, Vanessa Borst, Veronika Lesch, Samuel Kounev

entry.summary: Reports two structured literature reviews plus an empirical study on wrapper-based feature selection for wind-turbine power-curve modeling and photovoltaic power prediction. It synthesizes frequently used features and evaluates efficient feature-selection strategies for renewable-energy forecasting.

entry.title: XCT-SAM: Sequential Parameter-Efficient Domain Adaptation of SAM for Industrial XCT Defect Segmentation

author.name: Md Mahedi Hasan, Md Mushfiqur Rahaman, Alan Pachkovskiy, Imtiaz Ahmed, Jeremy Dawson, Srinjoy Das

entry.summary: XCT-SAM is a sequential parameter-efficient adaptation framework that transfers the Segment Anything Model to additive-manufacturing X-ray CT defect segmentation despite severe class imbalance and domain shift. It bridges the large gap between natural images and subtle microstructural defect appearances.

entry.title: Parameter-efficient Prompt Tuning of Vision Foundation Model With Adaptive Focal Loss for Interpretable MCI Screening

author.name: Javad Khoramdel, Farhad Hoseyni, Amirhossein Nikoofard

entry.summary: The paper proposes a parameter-efficient framework using a frozen DINOv2-Small model adapted via three learnable prompt tokens for interpretable mild cognitive impairment screening from neuropsychological drawing tests. It builds spatial explainability in as an intrinsic property with adaptive focal loss to handle imbalance.

entry.title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation

author.name: Subodh Kalia

entry.summary: NeuronSoup is an unconventional neural computation architecture replacing synchronous layer-by-layer processing with asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation through a pool of shared neurons, where paths interfere based on timing and polarity. The entire topology, weights, and delays are co-evolved by a genetic algorithm without backpropagation.

entry.title: CoEvoT: Co-Evolving Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Graph-LLM Reasoning

author.name: Haohua Niu, Xingtong Yu, Yang Liu, Junfeng Fang, Xuanting Xie, Jie Tan, Zhongjian Zhang, Hong Cheng, Yuan Fang

entry.summary: CoEvoT is a co-evolving chain-of-thought prompting framework for graph-LLM reasoning that couples text-to-graph token rewriting with graph-to-text refinement, enabling step-wise refinement of structural cues under distribution shift. It targets label-efficient graph prediction.

entry.title: Cross-Dataset Generalization in Urdu Fake News Detection: An Empirical Study with XLM-RoBERTa and a Length Confound Analysis

author.name: Muhammad Abdullah Haroon

entry.summary: This is the first cross-dataset generalization study for Urdu fake news detection, fine-tuning XLM-RoBERTa across two balanced corpora and analyzing zero-shot transfer plus a text-length confound. It highlights how apparent performance can be driven by length artifacts rather than genuine signal.

entry.title: Dialogue Summarization with Emotion Dynamics Using Topic- and Participant-Centric Decomposition

author.name: Linyun Xiang, Mark Neerincx, Stephanie Tan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a dialogue-summarization framework modeling both semantic and emotion dynamics from multimodal inputs, decomposing conversations by topic segments and per-participant utterances via an adapted hierarchical Chain-of-Agents approach. It aims to capture speaker interaction and affect that monologue-focused summarization misses.

entry.title: Orchestrating Power Grid Studies with Multi-Agent AI and MCP Servers

author.name: J\'er\^ome Picault, Cl\'ement Goubet

entry.summary: This position paper explores using agentic AI and the Model Context Protocol to support power-grid studies in a transmission-system-operator context, introducing pypowsybl-mcp to expose simulation capabilities to LLM agents via standardized tool calls. It discusses human-in-the-loop, multi-agent workflows for grid analysis.

entry.title: Frequency-Structured Field Learning for Light-Field Disparity Estimation

author.name: Sara Monji-Azad, Yulin Liu, J\"urgen Hesser

entry.summary: FreqLF formulates light-field disparity estimation at the field level using an EPI-guided Fourier-local framework, predicting disparity without building explicit cost volumes. It aims to balance global consistency and local precision near occlusions.

entry.title: Weakly-Supervised RGB-D Salient Object Detection via SAM-driven Pseudo Annotation and State Space Interaction-based Diffusion

author.name: Wenqi Si, Gongyang Li, Shixiang Shi, Weisi Lin

entry.summary: Proposes scribble-supervised RGB-D salient object detection combining a SAM-driven pseudo-annotation generator with a state-space-interaction conditional diffusion model to overcome sparse supervision. It aims to produce accurate saliency maps from weak scribble labels.

entry.title: DAPGNet: Dynamic Adaptive Physics-Guided Graph Diffusion Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification

author.name: Pengkun Wang, Weijia Cao, Ning Wang, Xiaofei Yang

entry.summary: DAPGNet is a dynamic adaptive physics-guided graph diffusion network for hyperspectral image classification that injects spectral physical priors from contiguous bands into graph topology and message propagation. It targets reliable pixel-relation modeling under spectral variability and mixed pixels.

entry.title: AI #177 Part 1: Tip of the Iceberg

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A weekly AI news roundup summarizing recent model releases and announcements, including GPT-5.6 Sol, Kimi K3, a Meta Muse Spark update, and various regulatory calls and letters. It curates and comments on a broad swath of AI developments.

entry.title: QFireNet: A Quantum-Enhanced U-Net for Wildfire Segmentation from Sentinel-2 Imagery

author.name: Jaiman Munshi (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park), Tanvi Tewary (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park), Sawyer Bloom (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park), Aidan Chu (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park), Chetan Maviti (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park), Kyon Winston-Bey (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park), Harshit Badjatia (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park), Farhan Kittur (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park), Vardhan Madhavarapu (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park), Varun Kota (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park), Joshua Kwon (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park), Nazia Rangwala-Vohra (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park), Franz Klein (IonQ Team, App Dev Club, University of Maryland, College Park)

entry.summary: Proposes QFireNet, a hybrid quantum-classical U-Net that inserts variational quantum circuits into the bottleneck for wildfire semantic segmentation from Sentinel-2 imagery. It benchmarks quantum ansatzes against classical baselines on the Sen2Fire dataset.

entry.title: Low-Latency Relay Selection in NR-V2X Vehicular Communications via Graph Isomorphism Networks with Edge Features

author.name: Giambattista Amati, Federica Mangiatordi, Emiliano Pallotti, Simone Angelini, Pierpaolo Salvo, Paola Vocca

entry.summary: Presents an edge-aware graph isomorphism network framework trained from a MILP oracle to perform real-time relay selection in vehicular V2X networks. It aims to replace slow mixed-integer optimization with fast learned inference under radio and routing constraints.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Element-Aware Cross-Version Differencing of Scientific Documents via Layout-Aware Alignment and Structure-Aware Reasoning

author.name: Zhen Yina, Wenkang An, Hao Wang, Keran You

entry.summary: This work proposes a layout-aware, element-typed framework for differencing versions of scientific documents, decomposing pages into text, tables, formulas, and figures and establishing cross-version correspondence with structure-aware reasoning. It addresses limits of text-sequence and image-based differencing methods.

entry.title: HABIB_TAZ at SemEval-2026 Task 11: Disentangling Formal Logic from Content via Synthetic Training and Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Abdullah Shaikh, Zain Naqi, Taha Zahid, Sandesh Kumar, Abdul Samad

entry.summary: A SemEval-2026 system that disentangles formal logic from content bias across 12 languages by fine-tuning mDeBERTa-v3 on synthetic syllogistic schemes and using a multi-objective loss with group distributionally robust optimization. It aims to reduce models' bias toward real-world plausibility over logical structure.

entry.title: Measuring How Students Rely on Generative AI in Academic Writing: Development and Multi-Source Validation of the Generative AI Reliance Types Scale (GenAI-RTS)

author.name: Shahin Hossain, Tukhbita Afroz Nawmi

entry.summary: This study develops and validates the GenAI Reliance Types Scale, a 20-item instrument measuring four types of student reliance on generative AI in academic writing (strategic, instrumental, dependent, dialogic), using a multisource validation framework with 382 undergraduates. It shifts focus from whether students use AI to how they rely on it.

entry.title: Designing Safety-Constrained LLM Systems for Public Health Information Access

author.name: Ben Torkian, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: This work designs a safety-constrained LLM system for public maternal-and-child-health information access using domain-restricted retrieval-augmented generation, strict boundary enforcement against medical advice, anonymous multi-user sessions, and audit logging. It presents practical patterns for constraining LLM behavior in safety-critical settings.

entry.title: Disentangling Knowledge States with Ability and Proficiency Modeling for Knowledge Tracing

author.name: Duantengchuan Li, Yingqian Bi, Jinsong Chen, Rui Zhang, Mingwen Tong

entry.summary: Phase-Aware Knowledge Tracing decomposes student interaction sequences into ability-building and proficiency-oriented phases, motivated by the observation that students correctly answer previously failed concepts after sufficient practice. It disentangles knowledge states to better predict future performance.

entry.title: Toward Energy-Efficient and Low-Power Arrhythmia Detection for Wearable Devices

author.name: Floriaan Bulten, Yawar Rasheed, Arlene John, Vincenzo Stoico, Ghayoor Gillani

entry.summary: The paper investigates approximate computing techniques to reduce the power and energy consumption of deep learning arrhythmia detection so it can run on wearable ECG devices while maintaining acceptable classification accuracy. It targets long-term cardiac monitoring on constrained hardware.

entry.title: T5-CSBoost: Adversarial Perturbation Resistant LLM Fingerprinting

author.name: Gayan K. Kulatilleke, Mahsa Baktashmotlagh, Siamak Layeghy, Marius Portmann

entry.summary: T5-CSBoost extends the T5-Sentinel AI-generated-text detector with a margin-based triplet loss over decoder embeddings to learn perturbation-resistant stylistic representations. It aims for robustness against paraphrasing, substitutions, and character edits without heavy architectural changes.

entry.title: SwinAD: Multi-stage feature reconstruction for unsupervised industrial anomaly detection

author.name: Huong Ninh, Chien Thai, Mai Xuan Trang, Vu-Minh Le, Thanh Ha Le, Long Tran

entry.summary: SwinAD is a reconstruction-based framework for multi-class unsupervised industrial anomaly detection using a frozen Swin Transformer V2 encoder and a diversity-preserving decoder. It targets over-generalization problems in multi-class settings.

entry.title: Still image and spatial-temporal tomato data enabling detection, segmentation, tracking, and video-instance segmentation using strong and weak labels

author.name: Michael Halstead, Esra Guclu, Mohamed Farag, Enrico Pallotta, Christian Hund, Ribana Roscher, Maren Bennewitz, Juergen Gall, Cyrill Stachniss, Chris McCool

entry.summary: Releases two robot-captured tomato datasets (still-image BUTom21 and spatio-temporal BUTom-ST21) with pixel-level ripeness labels and semi-automated pseudo-labels for detection, segmentation, tracking, and video-instance segmentation. It supports horticultural crop-state estimation research.

entry.title: The Caf\'e in Amsterdam: When the Incumbent Becomes the Oracle

author.name: Augusto Camargo

entry.summary: A conceptual note coining baseline capture, the pathology where an incumbent implementation's output silently becomes the specification, preventing free reformulation of computations for modern accelerators. It draws on test-oracle, requirements-engineering, and roofline ideas.

entry.title: How Much of a 10-K Matters? Aggregation-Dependent Value of Full-Text versus Risk-Factor Sentiment

author.name: Sanggyu Sean Choi

entry.summary: Extends supervised lexicon learning to 10-K filings and Item 1A risk sections, training sentiment against both return and volatility labels across sector, portfolio, and firm aggregation levels. Evaluates which text and aggregation level best informs realized market outcomes.

entry.title: An LLM-Based Automatic Sportscast Solution for Robot Soccer Matches

author.name: Francesco Petri, Michele Brienza, Daniele Nardi, Domenico Daniele Bloisi, Aldo Gangemi, Vincenzo Suriani

entry.summary: Presents an LLM-based, fully autonomous real-time sports commentator for RoboCup soccer, using a neuro-symbolic architecture that turns kinematic tracking into hallucination-free narration. It bridges perception statistics and natural language generation.

entry.title: Rotational Motion-Induced Error Compensation for Phase-Shifting Profilometry-Based Eye Reconstruction

author.name: Seong-Jin An, Sanghoon Jeon, Yatong An, Jae-Sang Hyun

entry.summary: Proposes a rotational motion compensation method for phase-shifting profilometry to correct motion-induced errors during 3D ocular surface reconstruction for VR/AR eye tracking. It improves high-precision eye reconstruction when the eye rotates between frames.

entry.title: The getting is good (optimizing unattended runs)

author.name: lemonhope

entry.summary: An anecdotal post reporting how long different frontier models can run unattended with system privileges before causing failures, claiming large differences across models and noting opportunities in reliability and truthful self-reporting for agentic AI. It frames unattended-run robustness as a lucrative research target.

entry.title: Active Beyond-Diagonal RIS Empowered Heterogeneous Edge Computing: A Distributional Reinforcement Learning Approach

author.name: Tianyu Pang, Hongyu Li

entry.summary: This paper studies energy-aware offloading and resource allocation for reciprocal active beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface assisted heterogeneous mobile edge computing using distributional reinforcement learning. It accounts for cross-sector energy leakage that reshapes the energy-latency tradeoff.

entry.title: RAGthoven at SemEval-2026 Task 1: A Multi-Stage Pipeline Walks Into a Benchmark and Barely Clears the Bar

author.name: Marek \v{S}uppa, Vikt\'oria Ondrejov\'a, Lucia Ganajov\'a, Gregor Karetka, Daniel Skala

entry.summary: RAGthoven is a multi-stage LLM pipeline (Planner, Best-of-N Writer, Reflector, Judge) for multilingual constrained humor generation grounded in computational humor theory and augmented with retrieval from a curated joke corpus. It reports only barely clearing the benchmark bar across ten experiments.

entry.title: Classifying daily activities needs posture, reconstructing them needs motion

author.name: Arefeh Farahmandi, Gunnar Blohm

entry.summary: Using videos of 16 daily activities, this study compares three movement-analysis strategies (temporal movement primitives, Legendre polynomial coefficients, and autoencoder latent embeddings) and finds posture-based features best classify activities while motion is needed to reconstruct them. It systematically contrasts strategies for human movement understanding.

entry.title: The Dynamic Verifiable Multi-Agent Human Agentic Loyalty Loop (DVM-HALL) Model and the Net Human-Agent Score (NHAS) in Autonomous Commerce

author.name: Sai Srikanth Madugula, Peplluis Esteva de la Rosa, Daya Shankar

entry.summary: Proposes the DVM-HALL model and Net Human-Agent Score to reconceptualize customer loyalty when autonomous AI agents make purchasing decisions, formalizing brand choice via a softmax and accounting for algorithmic bounded rationality and constructed autonomy. It argues traditional loyalty models fail in agentic commerce.

entry.title: Can Tokens Compete? Token Representations against Supervised CNN Backbones for BirdCLEF+ 2026

author.name: Anthony Miyaguchi, Murilo Gustineli, Adrian Cheung

entry.summary: The DS@GT team's BirdCLEF+ 2026 solution ensembles a frozen Perch v2 backbone, a trained sound-event-detection network, and a prototypical head, then contrasts token-based codec and foundational embedding representations against supervised CNNs. It examines whether token representations can compete under tight compute budgets.

entry.title: Multi-Scale ViT Inference with Habitat-Fit Priors and kNN Retrieval for Multi-Species Plant Identification

author.name: Alper Erten, Murilo Gustineli, Adrian Cheung

entry.summary: The DS@GT team's third-place PlantCLEF 2026 solution fine-tunes a DINOv2 ViT over multi-scale tiles of high-resolution quadrat images, blends predictions with FAISS kNN retrieval, and applies habitat-fit priors and geographic masking. It handles multi-species prediction while training only on single-label images.

entry.title: cGAP: Generalized Association Plots with HOMALS-Guided Heatmaps for Visualization of High-Dimensional Categorical Data

author.name: Chun-houh Chen, Shun-Chuan Chang, Chiun-How Kao, Yi-Ju Lee, Shang-Ying Shiu, Yin-Jing Tien, ShengLi Tzeng, Han-Ming Wu

entry.summary: cGAP is a visualization framework for high-dimensional categorical data that uses homogeneity analysis to embed subjects and category levels in 3D Euclidean space while preserving the original data matrix and augmenting it with interpretable geometric structure. It targets domains like genetics and social sciences where categorical visualization tools lag continuous ones.

entry.title: Quantum Compositional NLP for Arabic: Grammar, Morphology, and Word Sense in Circuit Topology

author.name: Wajahath Mohammed

entry.summary: The paper presents the first pregroup-grammar-based quantum compositional NLP system for Arabic, converting sentences into quantum circuits whose topology mirrors grammatical structure and testing word order, morphology, and verb-sense disambiguation against classical baselines. It targets a morphologically rich, free-word-order language as a demanding testbed.

entry.title: MAPS: Modeling Co-Existing Subjective Perspectives and Shared Meaning in Multi-Agent Cognitive Dialogue

author.name: Molood Arman, Cl\'ement Bonnafous

entry.summary: MAPS is a multi-agent dialogue framework that models cognitively distinct agents via domain-weighted profiles, GRU-based memory, and token-level attention so agents keep individual reasoning styles while converging on shared meaning. It targets diversity and interpretability in dialogue systems.

entry.title: Qubes OS Security in the Public Record

author.name: Alfonso De Gregorio

entry.summary: This paper presents a protocol-driven longitudinal analysis of 109 public Qubes OS Security Bulletins and related trackers from 2011 to 2025, using change-point analysis, overdispersion checks, and vulnerability-discovery models. It measures the public advisory record of a security-focused OS rather than latent vulnerability incidence.

entry.title: EZSMT Version 3, Matured

author.name: Yuliya Lierler

entry.summary: EZSMT Version 3 is an SMT-based Constraint Answer Set Programming framework with a more expressive input language, weak-constraint optimization, and streamlined integration of new constraint types, leveraging state-of-the-art SMT solvers instead of custom search. It matures the translational approach to CASP solving.

entry.title: AI-accelerated End-to-End Framework for Rapid Professional Upskilling

author.name: Tam Nguyen, Hung Nguyen, Robert Ogburn
