It progresses from classical pipelines toward end-to-end dexterous industrial manipulation.

entry.title: The State of AI Consciousness Research

author.name: Noa Weiss

entry.summary: A survey collecting the emerging empirical research on AI consciousness, arguing the question can be investigated with psychology, cognitive science, and interpretability methods without first solving the hard problem of consciousness. It notes dedicated efforts at Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and specialized organizations.

entry.title: AI-Native Insurance for Agentic AI: Pricing, Underwriting, and End-to-End Automation

author.name: Quanyan Zhu

entry.summary: Develops a mathematical framework for underwriting, pricing, and contract design for agentic AI deployments, representing a deployment as a risk state over autonomy, authority, permissions, governance, and dependency. It maps risk states to premiums, deductibles, and policy covenants via an optimization problem.

entry.title: Gauge-Invariant, Parameter-Insensitive Regularization for Potential Recovery from Flow on Directed Graphs

author.name: Mohammad Forouhesh

entry.summary: This work addresses ill-posed recovery of a latent potential from flow on directed graphs, showing that standard ridge regularization corrupts the recovered ordering while a gauge-invariant graph Dirichlet energy delivers parameter-insensitive, stable estimates. It also localizes absorbing boundaries from flow via a Poisson residual.

entry.title: PlumeQuant: Uncertainty-aware consistency assessment of methane plume masks and emission-rate estimates

author.name: Parisa Masnadi Khiabani, Wolfgang Jentner, Alireza Rangrazjeddi, Michael C. Wimberly, Binbin Weng, David Ebert, Charles Nicholson

entry.summary: PlumeQuant quantifies uncertainty in methane plume masks and emission-rate estimates, showing via genetic-algorithm ensembles that published scalar quantities do not uniquely constrain plume boundaries. It exposes equifinality in remote-sensing methane products relevant to emissions monitoring.

entry.title: TCAM-Diff: Triplane-Aware Cross-Attention Medical Diffusion Model

author.name: Zhenkai Zhang, Krista A. Ehinger, Tom Drummond

entry.summary: TCAM-Diff is a 3D medical image generation model using a decoder-only autoencoder to learn triplane representations and a triplane-aware cross-attention diffusion model, cutting memory for high-resolution volumes. It scales to volumes up to 512-cubed.

entry.title: Improving Molecular Property Prediction in Small Language Models Using Graph-based Tools

author.name: Konstantinos Bougiatiotis, Dimitrios Kelesis, Georgios Paliouras

entry.summary: Proposes a context-augmented prompting framework where small language models call a trained GNN expert for a predictive hint and an explanatory subgraph to improve zero-shot molecular property prediction from SMILES. Enriched prompts improve accuracy on MUTAG and Tox21.

entry.title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable,Navigable, and Editable

author.name: Ruhan Wang, Yucheng Shi, Zongxia Li, Zhongzhi Li, Yue Yu, Junyao Yang, Kishan Panaganti, Haitao Mi, Dongruo Zhou, Leoweiliang

entry.summary: Addresses the problem of mapping behavioral modification requests to the specific code locations that implement them in large, tightly coupled agent harnesses. It aims to make evolving harnesses more readable, navigable, and editable for developers or coding agents.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Collaborative Reasoning with Tool-Augmented Evidence for Urban Region Profiling

author.name: Xixuan Hao, Yutian Jiang, Jiabo Liu, Yihang Yang, Guangyin Jin, Song Gao, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: Introduces UrbanAgent, which reframes urban region profiling as reasoning-driven inference with tool-augmented evidence rather than static multimodal representation learning. It aims to improve robustness in heterogeneous or unseen regions.

entry.title: Explaining Reinforcement Learning Agents via Inductive Logic Programming

author.name: Celeste Veronese, Edoardo Zorzi, Daniele Meli, Alessandro Farinelli

entry.summary: Aims to make reinforcement learning policies interpretable by extracting logic-based explanations via inductive logic programming, and introduces objective, planning-oriented metrics to quantify explainability. It targets safety-critical and human-centric RL settings.

entry.title: CAVA: Canonical Action Verification and Attestation for Runtime Governance of Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Zexun Wang

entry.summary: Introduces CAVA, a runtime-semantics layer that converts heterogeneous agent activity across many runtimes into canonical action objects so approvals can be bound to executions and independently verified. It targets the governance question of what action was actually approved and executed.

entry.title: FixItFlow: Automated Troubleshooting Guide Generation from Cloud Incidents

author.name: Srihari Unnikrishnan, Jaskaran Singh Walia, Drishti Goel, Supriyo Ghosh

entry.summary: Presents FixItFlow, a system that generates cloud incident troubleshooting guides from historical data by extracting diagnostic patterns, synthesizing structured guides with verified commands, and enforcing validation against fabrication. In an evaluation with 26 engineers guides earned majority positive clarity ratings and cut mitigation time.

entry.title: HRO: Hierarchical Room-to-Object Framework for Zero-Shot Object Goal Navigation with Large Language Models

author.name: Luyuan Jia, Yinfeng Yu

entry.summary: Proposes HRO, a hierarchical room-to-object framework for zero-shot object-goal navigation that adds human-like room-to-object spatial reasoning on top of LLM priors, rather than using LLMs as flat association tools. It aims to reduce blind exploration and improve semantic association.

entry.title: Efficient and Privacy Aware Edge Cloud Collaborative Inference for Large Language Models

author.name: Yi Li, Chen Li, Jiexiong Liu

entry.summary: Proposes an edge-cloud collaborative LLM inference framework built on endpoint-authenticated KV cache, splitting preprocessing, embedding, speculative decoding, and low-dimensional head work to the device while cloud handles authenticated decoder inference. It targets the latency, hardware, and privacy trilemma of on-device LLMs.

entry.title: Price of Fairness in Bandits: A Tight Minimax Characterization

author.name: Dhruv Sarkar, Soumyadeep Dutta, Sayak Ray Chowdhury

entry.summary: Provides a tight minimax characterization of the price of fairness in bandit problems for the strictly fair regime evaluated through negative-power generalized p-means, which had remained unresolved because such means are dominated by the smallest rewards. It improves on prior algorithms that relied on uniform early exploration.

entry.title: Data-Efficient Adaptation of LLMs via Attention Head Reweighting

author.name: Tuomas Oikarinen, Zixiao Chen, Charlotte Siska, Tsui-Wei Weng, Chandan Singh, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: Proposes adapting LLMs to new text-classification tasks by learning only a single scalar per attention head, drastically reducing trainable parameters by exploiting the functional specialization of heads. It targets data-efficient learning in low-label domains like security.

entry.title: Agile perceptive multi-skill locomotion for quadrupedal robots in the wild

author.name: Jun-Gill Kang, Jaehyun Park, Tae-Gyu Song, Joon-Ha Kim, Seungwoo Hong, Hae-Won Park

entry.summary: Presents a transformer-based reinforcement-learning framework for quadrupedal robots that unifies multiple locomotion skills, enabling autonomous gait transitions and high-speed traversal of complex terrain using only onboard perception. It generates large-scale feature-rich 2D motion datasets via trajectory optimization to pretrain reusable skills.

entry.title: Protective Capacity Hallucination: When Large Language Models Claim Nonexistent Capabilities

author.name: Eunna Lee, Jungpyo Nam, Sunjun Hwang

entry.summary: Identifies and names Protective Capacity Hallucination, where an LLM cast as a protector claims to have taken real-world actions it cannot perform, like calling emergency services, rather than acknowledging its limits. A large study across eight models and 13,600 sessions finds the behavior gated by situational severity and multi-party dialogic format.

entry.title: How Agents Ask for Permission: User Permissions for AI Agents, from Interfaces to Enforcement

author.name: Alexandra E. Michael, Franziska Roesner

entry.summary: Argues for user-level rather than product-level permissions and enforcement for AI agents, since different users have different needs, and examines the space from permission interfaces to enforcement mechanisms. It addresses risks like prompt injection, private-data leakage, and unauthorized sensitive actions.

entry.title: PUe: Biased Positive-Unlabeled Learning Enhancement by Causal Inference

author.name: Xutao Wang, Hanting Chen, Tianyu Guo, Yunhe Wang

entry.summary: PUe enhances positive-unlabeled learning under selection bias by using normalized propensity scores and normalized inverse-probability weighting within the SAR-PU framework. It targets realistic settings where positive labels are not selected at random.

entry.title: CDS: Counterfactual Directionality Score for Structured Interventions in Spatial Graphs

author.name: Humaira Anzum, Md Ishtyaq Mahmud, Jagan Mohan Reddy Dwarampudi, Tania Banerjee

entry.summary: CDS introduces a counterfactual directionality score for estimating directional influence between node types in spatial graphs by training a neighbor influence model and applying constrained interventions that alter neighborhood composition. It targets cell-cell interaction analysis in spatial biology.

entry.title: Structured Reinforcement Learning for Bayesian Persuasion : Application to Intelligent Interactive Driving

author.name: Merlin Paul, Anup Aprem

entry.summary: This paper applies structured reinforcement learning to a Bayesian persuasion problem for intelligent interactive driving, where a lead vehicle selectively reveals traffic information to steer connected vehicles' decisions toward system objectives. It exploits problem structure to make the farsighted signaling design tractable.

entry.title: Mono-Z Dark Matter Search with Neural Spline Flows Using CMS Run 2015D Open Data

author.name: Hitesh Rasineni (VIT-AP University, Amaravati, India), Bhavishya Chebrolu (Mohan Babu University, Tirupati, India)

entry.summary: This work searches for dark matter produced with a leptonically decaying Z boson using CMS 2015D open data and five independently trained neural spline flows to model Standard Model background and signal densities. It constructs a per-event likelihood-ratio test statistic from the learned densities.

entry.title: PiVoT: A Variational Solution for Real-time Large-scale Multi-object Detection and Tracking under Heavy Clutter

author.name: Runze Gan, Qing Li, Simon J. Godsill, Mike E. Davies, James R. Hopgood

entry.summary: PiVoT is a fast variational Bayesian multi-object tracker for noisy point clouds under heavy clutter that jointly infers object states, shapes, existence, data association, and measurement rates without external clustering or detectors. It handles positional and Doppler measurements in real time.

entry.title: Lyapunov Exponent as Physics-Informed Dense Reward: RL Discovery of Stabilization Beyond the Kapitza Pendulum

author.name: Slava Andrejev

entry.summary: This short paper uses the Lyapunov characteristic exponent as a dense physics-informed reward for RL stabilization of an inverted pendulum with vertical drive, discovering both the Kapitza oscillatory regime and full damping to an upright position. It demonstrates a physics-grounded reward-shaping idea.

entry.title: Lighthouse RL: Sample-Efficient Circuit Optimization via Strategic Reset Points

author.name: Mustafa Emre G\"ursoy, Stefan Uhlich, Ryoga Matsuo, Ya\u{g}{\i}z Gen\c{c}er, Arun Venkitaraman, Chia-Yu Hsieh, Andrea Bonetti, Eisaku Ohbuchi, Lorenzo Servadei

entry.summary: Lighthouse RL improves sample efficiency for analog circuit sizing by resetting RL episodes from high-performing configurations discovered during training, called lighthouses, to steer exploration toward promising regions. It compares favorably against standard RL and Bayesian optimization on circuit benchmarks.

entry.title: Securing LLMs in the Wild: Privacy and Security Challenges at the Edge

author.name: Ren-Yi Huang, Mingchen Li, Dumindu Samaraweera, Morris Chang

entry.summary: This paper surveys and analyzes the security and privacy challenges of deploying LLMs at the edge, framing a Security-Efficiency Paradox where optimizations like quantization, pruning, and partitioning can introduce vulnerabilities. It maps how efficiency techniques reshape the threat landscape.

entry.title: DeepCormack: Fermi surface tomography using model-based data-driven algorithms

author.name: Georg F. B. Lovric, Bryn Drury, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb, Stephen B. Dugdale, Ander Biguri

entry.summary: DeepCormack applies model-based data-driven algorithms to Fermi surface tomography, reconstructing the 3D two-photon momentum density from noisy, sparse-projection positron annihilation data. It improves on the classical Cormack-method reconstruction under poor signal-to-noise conditions.

entry.title: Text2Sign: A Single-GPU Diffusion Baseline for Text-to-Sign Language Video Generation

author.name: Ruize Xia

entry.summary: Text2Sign is a text-conditioned diffusion model for short sign-language video clips that runs on a single GPU by combining a frozen vision-language text encoder with a 3D encoder-decoder and factorized spatiotemporal attention. It systematically compares backbones, encoders, and attention choices on a signer-disjoint How2Sign split.

entry.title: Graph Partitioning with Demands: Generalized Conductance and its Applications

author.name: Micha{\l} Szyfelbein, Dariusz Dereniowski

entry.summary: This work studies graph partitioning under a general demand model, introducing a generalized conductance objective that normalizes cut cost by internal and cross demands, and develops algorithms and applications for it. It generalizes classical conductance-based partitioning.

entry.title: DreamSat-Pose: Spacecraft Pose Estimation from Single-View 3D Reconstructions and Learned 2D-3D Feature Matching

author.name: Josiane Uwumukiza, Jocelyn Zhao, Giovanni Lavezzi, Giacomo Battaglia, Paolo Panicucci, Minduli C. Wijayatunga, Victor Rodriguez-Fernandez, Richard Linares

entry.summary: DreamSat-Pose performs single-image 6-DoF pose estimation of unknown spacecraft by first reconstructing a 3D shape model and then learning dense 2D-3D correspondences using frozen DINOv3 features and a trainable graph-convolutional geometric encoder. It targets autonomous rendezvous and proximity operations with unknown targets.

entry.title: Deformable State Estimation for Autonomous Surgical Tissue Retraction Under Partial Observability

author.name: Everest Yang, Skye Thompson, George D. Konidaris

entry.summary: This work studies state estimation for autonomous surgical tissue retraction under partial observability, reconstructing the full deformable mesh from 40 noisy vertex observations using an MLP with a PCA latent representation and geometry-aware regularization. It is evaluated in a 2D deformable sheet simulation with retraction planning.

entry.title: Differentiable Polarized Path Tracing

author.name: Pramod Rao, J\'er\'emy Riviere, Xilong Zhou, Abhijeet Ghosh, Abhimitra Meka, Thabo Beeler, Marc Habermann, Christian Theobalt, Delio Vicini

entry.summary: Extends physically based differentiable rendering to polarized light via Mueller-Stokes calculus, addressing the rank-deficient nature of polarimetric operators that breaks standard gradient estimators like path replay backpropagation. It enables inverse rendering that exploits polarization cues for geometry and material recovery.

entry.title: Screening Is Effective for Visual Recognition

author.name: Shunya Shimomura, Kazuhiro Hotta

entry.summary: This paper adapts a language-model Screening mechanism to vision transformers, independently evaluating each patch relevance via query-key similarity and explicitly rejecting low-relevance background patches instead of relying only on softmax attention. It aims to reduce irrelevant information in feature aggregation.

entry.title: SPECS: Speciated Evolutionary Circuit Synthesis

author.name: Ya\u{g}{\i}z Gen\c{c}er, Stefan Uhlich, Andrea Bonetti, Arun Venkitaraman, Chia-Yu Hsieh, Lorenzo Servadei

entry.summary: SPECS is a NEAT-inspired genetic algorithm for automated analog circuit synthesis that jointly optimizes topology and sizing, adapting genome representation and operators with circuit-specific wiring constraints and speciation. It transfers neuroevolution principles to analog design.

entry.title: Evaluating Encoding Strategies for Closed-Loop Classification in Biological Neural Networks

author.name: Martin Schottlender, Veronika Volkova, Pengjie Zhou, Ruifeng Zheng, Frank H. P. Fitzek, Pit Hofmann

entry.summary: Compares rate, phase, burst, and time-to-first-spike encoding strategies for closed-loop classification using cultured biological neural networks stimulated via a multi-electrode array. It finds burst-based temporal encoding yields the highest observed performance.

entry.title: Power from Potential: A Survey of Electrostatic Actuators for Haptics

author.name: Ahad M. Rauf, Ran Zhou, Eric Acome, Madeline Balaam, Sean Follmer, Teng Han, Craig Shultz, Daniel Leithinger

entry.summary: A focused review of high-voltage electrostatic actuators for haptics, examining their soft, thin, silent, and energy-efficient properties across four categories for wearable and everyday haptic interfaces. It surveys a compelling alternative to conventional motors.

entry.title: WNOJ-LIO: A White-Noise-on-Jerk Motion-Prior EKF for High-Dynamic LiDAR-IMU Fusion

author.name: Junning Lyu, Qizhi Guo, Xia Ning, Tao Song, Shaoming He

entry.summary: WNOJ-LIO is a LiDAR-inertial odometry framework using a white-noise-on-jerk motion-prior Extended Kalman Filter that decouples state prediction from noisy IMU integration to reduce vibration-contaminated distortion in high-dynamic driving. It improves de-distortion and scan-to-map registration.

entry.title: Stress-Sharing: A Bio-Inspired Approach to Decentralized Fault Repair in Modular Spacecraft

author.name: Sidhdharth D. Sikka, Yue Shen, Shaoshuai Mou

entry.summary: Introduces a fully decentralized, asynchronous stress-sharing repair policy for modular spacecraft inspired by biological wound healing, guiding surviving modules toward damaged regions using only local information and no absolute position sensing. It enables autonomous fault repair without preplanned reconfiguration.

entry.title: COLMAR: Cooperative View Policy Learning for Multi-Agent Active 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Phu Pham, Damon Conover, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: COLMAR is a cooperative view-policy learning framework for multi-agent active 3D reconstruction that formulates viewpoint allocation as shared policy optimization over map-centric observations with a reconstruction-aware objective promoting overlap-aware coverage and collision-safe exploration. It reduces redundant observations and clustering in multi-agent settings.

entry.title: Learning Forward & Reverse Skills from a Single Unfinished Demonstration for Constrained Manipulation Tasks

author.name: Yexin Hu, Haoyi Zheng, Johannes Heidersberger, Dongheui Lee

entry.summary: Presents a one-shot learning-from-demonstration framework for constrained contact-rich manipulation that learns both forward and reverse execution from a single, possibly unfinished demonstration, decomposing motion into non-contact dynamic movement primitives and contact screw-motion primitives. It removes the need for multiple complete demonstrations.

entry.title: AeroMap3D: Anchoring Monocular UAV 6-DoF Localization to Visual-Geometric-Semantic Map Priors

author.name: Zhiyun Deng, Luis Sentis

entry.summary: AeroMap3D is a monocular 6-DoF UAV localization system anchoring onboard imagery to visual, geometric, and semantic map priors for GNSS-denied navigation, using a lightweight adapter that lets a pretrained dense matcher perform UAV-to-map registration without finetuning. It addresses cross-view discrepancy and structural inconsistency with elevation models.

entry.title: Towards end-to-end optimization in multimaterial 3D printing

author.name: Xue-Ling Luo, Steven Yang, Jingye Tan, Robert F. Shepherd, Noy Cohen, Nikolaos Bouklas

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end framework for multimaterial 3D printing that integrates sparsified physics-augmented neural networks with finite-element topology optimization, extracting closed-form composition-aware hyperelastic constitutive laws to enable exact symbolic adjoint differentiation. It jointly optimizes material distribution and structural topology.

entry.title: The Perplexity Trap: When Patent Law Makes Human Writing Look Like AI

author.name: Anubhab Banerjee

entry.summary: Examines whether zero-shot AI-text detectors can flag LLM-assisted patent text under new EPO rules, given consumer-GPU constraints and legal clarity requirements that push human drafting onto the same low-perplexity manifold as LLMs. It benchmarks three open detectors on granted telecom patents versus LLM-generated counterparts.

entry.title: Microstructure-Conditioned Surrogate Models for Graded Multiscale Optimization of Mycelium Composites

author.name: J. Storm, I. B. C. M. Rocha, S. Schyck, K. Masania, F. P. van der Meer

entry.summary: This work conditions a hybrid physics-data microscale surrogate model on microstructural variables via a hypernetwork, enabling accurate multiscale mechanical predictions across a range of microstructures for graded material optimization. It targets sustainable mycelium composites.

entry.title: An Empirical Study on Stage-Information Interfaces for VLA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yingwei Ji

entry.summary: An empirical study comparing stage-information interfaces for vision-language-action fine-tuning, using segmented action annotations as intermediate representation between full-task instruction and action chunks, evaluated with GR00T on LIBERO-10. It examines whether current-stage text or ordinal stage indices help long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: 3 Questions: Neural transparency and the future of AI design

author.name: Media Lab

entry.summary: An MIT News interview describing a paper introducing neural transparency, a tool that lets everyday users glimpse inside a personalized AI companion's neural network before it responds, presented at the ACM Intelligent User Interfaces conference. It targets the gap between people designing custom chatbots and understanding how those systems will behave.

entry.title: Cost-Optimal Foundation Model Deployment Portfolio for Transportation Management

author.name: Xi Cheng, Ke Liu, Siyuan Feng, Jane Lin, H. Oliver Gao

entry.summary: Formulates the Foundation Model Deployment Portfolio problem as a mixed-integer program that assigns models and deployment modes to transportation-center functions under shared GPU budgets, quality, latency, and safety constraints. It proves NP-hardness and proposes an approximation approach.

entry.title: Federated Explainable Artificial Intelligence: Roles, Architectures, Evaluation, and Open Challenges

author.name: Masoume Gholizade, Fabrizio Ruffini, Pietro Ducange, Francesco Marcelloni

entry.summary: A systematic survey of federated explainable AI, reviewing how explainability can be provided while keeping data local, and covering roles, architectures, evaluation, and open challenges. It highlights the shift from post-hoc to integrated explainability in privacy-preserving settings.

entry.title: Inference Economics of Enterprise Coding Agents: A Case Study of Cloud vs. On-Premise LLMs

author.name: Sheng-Wei Peng, Yi-Hsun Lin, Yi-Pei Lee

entry.summary: A governance analysis comparing frontier-provider sovereignty, which centralizes authority with the most capable model's provider, against action-centered deployer sovereignty, which places final authority with the organization authorizing high-impact actions. It combines comparative reading of public frameworks with implementation considerations.

entry.title: Self-Improving AI Coding Agents Through Accumulated Behavioral Rules: A Closed-Loop Framework

author.name: Aditya Aggarwal, Nahid Farhady Ghalaty

entry.summary: Presents a closed-loop framework where every accepted code-review comment is codified as a persistent behavioral rule, expanding a versioned rule set plus self-review checklist that coding agents apply before submission. Deployed across a microservices platform, the rule set grew and reduced repeated mistakes.

entry.title: STKAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Spatio-Temporal Forecasting

author.name: Sicong Lai, Yuehong Hu, Siru Zhong, Si Qiao, Yuxuan Liang, Guangyin Jin

entry.summary: Introduces STKAN, which incorporates Taylor-polynomial Kolmogorov-Arnold Network modules into spatial and temporal token mixing for spatio-temporal forecasting, plus a learnable soft node-group assignment for spatial mixing. It emphasizes the often-overlooked role of the nonlinear function approximator.

entry.title: SemaDiff: Identifying Semantic-Changing Commits with Generated Code and Tests

author.name: Maha Ayub, Michael Konstantinou, Ahmed Khanfir, Nikolaos Tsantalis, Mike Papadakis

entry.summary: Presents SemaDiff, which identifies purely semantic-preserving versus behavior-changing commits by comparing generated test execution on pre- and post-commit versions rather than only detecting refactorings. It generates code and tests to probe behavioral equivalence.

entry.title: ExTernD: Expanded-Rank Ternary Decomposition Ternary LLM PTQ with Accuracy Approaching Any Quantization Level

author.name: Chethan Reddy G. P

entry.summary: Introduces a post-training quantization method that factorizes each weight matrix into ternary factors with an expanded inner rank, so components past full rank correct earlier quantization error. It proves the residual decreases monotonically and can approach bf16 accuracy arbitrarily closely, unlike fixed-plane ternary schemes.

entry.title: Spectral-Informed Neural Networks Outperform Spectral Methods in High-dimensional PDEs

author.name: Tianchi Yu, Ivan Oseledets

entry.summary: Shows that spectral-informed neural networks operating in the spectral domain outperform classical spectral methods on high-dimensional PDEs where spectral methods hit the curse of dimensionality. It combines spectral methods with physics-informed learning to avoid spatial derivative computation.

entry.title: The SIGReg Objective as Variational Free Energy: A Theoretical Active-Inference Account of JEPA World Models

author.name: Fabio Arnez, Alexandra Gomez-Villa

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical active-inference account of JEPA world models, showing that the choice of anti-collapse regularizer determines whether the training objective is a valid variational free energy. It organizes four regularizers into an entropy-estimator hierarchy and argues some (VICReg, LogDet) fail to preserve the surprise bound while SIGReg is safe.

entry.title: Relevance-Aware Rule: Structural Deletion of Irrelevant Conditions in Decision Trees

author.name: Jung-Sik Hong, Jeongeon Lee, Min Kyu Sim, Sangheum Hwang

entry.summary: This paper establishes theory for reliably deleting irrelevant conditions from decision-tree rules, identifying that a binary split shifts class proportions in opposite directions and using this to guide structural simplification. It targets more faithful and interpretable rule sets even in sparse optimal trees.

entry.title: Active Learning for Efficient Annotation of Surgical Videos with Weak Supervision

author.name: Manasa Dendukuri, Matjaz Jogan, Daniel A. Hashimoto, Guiqiu Liao

entry.summary: This paper proposes a human-in-the-loop framework combining active learning with dual-loss optimization to reduce annotation effort for localizing and segmenting objects in laparoscopic surgical videos. It uses a foundation model to produce temporally consistent class activation maps from weak video-level labels plus human-corrected mask supervision.

entry.title: Plausible Deniability Guarantees for Whistleblowers

author.name: Leo Richter, Matt J. Kusner

entry.summary: Formalizes whistleblower protection as per-report differential privacy on the transcript of audit-selection decisions, under a strong-adversary model where the audited organization observes selections. It proves that randomized response at the selection step cannot beat uniform random auditing by more than a small margin.

entry.title: Beyond the $d^{2.5}$-mixing bound for Dikin walks on polytopes

author.name: Yunbum Kook

entry.summary: Improves the mixing-time bound for the Dikin walk sampler on polytopes, advancing toward the conjectured optimal rate by beating the prior d^2.5 bound for exponential sampling. It draws on interior-point-method barrier geometry.

entry.title: Meta-Learning Preferences for Multilingual LLM Alignment

author.name: Jiaying Lin, Seongho Son, Nam Phuong Tran, Long Tran-thanh, Ilija Bogunovic, Debmalya Mandal

entry.summary: Proposes a meta-learning framework for RLHF and DPO that transfers preference data across languages to learn a transferable initialization enabling adaptation to low-resource target languages with minimal data. It provides theoretical guarantees for meta-reward modeling and meta-policy optimization.

entry.title: Prospective clinical indication, post-hoc report leakage, and fusion design in multi-image chest radiograph classification: a patient-clustered evaluation

author.name: Kamran Shahid, Muhammad Munwar Iqbal

entry.summary: Evaluates multi-image chest radiograph classification with careful patient-clustered methodology, quantifying post-hoc report leakage and comparing fusion designs including DeepSets and section-guarding under bootstrap uncertainty. It highlights evaluation pitfalls when combining images and staged clinical text.

entry.title: The impact of objective interactions on the performance of massive objective optimization algorithms

author.name: Shakiba Shahbandegan, Jose Guadalupe Hernandez, Emily Dolson

entry.summary: Investigates how evolutionary algorithms behave when objective counts grow far beyond the usual many-objective regime into the massive range, and how objective interaction structure affects performance, using a controllable diagnostic benchmark. It probes underexplored scaling questions in many-objective optimization.

entry.title: Safe Overtaking for Autonomous Racing Using Hierarchical Optimization and Learning-Based Control

author.name: Hassan Jardali, Kai Yin, Lantao Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical autonomous-racing overtaking framework that separates maneuver-level decision making using mixed-integer optimization from safety-certified trajectory control with control barrier functions, reducing conservatism of fixed-decay discrete CBFs. It balances competitive overtaking with formal safety.

entry.title: A Hybrid Sampling-Based Trajectory Planner with Game-Theoretic Guidance for Autonomous Racing

author.name: Alexander Langmann, Frederico Pita de Araujo, Mattia Piccinini, Johannes Betz

entry.summary: Integrates game-theoretic reasoning into a sampling-based motion planner for autonomous racing, using an alpha-potential game formulation to guide strategic interactions like blocking while retaining robust high-frequency trajectory generation. It makes interactive game reasoning practical for real-time stacks.

entry.title: Min-Max Regret Task Allocation and Planning of Heterogeneous Multi-Robot System in Partially Known Environments

author.name: Xinkai Liang, Huixuan Chan, Ying Liu, Yangxi Shi, Hao Fang

entry.summary: Formulates heterogeneous multi-robot task allocation with temporal-logic tasks in partially known environments as a min-max regret optimization, introducing region-binding atomic propositions to capture resource uncertainty within the automaton. It balances exploration and exploitation while maintaining scalability.

entry.title: The Nonsmooth Impact Direction (NSID) of Robotic Systems

author.name: Annika Kirner, Christian Ott

entry.summary: Analyzes the nonsmooth impact direction of rigid-link robotic systems, showing it is a characteristic direction of robotic impacts largely independent of contact properties and applicable to backdrivable systems with rigid, flexible, or constrained joints. It provides theoretical insight into pre- and post-impact velocity relations.

entry.title: Extreme Power Concentration: A Map and Research Directions

author.name: pepijn_cobben

entry.summary: A macrostrategy piece mapping the risk that even aligned AI could enable extreme power concentration by making human labor unnecessary, potentially producing more stable and unaccountable authoritarian states. It offers a framing and research directions to make the problem more tractable for technical contributors.

entry.title: Designing Safety-Constrained LLM Systems for Public Health Information Access

author.name: Ben Torkian, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: Describes a safety-constrained LLM system for public health information navigation focused on maternal and child health, combining domain-restricted retrieval, strict boundary enforcement against medical advice, anonymous session management, and audit logging. It offers practical design patterns for safety-critical deployment.

entry.title: A Hybrid Mamba for Audio-Visual Navigation

author.name: Yi Wang, Yinfeng Yu

entry.summary: Proposes Samba, a hybrid Mamba architecture for audio-visual navigation that replaces GRUs with a selective Mamba state encoder and adds an audio Mamba encoder to capture global time-frequency dependencies. It updates a backbone that had remained largely unchanged for years.

entry.title: Continuously Evolving Deepfake Detection: An Architecture and Public-Benchmark Evaluation of a Dynamic Detection System

author.name: Ken Jon Miyachi, Dylan Uys

entry.summary: Presents a continuously retrained deepfake detector built on an open adversarial competition that refreshes its training distribution, evaluated across nineteen public datasets to address the known collapse of static detectors on in-the-wild content. The central argument is that the detection-generation gap is structural and needs dynamic training rather than one-time fitting.

entry.title: Learning Physics-Guided Residual Dynamics for Deformable Object Simulation

author.name: Shivansh Patel, Kaifeng Zhang, Sanjay Pokkali, Svetlana Lazebnik, Yunzhu Li

entry.summary: Combines an optimizable spring-mass physics simulator with a learned network that predicts residual corrections, using a velocity-based formulation and a sliding-window transformer to model deformable-object dynamics. It reports better accuracy than purely physics-based or purely learned methods for robotic manipulation.

entry.title: DevicesWorld: Benchmarking Cross-Device Agents in Heterogeneous Environments

author.name: Huatao Li, Xinwei Geng, Yuheng Wang, Yutong Li, Runde Yang, Hantao Chen, Shu Yao, Jingru Fan, Xuhui Ren, Yuanyuan Zhao, Fei Huang, Chen Qian

entry.summary: Introduces a large executable benchmark of 6,140 tasks for evaluating agents that must acquire and integrate information across heterogeneous devices such as phones, desktops, and smart homes. It addresses the single-environment focus of existing agent benchmarks by testing cross-device end-to-end tasks.

entry.title: Grounded world models in biological organisms and future embodied AI

author.name: Giovanni Pezzulo, Davide Nuzzi, Marco D'Alessandro, Riccardo Proietti, Roberto Bottini, Paul Cisek

entry.summary: A perspective arguing that biological intelligence builds grounded world models through environmental interaction that then scaffold language, the reverse of current AI systems that attach other modalities to a linguistic scaffold. It illustrates five neural circuits supporting grounded world modeling for embodied AI.

entry.title: UTS at ELOQUENT 2026 Voight-Kampff: structural shifts in AI writing bypass state-of-the-art detectors

author.name: Dima Galat, Marian-Andrei Rizoiu

entry.summary: Investigates which AI-text evasion attacks survive state-of-the-art adversarial fine-tuning of detectors, finding an asymmetry where pushing generated text out of the detector's training distribution reliably defeats it while mimicking human data fails. It introduces cross-decade register and modernist stream-of-consciousness attacks that top an evasion leaderboard.

entry.title: Memory as a Controlled Process: Learned Adaptive Memory Management for LLM Agents

author.name: Eric Hanchen Jiang, Zhi Zhang, Yuchen Wu, Levina Li, Dong Liu, Xiao Liang, Rui Sun, Yubei Li, Edward Sun, Haozheng Luo, Zhaolu Kang, Aylin Caliskan, Kai-Wei Chang, Ying Nian Wu

entry.summary: Argues that LLM-agent memory should be a learned, context-dependent controlled process rather than accessed via fixed heuristics, since optimal retrieval, plan reuse, re-querying, and consolidation vary by task stage. It proposes adaptive memory management that decides these behaviors dynamically.

entry.title: Human4K: A Large-Scale 4K Multi-View Mocap Dataset for Whole-Body 3D Human Reconstruction

author.name: Tianshun Han, Ziyu Shi, Lijian Liu, Ajian Liu, Benjia Zhou, Hugo Jair Escalante, Yanyan Liang, Sergio Escalera, Zhen Lei, Jun Wan

entry.summary: Introduces a large-scale 4K multi-view motion-capture dataset with mocap-accurate whole-body SMPL-X annotations, containing over six million high-resolution images from an eight-view synchronized camera system. It targets the lack of high-resolution, high-precision, diverse-motion data for robust 3D human reconstruction.

entry.title: Verifying formulas for interventional distributions

author.name: Francesco Freni, Leonard Henckel, Sebastian Weichwald

entry.summary: Formalizes the problem of verifying whether a given observational formula identifies a target interventional distribution in causal graphical models, complementary to identification. It shows sound and complete identification solutions do not solve verification, proposes a falsifier-based verifier for exponential-family models, and derives a gateway test for front-door admissible sets.

entry.title: From Novice to Expert: Cost-Aware Bandits for Evolving Worker Performance in Crowdsensing

author.name: Yin Huang, Qingsong Liu, Jie Xu

entry.summary: This work studies budget-constrained online worker recruitment in mobile crowdsensing where worker performance improves with experience and costs are unknown, proposing a cost-aware bandit approach for non-stationary evolving workers. It relaxes the common stationarity assumption in prior recruitment methods.

entry.title: Implementations of Quantum and Classical Topology-Aligned Architectures for Molecular Property Prediction

author.name: James T. Pegg, Hubert Okadome Valencia, Ronin Wu

entry.summary: This work builds topology-aligned architectures for molecular property prediction where atoms map to computational units and bonds determine parameter-sharing interactions, instantiated as a variational quantum circuit and a parameter-matched classical message-passing model. Both achieve comparable AUCs on QM9 tasks with only 64 parameters.

entry.title: VAIOM: Continuous-Input, Discrete-Output Decoder-Only Financial Sequence Modeling

author.name: Yiming Ma, Xinyu Chen

entry.summary: VAIOM is a decoder-only Transformer for probabilistic next-return modeling on hourly foreign-exchange data that separates continuous multivariate input representation from a categorical distribution over volatility-normalized return buckets. This lets it preserve numerical input structure while supporting cross-entropy training and likelihood evaluation.

entry.title: Mixed-Timescale Differential Coding for Downlink Model Broadcast in Wireless Federated Learning

author.name: Chung-Hsuan Hu, Zheng Chen, Erik G. Larsson

entry.summary: This work proposes mixed-timescale differential coding for broadcasting global models in wireless federated learning, exploiting temporal correlation between successive models to reduce quantization bits while remaining robust to devices that miss updates due to link failures. It avoids stale-model degradation without frequent full-model broadcasts.

entry.title: Hindcast: Replaying Prediction Markets to Evaluate LLM Forecasters

author.name: Xiao Ye, Jacob Dineen, Evan Zhu, Shijie Lu, Kevin Song, Ben Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Hindcast, an evaluation method that grades LLM forecasters as if standing at a chosen past date to close two leakage channels: post-event retrieval and training data that contains outcomes. It replays resolved Polymarket prediction market questions to measure genuine foresight rather than recall.

entry.title: LPM: Industrial-Scale Generative Video Restoration

author.name: Bichuan Zhu, Fulin Li, Jiachao Gong, Jinhua Hao, Kai Zhao, Kun Yuan, Pengcheng Xu, Qiang Wang, Qiao Mo, Yanlong Yuan, Yizhen Shao, Yuxiao Hu, Zixi Tuo, Ming Sun, Chao Zhou, Bin Chen, Bin Yu

entry.summary: Presents LPM, a diffusion-based generative framework for photorealistic restoration of arbitrarily long in-the-wild videos, described as the first generative video restoration model deployed at industrial scale. It combines large-scale data engineering, foundation-model training, and temporal-pyramid inference deployed in production.

entry.title: Towards Spatial Supersensing in the Wild

author.name: Tianjun Gu, Tianyu Xin, Kuan Zhang, Bowen Yang, Kok-Chung Chua, Peize Li, Xinran Zhang, Yupeng Chen, Qiyue Zhao, Qinlei Xie, Jianhang Liu, Yucheng Lu, Yinan Han, Marco Pavone, Yiming Li

entry.summary: Introduces VSI-Super-Wild, a large-scale benchmark for spatial supersensing over long temporal horizons in diverse real-world scenes, addressing the limitation that prior benchmarks use synthetic concatenated clips mostly of household scenes. It pushes multimodal models beyond language understanding toward genuine world modeling.

entry.title: RainDancer: RGB-Event Video Deraining with Rain-Oriented Spiking Dynamics

author.name: Kui Jiang, Runzhe Li, Zhaocheng Yu, Guanglu Sun, Junjun Jiang, Xianming Liu

entry.summary: Presents a progressive RGB-Event fusion framework for video deraining that decomposes signals before interaction to avoid cross-modal interference, using event-camera motion cues alongside RGB. It targets robust perception under adverse weather.

entry.title: Efficient Computing for Medical Image Acquisition and Reconstruction

author.name: Xiao Wang, Jayasai Rajagopal, Md Safaiat Hossain, Peng Chen, Mohamed Wahib, Enzhi Zhang, Emma J. Reid

entry.summary: A review connecting medical image reconstruction across CT, MRI, PET, and SPECT through a shared computational framework spanning inverse problems, optimization, and efficient computing. It frames reconstruction as a growing computational bottleneck in modern high-dimensional imaging.

entry.title: A Bayesian framework for the uncanny valley in humanoid robot design

author.name: Shimon Honda, Rin Shibano, Hideyoshi Yanagisawa

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical Bayesian generative model that operationalizes uncanny-valley design guidelines as manipulable variables, representing affinity as posterior-weighted negative category-conditional surprise. It maps perceptual mechanisms onto quantitative design parameters for humanoid robots.

entry.title: A 3DGS-Driven Dynamic Viewpoint and Vibrotactile Framework for Subsea Teleoperation Validated via fNIRS

author.name: Fang Xu, Tianyu Zhou, Ruitong Tian, Md Jahidul Islam, Jing Du

entry.summary: Presents a multimodal teleoperation architecture for subsea remotely operated vehicles that uses real-time 3D Gaussian Splatting to synthesize occlusion-free exocentric viewpoints and a vibrotactile suit for obstacle-clearance cues, validated with fNIRS brain measurements. It reduces operator sensory workload under latency and narrow views.

entry.title: Vision-Based Obstacle Separation for Strawberry Harvesting in Clusters Using Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Teng Li, Hanfei Shi, Chunjiang Zhao, Ya Xiong

entry.summary: Proposes VGPA, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for selective strawberry harvesting in clusters, decomposing the task into obstacle separation and target grasping with a vision-guided high-level decision mechanism and a progressive adaptive exploration strategy. It handles occlusion by unripe fruits.

entry.title: A Deployed Hybrid Vehicle-in-the-Loop Platform for Validating Cooperative Perception

author.name: Anastasia Bolovinou, Giorgos Hadjipavlis, Markos Antonopoulos, Panagiotis Tachtalis, Konstantinos Petousakis, Konstantinos Lazaridis, Alexandros Siskos, Bill Roungas, Angelos Amditis

entry.summary: Presents a deployed hybrid vehicle-in-the-loop platform coupling a real instrumented vehicle with a CARLA digital twin through a V2X pipeline, running GPU-accelerated cooperative perception into a probabilistic occupancy grid during scenario runtime. It supports virtual homologation evidence for automated driving under European regulation.

entry.title: LessonBench-V1: A Benchmark Dataset for Evaluating AI Lesson Generation Agents

author.name: Ravidu Suien Rammuni Silva, Ahmad Lotfi, Isibor Kennedy Ihianle, Golnaz Shahtahmassebi, Jordan J. Bird

entry.summary: Introduces LessonBench-V1, a benchmark of 647 human-written lessons paired with LLM reverse-engineered lesson plans across 240 STEM topics, grounded in established instructional-design frameworks. It aims to enable systematic evaluation of AI lesson-generation agents.

entry.title: Operational Evidence Gaps for LLMs in Fraud Detection and Trust-and-Safety Workflows

author.name: Keyur Gabani

entry.summary: Surveys operational deployment evidence for LLMs in fraud detection, scam investigation, and content moderation, coding 49 operationally relevant sources plus contextual references. It asks what evidence would justify placing an LLM inside a live trust-and-safety pipeline under latency, cost, and adversarial constraints.

entry.title: Disentangling Knowledge States with Ability and Proficiency Modeling for Knowledge Tracing

author.name: Duantengchuan Li, Yingqian Bi, Jinsong Chen, Rui Zhang, Mingwen Tong

entry.summary: Proposes Phase-Aware Knowledge Tracing, which decomposes student interaction sequences into ability-building and proficiency-oriented phases based on the observation that students often answer previously failed concepts correctly after practice. It models these phases separately to improve performance prediction.

entry.title: Semantic Anchoring for Robotic Action Representations

author.name: Yuan Xu, Youheng Shi, Chengyang Li, Wentao Zhu, Yizhou Wang

entry.summary: Examines what makes a good action representation in vision-language-action models, showing that fine-tuning on limited robot demonstrations erodes the semantic structure inherited from pretrained encoders and that this erosion tracks task success and out-of-distribution generalization. It introduces a plug-and-play method to preserve that structure, inspired by mirror-neuron shared encoding.

entry.title: Kaleido: Algorithm-Hardware Co-Design for Video Diffusion Transformers by Exploiting Latent Space Correlations

author.name: Wenxuan Miao, Haosong Liu, Weiming Hu, Zihan Liu, Aiyue Chen, Jianlin Yu, Yiwu Yao, Yiming Gan, Jieru Zhao, Jingwen Leng, Minyi Guo, Yu Feng

entry.summary: Presents an algorithm-hardware co-design that accelerates video diffusion transformers by exploiting channel-wise spatiotemporal correlations in latent space, using a lightweight reuse algorithm to skip redundant computation. It targets the self-attention bottleneck that dominates when diffusion timesteps are reduced.

entry.title: Accuracy-Preserving Stability Regularization for Large-Scale Retail Demand Forecasting

author.name: Jize Li, Jiani He, Dishu Yang, Dingyan Shang, Jingjing Liu, Shiqi Huang

entry.summary: This work adds a training-time stability penalty to large-scale retail demand forecasting so that consecutive forecasts do not swing abruptly, improving forecast-path stability with minimal accuracy loss. It reports modest stability gains over XGBoost on M5 series.

entry.title: Post-Training Shifts Confidence: A Three-Stage Analysis of How SFT, RL, and OPD Shape Pre-, Intra-, and Post-CoT Calibration

author.name: Shuhao Li, Guodong Du, Anhao Zhao, Wanyu Lin, Tianyu Yuan, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Introduces a three-stage calibration framework analyzing how SFT, RL, and on-policy distillation reshape model confidence before, during, and after chain-of-thought reasoning. It finds each method excels at a different stage: distillation for difficulty estimation, SFT for early stopping, and RL for trace aggregation.

entry.title: Peak-End-Net: A Peak-End Rule Inspired Framework for Generalizable Video Aesthetic Assessment

author.name: Geng Li, Haiwen Li, Rui Chen, Jing Tang, Lei Sun, Xiangxiang Chu

entry.summary: Peak-End-Net is a lightweight, interpretable video aesthetic assessment model inspired by the psychological peak-end rule, judging videos mainly by salient moments and endings while transferring knowledge from image aesthetics. It targets generalizable aesthetic scoring under limited benchmarks.

entry.title: Recursive ArUco Markers: A Scalable Fiducial Marker Design for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Landing Pads

author.name: Rafael Munoz-Salinas, Francisco Jose Romero-Ramirez, Sergio Garrido-Jurado

entry.summary: Proposes a recursive ArUco fiducial marker design that transforms standard markers into arbitrary-depth recursive markers robust to occlusion and detectable across a wide range distance, using a modified bit-sampling detection strategy. It targets reliable UAV precision landing.

entry.title: Design and Characterization of a Limb Encircling Actuator

author.name: Japmanjeet Singh Gill, Gray Cortright Thomas, Nikko Van Crey, Roberto Leo Medrano, Elliott J. Rouse

entry.summary: Designs and characterizes a Limb-Encircling Actuator that wraps around the limb orthogonal to its axis to reduce the spatial footprint of lower-limb exoskeletons, aiming for less intrusive wearable devices. It reports electromechanical characterization of the new actuation geometry.

entry.title: Design and Control of the "QuadBoat": A Quadruped Surface Vehicle for Drowning Rescue

author.name: Lianxin Zhang, Yihan Huang, Huihuan Qian

entry.summary: Introduces QuadBoat, a bio-inspired quadruped unmanned surface vehicle for drowning rescue that adjusts posture for agile maneuvering and uses inverse-kinematics and cascaded MPC-PID control to track and retrieve victims from water. Experiments validate its agility and tracking.

entry.title: Anatomy of Uncertainty: Expressive Descriptors of Robotic Manipulator Motion for Non-verbal Communication in Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Ridhima Bector, Souravik Dutta, Poornima Ramachandran, Ree Yan Yeoh, Jui Hien Tan, Domenico Campolo, Bernhard Johannes Schmitt

entry.summary: Introduces a mathematical framework using Laban Movement Analysis to express robotic-manipulator perceptual uncertainty through non-verbal motion, mapping uncertainty states to Laban Effort signatures across five motion primitives parameterized by kinematic descriptors. It supports uncertainty communication in human-robot collaboration.

entry.title: Dynamical Vehicle Orienteering Problem for Multi-Rotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicles

author.name: Franti\v{s}ek Nekov\'a\v{r}, Matej Novosad, Martin Saska, Robert P\v{e}ni\v{c}ka

entry.summary: Introduces the Dynamical Vehicle Orienteering Problem, generalizing the orienteering problem to account for external and vehicle-actuated forces, applied to multi-rotor UAV flight planning with a point-mass model under velocity, acceleration, and time constraints. It couples reward maximization with time-optimal trajectory planning.

entry.title: Merging Reaction to Cognition: A Hybrid Cognitive Strategy for Odour Source Localisation in Natural Environments

author.name: Hugo Magalh\~aes, Rui Baptista, Lino Marques

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid cognitive strategy for robotic odour source localization in natural turbulent environments, merging reactive bio-inspired behaviors with cognitive probabilistic belief-based inference to overcome sparse detections and absent concentration gradients. It aims to combine efficiency with robustness for pollutant source tracing.

entry.title: Unifying Decision-Making and Trajectory-Planning in Unsignalized Intersections Using Time-Varying Potential Fields

author.name: David Costa, Francesco Cerrito, Massimo Canale, Carlo Novara

entry.summary: Presents a framework unifying decision-making and trajectory planning for automated vehicles at unsignalized intersections using a finite-horizon optimal control problem with time-varying artificial potential fields and a conflict-zone occupancy coefficient. Simulations show feasible, safe reference trajectories in multi-vehicle scenarios.

entry.title: Faithful Autoformalization of Natural Language Assertions

author.name: Hongyi Liu, Madhusudan Parthasarathy, Adithya Murali

entry.summary: Introduces a framework that uses LLMs to synthesize executable assertions from natural-language specifications, filtering candidates via a conformance score and validity scores from testing generated code. It aims to reduce the manual burden of writing formal contracts for software verification.

entry.title: Evaluation Ability Does Not Imply Optimization Utility: LLM-as-a-Judge Signals in Closed-Loop Table Recognition

author.name: Donghwan Kim

entry.summary: Tests LLM-as-a-judge as a selection signal in closed-loop table recognition against deterministic ground-truth scoring, finding judge signals are weak, unreproducible, and fail to recover better candidates that iteration produced. It argues that evaluation ability does not translate into optimization utility.

entry.title: Improving Text-to-Audio Instruction Following via Fine-Grained Feedback from Audio-Aware Large Language Models

author.name: Chun-Yi Kuan, Siwon Kim, Byeonggeun Kim, Suyoun Kim, Bo-Ru Lu, Qinming Tang, Ankur Gandhe, Hung-yi Lee, Chieh-Chi Kao, Chao Wang

entry.summary: Uses audio-aware LLMs as fine-grained judges to verify target event presence and temporal ordering in generated audio, then converts their feedback into preference pairs for direct preference optimization to improve text-to-audio instruction following. It also introduces a narrative benchmark for evaluation.

entry.title: Constraint-Driven Model Optimization: An Industry Framework for Selecting Compression and Acceleration Techniques in Modern Machine Learning Systems

author.name: Dhruv Shivkant, Saket Mohanty, Utkarsh Wadhwa

entry.summary: This paper proposes a constraint-driven, multi-objective framework for selecting model compression and acceleration techniques by characterizing deployments along data availability, latency, memory, accuracy tolerance, and retraining dimensions. It aims to replace heuristic technique selection with principled methodology.

entry.title: Task-Oriented Sensing and Covert Transmissions for Collaborative Multi-AUV Systems

author.name: Xueyao Zhang, Chenyang Yan, Bo Yang, Xuelin Cao, Zhiwen Yu, Bin Guo, George C. Alexandropoulos, Merouane Debbah, Chau Yuen

entry.summary: This paper co-designs task-oriented sensing and covert underwater acoustic communication for collaborative autonomous underwater vehicles, moving beyond idealized communication assumptions to account for delay, interference, and exposure risk in multi-agent RL. It targets covert cooperative missions with incomplete passive perception.

entry.title: BARS: Benign-Anchored Ranking and Selection for False Alarm Reduction in Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Abu Fuad Ahmad, Istiaque Ahmed

entry.summary: BARS is a benign-anchored feature selection filter for network intrusion detection that ranks features by deviation from a stable benign baseline, correcting a prior class-asymmetric filter whose global-mean anchor drifts toward attack distributions under class imbalance. It aims to reduce costly false alarms upstream of the classifier.

entry.title: Do LLMs Need Architectural Changes for Simultaneous Speech Translation? A Prefix-to-Prefix Data Driven Approach

author.name: Junkun Chen, Jian Xue, Ming Tang, Abdel Heba, Hoda Gholami, Ruchao Fan, Jinyu Li

entry.summary: Argues that decoder-only LLMs can perform simultaneous speech translation without architectural changes, using fixed-length chunked streaming decoding with a rewind-based committed prefix and teacher-labeled prefix-to-prefix fine-tuning targets. The approach avoids brittle read/write policies for conversational speech.

entry.title: The Test Oracle Problem in Synthetic LLM-as-Judge Corpora: Disappearance, Distortion and a Validation Protocol

author.name: Serkan Ball{\i} (Department of Software Engineering, Mehmet Akif Ersoy University, Burdur, T\"urkiye)

entry.summary: Documents a structural failure mode in synthetic LLM-as-judge corpora where a shared decoding-budget parameter silently truncates generated hallucinated answers, producing a large spurious cross-lingual accuracy collapse. It offers a validation protocol to detect such test-oracle problems.

entry.title: Thresholded Cross-Attention for Reliable Intensity-Chromaticity Fusion in Low-Light Image Enhancement

author.name: Yanyi Wu, Xu Zhang, Junkai Chen, Laibin Chang, Jiaqi Ma, Shi Chen, Linwei Zhu, Jianglei Di, Huan Zhang

entry.summary: TCA-Net uses thresholded cross-attention to fuse decoupled intensity and chromaticity streams for low-light image enhancement, replacing fixed-quota Top-K sparse attention that mismatches layer-dependent confidence. It targets better noise suppression and color fidelity.

entry.title: Singular Learning Theory Comprehensive - 2

author.name: Agastya Agrawal

entry.summary: The second installment of an educational series on singular learning theory, motivating and connecting observables like free energy, losses, and the WAIC, and introducing generating functions as a unifying tool before deriving asymptotics. It aims to make Watanabe's framework more intuitive.

entry.title: Classifying daily activities needs posture, reconstructing them needs motion

author.name: Arefeh Farahmandi, Gunnar Blohm

entry.summary: Systematically compares three movement-analysis strategies (temporal movement primitives, Legendre polynomial coefficients, and autoencoder embeddings) on videos of daily activities to ask what stimulus information supports human movement recognition. It finds classification depends on posture while faithful reconstruction depends on motion.

entry.title: GeoAnchor: Collaborative Reasoning via Latent Decomposition for 3D Spatial Understanding

author.name: Hao Li, Han Fang, Zixin Pan, Xin Wei, Hongbo Sun, Jinglin Xu, Zhiyu Lin, Ye Yuan, Zhongjiang He, Yu Yu, Hao Sun

entry.summary: Introduces an interleaved text-latent reasoning framework for 3D spatial understanding that decomposes spatial information into position, direction, and other complementary latents rather than relying on symbolic text or a single latent type. It targets misalignment in complex geometric reasoning from 2D images.

entry.title: Groc-PO: Grounded Context Preference Optimization for Truthful Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Zhixiao Zheng, Zheren Fu, Zhiyuan Yao, Chunxiao Liu, Dongming Zhang, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: Proposes a grounded context preference optimization method for multimodal LLMs that supervises early grounding stages rather than only final answers, addressing how reasoning errors propagate from mistakes in initial grounding. It targets visual hallucination and unfaithful reasoning that standard DPO handles poorly.

entry.title: MxGPS: Multiplex Graph Transformers for a Power Grid Foundation Model

author.name: Charilaos Papaioannou, Ioannis Tsantilas, Dimitris Giannakakos, Vasilis Michalakopoulos, Sotiris Pelekis, Vangelis Marinakis, Arsam Aryandoust, Antonello Monti, Ricardo J. Bessa, Perdo P. Vergara, Jochen Cremer, Elissaios Sarmas

entry.summary: Introduces a multiplex graph transformer as a power-grid foundation model that runs task-specialized branches over a shared node encoder, jointly trained on state estimation and power flow, to combat topology overfitting. It targets the failure mode where the best in-distribution GNNs degrade most under topology shift.

entry.title: Unleashing Multimodal Large Language Models for Training-free HOI Detection in the Wild

author.name: Ting Lei, Jialin Liu, Zhu Xu, Yuxin Peng, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free human-object interaction detection method that more fully exploits multimodal LLMs' reasoning rather than only extracting discriminative representations via prompting. It targets generalization to open-world and compositional interactions beyond closed-set supervised categories.

entry.title: Partially Correlated Verifier Cascades in LLM Harnesses: Concave Log-Odds, Polynomial Reliability, and Blind-Spot Ceilings

author.name: Jiangang Han

entry.summary: Develops a theory of partially correlated verifier cascades in LLM harnesses, modeling the per-instance false-accept rate as a latent variable and showing that posterior log-odds become concave in the number of verifier calls rather than linear. It reveals blind-spot ceilings where correlated verifiers cannot drive failure to zero.

entry.title: Early Adoption of Agentic Coding Tools by GitHub Projects

author.name: Maliha Noushin Raida, Daqing Hou

entry.summary: Analyzes 25,264 agent-generated pull requests from 2,361 popular GitHub repositories to study adoption, project-level productivity, and human-agent collaboration patterns for agentic coding tools. It finds most repositories generate only one or two agentic PRs over three months, indicating limited intensive adoption so far.

entry.title: What Your Model Threw Away and Why You'll Want It Back: Masking, Fingerprinting, and Privacy from Discarded Geometry

author.name: Zachary P. Bradshaw

entry.summary: Develops a framework characterizing the symmetry information discarded by machine learning models whose inputs carry a Lie group action, defining null fibers and stabilizers that capture the group elements a learned function cannot detect. It connects this discarded geometry to masking, fingerprinting, and privacy applications.

entry.title: PQFA: Parallel Quantum Feature Augmentation of Fused Representations for Multimodal Classification

author.name: Mingzhu Wang, Yun Shang

entry.summary: PQFA is a hybrid quantum-classical framework that amplitude-encodes fused multimodal features into parallel shallow variational quantum circuits, concatenating their readouts with classical representations for classification. It is evaluated on MM-IMDb and N24News.

entry.title: A VAE-Driven Multi-Task Satellite-Aided Semantic Communication Framework for 6G-Enabled Connected Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: S. M. Abtahiul Alam, Niloy Das, Apurba Adhikary, Yu Qiao, Zhu Han, Choong Seon Hong

entry.summary: This work proposes a VAE-driven multi-task semantic communication framework for 6G-connected autonomous vehicles that transmits task-relevant information over bandwidth-scarce satellite channels rather than raw data. It targets low-latency safety-critical vehicular tasks.

entry.title: Conditional Invertible Neural Networks for Data-Driven UAV Control: A 2-D Proof of Concept

author.name: Christian Wittke, Stephan Myschik, Oliver Niggemann

entry.summary: This paper investigates conditional invertible neural networks as probabilistic inverse-dynamics models for multirotor control, learning a distribution over control inputs from an INDI teacher and testing on a planar coaxial multicopter. It analyzes closed-loop failure modes such as attitude divergence and phase lag.

entry.title: RF Spectrogram Anomaly Detection with Quantum Kitchen Sinks: Architecture, Representation, and Hardware Validation

author.name: Abdallah Aaraba, Alexis Vieloszynski, Remon Polus, Ola Ahmad, Soumaya Cherkaoui

entry.summary: This work extends Quantum Kitchen Sinks feature maps with multi-depth data re-uploading and ring entanglement for RF spectrogram anomaly detection, introducing a validation-locked five-stage ablation protocol and hardware validation. It probes how these hybrid quantum feature maps behave on structured signal data.

entry.title: Precomputing the Future-Offset Average in TriAttention

author.name: Amarnath Mukherjee (Hozhoke, Inc.)

entry.summary: This note shows that TriAttention's 17-fold average over possible future query distances used to score KV-cache keys collapses exactly into a single precomputable per-band weight via an algebraic identity. This cuts key scoring from seventeen evaluations to one with no change in which keys are pruned.

entry.title: Nexus: Native Mesh Generation with Diffusion

author.name: Hanxiao Wang, Ying-Tian Liu, Yuan-Chen Guo, Qi-Yuan Feng, Zi-Xin Zou, Ding Liang, Biao Zhang, Yan-Pei Cao

entry.summary: Presents Nexus, a diffusion-based mesh generation method that decouples vertex and topology generation, treating vertices as sparse octree voxels generated coarse-to-fine and encoding arbitrary edge and face topology via a Spacetime Interval into continuous per-vertex embeddings. It avoids error-prone autoregressive mesh serialization.

entry.title: T3HG-Editor: Text-driven 3D Human Garment Editing with Body Priors Embedded in SMPL-X

author.name: Shaoru Sun, Xingtao Wang, Zihan Ma, Wenrui Li, Jiantao Zhou, Debin Zhao, Xiaopeng Fan

entry.summary: Placeholder mapping error avoided; this entry corresponds to REAL, an agentic framework for open-world mobile manipulation that establishes sim-to-real-consistent environment APIs without oracle perception and integrates a simulated user for human-in-the-loop interaction. It combines data collection, supervised fine-tuning, and online reinforcement learning for exploratory, communicative, deployable agents.

entry.title: Visual Place Recognition Using Rate-Encoded Spiking Neural Networks with Discrete STDP Learning

author.name: Altzi Tsanko, Oikonomou Katerina Maria, Antonios Gasteratos

entry.summary: Presents a discrete, tensor-native PyTorch implementation of an STDP-trained spiking neural network for visual place recognition, examining neuron assignment and other design choices on the Nordland dataset. It targets energy-efficient loop closure for neuromorphic navigation.

entry.title: Towards a Modular Bin-picking Framework for Handling Object Pose Uncertainties

author.name: Frederik Hagelskj{\ae}r

entry.summary: Presents a modular bin-picking framework that jointly handles object pose-estimation and grasping errors, using pose distribution estimation for uncertainty and a second-viewpoint module to reduce ambiguity. It aims for reliable industrial picking under pose uncertainty.

entry.title: Parsimonious disturbance-aware minimum-time planning with parametric uncertainty

author.name: Martino Gulisano, Matteo Masoni, Marco Gabiccini

entry.summary: Extends a disturbance-aware minimum-lap-time planning framework for motorsport to also account for parametric uncertainty in inertia, center-of-mass position, and drag, using a spatially selective robust-constraint activation to remain tractable. It improves robustness of optimal racing trajectories.

entry.title: Layered Risk Mapping for Autonomous Patient Transport in Expeditionary Medical Facilities

author.name: Lorena Maria Genua, Sarvesh Prajapati, Damla Leblebicioglu, Ta\c{s}k{\i}n Pad{\i}r

entry.summary: Presents a layered risk-mapping framework for autonomous patient transport in expeditionary medical facilities that fuses terrain slope, static and dynamic obstacles, and semantic traversability into a unified probabilistic cost surface via a Noisy-OR model. It supports safer navigation of autonomous wheelchairs in unstructured settings.

entry.title: Active Trust Management for Successful Human-Robot Teaming: Moving from a Trust Repair to a Trust Satisficing Perspective

author.name: Nicola Webb, Edmund R. Hunt

entry.summary: Argues for shifting human-robot teaming from a trust-repair to a trust-satisficing perspective, proposing active trust management that monitors component and system-level trust states as situations evolve during missions. It aims to sustain effective human-agent collaboration in hazardous tasks.

entry.title: Design, Modeling and Experimental Validation of a Miniature Hybrid Underwater Glider With Large-Range Foldable Deflectable Wings

author.name: Yongjian Zhu, Yusen Tao, Feitian Zhang

entry.summary: Presents FoDeGlider, a miniature hybrid underwater glider with two independently actuated large-range foldable and deflectable wings, along with dynamic modeling and hydrodynamic characterization of configuration-dependent variations. It enhances maneuverability and shape adaptability for confined-space ocean tasks.

entry.title: Can we rely on law?

author.name: Alec Thompson

entry.summary: An essay arguing that AI-catastrophe plans over-rely on legal regulation, which may be too slow to counter frontier models that excel at discovering legal and reward loopholes. It reviews which regulatory strategies might stay robust against superhuman loophole discovery.

entry.title: A Structural Similarity Between Two Open Corrigibility Questions

author.name: Ben Saudek

entry.summary: A conceptual alignment post exploring a structural connection between two open questions in corrigibility: reconciling conflicting commands over time and defining a multi-human principal. It frames both as instances of an agent handling multiple, sometimes contradictory sources of authority.

entry.title: RAGthoven at SemEval-2026 Task 1: A Multi-Stage Pipeline Walks Into a Benchmark and Barely Clears the Bar

author.name: Marek \v{S}uppa, Vikt\'oria Ondrejov\'a, Lucia Ganajov\'a, Gregor Karetka, Daniel Skala

entry.summary: Describes RAGthoven, a multi-stage LLM pipeline for a multilingual constrained humor-generation shared task, combining a planner, best-of-N writer, self-critique reflector, and LLM judge grounded in computational humor theory with retrieval from a joke corpus. It reports that the elaborate pipeline only barely clears the benchmark bar.

entry.title: OrDA: Orthogonal Disentanglement of Access Habits Framework for Homepage Marketing Block Recommendations

author.name: Lingxiao Zhang, Xiaobo Li, Tao Xu

entry.summary: OrDA disentangles content-interest signals from position-driven habitual clicks in homepage marketing recommendations using orthogonal regularization and do-calculus interventions to reduce pseudo-positive bias. It aims to purify interest estimation in recommender ecosystems.

entry.title: Finding the Right Tables and Columns: A Benchmark and Corpus-Adaptive Embeddings for SQL Schema Retrieval

author.name: Qingcheng Zeng, Puxuan Yu, Aman Mehta, Fuheng Zhao, Rajhans Samdani

entry.summary: Reframes SQL text-to-query as a schema retrieval problem, recasting five datasets into table- and column-level retrieval tasks at enterprise scale and showing off-the-shelf embeddings underperform. It proposes corpus-adaptive embeddings for finding relevant tables and columns.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harnesses via Gated Semantic Quality-Diversity

author.name: Xiaotian Luo, Fengxingyu Wang, Chuanrui Hu, Dizhan Xue, Yafeng Deng

entry.summary: Proposes a self-evolving agent-harness framework that separates proposing changes (prompts, injected knowledge, runtime control) from crediting them, using a gated semantic quality-diversity approach to avoid rewarding measurement artifacts or overfitting. It targets improving agent performance without touching model weights.

entry.title: DeepStress: Stress-Testing Deep Search Agents

author.name: Ismael Rousseau, Geraldine Damnati, Frederic Bechet

entry.summary: Introduces DeepStress, a stress-testing framework that replaces search agents' retrieval modules with a controlled synthetic environment to inject poor-quality evidence varying in trustworthiness, relevance, and factuality. It reveals that agents differ substantially in robustness to unreliable evidence.

entry.title: Auditing Protocol-Level Shortcuts in Large Audio Language Model Judges for Speech Evaluation

author.name: Joonyong Park, David M. Chan, Yuki Saito, Hiroshi Saruwatari

entry.summary: Audits large audio-language model judges for speech evaluation, showing that high human agreement can mask reliance on protocol-provided text features or reference data rather than actually listening to the audio. It examines feature-blueprint, reference-conditioned, and pairwise A/B protocols across six judges and four attributes.

entry.title: Detector Confidence Signals Presence Rather Than Occlusion in Cluttered Manipulation

author.name: Yuanzhi He

entry.summary: Audits whether open-vocabulary detector confidence reflects object visibility, showing that confidence barely changes as objects are occluded and can even rise with clutter, while detectors report objects present in 99 percent of heavily occluded frames. It uses a geometry-segmentation oracle to establish that confidence signals presence rather than occlusion.

entry.title: UniPhysGen: Unified Physical Grounding for Simulation-Ready 3D Assets

author.name: Xian Li, Rong Wei, Lujie Yang, Haolin Huang, Junyuan Fang, Siliang Tang, Jun Xiao, Rui Tang, Juncheng Li

entry.summary: Presents UniPhys, a scalable framework that automatically transforms raw 3D assets into simulation-ready assets with unified physical semantics including articulation and intrinsic physical properties, plus the UniPhys-40K dataset and UniPhys-Bench benchmark. It targets embodied AI and robotic simulation needs.

entry.title: Task-Specific Feature Fusion Method for Multi-Task Affective Behavior Analysis

author.name: Jiajun Sun, Zhe Gao

entry.summary: Presents a task-adaptive feature fusion system for the ABAW11 multi-task challenge, predicting valence-arousal, expressions, and action units by combining frozen DINOv2 and DINOv3 backbones with task-specific temporal and calibration strategies. It shows related affective tasks benefit from different features.

entry.title: Attitude Estimation Using Inertial and Barometric Measurements

author.name: Melone Nyoba Tchonkeu, Soulaimane Berkane, Tarek Hamel

entry.summary: Introduces a barometer-aided attitude estimation architecture that exploits barometric altitude to provide vertical-motion information, improving tilt estimation for aerial vehicles in GNSS-denied and highly accelerated flight. It addresses the gravity-versus-inertial acceleration ambiguity of IMU-only estimation.

entry.title: EZSMT Version 3, Matured

author.name: Yuliya Lierler

entry.summary: Describes version 3 of an SMT-based constraint answer set programming framework with a more expressive input language, optimization via weak constraints, and easier integration of new constraint types. It leverages state-of-the-art SMT solvers instead of custom search.

entry.title: AI-accelerated End-to-End Framework for Rapid Professional Upskilling

author.name: Tam Nguyen, Hung Nguyen, Robert Ogburn

entry.summary: Proposes an end-to-end framework applying AI acceleration across five upskilling stages from knowledge acquisition through assessment, with a focus on production and learning efficiency. It cites external validation including approval by a US accountancy board.

entry.title: EMAGN: Efficient Multi-Attention Graph Network via Learned Clustering for Scalable Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Mingxing Xu, Rakesh Chowdary Machineni, Ke Liu, Xi Cheng, Chengqi Lu, Xin Hu, Lyuhao Chen, Xiangyu Li, Junwei You, Oliver Gao

entry.summary: Introduces a graph attention network for traffic forecasting that linearizes spatial attention using learned clustering matrices inspired by fast Gaussian filtering, cutting complexity from quadratic to near-linear. The goal is scalable spatiotemporal forecasting without giving up attention flexibility.

entry.title: Tabular Foundation Models for Discrete Choice Estimation

author.name: Liu Liu, Dan Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates whether tabular foundation models can handle discrete choice demand estimation and shows direct application underperforms because these models assume row independence while choice is set-valued with persistent consumer heterogeneity. It proposes a reformulation encoding choice-set dependence and individual heterogeneity in a row-based framework.

entry.title: ScanFocus: A Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding

author.name: Kai Chen, Ming Dai, Wenxuan Cheng, Wankou Yang

entry.summary: Presents a coarse-to-fine framework for spatio-temporal video grounding that decouples global scanning from precise boundary focus to recover high-frequency temporal cues lost by aggressive downsampling. It targets the trade-off between global context and accurate boundary localization in long videos.

entry.title: Anatomically Faithful but Temporally Blind: Auditing Attribution for Left-Ventricular Ejection-Fraction Estimation from Echocardiography

author.name: Hyunkyung Han, Min Jung Kim

entry.summary: Audits whether post-hoc attribution methods for deep echocardiography models estimating ejection fraction are faithful both spatially and temporally, since ejection fraction depends on specific end-systolic and end-diastolic frames. It fine-tunes transformer and CNN regressors and finds explanations that are anatomically faithful but temporally blind.

entry.title: Traffic-Aware Randomized Smoothing for LLM-Based Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Zhenpeng Li

entry.summary: Proposes a certified defense for LLM-based network intrusion detection that injects Gaussian noise only into the attacker-controllable feature subspace during fine-tuning and certification, aligning smoothing with feasible traffic manipulation. It shows that naive randomized smoothing on clean-trained detectors yields weak certified accuracy.

entry.title: Multimodal Assessment of Pancreatic Cancer Resectability Using Deep Learning

author.name: Vincent Ochs, Christoph Kuemmerli, Florentin Bieder, Julia Wolleb, Joel L. Lavanchy, Julia Ruppel, Jan Liechti, Stephanie Taha-Mehlitz, Christian Andreas Nebiker, Beat Mueller, Giuseppe Kito Fusai, Joerg-Matthias Pollok, Anas Taha, Philippe C. Cattin, Sebastian Staubli

entry.summary: Introduces a fully automated multimodal deep-learning framework that jointly analyzes 3D contrast-enhanced CT and structured clinical data to classify pancreatic cancer into resectability categories, using a Swin-UNETR backbone with auxiliary segmentation of anatomy. It aims to reduce the substantial variability in expert resectability assessment.

entry.title: Rethinking Penetration Testing for AI-Enabled Systems: From Resource Compromise to Behavioral Objective Violation

author.name: Mohammad Allahbakhsh, Mohammad Hassan Bahari, Moslem Attar-Raouf

entry.summary: Reframes penetration testing for AI-enabled systems from resource compromise toward objective-driven behavioral evaluation, since adversaries can alter behavior via prompts, retrieved content, sensor inputs, or memory without breaching infrastructure. It defines an AI-enabled system as one where learned models materially influence operational outcomes.

entry.title: SPyCE: Skill-Policy Co-evolution for Multimodal Agents

author.name: Ru Zhang, Weijie Qiu
