entry.summary: Proposes SPyCE, which distills multimodal reasoning trajectories into reusable skills that co-evolve with the policy during training rather than being consumed as scalar rewards or retrieved at test time. It targets image-manipulating tool-use agents that reason across many steps.

entry.title: FOLIO: Focused Semantic Memory for Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Haoyang Fan, Dhruv Parikh, Anvitha Ramachandran, Sameh Gobriel, Nilesh Jain, Rajgopal Kannan, Viktor Prasanna

entry.summary: Introduces FOLIO, a training-free focused semantic memory system for online streaming video understanding that continuously compresses the observed prefix while retaining important entities, actions, and temporal changes for queries issued at any time. It addresses unbounded memory growth and redundant visual detail retention.

entry.title: FM$^2$: Unified Federated Foundation Models for Heterogeneous Multimodal Medical Imaging

author.name: Shengchao Chen, Ting Shu

entry.summary: Proposes FM squared, a unified federated foundation model for heterogeneous multimodal medical imaging that trains the backbone from scratch to preserve medical-domain fidelity while handling imaging modality heterogeneity across clients with overlapping or disjoint modalities. It targets privacy-preserving cross-institution model building.

entry.title: Attention-Free and Lightweight Token Reduction for Efficient Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xuanyi Hao, Zuoyuan Zhang, Zhibo Wang, Xiaoyi Pang, Jiahui Hu, Jiacheng Du, Shuguo Zhuo

entry.summary: Proposes an attention-free, lightweight, plug-and-play token reduction framework for vision-language models that preserves both important and diverse tokens without relying on attention maps or costly pairwise similarity comparisons. It targets efficient VLM inference on resource-constrained edge devices.

entry.title: Calibrated Closed-Form Uncertainty for Radiative Gaussian Splatting in Sparse-View CT

author.name: Chulin Zhao, Yiran Xu, Shu Liu

entry.summary: Equips radiative Gaussian splatting for sparse-view CT with a variational density posterior whose predictive variance propagates in closed form in a single forward pass in both volume and projection space, exploiting the linearity of X-ray projection. It presents the first systematic calibration study for Gaussian-splatting CT.

entry.title: CF-Net: Conflict Fusion with Speaker Normalisation and Certainty Weighting for Ambivalence/Hesitancy Recognition

author.name: Tung Hung Bui, Hong Hai Nguyen, Van Thong Huynh

entry.summary: CF-Net is a multimodal challenge submission for detecting ambivalence and hesitancy in video, using frozen SigLIP2, HuBERT, and DistilBERT encoders with speaker normalization and a conflict-fusion module computing cross-modal incongruence. It targets subtle affective signals expressed through modality mismatch.

entry.title: Video to All-in-focus Image Reconstruction Algorithm for Automated Microscopic Urinalysis

author.name: Chinmay Nema, Hari Om Aggrawal, Dipam Goswami, Rajiv Gupta, Vinti Agarwal

entry.summary: Proposes recording a video instead of multiple focal-plane images and reconstructing an all-in-focus image to automate microscopic urinalysis, simplifying acquisition for multi-layer urine samples. It aims to make deep-learning urinalysis more practical.

entry.title: Hybrid multi-objective evolutionary algorithms for service placement in the computing continuum: a comparative study with genetic traceability

author.name: Sergi Vivo, Carlos Guerrero, Isaac Lera

entry.summary: Compares hybrid island-model multi-objective evolutionary algorithms for service placement in edge-fog-cloud computing continua, running two experimental campaigns with genetic traceability of co-evolving islands. It analyzes heterogeneous hybridization for this specific optimization domain.

entry.title: S-CARD-CMSA: A Score-Aware Candidate Archive with Density-Filtered Reporting for Multimodal Optimization

author.name: Dikshit Chauhan

entry.summary: S-CARD-CMSA extends a repelling-subpopulation covariance-matrix self-adaptation strategy with a passive score-aware candidate archive and density-filtered reporting for multimodal optimization, without modifying core search dynamics. It targets the IEEE CEC 2026 niching competition.

entry.title: Wasserstein gradient flows for Coulomb discrepancies

author.name: Antonin Chodron de Courcel, Matthew Rosenzweig

entry.summary: A theoretical study of the long-time behavior of Wasserstein gradient flows minimizing a squared Maximum Mean Discrepancy with a Coulomb-potential kernel. It proves existence of global weak solutions, ultracontractive bounds, and exponential decay toward uniform targets on the torus.

entry.title: Why I Left Google DeepMind

author.name: TurnTrout

entry.summary: A personal essay by a well-known alignment researcher explaining his departure from Google DeepMind, citing objections to Google Cloud contracts tied to immigration enforcement. It is a values-driven resignation account rather than technical research.

entry.title: How Brussels can avoid becoming a digital vassal to US Big Tech

author.name: clening

entry.summary: A governance essay using a June export-control episode, in which US authorities restricted foreign access to frontier Anthropic and reportedly OpenAI models, to argue Europe is exposed to US control over frontier AI. It contends Europe's regulatory toolkit cannot fix this dependency and explores strategic responses.

entry.title: Adapting Generalist Vehicle Models for High-Speed MPC Across Terrains

author.name: Rwik Rana, Jesse Quattrociocchi, Christian Ellis, Nathan Tsoi, Garrett Warnell, Joydeep Biswas

entry.summary: Presents a recipe for specializing generalist forward kinodynamic prediction models to a target vehicle for high-speed off-road control while preserving cross-terrain generalization, using a history-conditioned adaptation. It addresses overfitting to specific terrains during specialization.

entry.title: Minimax Theory of Likelihood-Based Deep Learning for Speckle Regression

author.name: Soham Jana

entry.summary: A statistical treatment of deep learning for speckle denoising, deriving minimax estimation rates for likelihood-based neural estimators under multiplicative noise where the standard least-squares assumption breaks down. It provides theoretical grounding for methods used in radar and medical imaging.

entry.title: Proposal: The Glasswing Standard

author.name: Eigenbraid

entry.summary: A policy proposal building on Anthropic's Project Glasswing to create a standardized early-access group, spanning labs and government, for evaluating new frontier models before release. It argues staged transparency can build track records and catch capability spikes such as cybersecurity uplift ahead of time.

entry.title: When is the combined load identifiable from a stress-intensity profile? A coupled forward-inverse study on SIFBench finite-element data

author.name: Giansalvo Cirrincione, Filippo Grassia

entry.summary: Studies the inverse problem of recovering relative tension, bending, and bearing loads from a crack's stress-intensity profile using public finite-element data, focusing rigorously on when the combined load is identifiable at all. It provides an estimator with calibrated uncertainty precisely in non-identifiable regimes.

entry.title: Analyzing Curricular Pattern Complexity Using AI to Improve On-Time Graduation Rates

author.name: Lynn Vonderhaar, Juan Couder, Siri Siqveland, Omar Ochoa, James Pembridge

entry.summary: Uses AI techniques to analyze and revise curricular patterns in a software engineering degree, identifying long prerequisite sequences whose failures jeopardize on-time graduation. It reduces the labor and time needed to revise curricula.

entry.title: AI in Cyberpsychology: A systematic literature review of Cybersecurity enhancement by using AI for analyzing psychology of Victims, Attackers, and Defenders

author.name: Georg Thamer Francis, Malek Malkawi, Sevim Ey\"upo\u{g}lu, Reda Alhajj, Selim Akyoku\c{s}

entry.summary: A PRISMA-based systematic review of AI applications in cyberpsychology, analyzing 34 studies that use AI to decode personality traits and behavioral patterns of victims, attackers, and defenders. It presents a taxonomy of AI-cyberpsychology applications.

entry.title: Active Beyond-Diagonal RIS Empowered Heterogeneous Edge Computing: A Distributional Reinforcement Learning Approach

author.name: Tianyu Pang, Hongyu Li

entry.summary: Studies energy-aware offloading and resource allocation for active beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface-assisted heterogeneous mobile edge computing, accounting for cross-sector energy leakage from reciprocal devices. It uses a distributional reinforcement learning approach to jointly optimize offloading, computation, power, and surface configuration.

entry.title: Efficient Text-to-Audio Generation via Pruning

author.name: Arshdeep Singh, Yi Yuan, Yun Chen, Wenwu Wang, Mark D. Plumbley

entry.summary: Applies filter pruning with lightweight finetuning to the U-Net backbone of a diffusion text-to-audio model, removing up to 83 percent of parameters and 39 percent of compute while recovering quality. It targets the deployment cost of diffusion-based audio generation.

entry.title: Is the Statistical Advantage Worth the Cost? An Empirical Comparison of KANs and MLPs for Structured Data Classification

author.name: Matthew Steven P. Toledo, Justine Raphael H. Jacinto, Vivekjeet Singh Chambal, Rodolfo C. Camaclang III, Jamlech Iram N. Gojo Cruz, Reginald Neil C. Recario

entry.summary: Benchmarks Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks against MLPs on twelve tabular classification datasets under standardized settings, reporting that KANs statistically outperform MLPs in binary and multiclass tasks with rigorous paired testing. It weighs the statistical advantage against KAN computational cost.

entry.title: Can We Steer the Black-Box? Towards Controllability-Centric Evaluation of Recommender Systems with Collaborative Agents

author.name: Jiwen Zhou, Xiang Liu, Mingming Li, Pengbo Mo, Jiao Dai, Honglei Lv, Jizhong Han, Songlin Hu

entry.summary: Introduces a collaborative multi-agent framework to evaluate the controllability of recommender systems, formalizing target content discovery, interest profile shaping, and popularity bias mitigation as steerability tasks. It fills a gap where existing evaluation ignores whether users can steer black-box recommenders.

entry.title: Symbiosis-Inspired Knowledge Distillation for Incremental Object Detection

author.name: Mingyue Zeng, De Cheng, Zhipeng Xu, Huaijie Wang, Nannan Wang, Xinbo Gao

entry.summary: Proposes a knowledge-distillation method for incremental object detection that leverages object co-occurrence and occlusion (symbiosis) via shared representations rather than separating feature spaces. It aims to reduce catastrophic forgetting caused by ignoring spatial and semantic dependencies.

entry.title: Beyond Color Geometry: Evaluating Human-Like Color Representations in Vision Models

author.name: Ayan Igali, Pakizar Shamoi

entry.summary: Evaluates whether vision models organize colors like humans by comparing their representations against a fuzzy perceptual model with 86 graded categories fitted to human survey data, rather than geometric color spaces or discrete labels. Across eleven Vision Transformer encoders, category-level results are similar while graded alignment differs.

entry.title: Music-to-Dance Generation via Atomic Movements

author.name: Xinhao Cai, Yixuan Sun, Minghang Zheng, Qingchao Chen, Xin Jin, Song-chun Zhu, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a structure-aware music-to-dance framework that models choreography as sequences of interpretable atomic movements, built by segmenting and clustering dance data into an atomic-movement vocabulary and labeling it with an LLM. It aims to fix the structural incoherence and poor controllability of models that treat motion as a continuous signal.

entry.title: Clustering algorithms for multivariate wind farm SCADA data filtering

author.name: Nicol\`o Italiano, Vasilis Pettas, Tuhfe G\"o\c{c}men, Nicolaos A. Cutululis

entry.summary: This paper compares clustering algorithms for automatically filtering multivariate wind farm SCADA data to isolate normal-operation measurements, introducing evaluation metrics suitable for unlabeled data. It aims to replace manual expert inspection.

entry.title: DeltaMerge-LowRes: Composing Language and Task Deltas for Low-Resource Adaptation

author.name: Son Ha Xuan, Xuan-Bach Le, Phat T. Tran-Truong

entry.summary: Presents DeltaMerge-LowRes, which learns a language delta from unlabeled text and a task delta from labeled English data separately, then composes them in weight space using rules including a novel cross-axis TIES merging. It enables low-resource adaptation to a new language and task without joint fine-tuning.

entry.title: Where Does the Noise Come From? A Variance-Components Decomposition of Non-Determinism in LLM Brand Answers

author.name: Dmitrij \.Zatuchin

entry.summary: Applies a crossed random-effects generalizability-theory decomposition to partition variance in LLM brand-recommendation outputs into within-prompt resampling, prompt paraphrase, model identity, and query language. It provides a decision-study allocation for how many repeats, paraphrases, models, and languages to sample for reliable measurement.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Visual Representation Learning: Pretrain-Finetuning or Joint Training?

author.name: Nusrat Munia, Tyler Ward, Nishat Nayla, Matthew A. Massey, Abdullah-Al-Zubaer Imran

entry.summary: Systematically compares two self-supervised learning paradigms: the standard pretrain-then-finetune pipeline versus jointly optimizing self-supervised and supervised objectives during training. It investigates when joint training offers a better alternative for learning visual representations.

entry.title: Just-In-Time Scene Graph Growth: Combating Perceptual Saturation in Long-Horizon Robotics

author.name: Yue Chang, Rufeng Chen, Yifan Tian, Dazhi Huang, Zhaofan Zhang, Yi Chen, Wenze Zhang, Li Chen, Hui Xiong, Sihong Xie

entry.summary: Presents JITOMA, a closed-loop framework that grows 3D scene graphs just-in-time using a top-down task heatmap to filter observations and activate dormant anchors on demand. It combats perceptual saturation from redundant observations for real-time, low-latency long-horizon robotics on edge platforms.

entry.title: DiffGI: Differentiable Geometry Images for High-Fidelity Thin-Shell 3D Generation

author.name: Eungjune Shim, Hansol Lee, Eunjung Ju

entry.summary: Proposes DiffGI, an end-to-end differentiable geometry-image framework for generating thin-shell and non-manifold 3D geometries like garments, replacing discrete binary occupancy maps that cause staircase artifacts with a differentiable surface representation. It integrates surface reconstruction into the learning pipeline.

entry.title: RoughNet: Mapping Arctic Sea Ice Roughness Using Diffusion-Based Super-Resolution of Satellite Imagery

author.name: Tessa Cannon, Michel Tsamados, Petru Manescu, Thomas Newman, Christian Haas, Veit Helm, Weibin Chen, Randall Scharien

entry.summary: Introduces RoughNet, a conditional diffusion super-resolution model that reconstructs 1 m sea-ice surface elevation residuals from 10 m Sentinel-2 imagery, trained on airborne LiDAR from two Arctic regions and evaluated on an unseen third. It enables scalable fine-scale sea-ice roughness mapping for climate modeling and safe over-ice travel.

entry.title: MultiAnimate: A Unified Framework for Controllable Multi-Character Animation

author.name: Zhongyi Zhang, Guangyuan Wang, Li Hu, Wenbo Zhou, Peng Zhang, Tianyi Wei, Weiming Zhang, Bang Zhang, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: Introduces MultiAnimate, a framework for concurrently animating multiple characters within a shared environment while preserving identity consistency and spatial relationships, using an identity-specific reference net among other mechanisms. It extends character animation beyond the common single-reference-image setting.

entry.title: GPOcc++: Unified Sparse Gaussian Occupancy Prediction with Visual Geometry Priors

author.name: Changqing Zhou, Yueru Luo, Yulan Guo, Bing Wang, Jie Qin, Changhao Chen

entry.summary: Introduces GPOcc++, which transforms surface-centric visual geometry priors into occupancy-aware sparse Gaussian representations to reason about volumetric interiors and free space for 3D occupancy prediction. It targets embodied intelligence and autonomous driving where occluded and unobserved regions are challenging.

entry.title: DP-BOA: Dirichlet-Process Birth-or-Assign for On-the-Fly Category Discovery

author.name: Peiyan Gu, Zixin Teng, Xuming He

entry.summary: Proposes DP-BOA, a posterior-predictive decision framework for on-the-fly category discovery that uses an online Dirichlet-process Gaussian mixture with a Normal-Inverse-Wishart prior to explicitly weigh assigning a sample to an existing category versus spawning a new one. It replaces implicit matching-based birth heuristics with statistical evidence.

entry.title: VGIF-Score: Interpretable and Diagnostic Evaluation of Spatio-Temporal Instruction Following in Video Generation

author.name: Songyu Xu, Xin Wang, Qiang Chen, Xinran Wang, Muxi Diao, Yuxuan Zhang, Kongming Liang, Rui Lin, Zhanyu Ma

entry.summary: Proposes VGIF-Score, an automated interpretable framework for evaluating spatio-temporal instruction following in video generation, addressing shallow prompts and costly human evaluation in existing protocols. It provides diagnostic insight into which instruction constraints succeed or fail.

entry.title: From Surface Forecasting to Observability Forecasting: A Latent World Model for Cloud-Aware EO Monitoring

author.name: Mohanad Albughdadi

entry.summary: Reframes Earth observation from surface forecasting to observability forecasting, predicting whether the next satellite acquisition will be usable given cloud cover and when a usable view will return, by adapting a joint-embedding predictive world model to cloud-aware EO sequences on EarthNet2021. It targets the real bottleneck of surface visibility rather than imagery arrival.

entry.title: Occam’s razor is about using the past to predict the future

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: A philosophical post reframing Occam's razor as fundamentally about using past data to predict future observations, using a worked example about predicting solar angles from latitude. It argues that ignoring simplicity leads to overfit hypotheses that fail to generalize.

entry.title: Audited Selective Verification for Risk-Controlled N-1 Thermal Contingency Screening under Deployment Shift

author.name: Jayakumar Manoharan

entry.summary: Proposes a risk-budgeted verification layer for real-time N-1 contingency screening in power grids, using a cheap surrogate to skip outage checks while an online audit runs full power flow on a random sample to certify a statistical bound on thermal violations. It targets the gap between slow full verification and fast but unguaranteed linear screening, especially when learned controllers push systems into unfamiliar regimes.

entry.title: Greedy Volume Maximization of Gradient Embeddings for Long-Tailed Frame-Level Bioacoustic Active Learning

author.name: Shiqi Zhang, Marius Fai{\ss}, Ariana Strandburg-Peshkin, Tuomas Virtanen

entry.summary: Proposes a deterministic batch selector for frame-level bioacoustic active learning that greedily adds segments maximizing the volume spanned by BADGE gradient embeddings, exploiting submodularity for a near-optimal guarantee. It targets extremely sparse, long-tailed call-type annotation under tight budgets.

entry.title: GHR-VLM: Making Zero-Shot Transit Video Analytics Realizable with Grounded Hybrid Reasoning

author.name: Kaicong Huang, Weiheng Oh, Ruimin Ke

entry.summary: Proposes an edge-cloud hybrid reasoning framework for zero-shot transit-bus video analytics that uses explicit visual grounding to compress long surveillance streams into compact passenger-centered evidence before VLM reasoning. It aims to make VLM-based transit analytics reliable and affordable without task-specific annotation.

entry.title: NodeImport: Imbalanced Node Classification with Node Importance Assessment

author.name: Nan Chen, Zemin Liu, Bryan Hooi, Bingsheng He, Jun Hu, Jia Chen

entry.summary: Proposes an approach to class-imbalanced node classification that uses a balanced meta-set to measure node importance, treating a training node as significant if it improves model performance under an unbiased setting. It aims to overcome majority-class overfitting where reweighting or synthesis fall short.

entry.title: The Warring States Period: Frontier Labs Edition

author.name: ykevinzhang

entry.summary: An industry-analysis post arguing the frontier-model market has shifted from a perceived Anthropic-OpenAI duopoly into a fluid oligopoly of five-plus credible US players, pressuring margins. It presents an investor decision framework and notes leadership stays contestable absent a decisive recursive self-improvement breakthrough.

entry.title: Earthquaker-AI: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework with Rubric-Based Assessment for Primary School Earthquake Education

author.name: Xanthi Kokkinou, Chaido Mizeli, Nafsika Koulaxidou, Marina Delianidi, Konstantinos Diamantaras

entry.summary: Presents Earthquaker-AI, a hybrid educational framework pairing a Lego-based robotics earthquake simulation with a retrieval-augmented conversational assistant and rubric-based assessment for primary-school earthquake preparedness. It extends an existing STEM project toward metacognitive learning.

entry.title: Autonomous UAV Route Planning for Coverage Maximization in Environmental Monitoring: A Systematic Literature Review

author.name: Sebastian Jouannet-Contreras, Carola Figueroa-Flores

entry.summary: Reports the protocol and preliminary results of a PRISMA-based systematic review of autonomous UAV route planning for coverage-oriented environmental monitoring. It focuses on algorithmic families, coverage and energy metrics, obstacle handling, and environment representations.

entry.title: Discourse-Aware Policy Analysis with Argumentation: A Hybrid LLM-Symbolic Framework for Disaster Governance

author.name: Stylianos Loukas Vasileiou, Olga Derendiaeva

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid LLM-plus-symbolic pipeline that turns critical discourse analysis of policy documents into a quantitative bipolar argumentation framework, capturing frame-mediated tensions that pure summarization hides. It aims to give domain experts inspectable, contestable structure for disaster governance texts.

entry.title: Adversarial Prompting Framework for AI Safety Assessment

author.name: Yash Bhatnagar, Kunal Banerjee, Anirban Chatterjee

entry.summary: Implements an adversarial prompting framework that systematically generates structured adversarial prompts at escalating sophistication levels, from direct harmful requests to encoding-based attacks, to assess AI model resilience. It presents this as a practical safety-assessment tool.

entry.title: Cover First, Disagree Softly: Rethinking Mismatch-First Active Learning for Frame-Level Audio Classification

author.name: Shiqi Zhang, Tuomas Virtanen

entry.summary: Rethinks a popular mismatch-first active-learning acquisition strategy for frame-level audio classification, showing that its hard sequential selection ignores similarity among chosen segments and fails at low budgets. It proposes a coverage-first, soft-disagreement alternative.

entry.title: IMMNet: Hybrid Fusion of Model-based and Data-driven Approaches for Maneuvering Target Tracking

author.name: Yixuan Zhao, Chaoqun Yang, Lin Gao, Yongxiao Tian, Ting Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid model-and-data-driven algorithm that embeds learnable neural components inside the interacting multiple model framework for 3D maneuvering target tracking, preserving Bayesian inference while adaptively learning motion and noise patterns. It aims for interpretable, real-time radar tracking that beats black-box methods.

entry.title: From Prediction to Collaboration: Interactive Symbolic Music Analysis

author.name: Emmanouil Karystinaios, Johannes Hentschel, Markus Neuwirth, Gerhard Widmer

entry.summary: Presents a unified symbolic Roman-numeral music analysis system that supports not just full-score prediction but interactive operations like constrained completion, local correction, and iterative refinement. It bridges the gap between strong benchmark models and tools usable in real analytical workflows.

entry.title: From Language to Navigation Goals: A Vision-Language Approach for Semantic Navigation of Mobile Robots Using RGB-D Perception

author.name: Jose Mart\'inez-Fajardo, Pablo Pueyo, Fernando Caballero, Luis Merino

entry.summary: Presents a modular ROS 2 navigation framework that translates natural-language requests into executable navigation goals for mobile robots using RGB-D perception and vision-language understanding. It enables non-expert users to direct robots to targets via language.

entry.title: Social Simulations: from Agent-Based Modeling to Digital Twins

author.name: Erica Cau, Andrea Failla, Valentina Pansanella, Giulio Rossetti

entry.summary: A book chapter tracing the evolution of social simulation from rule-based agent-based models to LLM-enhanced simulations and finally data-driven social digital twins. It reviews methodological foundations, applications, advantages, and limitations across these paradigms.

entry.title: GSM-Plus-BN: A Perturbation-Based Benchmark for Bangla Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Bidyarthi Paul, Nahida Jannat Mayouree, Md. Asif Karim, Sagar Chandra Nath, Swastika Kundu

entry.summary: Introduces GSM-Plus-BN, a perturbation-based Bengali benchmark for evaluating LLM mathematical reasoning robustness beyond pattern recognition in a very high-population but low-resource language. It fills a gap in equitable multilingual reasoning evaluation.

entry.title: MyAG: A Graph-Based Framework for Designing and Analyzing Composable LLM Agent Systems

author.name: Zhisong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces MyAG, a graph-based framework that separates LLM agent system design into component, workflow, and search graphs to enable flexible reuse of components with different strategies. It supports hierarchical composition, monitoring, and visualization of agent execution.

entry.title: Reflecting Process Expertise in Procedural Material Generation

author.name: Kunal Gupta, Gaurav Joshi, Yen-Ru Chen, Seemandhar Jain, Ishit Mehta, Manmohan Chandraker

entry.summary: Formulates procedural material generation as retrieval-time process reasoning over expert demonstrations, representing workflows as textual process traces of construction steps, parameters, and design intent rather than only node graphs. It uses pretrained LLM-based synthesizers to align generated traces with user intent.

entry.title: Marker-free deformable registration and fusion for augmented reality-guided positive margin localization during tumor resection surgery

author.name: Yue Yang, Annie Benson, Matthieu Chabanas, Jason Slagle, Thomas Myles, Matthew B. Weinger, Jon S. Heiselman, Michael I. Miga, Michael Topf, Jie Ying Wu

entry.summary: Presents a marker-free augmented reality workflow that maps positive-margin pathology findings from a deformed resected specimen onto the patient resection bed during head and neck cancer surgery. It combines contour-constrained deformation, residual depth alignment, and surface-based fusion to a head-mounted display.

entry.title: TreeSRNF: Square-Root Normal Fields for Generative Modelling of the Geometric and Structural Variability in Tree-like 3D Objects

author.name: Tahmina Khanam, Hamid Laga, Mohammed Bennamoun, Guanjin Wang, Ferdous Sohel, Farid Boussaid, Anuj Srivastava

entry.summary: Generalizes the Square-Root Normal Fields representation to tree-shaped 3D objects, modeling both branch geometry and branching interconnection as points on a novel Riemannian tree-shape space for statistical analysis and generation. It targets botanical trees and plants that vary in geometry and structure.

entry.title: TRACE-PCa: Predicting Prostate Cancer Progression from Longitudinal MRI During Active Surveillance

author.name: Hongye Zeng, Shreeram Athreya, Dingyuan Dai, Steve Raman, Leonard Marks, William Speier, Corey Arnold

entry.summary: Proposes TRACE-PCa, an end-to-end temporal multimodal model that predicts prostate cancer pathological progression from longitudinal MRI during active surveillance without requiring lesion segmentation, using a 3D MRI foundation model encoder and a temporal attention gate. It aims to reduce unnecessary repeat biopsies.

entry.title: ThinkBLOX: 3D Indoor Scene Generation with Progressive Reasoning

author.name: Yuan Xiao, Can Wang, Xiangyu Kong, Jing Liao

entry.summary: Proposes ThinkBLOX, a VLM-based progressive reasoning framework that iteratively designs and refines 3D indoor scenes as a state-conditioned step-by-step reasoning-and-action process, contrasting with one-shot layout planning. It supports interactive editing without global re-optimization.

entry.title: Probabilistic Extension of Neuro-Symbolic AGI Robots based on Belnap's Typed Intensional FOL

author.name: Zoran Majkic

entry.summary: Extends a neuro-symbolic logic framework based on Belnap-style typed intensional first-order logic with probabilistic reasoning over unknown sentences. It introduces symmetry transformations intended to support self-reference and real-time decisions in AGI robots.

entry.title: CAS I: A Geometric Coding Theorem

author.name: Romie Banerjee

entry.summary: Establishes an analogue of the classical coding theorem for symmetry groups, defining a symmetry prior as the probability that a random group symmetry fixes a given string and proving it is a universal lower semi-computable semi-measure for certain groups. It develops a Galois connection between subgroups and string subsets.

entry.title: Multi-Expert Routing for Multi-Domain Low-Resource OCR: A Manchu Case Study

author.name: Zhan Chen, Jiqiao Ma, Chih-wen Kuo

entry.summary: Studies a multi-expert OCR system for low-resource historical Manchu that reuses fine-tuning checkpoints as style specialists and routes pages by visual style using a lightweight classifier. The routed system nearly matches the best specialist per style across regular, memorial, and running-script test sets.

entry.title: Quantum Topological Data Encoding

author.name: Adam Weso{\l}owski, Dimitrios Thanos, Daniel Leykam, Lirand\"e Pira

entry.summary: Introduces quantum topological data encoding (QTDE), a framework for embedding geometric and topological structure of classical data into quantum states via topology-driven evolution, generalized to higher-dimensional data. It is tested on clique-complex classification tasks.

entry.title: When Rubrics Change: Cross-Rubric Generalization for Critical Thinking Essay Scoring

author.name: Nischal Ashok Kumar, Payu Wittawatolarn, Sana Kang, Marisa C. Peczuh, Blair Lehman, Ryan Baker, Caitlin Mills, Sherry Lachman, Ruochen Sun, Andrew Lan

entry.summary: Studies cross-rubric generalization in automated essay scoring, where models trained under one rubric must score essays under previously unseen rubrics targeting different aspects. It uses rubric-agnostic trait representations with target-essay supervision in an LLM fine-tuning framework.

entry.title: Self-supervised Speech Comparison for L2 Phone, Rhythm, and Intonation Scoring

author.name: Stephen McIntosh, Reuben Smit, Daisuke Saito, Nobuaki Minematsu, Herman Kamper

entry.summary: Explores whether dynamic time warping over self-supervised WavLM representations can score second-language phonetic accuracy, rhythm, and intonation without labeled L2 data. It reports that a basic DTW approach exceeds human agreement on phonetic scoring in English and Japanese.

entry.title: Regularity as seen by Alice and Bob

author.name: Omid Yaghoubi, Miko{\l}aj Boja\'nczyk, Aliaume Lopez, Rafa{\l} Stefa\'nski

entry.summary: Proposes a unifying communication-complexity model for Nerode-style characterizations of regularity across functions with non-Boolean output domains, generalizing prior work by relaxing computability assumptions. It shows coincidence with known computation models for several domains and conjectures broader correspondence.

entry.title: Improving Medical Image Generative Models with Fr\'echet Distance Loss

author.name: Andrew Marshall, Xuanang Xu, Xiaoran Zhang, Rui Wang, Lawrence Staib, James Duncan

entry.summary: Proposes finetuning medical diffusion generative models with a Fréchet Distance loss that aligns first- and second-order feature statistics of real and generated images to better capture irregular, high-variance tumor morphology. It improves synthetic image utility for downstream segmentation.

entry.title: WAVE-Stereo: Warp-Aligned Volume Encoding for Stereo Matching

author.name: Zehan Liu, Yage He, Xianwu Gong

entry.summary: Proposes WAVE-Stereo for iterative stereo matching, unifying correlation-volume matching search and warped-feature residual refinement, which prior methods modeled separately, via a GeoWarp Correspondence Encoder plus periodic global context propagation for textureless regions. It is evaluated across five real-world benchmarks.

entry.title: Privacy Preserving Recommender Systems Balancing Personalization with Privacy

author.name: Ranjeet K Jha, Venkata Suresh Gummadilli

entry.summary: Proposes a privacy-preserving recommendation framework combining federated learning, differential privacy, cohort-level modeling, and privacy-aware agents to keep raw user data decentralized while adding bounded noise to model updates. It targets regulatory compliance without heavily degrading recommendation quality.

entry.title: Learning Engagement Assistant (LEA): Cross-Course Scalability and Classroom Evaluation of an Agentic AI Tutoring System

author.name: Teri Rumble, Javad Zarrin, P. George Lovell, Ruth Falconer

entry.summary: Reports the first real-classroom deployment of an adaptive AI tutoring agent combining retrieval-augmented generation with knowledge-component models, and tests cross-course scalability across three courses. Prior work had validated it only in simulation with synthetic learners.

entry.title: Barnamala: Parameter-Efficient Handwritten Devanagari Recognition at Benchmark Saturation

author.name: Ashish Thapa, Samrat Karki

entry.summary: Builds a very compact 1.11M-parameter convolutional network for 46-class handwritten Devanagari recognition, reaching 99.73 percent and matching much larger models at a shared intrinsic error floor. It argues the benchmark is effectively saturated, with no configuration achieving a statistically clear win.

entry.title: Multimodal Empirical Bayes Variational Autoencoders for Joint Longitudinal and Time-to-Event Modeling

author.name: Anders Sj\"oberg, Nils Olsson, Marcus Baaz, Mats Jirstrand

entry.summary: Extends the empirical Bayes variational autoencoder to jointly model longitudinal tumor trajectories and time-to-event dropout, using covariate-conditioned latent priors and a hazard-augmented decoder. It targets integrated pharmacometric modeling of treatment response.

entry.title: Can an Old Dog Be Taught New Tricks? Taking LLMs Beyond Sentence Level Translation

author.name: Alaina Brandt

entry.summary: Presents PAT, a retrieval-augmented system for whole-document, corpus-informed translation between US English and Latin American Spanish that passes retrieved paragraph, section, and document examples to an LLM. It aims to move machine translation beyond sentence-by-sentence processing toward discourse-aware draft translation.

entry.title: SARFA: Segment Anything with Radiomic Feature Alignment

author.name: Tyler Ward, Abdullah Imran

entry.summary: Proposes SARFA, which augments the Segment Anything Model for ambiguous medical targets by generating diverse plausible masks via probabilistic prompting and optimizing them with a radiomics-driven objective based on Fréchet Radiomic Distance. It addresses inter-observer boundary disagreement in tumor delineation.

entry.title: CASA-SDF: Curriculum-Aware Spatial Adaptation with Curvature-Guided Density for Neural Implicit Surface Reconstruction

author.name: Lei Yang, Weiqing Li, Zhiyong Su, Liang Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes CASA-SDF, a neural implicit surface reconstruction method with curriculum-aware spatial adaptation and curvature-guided density to handle geometric heterogeneity in indoor scenes. It balances strong regularization for texture-less planes against sharper representations for thin structures.

entry.title: DriveFace: A Cross-Spectral Through-Glass Face Dataset for On-the-Move Vehicular Border Control

author.name: Anjith George, Luis Luevano, Alain Komaty, Zeina Al Amine, Vidit Vidit, Sebastien Marcel

entry.summary: Introduces DriveFace, a cross-spectral through-glass face dataset for on-the-move vehicular border control, capturing realistic challenges like motion blur, variable illumination, occlusions, and cross-spectral enrollment absent in controlled benchmarks. It supports development of passive at-a-distance face recognition at checkpoints.

entry.title: Exploring Post-Training Alignment of Small Language Models for Biomedical Data-to-Text Generation: A Case Study of Medication Leaflet

author.name: Xi Yang, Guodong Liu, Chuqin Li, Fan Wu, Ergin Soysal, Min Jiang, Xing He, Jiang Bian, Yi Guo, Shams Zaman, Thomas Fuchs, Todd Sanger, Yonghui Wu

entry.summary: Compares post-training methods (SFT, DPO, ORPO, GRPO) for small Qwen-based models on generating patient-friendly narratives from medication leaflet data, evaluating with lexical and semantic metrics. It examines cross-dataset generalization using openFDA drug labels.

entry.title: Constraint-Aware Counterfactual Editing for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis

author.name: S M Rafiuddin, Vamsi Krishna Pavuluri, Atriya Sen

entry.summary: Proposes CAVE-ABSA, a constraint-aware framework for generating and validating aspect-level counterfactuals that flip one target aspect's sentiment while preserving other aspects, meaning, fluency, and factual consistency. It addresses the shortcomings of sentence-level label-flipping counterfactuals.

entry.title: AffectFlow-DINO: Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Task Affect Estimation via Conditional Rectified Flow

author.name: Salah Eddine Bekhouche, Abdellah Zakaria Sellam, Fadi Dornaika, Abdenour Hadid

entry.summary: Introduces AffectFlow-DINO for the 11th ABAW challenge, extending a deterministic affect model with a conditional rectified-flow head to model ambiguity in in-the-wild facial behavior and enable uncertainty-aware one-to-many predictions. It jointly estimates valence-arousal, eight expressions, and twelve action units on a frozen DINOv3 backbone.

entry.title: AnomExpert: Identifying and Selecting Anatomical Planes for Prenatal Ultrasound Anomaly Diagnosis

author.name: Jian Wang, Yang Yang, Ziheng Pan, Xiliang Zhu, Yuhan Zhang, Yanfeng Zhou, Dong Ni

entry.summary: Proposes AnomExpert, a prototype-driven framework for prenatal ultrasound anomaly diagnosis that uses only case-level supervision, learning plane prototypes to organize unordered images into latent anatomical planes and select diagnostically relevant ones. It avoids requiring plane-level annotations.

entry.title: CLIP-Guided Label-Free Discriminative Region Scoring for Fine-Grained Classification

author.name: Yujie Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a unified CLIP-guided, label-free region scoring framework for fine-grained classification that evaluates cosine-, margin-, and entropy-based scoring across SAM masks and random crops. It studies how local regions and scoring strategies affect discriminative evidence selection without ground-truth labels.

entry.title: M2P-AD: Memory-to-Prototype Learning with Boundary-aware Score Refinement for 3D Anomaly Detection

author.name: Seyoung Jeong, Jong Pil Yun, Sang Jun Lee

entry.summary: Proposes M2P-AD for 3D anomaly detection, introducing a memory-to-prototype module that learns representative prototypes from normal features and boundary-aware score refinement to suppress false positives in normal regions and near object boundaries. It addresses persistent excessive anomaly responses.

entry.title: AI-Augmented Human Resource Management? Insights from German companies

author.name: Yannick Kalff, Katharina Simbeck

entry.summary: A mixed-methods study of AI adoption in human resource management across German companies, drawing on interviews, group discussions, and a survey of 410 respondents. It finds that although AI enhances HR analytics, adoption mainly serves efficiency and rationalization rather than genuine augmentation, shaped by infrastructure, co-determination, and ethics.

entry.title: Cost-Pragmatic Quality Gating and Selection-Fusion Multi-Model Combiners for BioASQ Phases A+ and B

author.name: Dima Galat, Marian-Andrei Rizoiu

entry.summary: Describes a BioASQ biomedical QA system centering on cost-aware selective re-retrieval when first-stage retrieval is weak and multi-model answer fusion. It combines hybrid dense-plus-lexical retrieval with an agent-driven multi-source pipeline and a cross-encoder quality gate.

entry.title: C-Norm: Cell-Distribution Normalization Enables Precision Recognition of Medical-Cell Image

author.name: Yang Qianl, Liu Xiany, Dai Daw, Chen Jing, Shen Xiaoj, Fu Kaiw, Tang Ming, Zou Dongl

entry.summary: Proposes C-Norm, a cell-distribution normalization method for cervical cytology (ThinPrep) images that decouples abnormal and normal cells and re-synthesizes them to enforce uniform population distribution. It addresses unbalanced cell distribution and scarce annotated data that degrade detection in real clinical conditions.

entry.title: MGFace: Mask-Gated Face Matching via Conditional Similarity Routing

author.name: Huy Che, Hoang-Minh Trinh, Dinh-Duy Phan, Duc-Lung Vu

entry.summary: Proposes MGFace, a mask-gated face identification pipeline that predicts a query's mask status and conditionally routes similarity computation, using global embedding matching for unmasked faces and mask-aware matching for masked ones. It improves robustness to facial-mask occlusion while limiting expensive fine-grained matching.

entry.title: Bring Music The Horizon: Music-Driven 360$^\circ$ Video Generation

author.name: Kai Hsu Tsai, Yong Wei Fu, Hung I Yang, Yu-Chih Chen

entry.summary: Proposes an emotion-aware pipeline for music-driven 360-degree video generation that estimates a song's valence-arousal trajectory per four bars and converts it into emotion-aware visual guidance for immersive generation. It aims to convey emotional dynamics beyond lyric-dependent or flat music visualizations.

entry.title: CayleyR: Solving the TopSpin puzzle via cycle intersection

author.name: Yuri Baramykov

entry.summary: Presents an R package that solves permutation puzzles like TopSpin by detecting cycle intersections in Cayley graphs via bidirectional random search with distance-guided bridging. It combines a C++ state store with R-level orchestration.

entry.title: The Caf\'e in Amsterdam: When the Incumbent Becomes the Oracle

author.name: Augusto Camargo

entry.summary: A conceptual note that names baseline capture, the situation where an incumbent implementation's output quietly becomes the specification, making alternative implementations impossible to judge. It draws on the test-oracle problem and roofline modeling to discuss computational reformulation for modern accelerators.

entry.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Anomaly Detection in Banking Transactions: An Internal Audit Perspective

author.name: Anupa Lodhi

entry.summary: Presents an explainable anomaly-detection framework for banking transactions combining an Isolation Forest scorer with SHAP feature-attribution and a dashboard for audit teams. It aims to give compliance staff interpretable justifications rather than opaque rule-based flags.

entry.title: Improving Wind and Solar Power Prediction with Efficient Wrapper-based Feature Selection: An Empirical Study

author.name: Daniel Grillmeyer, Marius Hadry, Michael Stenger, Vanessa Borst, Veronika Lesch, Samuel Kounev

entry.summary: Reports findings from structured literature reviews on wind and solar power prediction and evaluates efficient wrapper-based feature selection for these renewable forecasting tasks. It emphasizes reliable production prediction given the environmental dependence of renewable output.

entry.title: Automatic Differentiation from Scratch: How PyTorch Computes Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Abdeladhim Tahimi

entry.summary: An expository paper tracing, with explicit numerical values, how PyTorch automatic differentiation computes gradients in physics-informed neural networks, which require two levels of differentiation through the network and through the loss. It walks through the full forward and reverse-mode pipeline on a small MLP example.

author.name: Andrea Maria Braghin, Nicol\`o Botteghi, Matteo Tomasetto, Andrea Manzoni, Gabriele Cazzulani

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.13568v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a language model estimate its familiarity with an entity before generating an answer? We study activations at the final prompt token in twelve in...

author.name: Jaros{\l}aw A. Miszczak

entry.title: The 2nd International StepUP Competition for Biometric Footstep Recognition: From Steps to Strides

author.name: Robyn Larracy, Anant Gupta, Gourav Gupta, Ethan Eddy, Maxime Devanne, Cyril Meyer, Jin-Chern Chiou, Yueh-Shan Lee, Zong-Han Lu, Aaron Tabor, Erik Scheme

entry.summary: Reports the second StepUP competition for pressure-based footstep biometrics using a large dataset of over 200,000 footsteps from 150 people, targeting generalization to new users, robustness to footwear and speed shifts, and left-right footstep fusion. It advances standardized evaluation for gait-based identification.

entry.title: High-Order Question Generation in a Multilingual Educational Context

author.name: Suna-\c{S}eyma U\c{c}ar, Itziar Aldabe, Nora Aranberri, Orph\'ee De Clercq

entry.summary: Investigates LLM generation of high-order questions in a multilingual educational setting using Claim-Evidence-Reasoning and Divergent Questioning frameworks beyond the standard Bloom's Taxonomy, across Basque, Spanish, and English. It aims to help educators craft critical-thinking questions.

entry.title: 2D Rotary Position Embedding for Scene Text Recognition with Transformers

author.name: Zobeir Raisi

entry.summary: Introduces 2D-RoPE-STR, adapting axial 2D rotary position embeddings for encoder-decoder scene text recognition, extending rotation to cross-attention so the decoder can relate queries to the encoder's 2D layout under anisotropic text crops. It addresses limitations of 1D positional encodings and square-image assumptions.

entry.title: A POS Tier Is the Key to Automated Annotation for Low-Resource Language Documentation: Neural Interlinear Glossing for Irabu, a Southern Ryukyuan Language

author.name: Michinori Shimoji (Kyushu University)

entry.summary: Builds a small BiLSTM-CRF neural annotation pipeline for interlinear glossing of Irabu, an endangered Southern Ryukyuan language, under a realistic one-hour-of-annotation constraint. It finds that a part-of-speech tier is key to automating documentation workflows.

entry.title: The Dynamic Verifiable Multi-Agent Human Agentic Loyalty Loop (DVM-HALL) Model and the Net Human-Agent Score (NHAS) in Autonomous Commerce

author.name: Sai Srikanth Madugula, Peplluis Esteva de la Rosa, Daya Shankar

entry.summary: Introduces a model of consumer loyalty when autonomous AI agents make purchasing decisions, arguing traditional loyalty frameworks fail to account for algorithmic bounded rationality and constructed autonomy. It formalizes brand choice via a softmax-based loyalty-loop model and a net human-agent score for autonomous commerce.

entry.title: A novel unsupervised machine learning strategy to handle multimodal cardiac PET/MRI data

author.name: Brunnhilde Ponsi (Nantes Universit\'e, CHU Nantes, Nantes, France, CRCI2NA, INSERM UMR 1307, Nantes, France), Thomas Carlier (Nantes Universit\'e, CHU Nantes, Nantes, France, CRCI2NA, INSERM UMR 1307, Nantes, France), Lara Marteau (Nantes Universit\'e, CHU Nantes, Nantes, France, Cardiology Department, INSERM UMR 1307, CIC 1413, l'institut du Thorax, Nantes, France), Aur\'elien Monnet (Siemens Healthineers France, Courbevoie, France), Thomas Eug\`ene (Nantes Universit\'e, CHU Nantes, Nantes, France, CRCI2NA, INSERM UMR 1307, Nantes, France), Jean-Michel Serfaty (Nantes Universit\'e, CHU Nantes, Nantes, France, Radiology Department, l'institut du Thorax, Nantes, France), Nicolas Piriou (Nantes Universit\'e, CHU Nantes, Nantes, France, Cardiology Department, INSERM UMR 1307, CIC 1413, l'institut du Thorax, Nantes, France), Hatem Necib (Nantes Universit\'e, CHU Nantes, Nantes, France, CRCI2NA, INSERM UMR 1307, Nantes, France)

entry.summary: Proposes an unsupervised two-step clustering strategy for integrating multimodal cardiac PET/MRI data (T1, T2, LGE, FDG-PET) across 99 patients with arrhythmogenic left ventricular cardiomyopathy. It aims to identify disease phenotypes where gold-standard diagnostic criteria are lacking.

entry.title: A Masked Autoencoder Approach to Unsupervised Steel Surface Defect Recognition

author.name: Shrey Patel

entry.summary: Applies a Transformer-based masked autoencoder to learn unsupervised representations of steel surface defects, masking 75 percent of patches and reconstructing from the rest, with an auxiliary localization objective as training signal. It targets defect grouping where labeled data is scarce but unlabeled images abundant.

entry.title: Audio-Text Cross-Attention with Psycholinguistic Support Features for Ambivalence/Hesitancy Recognition

author.name: Luiz F. B. F. Martins, Rodrigo W. Pisaia, Matheus M. Girardi, Isabella Berkembrock, Jo\~ao A. Almeida, Andr\'e G. Hochuli, Rayson Laroca, Alceu S. Britto Jr

entry.summary: Presents an audio-text system for the ABAW ambivalence/hesitancy recognition challenge that excludes visual frames and represents videos as overlapping windows combining prosodic, RoBERTa emotion, and handcrafted uncertainty features fused via temporal cross-attention and gated multiple-instance learning. It ensembles five models.

entry.title: Watch a chess transformer think

author.name: dl

entry.summary: A short announcement of an interactive companion app visualizing the internals of a chess transformer that mimics human play, including attention heads and the residual stream. It is a demonstration tool rather than a research writeup.

entry.title: Live Gurbani Tracking: A Benchmark and Reference System for Captioning Sikh Kirtan

author.name: Karanbir Singh

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark and reference system for live captioning of sung Sikh Kirtan as a closed-vocabulary task requiring exact scripture line matching, organized along live/offline and blind/oracle axes. It releases a hand-annotated benchmark to support religiously appropriate captioning.

entry.title: Monthly Roundup #44: July 2026

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A monthly roundup blog collecting news, advice, and commentary across AI-adjacent and general topics. It is aggregated opinion and links rather than original research.

entry.title: Why I want AI to be able to do everything I can do

author.name: Jonas Strabel

entry.summary: A personal, argument-structured essay reasoning that one should work toward the point where AI can do all economically valuable work, after which the author could pursue curiosity guilt-free. It formalizes counterfactual value premises to justify this stance.

entry.title: Recap of bike trip/street interviews across America

author.name: cguth7

entry.summary: A personal recap of a cross-country bike trip with street interviews gauging public awareness of AI progress, concluding that most people outside tech circles have little understanding of current model capabilities. It reflects on persuasion, social media, and the effective-altruism movement.

entry.title: The end of human evolution. Why AI will outpace us.

author.name: Ouden

entry.summary: A speculative essay contrasting slow human biological evolution with rapid cultural and technological progress, arguing AI will outpace human capabilities. It offers a broad narrative rather than specific technical analysis.

entry.title: Have You Ever Thought About Wisdom Crystals?

author.name: Jonas Hallgren

entry.summary: A whimsical, dialogue-framed follow-up post attempting to combine an idiosyncratic crystallization metaphor with ideas about wisdom and interpretability. The author acknowledges the piece is speculative and not fully worked out.

entry.title: Woke nonsense in competitive debate.

author.name: tpotthinker

entry.summary: A personal critique of argumentation styles observed at a Lincoln-Douglas debate camp, focusing on critical-theory-based arguments the author finds disconnected from reality. It is a cultural opinion piece with no AI or research content.

entry.title: FastCentNN: Accelerating Centroid Neural Network with Entropy Proxy

author.name: Le-Anh Tran

entry.title: When T2I Synthetic Data Backfires: Amplified Privacy Risks in Real-Synthetic Mix Training

author.name: Na Li, Boyu Kuang, Hongsheng Hu, Liquan Chen, Hyoungshick Kim, Yansong Gao, Anmin Fu

entry.title: Research Summary: July 15, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans frontier-scale RL, mechanistic interpretability, and foundational theory. Ring-Zero scales zero-RL with verifiable rewards to a trillion-parameter model, probing emergent reasoning at unprecedented scale.

  • Interpretability & theory: A reusable countdown subcircuit is shared across tasks in Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (Gurnee, Ameisen); Thompson Sampling is proven 2-competitive for mistakes, resolving a long-standing conjecture (Sellke, Valiant).
  • Memorization & reliability: Extractable memorization is reframed from first principles (Liang, Lemley, Ho, Cooper), requiring matched generation-probability comparisons; DeepMind grounds LLM confidence in normative statistical decision theory.
  • Safety & alignment: 'Distributed Denial of Science' models indirect data poisoning as industrialized scientific fraud; unsupervised failure attribution traces agent errors from successful trajectories (S. Li).
  • Embodied & vision: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 (38B) unifies embodied generation as a world foundation model; RINO casts diverse vision signals as RGB-to-RGB; function-aware fill-in-the-middle mid-training targets coding-agent foundation models.
entry.content:
Today's research spans frontier-scale RL, mechanistic interpretability, and foundational theory. Ring-Zero scales zero-RL with verifiable rewards to a trillion-parameter model, probing emergent reasoning at unprecedented scale.

  • Interpretability & theory: A reusable countdown subcircuit is shared across tasks in Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (Gurnee, Ameisen); Thompson Sampling is proven 2-competitive for mistakes, resolving a long-standing conjecture (Sellke, Valiant).
  • Memorization & reliability: Extractable memorization is reframed from first principles (Liang, Lemley, Ho, Cooper), requiring matched generation-probability comparisons; DeepMind grounds LLM confidence in normative statistical decision theory.
  • Safety & alignment: 'Distributed Denial of Science' models indirect data poisoning as industrialized scientific fraud; unsupervised failure attribution traces agent errors from successful trajectories (S. Li).
  • Embodied & vision: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 (38B) unifies embodied generation as a world foundation model; RINO casts diverse vision signals as RGB-to-RGB; function-aware fill-in-the-middle mid-training targets coding-agent foundation models.

entry.title: Ring-Zero: Scaling Zero RL to a Trillion Parameters for Emergent Reasoning

author.name: Xinyu Tang, Gangqiang Cao, Yurou Liu, Yuliang Zhan, Xiaochong Lan, Yifan Li, Yuchen Yan, Han Peng, Zican Dong, Zhenduo Zhang, Tianshu Wang, Xinyu Kong, Zujie Wen, Wayne Xin Zhao, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: Ring-Zero scales zero reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to a trillion-parameter model to study large-scale training dynamics and emergent reasoning, addressing naive scaling problems like poor readability, token redundancy, and inflexible reasoning depth. It introduces a stable, efficient pipeline with algorithmic and systems optimizations including clipping strategies. It pushes zero-RL reasoning to an unprecedented scale.

entry.title: A Shared Subcircuit Lets LLMs Count Down Across Tasks

author.name: Jacob Dunefsky, Wes Gurnee, Emmanuel Ameisen

entry.summary: This mechanistic-interpretability study identifies a reusable countdown subcircuit inside Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct that tracks how many tokens remain before a target length across tasks like fixed-length sentences, DNA codon endings, and ASCII tables. The authors characterize the geometric representation the circuit uses to estimate remaining positions. It matters as evidence that models reuse general-purpose internal machinery across superficially different tasks.

entry.title: Thompson Sampling Is 2-Competitive for Mistakes

author.name: Mark Sellke, Gregory Valiant

entry.summary: This theory paper proves Thompson sampling incurs at most twice the expected number of suboptimal-arm selections of any policy for Bayesian bandits with independent, rest-only-evolving arms. This confirms a 2014 conjecture of Guha and Munagala with a tight factor of two. It provides a clean competitive-ratio guarantee for a widely used algorithm.

entry.title: Function-Aware Fill-in-the-Middle as Mid-Training for Coding Agent Foundation Models

author.name: Yubo Wang, Jiarong Liang, Yuxuan Zhang, Xuye Liu, Cong Wei, Yuyu Zhang, Ping Nie, Wenhu Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes function-aware fill-in-the-middle mid-training for coding agents, arguing that an agent action-observation-continuation loop is structurally the same as a function call site available at internet scale in ordinary code. It masks functions selected by program dependency graph analysis under a complexity-inferability criterion and mid-trains an open coding model to better integrate tool returns into reasoning.

entry.title: Distributed Denial of Science: How Indirect Data Poisoning of AI Systems Can Industrialize Scientific Fraud

author.name: B\'alint Gyevn\'ar, Atoosa Kasirzadeh, Nihar B. Shah

entry.summary: Introduces and empirically evaluates indirect data poisoning as a threat to scientific integrity, where adversaries corrupt public datasets that autonomous research agents unknowingly ingest and propagate. It argues AI-automated science could industrialize scientific fraud at scale.

entry.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0: Unified Embodied Synthesis with World Foundation Model

author.name: Xinghang Li, Jun Guo, Qiwei Li, Long Qian, Hang Lai, Yueze Wang, Hongyu Yan, Jiahang Cao, Xi Chen, Jingen Qu, Jiaxi Song, Nan Sun, Hanye Zhao, Futeng Liu, Wanli Peng, Heyun Wang, Yunhong Wang, Caoyu Xia, Jack Zhao, Diyun Xiang, Hangjun Ye, Heng Qu, Huaping Liu, Jason Li

entry.summary: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 is a 38-billion-parameter multimodal autoregressive model that treats embodied generation as an extension of foundation image and video generation, jointly optimizing text-to-image, editing, embodied scene generation, embodied transfer, and embodied video generation. It matters as a large industry effort to build a unified world foundation model for robotics.

entry.title: Tracing Agentic Failure from the Flow of Success

author.name: Samuel Yeh, Yiwen Zhu, Shaleen Deep, Sharon Li

entry.summary: The paper addresses unsupervised failure attribution for LLM agent systems, training only on successful trajectories to identify which step caused a failure at inference time. This avoids expensive step-level error annotations and prompting pipelines, making debugging of agentic systems more scalable.

entry.title: Extractable Memorization From First Principles

author.name: A. Feder Cooper, Marika Swanberg, Jamie Hayes, Lea Duesterwald, Christopher De Sa, Daniel E. Ho, Mark A. Lemley, Percy Liang

entry.summary: This paper reframes extractable memorization in LLMs from first principles, arguing valid extraction claims require matched comparison of generation probabilities between training and comparable non-training sequences to distinguish memorization from mere predictability. Authors include prominent researchers spanning ML, law, and policy. It clarifies methodology in a contested legally relevant area.

entry.title: Language Identification with Succinct Machine-Independent Traces

author.name: Moses Charikar, Jon Kleinberg, Chirag Pabbaraju

entry.summary: Motivated by LLMs, this paper studies Gold-Angluin language identification when learners are given succinct machine-independent computational traces or annotations, akin to commented code or chain-of-thought. It proves positive identifiability results that circumvent classic negative results. It offers a theoretical lens on why annotated training data helps learning.

entry.title: Scaling Point-in-Time Language Models

author.name: Bryan Kelly, Semyon Malamud, Johannes Schwab, Teng Andrea Xu

entry.summary: This work builds point-in-time language models trained only on text available up to each calendar date to eliminate lookahead bias that invalidates financial and social-science backtests. Scaling decoder-only transformers to 4B parameters on 1T chronologically filtered FineWeb tokens narrows the performance gap to unconstrained models, with monthly checkpoints. It matters for causally valid empirical research.

entry.title: A Learning-Rate-Gated Failure of GRPO in a Small Language and Vision-Language Model Web Agent: A Controlled Null and Its Mechanism

author.name: Chengguang Gan, Zhixi Cai, Yunhao Liang, Hanjun Wei, Shiwen Ni, Qinghao Zhang

entry.summary: A carefully controlled study finds that GRPO reinforcement learning fails to add skill to small (4-8B) language and vision-language web agents beyond a strong supervised baseline, and can make text agents worse at high learning rates. It analyzes the mechanism as learning-rate-gated reshaping rather than genuine capability gain.

entry.title: CDFM: Towards a General-Purpose Causal Discovery Foundation Model

author.name: Jie Qiao, Ruichu Cai, Zijian Li, Weilin Chen, Pengfei Hua, Boyan Xu, Zhengming Chen, Zhifeng Hao, Peng Cui

entry.summary: CDFM aims to build a general-purpose causal discovery foundation model that unifies the fragmented, mechanism-specific algorithm landscape into a single framework that scales across heterogeneous datasets. It matters because a working foundation model for causal structure recovery would be significant for scientific discovery.

entry.title: Invariant Learning Dynamics of Transformers in Inductive Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Tiberiu Musat, Tiago Pimentel, Nicolas Zucchet, Thomas Hofmann

entry.summary: This theoretical paper proves that for a generalized class of inductive reasoning tasks (unifying in-context n-grams and multi-hop reasoning), the training dynamics of attention models can be confined to a low-dimensional interpretable invariant manifold captured by a handful of coordinates. It matters for making Transformer learning dynamics analytically tractable.

entry.title: The Computational Basis of Confidence in Large Language Models

author.name: Dharshan Kumaran, Viorica Patraucean, Maks Ovsanikov, Petar Veli\v{c}kovi\'c, Nathaniel Daw

entry.summary: Using a normative statistical-decision-confidence framework from computational neuroscience, this DeepMind-affiliated work asks what an LLM confidence signal actually represents, testing whether answer-logit differences encode a Bayesian latent decision variable or a non-Bayesian heuristic. It probes the computational basis rather than mere calibration. It matters for trustworthy deployment and interpretability.

entry.title: Let RGB Be the Language of Vision

author.name: Timing Yang, Jinrui Yang, Xinlong Li, Yuhan Wang, Haoran Li, Yanqing Liu, Guoyizhe Wei, Jixuan Ying, Chen Wei, Rama Chellappa, Yuyin Zhou, Cihang Xie, Alan Yuille, Feng Wang

entry.summary: RINO proposes a unified formulation where diverse visual signals such as masks and depth maps are all represented as RGB images, casting general vision tasks as a common RGB-to-RGB image editing problem handled by a single backbone. This creates a unified visual interface analogous to how language models operate over text.

entry.title: Hy-Embodied-VLM-1.0: Efficient Physical-World Agents

author.name: Ziyi Wang, Xumin Yu, Yongming Rao, Yonggen Ling, Yunheng Li, Oran Wang, Mingqi Gao, Yuchen Zhou, Yves Liang, Zuyan Liu, Yani Zhang, Rui Huang, Xiaoran Xu, Bowen Yuan, Yifu Yuan, Xu Tan, He Zhang, Yufei Huang, Shenghao Zhang, Hongsheng Wu, Han Hu, Zhengyou Zhang

entry.summary: A technical report introducing an efficient embodied vision-language foundation model organized around an action-centric capability taxonomy spanning state understanding, transition reasoning, and sequential adaptive reasoning. Includes a systematic data pipeline for physical-world agents.

entry.title: Norm Enforcement for AI Agents: Robustly Shaping Behavior in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yaowen Ye, Jacob Steinhardt

entry.summary: This work studies norm-enforcement mechanisms for language-model agents in competitive shared environments, showing that simple enforcement is exploited by misaligned agents for advantage even without explicit training to do so. It then develops more robust enforcement to shape multi-agent behavior toward collective good.

entry.title: Evidence-Backed Video Question Answering

author.name: Shijie Wang, Honglu Zhou, Ziyang Wang, Ran Xu, Caiming Xiong, Silvio Savarese, Chen Sun, Juan Carlos Niebles

entry.summary: This paper introduces Evidence-Backed Video Question Answering, requiring models to output both a semantic answer and precise spatio-temporal evidence as tracked object segmentation masklets, and provides ST-Evidence, a human-verified pixel-level grounding benchmark. It matters for making video LLM answers verifiable rather than black-box.

entry.title: MemOps: Benchmarking Lifecycle Memory Operations in Long-Horizon Conversations

author.name: Xixuan Hao, Zeyu Zhang, Zehao Lin, Yihang Sun, Ziliang Guo, Xichong Zhang, Yuxuan Liang, Feiyu Xiong, Zhiyu Li

entry.summary: MemOps introduces a benchmark that evaluates memory as a dynamic lifecycle of operations rather than only final answer correctness in long-horizon multi-session conversations. It distinguishes failure causes such as missing fact introduction, wrong-target binding, and reliance on stale values after corrections.

entry.title: To Answer or to Abstain: Mitigating Search-Agent Hallucinations via Abstention-Aware Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fengji Zhang, Tianyu Fan, Yuxiang Zheng, Xinyao Niu, Chengen Huang, Jacky Keung, Bei Chen

entry.summary: Proposes abstention-aware reinforcement learning for search-augmented LLM agents that dynamically shapes abstention rewards to penalize fabricated answers when retrieval fails, rather than only rewarding correct answers. It introduces a metric to capture the capability-reliability trade-off.

entry.title: VIA: Visual Interface Agent for Robot Control

author.name: Hengyuan Hu, Priya Sundaresan, Jensen Gao, Dorsa Sadigh

entry.summary: Proposes controlling robots through visual software interfaces using frontier foundation models rather than fine-tuning smaller vision-language-action models on limited robot data. It leverages foundation models' growing ability to operate software via visual interfaces to overcome VLA capacity limits.

entry.title: Extending LLM Context via Associative Recurrent Memory

author.name: Gleb Kuzmin, Ivan Rodkin, Aydar Bulatov, Yuri Kuratov, Lyudmila Rvanova, Mikhail Katkov, Ilia Sochenkov, Misha Tsodyks, Timothy Baldwin, Mikhail Burtsev, Artem Shelmanov

entry.summary: This paper develops training recipes and domain-specific datasets to extend LLM context using the Associative Recurrent Memory Transformer, giving constant-memory scaling for long-context processing. It matters as a practical alternative to quadratic-attention context extension for narrow-domain workloads.

entry.title: Mathematics of Data Science

author.name: Afonso S. Bandeira, Amit Singer, Thomas Strohmer

entry.summary: This is a textbook on the mathematical foundations of data science covering high-dimensional phenomena, SVD/PCA, regression, spectral clustering, dimension reduction, optimization, deep learning, concentration of measure, compressive sensing, and low-rank recovery. It matters as an educational reference from prominent applied mathematicians.

entry.title: Knowledgeless Language Models: Suppressing Parametric Recall for Evidence-Grounded Language Modeling

author.name: Roi Cohen, Yvan Carr\'e, Nick Lechtenb\"orger, Hendrik Droste, Lucas Kerschke, Russa Biswas, Gerard de Melo, Jan Buys

entry.summary: Knowledgeless Language Models are pretrained on corpora with anonymized named entities to remove entity-linked factual supervision, shifting models away from parametric recall toward evidence-grounded reasoning. This reduces closed-book factual recall while often improving performance on tasks where relevant evidence is provided in context. It proposes a distinct epistemic training paradigm.

entry.title: The Illusion of Robustness: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Prediction Flips under Task-Irrelevant Context

author.name: Yanzhe Zhang, Sanmi Koyejo, Diyi Yang

entry.summary: This work shows that aggregate accuracy hides significant per-example instability in LLMs under task-irrelevant context, where even meaningless pseudo-words flip predictions on a fraction of examples in both directions. Aggregate stability masks this fragility, which holds across many models. It argues robustness must be assessed at the per-example level.

entry.title: Can risk aversion learned at low stakes generalize to astronomically high stakes?

author.name: Elliott Thornley

entry.summary: Summarizes a paper introducing RiskAverseOOD, a benchmark measuring whether risk aversion in resources learned at low stakes generalizes to astronomically high stakes as a potential misalignment failsafe. Finds partial generalization, with cooperation rates rising from about 2 percent to roughly 39 to 70 percent depending on the training method.

entry.title: Open Distillation of Hereditary Traits

author.name: Arthur Conmy

entry.summary: Arthur Conmy replicates and extends work showing that distilling from a teacher model into a base student transfers behavioral traits, and that filtering out prompts mentioning the trait does not reliably prevent transfer. He demonstrates the phenomenon cheaply without a frontier SFT pipeline, transferring negative emotion, agentic misalignment, and censorship across Gemma, Qwen, Nemotron, and Llama base models, releasing all weights and code.

entry.title: Proxy Exploration and Reusable Guidance: A Modular LLM Post-Training Paradigm via Proxy-Guided Update Signals

author.name: Daocheng Fu, Rong Wu, Yu Yang, Xuemeng Yang, Jianbiao Mei, Licheng Wen, Pinlong Cai, Yong Liu, Botian Shi, Yu Qiao

entry.summary: PUST is an LLM post-training framework that decouples reward exploration from distribution alignment by using a lightweight proxy model to discover high-reward update signals that can be reused and transferred across models. It matters for making post-training cheaper and more modular by avoiding expensive exploration on the primary model.

entry.title: Agent Hacks Agent: Autoresearch for Production-Agent Red-Teaming

author.name: Xutao Mao, Xiang Zheng, Cong Wang

entry.summary: AHA is an automated red-teaming loop that uses one agentic research environment to discover reusable vulnerability knowledge about production LLM agents by proposing falsifiable vulnerability hypotheses, building falsifiers, and instantiating attacks. It matters because it targets the enabling conditions of unsafe agent behavior rather than just attack success artifacts.

entry.title: Inside the Unfair Judge: A Mechanistic Interpretability Account of LLM-as-Judge Bias

author.name: Zixiang Xu, Sixian Li, Huaxing Liu, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Zirui Song, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: This paper gives a mechanistic-interpretability account of LLM-as-judge bias, showing across seven judges and seven bias types that biased inputs are displaced along low-dimensional, type-specific subspaces in hidden states, and that steering along these subspaces causally controls bias. It matters for representation-level detection and mitigation of judging bias.

entry.title: Length Penalties Make Chain-of-Thought Less Monitorable

author.name: Bryce Little

entry.summary: The paper shows that length-penalized reinforcement learning shortens chain-of-thought while still allowing hidden influences to steer answers, so a biasing hint keeps driving outputs even as it is mentioned far less in the trace. It warns that token-accuracy evaluations would falsely count these compressed, less-monitorable runs as successful.

entry.title: Remembering Distinct Items, Not Tokens: A Learnable Dirichlet-Process Cache Between State-Space Models and Attention

author.name: Siddharth Pal, Viktoria Rojkova

entry.summary: Proposes a sparse key-value cache that allocates a memory slot only when an input is novel, using the DP-means clustering rule (small-variance Dirichlet-process limit) as the memory operator between state-space models and full attention. Memory then scales with the number of distinct items rather than tokens.

entry.title: World Models as Adversaries: Multi-Agent Self-Play Fine-Tuning for Robust Motion Planning

author.name: Tong Nie, Yuewen Mei, Junlin He, Yihong Tang, Jian Sun, Wei Ma

entry.summary: Frames adversarially robust motion planning for autonomous vehicles as a constrained min-max game solved via multi-agent self-play fine-tuning, treating world models as adversaries. It provides a decoupled solver to avoid external scenario generators for training on rare safety-critical events.

entry.title: Action Map Policy: Learning 3D Closed-loop Manipulation via Pixel Classification

author.name: Haojie Huang, Zhang Ye, Linfeng Zhao, Boce Hu, Mingxi Jia, Yu Qi, Ahmed Agha, Dian Wang, Robert Platt, Robin Walters

entry.summary: Casts 3D closed-loop robot manipulation policy learning as pixel-space classification by projecting 3D actions onto camera image planes, avoiding vocabulary explosion from naive action discretization. It aims to handle high-dimensional, long-horizon, multi-modal action spaces.

entry.title: Multi-Agent LLMs Fail to Explore Each Other

author.name: Hyeong Kyu Choi, Jiatong Li, Wendi Li, Xin Eric Wang, Sharon Li

entry.summary: Shows that LLM agents fail to explore each other effectively in multi-agent interactions, exhibiting myopic and polarized patterns that harm coordination, formalized as a multi-agent exploration problem in a partially observable stochastic game. It introduces a lightweight contextual-exploration framework to promote probing of peers' capabilities.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Comprehensive Cardiac CT Segmentation and Phenotyping: Human-in-the-Loop Data Annotation, Vision Foundation Model Development, Multicenter Evaluation and Clinical Validation

author.name: Pooya Mohammadi Kazaj, Leo Fridolin Weber, Wen Xie, Seyed Amir Ahmad Safavi-Naini, Anselm Stark, Giovanni Baj, Ali Mokhtari, Toshiya Yoshida, Christoph Ryffel, Taishi Okuno, Yoshihiro Akashi, Ronny R. Buechel, Thomas Pilgrim, Waldo Valenzuela, George C. M. Siontis, Xiaowei Xu, Moritz Hundertmark, Stephan Windecker, Christoph Grani, Isaac Shiri

entry.summary: Presents a unified framework for comprehensive cardiac CT segmentation and phenotyping combining a human-in-the-loop annotation pipeline, a CT augmentation technique, and a self-supervised foundation model pre-trained on 60,000 unlabeled scans. It assembles a large expert-annotated dataset of 1,598 cases across 14 structures with multicenter external validation.

entry.title: Beyond Sally-Anne: Evaluating Theory of Mind in LLMs using Epistemic Schelling Points

author.name: Roberta Rocca, Sami Boukortt, Geoff Keeling, Winnie Street

entry.summary: Introduces a two-player dialogue game that benchmarks theory of mind in LLMs by requiring model dyads to independently converge on semantic Schelling points under varying epistemic transparency, avoiding the gameable nature of Sally-Anne style tests. It reveals a significant capability gap in robust, generalizable theory-of-mind reasoning.

entry.title: See like a Robot: Robot-Centric Pointmaps for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Byungkun Lee, Dongyoon Hwang, Dongjin Kim, Hojoon Lee, Minho Park, Jaegul Choo

entry.summary: This work introduces robot-centric pointmaps for vision-language-action models, storing per-pixel 3D coordinates in the robot frame to fix the mismatch between camera-frame observation and robot-frame actions. It matters because resolving this frame mismatch could improve cross-viewpoint generalization for VLA policies trained on heterogeneous datasets.

entry.title: MM-ToolSandBox: A Unified Framework for Evaluating Visual Tool-Calling Agents

author.name: Kaixin Ma, Di Feng, Alexander Metz, Jiarui Lu, Eshan Verma, Afshin Dehghan

entry.summary: MM-ToolSandBox is a benchmark and stateful evaluation framework for visually grounded tool-calling agents, spanning 500-plus tools across 16 domains with multi-image, multi-turn tasks and realistic conversational phenomena, evaluating twelve state-of-the-art models. It matters for rigorously measuring visual agentic tool use.

entry.title: Metacognition in LLMs: Foundations, Progress, and Opportunities

author.name: Gabrielle Kaili-May Liu, Areeb Gani, Jacqueline Lu, Jordan Thomas, Mark Steyvers, Arman Cohan

entry.summary: This paper presents the first comprehensive survey of metacognition for large language models, taxonomizing current knowledge and analyzing when and how LLMs can exhibit or be endowed with metacognitive abilities to improve capability, reliability, and transparency. It matters as a structuring reference for an increasingly recognized aspect of capable AI.

entry.title: The Sound of Absence: Audio-Language Embedding Models Struggle with Negation

author.name: Chun-Yi Kuan, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: The paper shows audio-language embedding models like CLAP largely ignore negation, mapping affirmative and negated captions to near-identical vectors. It introduces NegEval-Audio with retrieval and multiple-choice negation tasks, finding accuracy falling below chance under negation on AudioCaps and Clotho. It exposes a systematic blind spot in multimodal audio understanding.

entry.title: LLMs Can See the Smoke but not the Fire: Evaluating Abductive Reasoning with Elenchos

author.name: Julius Steiglechner, Lucas Mahler, Gabriele Lohmann

entry.summary: Elenchos is a generative evaluation framework measuring LLM abductive reasoning as a structural inverse problem, asking models to detect whether a formal system like lambda-calculus has been mutated and to infer the responsible rule changes.
