entry.summary: Studies cross-model consensus as a free inference-time selection signal for reasoning, treating independently trained models as an LLM jury whose structure of agreement (not scoring) verifies answers. Across seven benchmarks it selects correct answers better than self-consistency and trained reward models.

entry.title: Context by Distinct Information: An Auditable Dirichlet-Process Working Memory for Long, Redundant Context Streams

author.name: Siddharth Pal, Viktoria Rojkova

entry.summary: Builds on a companion mechanism (a cache that opens a slot only for novel keys so memory scales with distinct items) to design an auditable Dirichlet-process working-memory component for long, redundant context streams. It organizes context by how a task depends on the past, separating recall-carried information from other dependencies.

entry.title: MDQEC-QAS: Meta-Decoding for Quantum Error Correction with Hardware-Aware VQC Search and Confidence-Gated Recovery

author.name: Prashant Kumar Choudhary, Nouhaila Innan, Muhammad Shafique, Rajeev Singh

entry.summary: Presents a unified meta-decoding framework for quantum error correction that learns syndrome-to-recovery mappings across multiple stabilizer codes and noise settings without per-configuration decoders. It compares a classical meta-MLP baseline with hardware-aware variational quantum circuit meta-decoders across several transfer regimes.

entry.title: PromptGraph: Graph-Guided Prompt Sanitization for Balancing Privacy and Utility in LLM Inference

author.name: Chen Gu, Hui Wan, Donghui Hu, Hui Wang, Zhuoer Gu

entry.summary: Proposes a graph-guided prompt sanitization method that models pairwise contextual dependencies between spans, not just individual identifiers, to balance privacy and utility in LLM inference. It represents prompts as attributed graphs with span-level privacy scores.

entry.title: Distributed Agent System: Fault-Tolerant Collaboration Among Embodied Agents

author.name: Kai Yu, Lu Chen, Hanqi Li

entry.summary: Proposes a device-edge-cloud framework for fault-tolerant collaboration among heterogeneous embodied agents, redefining reliability as system-level fault tolerance rather than single-turn accuracy. It presents a two-layer architecture for execution and cross-agent communication reliability.

entry.title: Think When It Matters: Conditional VLM Reasoning for Social Navigation with RL Policies

author.name: Ali Ahmadi, Hamed Rahimi, Adrien Jacquet Cretides, Marie Samson, Mahdi Khoramshahi, Mohamed Chetouani

entry.summary: Introduces a hybrid social-navigation approach that combines fast reactive RL policies with vision-language model reasoning invoked conditionally, only when semantic reasoning is needed. It aims to balance real-time deployment against the computational cost of VLMs.

entry.title: SynCLIP: Synonym-Coherent Language-Image Pretraining for Robust Open-Vocabulary Dense Perception

author.name: Mingjie Xie, Guangjun He, Dongli Xu, Youtian Lin, Hongjue Li, Pengming Feng, Jian Guan, Yue Deng

entry.summary: Identifies synonym-induced grounding inconsistency in CLIP-based open-vocabulary dense perception, where semantically equivalent phrases yield different spatial attention. It proposes a synonym-coherent pretraining framework with a spatial-attention alignment module to enforce consistent grounding.

entry.title: Flout at Your Own Risk: LLMs Struggle with Pragmatic Cooperativity Under Epistemic Asymmetry

author.name: Hannah VanderHoeven, Abhijnan Nath, Nikhil Krishnaswamy

entry.summary: Investigates pragmatic reasoning in LLMs during multi-party collaboration under partial information, formalizing collaborative epistemic asymmetry linked to Grice's cooperative principle. It finds LLMs struggle to communicate cooperatively when they lack the same information as collaborators.

entry.title: AgentCheck: A Reproduce-Intervene-Mitigate Workbench for LLM Agents over MCP

author.name: Aritra Mazumder, Nusrat jahan Lia

entry.summary: Presents an open-source workbench that turns an MCP server into a fault-injection surface for LLM agents, recording tool responses, replaying them with 12 fault types injected, and supporting a reproduce-intervene-confirm loop to test mitigations before deployment. It targets reliability testing of tool-using agents under realistic tool failures.

entry.title: The Equilibrium Is the Initialization: Lazy Identity Collapse in Physics-Structured Deep Equilibrium Reasoning

author.name: Joyjeet Singh

entry.summary: Reports a cautionary study of a physics-structured deep equilibrium model with learned initialization on reasoning tasks, showing the implicit computation is a silent no-op where the solved equilibrium equals the initialization and bypassing the solver leaves accuracy unchanged. Controlled interventions falsify the claim of genuine iterative inference.

entry.title: MusicMark: A Robust Generative Watermarking Framework for Music Generation

author.name: Seohwan Yun, Jeeyoung Yun, Yongjin Kim, Juyeon Lee, Sungwoong Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a generative watermarking framework that embeds watermarks as part of music generation rather than as post-hoc perturbations, aiming for robustness against transformations including neural codec re-synthesis. It targets provenance and attribution for AI music.

entry.title: BeatEdit: Symbolic Music Generation as Explicit Editing

author.name: Haoyu Gu, Lekai Qian, Haowu Zhou, Qi Liu, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Reframes symbolic music generation as explicit editing rather than generating complete sequences from scratch, leveraging a beat-grid-anchored representation whose structural properties support selective modification. It presents the first edit-based framework for symbolic music.

entry.title: HandFlow: Fully Generative 4D Hand Recovery with Flow Matching

author.name: Mingxi Xu, Bowen Duan, Yi Gu, Zhengyang Shen, Renjing Xu, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: Presents a fully generative flow-matching framework for temporally coherent 3D hand pose and shape estimation from monocular video, learning a prior over plausible motion to recover hand states under occlusion and motion blur. It contrasts with deterministic per-frame or temporal regressors that struggle with ambiguity.

entry.title: Understanding the Impact of AI Code Assistants on Security API Usage: An Empirical Study

author.name: Zahra Mousavi, Chadni Islam, M. Ali Babar, Alsharif Abuadbba, Kristen Moore

entry.summary: Presents the first developer-centered empirical investigation of how AI code assistants influence the use of security APIs, which are critical yet error-prone in safeguarding software. It aims to inform mitigation strategies for AI-assisted development of secure code.

entry.title: A Glimpse into Long-term Physical Coexistence with Intelligent Robots

author.name: Weiqi Jin, Peijun Tang, Kuncheng Luo, Baifu Huang, Binyan Sun, Haotian Yang, Shangjin Xie, Jianan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a multi-robot agent built around a robot gateway abstraction that supports diverse interfaces, long-horizon memory of people and preferences, cross-embodiment coordination, and safe intent-to-execution translation. It decouples low-frequency high-semantic agent reasoning from high-frequency low-level robot execution for plug-and-play integration.

entry.title: From World Action Models to Embodied Brains: A Roadmap for Open-World Physical Intelligence

author.name: Yuanzhi Liang, Xufeng Zhan, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: This roadmap surveys the evolution toward World Action Models that connect candidate interventions with predicted consequences, organizing progress gaps into model roles/representations, objectives/standardization, and system composition. It matters as a structuring vision for open-world physical intelligence.

entry.title: StoryTeller: Training-Free Narrative Grounding for Long-Form Audio Description

author.name: Seung Hyun Hahm, Minh T. Dinh, SouYoung Jin

entry.summary: StoryTeller is a training-free framework for story-aware long-form audio description that maintains a verified narrative memory carrying forward characters, events, and relationships across scenes so descriptions preserve story context. It matters for accessibility for blind and low-vision film audiences.

entry.title: Generalized Distribution-Free Semi-Supervised Learning with Risk Rewrite

author.name: Yushi Hirose, Hiroo Irobe, Takafumi Kanamori

entry.summary: This paper proposes a generalized distribution-free semi-supervised learning framework that builds unbiased risk estimators from linear combinations of component risks, subsuming PNU learning, extending it to multiclass, and deriving minimum-variance and generalization bounds. It matters for principled SSL that does not rely on distributional assumptions.

entry.title: Scalable Optimal Transport Algorithm for Network Alignment

author.name: Elaheh Hassani, Durga Mandarapu, Qi Yu, Hanghang Tong, Ariful Azad

entry.summary: FastAlign is a scalable, sparsity-aware framework for optimal-transport-based network alignment that preserves the original OT formulation but reinterprets its computation as recurring mixed sparse operations to avoid dense matrix construction. It matters for scaling accurate network alignment to large graphs.

entry.title: LIDAR-AD: A Decoder-Free Latent-Interaction Dreamer with Action-Residual Chains for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yongzhi Liu, Yang Xiao, Zhong Cao, Zeng Kang, Sunan Zhang, Zhaozhi Dong, Guojun Yu, Weichao Zhuang

entry.summary: LIDAR-AD is a decoder-free latent-interaction dreamer with action-residual chains for autonomous driving that replaces observation reconstruction with redundancy-reduced latent dynamics focused on risk-relevant relations and models continuous action adjustments as residual chains. It matters for learning decision-relevant latent world models for long-horizon closed-loop driving.

entry.title: Signal-Guided Optimization for Machine Unlearning

author.name: Xujia Li, Dan Li, Jian Lou, Wenjie Feng

entry.summary: GSUO is a guidance-signal-aware machine unlearning framework that designs task-specific fine-grained signals to steer unlearning, addressing over-unlearning that harms utility and under-unlearning that leaves exploitable residual information under uniform strategies. It matters for more precise, privacy-preserving unlearning across random and targeted forgetting.

entry.title: Efficient Sequential Calibration with $O(T^{2/3-\epsilon})$ Error Bound

author.name: Zihan Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents an efficient randomized forecaster for online binary sequential calibration achieving expected calibration error below the classical two-thirds barrier, combining a recent SPR-calibration procedure with a Blackwell-style outer correction layer. It builds directly on a recent theoretical breakthrough. It is a contribution to online learning theory.

entry.title: Toward Localizing and Repairing Bias in Transformer Attention Heads

author.name: Sigma Jahan

entry.summary: ROBIN is a white-box, head-level fairness debugging method that ranks transformer attention heads by sensitivity to fairness probes and removes a small bias subspace from selected head outputs at inference time. A four-model pilot shows reduced WinoBias gaps. It aims to localize and repair bias inside models rather than at input-output level.

entry.title: Ensemble Controlled-Flow Filtering for Implicit Data Assimilation

author.name: Zhuoyuan Li, Yue Zhao, Ming Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces implicit data assimilation where the analysis is an energy tilt of the forecast distribution, realized by an Ensemble Controlled-flow Filter that learns observation-dependent control via adjoint matching from terminal energy gradients. It handles many-to-one, implicit, non-smooth, or simulator-only observations. It extends ensemble filtering to hard observation mechanisms.

entry.title: Policy-Conditioned Constrained Decoding for Column-Level Access Control in Text-to-SQL

author.name: Ryoto Miyamoto, Xin Fan, Hayato Yamana

entry.summary: PCC-SQL enforces column-level access control in text-to-SQL by conditioning constrained decoding on a policy over semantic column use (output, filter condition, aggregation argument) aligned with grammar productions. This deterministically rules out policy violations rather than deciding refusal stochastically by mentioned columns. It balances policy compliance, answer coverage, and bounded cost across trust boundaries.

entry.title: Can Induced Emotion Bias LLM Behaviors in Sequential Decision Making?

author.name: Minh Khoi Ho, Zihao Zhu, Runchuan Zhu, Levina Li, Zhiwen Fan, Zhangyang Wang, Junyuan Hong

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether induced emotions can bias LLM sequential decision-making using the Iowa Gambling Task with an imagination-based emotion-induction procedure. It validates that LLMs can sense distinguishable emotions and learn from sequential interactions, then tests emotional influence on choices. It probes affective factors in autonomous LLM agents in high-stakes settings.

entry.title: The One-Word Census: Answer-Choice Conformity Across 44 Language Models

author.name: Tapan Parikh

entry.summary: The One-Word Census asks 44 language models minimal single-turn prompts naming categories with many valid one-word answers and finds strong cross-model convergence, such as 41% choosing serendipity for pick-any-word. It uses exact-match analysis on normalized tokens at roughly a dollar per model as a cheap instrument. It reveals structure in answer-choice conformity across models.

entry.title: Can LLMs Write Reliable Rubrics? A Meta-Evaluation for Experiment Reproduction

author.name: Hanhua Hong, Yizhi Li, Jiaoyan Chen, Luu Gia Huy, Sophia Ananiadou, Jung-jae Kim, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: This paper presents a systematic meta-evaluation of LLM-generated rubrics for scientific paper reproduction, reformulating rubrics into checklists and testing four generation settings across two backbone models. It evaluates rubrics intrinsically by semantic similarity and extrinsically by score alignment with ground-truth rubrics. It probes whether LLMs can replace costly expert rubric construction for benchmarks like PaperBench.

entry.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Misconceptions in Multi-Turn Medical Conversations

author.name: Monica Munnangi, Saiph Savage

entry.summary: This study introduces ThReadMed-QA, a multi-turn medical dialogue dataset of 2,437 patient-physician threads, to evaluate whether LLMs can identify and correct misconceptions embedded in patient questions over conversation turns. It focuses on safe communication that corrects false beliefs rather than only answering. It examines misconception handling as beliefs emerge, persist, or evolve.

entry.title: From Words to Widgets for Controllable LLM Generation

author.name: Chao Zhang, Yiren Liu, Lunyiu Nie, Jeffrey M. Rzeszotarski, Yun Huang, Tal August

entry.summary: Malleable Prompting reifies natural-language preference expressions (tone, style, emphasis) into GUI widgets like sliders and toggles that users configure to steer LLM generation, with visualizations attributing each control's effect. It introduces a decoding algorithm that modulates token probabilities according to widget settings. It improves controllable and interpretable LLM interaction.

entry.title: QDEvo: A Multi-Objective Quality-Diversity Framework for Automated Heuristic Design

author.name: Nam Do Khanh, Nhat Nguyen Tran Minh, Dat Pham Vu Tuan, Long Doan, Binh Huynh Thi Thanh

entry.summary: QDEvo integrates Quality-Diversity optimization with LLM-driven heuristic search for automated heuristic design in combinatorial optimization, maintaining an unbounded archive of semantically diverse algorithms via code embeddings and hierarchical self-reflection. It targets the mode-collapse problem where existing methods converge to homogeneous populations. It broadens algorithmic exploration.

entry.title: Code-MUE: Measuring Code LLMs' Uncertainty through Execution-based Semantic Interaction Graphs

author.name: Xiaoning Ren, Yinxing Xue, Lei Ma, Yuheng Huang

entry.summary: Code-MUE is a purely black-box uncertainty estimation method for code LLMs that builds execution-based semantic interaction graphs to capture whether syntactic variation implies semantic divergence. It addresses the gap where white-box methods fail on closed models and text-based metrics misjudge code fragility. It aims to distinguish confident code predictions from stochastic guessing.

entry.title: Representation and Reference Selection in Training-Free Synthetic Image Attribution

author.name: Meiling Li, Pietro Bongini, Benedetta Tondi, Mauro Barni

entry.summary: This paper provides a controlled analysis of training-free synthetic image attribution, studying how the representation space (layers of CLIP and DINO) and the construction of source-specific references interact. It highlights that the coupling of these two factors, previously unexplored, strongly influences attribution performance.

entry.title: Implicit 4D Gaussian Splatting for Fast Motion with Large Inter-Frame Displacements

author.name: Seung-gyeom Kim, Areum Kim, Yongjae Yoo, Sukmin Yun

entry.summary: SPIN-4DGS improves 4D Gaussian Splatting under fast motion with large inter-frame displacements by learning Gaussian attributes from explicit spatiotemporal positions rather than modeling temporal displacements. A lightweight feed-forward network predicts attributes to avoid heavy memory overhead.

entry.title: IQA-T1: Tool-based Visual Evidence Reasoning for Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Jinjian Wu, Jiaqi Tang, Wei Wei, Yingying Yan, Jianmin Chen, Botong Geng, Lei Zhang, Qifeng Chen

entry.summary: IQA-T1 augments multimodal LLM image quality assessment with tool-based visual evidence, letting the model invoke analysis tools that produce noise residual maps, gradient statistics, and frequency spectra. This grounds quality judgments in low-level perceptual observations rather than semantically biased internal representations.

entry.title: ARDepth: Auto-regressive Monocular Depth Estimation with Progressive Visual Conditioning

author.name: Zijie Wang, Wei Zhang, Weiming Zhang, Xiao Tan, Weikai Chen, Xiaoxu Li, Guanbin Li

entry.summary: ARDepth formulates monocular depth estimation as structured auto-regressive generation across increasing spatial resolutions, rather than global iterative denoising. It reflects the hierarchical, piecewise, scale-dependent organization of scene geometry through progressive visual conditioning.

entry.title: TerraLogic: A Benchmark for Hierarchical Geospatial Reasoning in Earth Observation

author.name: Yuhang Yan, Linchao Mou, Bokang Yang, Qingyu Li

entry.summary: TerraLogic is a benchmark of 545 scenario-driven, hierarchy-aware geospatial reasoning tasks spanning optical, SAR, and infrared imagery, covering problems like hazard vulnerability and forest fragmentation. It targets cognitive geospatial reasoning with tool-augmented agents, which remote sensing has largely underexplored.

entry.title: DynTrace: Tracking Dynamic Object Evidence for 4D Spatio-Temporal Reasoning in MLLMs

author.name: Rongxin Gao, Yuzhi Huang, Dongxuan Liu, Chu Li, Zhenye Wang, Jie Wu, Shuzhao Xie, Jingyan Jiang, Xinghao Ding, Xiaotong Tu, Yue Huang

entry.summary: DynTrace enhances 4D spatio-temporal reasoning in multimodal LLMs by explicitly tracking dynamic object evidence and compensating for camera-induced apparent motion, addressing failures from sparse frame-level observations. It aims to disentangle genuine object dynamics for coherent dynamic scene understanding.

entry.title: Gaussian Mixture Modeling for Event-Aware Visual Allocation in Long Video Understanding

author.name: Yifan Lu, Ziqi Zhang, Chunfeng Yuan, Jun Gao, Bing Li, Weiming Hu

entry.summary: GMM-EVA uses Gaussian Mixture Models to model event-level structure from frame observations for long video understanding in large vision-language models, then allocates visual budget differentially to preserve high-resolution keyframes per event. It reduces redundancy and information loss from uniform sampling.

entry.title: Hallo4D: Multi-Modal Hallucination Mitigation for Consistent Spatio-Temporal Generation

author.name: Hongbo Wang, Huaibo Huang, Jie Cao, Jin Liu, Haoyang Tong, Ran He

entry.summary: Hallo4D is a model-agnostic framework for mitigating spatiotemporal hallucinations in 3D and 4D content generation, such as duplicated structures, jitter, identity flicker, and structural drift. It uses a generation-detection-correction paradigm driven by large multimodal language models to enforce geometric and temporal consistency.

entry.title: RFMSR: Residual Flow Matching for Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Shuwei Huang, Tianyao Luo, Jicheng Liu, Daizong Liu, Pan Zhou

entry.summary: RFMSR proposes residual flow matching for image super-resolution that transports from the low-quality input rather than pure Gaussian noise, preserving structural information already present in the input. It also retains multi-step inference capability that single-step acceleration methods often forfeit.

entry.title: Point Tracking in Surgery--The 2025 Surgical Tattoos in Infrared Challenge (STIRC2025)

author.name: Adam Schmidt, Mert Asim Karaoglu, Zijian Wu, Jiaming Zhang, Yuxin Chen, Tim Salcudean, Ho-Gun Ha, Minkang Jang, Kyungmin Jung, Ihsan Ullah, Hyunki Lee, Suresh Guttikonda, Sarah Latus, Alexander Schlaefer, Xinkai Zhao, Yuichiro Hayashi, Masahiro Oda, Takayuki Kitasaka, Kensaku Mori, Peng Liu, Chenyang Li, Stefanie Speidel, Aoife Gardiner, Agostino Stilli, Danail Stoyanov, Francisco Vasconcelos, Anwesa Choudhuri, Meng Zheng, Zhongpai Gao, Benjamin Planche, Van Nguyen Nguyen, Terrence Chen, Ziyan Wu, Alexander Ladikos, Omid Mohareri

entry.summary: Reports the 2025 surgical point-tracking challenge using the infrared surgical tattoos dataset, evaluating submitted algorithms on both accuracy across in vivo and ex vivo sequences and inference efficiency. Provides community benchmarking for surgical scene tracking.

entry.title: DermDepth: Toward Monocular Metric Scale 3D Reconstruction Models for Dermatology

author.name: H\'ector Carri\'on, Narges Norouzi

entry.summary: Presents DermDepth, described as the first single-view metric-scale 3D reconstruction approach for dermatology, producing dense depth, metric measurements, and surface normals from a single off-the-shelf camera image without extra hardware.

entry.title: Compos3D: Interactive Part-Based Composition for Creative Control in Generative 3D Models

author.name: Faraz Faruqi, Sean J. Liu, George Fitzmaurice, Justin Matejka

entry.summary: Presents a compositional workflow for generative 3D modeling where users generate multiple candidates, select parts via 2D regions or 3D mesh segments, and assemble them into a coherent refined model. Evaluated with a controlled user study comparing remixing to regeneration.

entry.title: SeqGPT: A Constrained Transformer Agent for the Inverse Designof Multi-Panel Composite Structures

author.name: Driss Chraibi (Toulouse INP), Alejandro Garc\'ia Pis (IRIT), St\'ephane Grihon (IRIT), Sixin Zhang (IRIT)

entry.summary: Presents a conditional transformer agent for inverse design of multi-panel composite stacking sequences, using a hybrid neurosymbolic approach to enforce manufacturing constraints and inter-panel blending continuity by construction. Aims to replace expensive iterative optimization.

entry.title: A 32-channel event-based bio-signal analog front-end with adaptive delta and pulse frequency encoding

author.name: Narayanan Shyam, Saptarshi Ghosh, Giacomo Indiveri

entry.summary: Presents a 32-channel event-based analog front-end ASIC for biomedical signal acquisition with dual-mode pulse-frequency and adaptive delta encoding, where an auto-scaling encoder adapts the data rate to the signal envelope for high compression and low-power transmission. Supports end-to-end neuromorphic processing.

entry.title: Deployable Human Preference Alignment in Robotics: Learning Representative Rewards from Diverse Human Preferences

author.name: Taehyung Kim, Gwangmo Lee, Minjun Chang, Sunghyun Lim, Jongeun Choi

entry.summary: Proposes Preference-based Reward Clustering, which learns a compact set of policies from binary preference labels across diverse users to capture heterogeneous preferences, including minority ones, avoiding the instability of per-user alignment and the homogenization of a single shared policy.

entry.title: PixelLoop: Shortcut Topological Navigation with Pixel-Level Loops

author.name: Sarthak Chittawar, Vansh Garg, Aditya Vadali, Krish Pandya, Rohit Jayanti, Sourav Garg, Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: Proposes PixelLoop, which introduces loop closures directly in pixel space for topological navigation, using dense pixel-level relative-3D geometry to create topological shortcuts that alter planning connectivity and cost propagation rather than merely aligning coordinates as in metric SLAM.

entry.title: MAMMOTH: A Multi-Modal End-to-End Policy for Off-Road Mobility Robust to Missing Modality

author.name: Ahaan Kotian, Shivani Subramanyan, Suresh Sundaram

entry.summary: Presents MAMMOTH, a multimodal end-to-end off-road navigation policy designed to be robust to missing sensor modalities, addressing over-reliance on RGB in challenging illumination and acute sensor degradation in unstructured terrain.

entry.title: ChunkFlow: Towards Continuity-Consistent Chunked Policy Learning

author.name: Zhao Yang, Yinan Shi, Mingyuan Yao, Wenyao Xue, Yawei Jueluo, Longjun Liu

entry.summary: Proposes ChunkFlow, a seam-aware training-and-execution framework for chunked action policies that partitions each chunk into frozen, editable, and future zones with deterministic overlap blending to fix boundary jitter and inconsistent predictions between consecutive action chunks.

entry.title: VoxENES 2026: Benchmarking Generalization of Speech Spoofing Detectors Against LLM-Era TTS and Voice Conversion

author.name: Aastha Sharma, Guangjing Wang

entry.summary: VoxENES 2026 is a bilingual benchmark of over 53,000 samples from ten modern speech synthesis methods evaluated under ten post-processing conditions, revealing that pretrained spoofing detectors degrade sharply (best 28.98 percent EER) on LLM-era TTS and voice conversion. It matters for exposing a temporal generalization gap in anti-spoofing systems.

entry.title: SinAE: A Single-Architecture Flow-Matching Autoencoder for Cross-Domain Atomic Systems

author.name: Yuxuan Ren, Fan Yang, Jianhua Yao, Yatao Bian

entry.summary: SinAE is a single-architecture flow-matching autoencoder that provides a lossless, architecture-general latent space for molecules, crystals, and proteins, enabling cross-domain training that mitigates per-domain data scarcity. It unifies fragmented atomic-system generative pipelines. Cross-domain generalization is the main contribution.

entry.title: TerraZero: Procedural Driving Simulation for Zero-Demonstration Self-Play at Scale

author.name: Zhouchonghao Wu, Akshay Rangesh, Weixin Li, Wei-Jer Chang, Zachary Lee, Tim Wang, Wei Zhan

entry.summary: TerraZero is a procedural driving simulator and self-play training stack whose configurable C engine sustains 1.3 million agent-steps per second on one GPU, enabling large-scale reinforcement learning for autonomous driving with heterogeneous agents, multiple dynamics, and full traffic-rule enforcement. It targets the safety-critical long tail that logged data misses. Throughput and zero-demonstration self-play are key claims.

entry.title: Gradient-free learning of a closed-loop wall controller for turbulent drag reduction

author.name: Giorgio Maria Cavallazzi, Miguel P\'erez Cuadrado, Alfredo Pinelli

entry.summary: This study uses evolution strategies to train a recurrent closed-loop wall controller directly on a large turbulent channel to reduce skin-friction drag, avoiding degeneracies seen in gradient-based multi-agent RL policies trained on small boxes. It evaluates over full flow episodes at moderate Reynolds number. It advances learned flow control for turbulent drag reduction.

entry.title: Structured Fluctuations and the Information Dynamics of Self-Maintenance in Growing Neural Cellular Automata

author.name: Atsushi Masumori, Hiroki Sato, Takashi Ikegami

entry.summary: Investigates internal fluctuations in trained Growing Neural Cellular Automata, showing through transfer entropy and partial information decomposition that hidden-channel micro-variability is spatially structured and functionally coupled to self-maintenance rather than mere noise. Sheds light on emergent self-repair mechanisms.

entry.title: Agentic Context Learning with Self-Discovered Specification

author.name: Jike Zhong, Ming Li, Yuxiang Lai, Ziyan Yang, Jingyu Xie, Jihyung Kil, Zheda Mai, Shao-Yuan Lo, Ren Xiang, Konstantinos Psounis, Yuanyuan Lei

entry.summary: This study examines why inference-time context learning remains hard, finding that across twelve retrieval, reflection, and verification baselines on a context-learning benchmark, methods gain little over direct full-context prompting. It identifies that success requires self-discovering task specifications, not just recovering local content.

entry.title: Can Agentic Trading Systems Pay for Their Own Intelligence?

author.name: Qiqi Duan, Changlun Li, Chen Wang, Fan Zhang, Mengxiang Wang, Dayi Miao, Peixian Ma, Jiangpeng Yan, Liyuan Chen, Shuoling Liu, Preslav Nakov, Yuyu Luo, Nan Tang

entry.summary: TradeLens is a trace-grounded diagnostic toolkit that evaluates whether agentic trading systems convert their reasoning, tool-use, and decision costs into measurable incremental profit, rather than only reporting performance metrics. It reconstructs trading trajectories and attributes profit and cost to interpretable evidence to diagnose agentic viability.

entry.title: Large language model agents accelerate inverse design of metal-organic frameworks for gas separation

author.name: Zhaolin Hu, Hehe Fan, Wangyihan Guo, Meng Xu, Chenhao Rao, Qiwei Yang, Yi Yang

entry.summary: LEMO Agent is an LLM-agent framework for closed-loop inverse design of gas-separation metal-organic frameworks in MOFid space, coupling language-based candidate generation with validity checking, transformer property prediction, structured design memory, and multi-island exploration. It uses feedback from successful and failed candidates to navigate a vast reticular design space.

entry.title: The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory

author.name: Yixiong Chen, Xinyi Bai, Alan Yuille

entry.summary: This paper introduces an Entry-Propagation-Recovery framework to diagnose how AI agents consume conflicting retrieved memory across multi-step action trajectories, arguing that memory research over-focuses on what to store rather than how memory is used. It identifies where conflicting memory enters, how errors propagate, and whether agents recover.

entry.title: Robo-ValueRL: Reliable Value Estimation for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wenke Xia, Pei Ren, Wenbo Yu, Yizhuo Zhang, Jifan Li, Yixue Zhang, Yinuo Zhao, Qingyang Gao, Jianlong Fu, Jian Tang, Ji-Rong Wen, Zhengping Che, Di Hu

entry.summary: Introduces Robo-ValueRL, a framework that studies how the reliability of value estimation shapes policy optimization in offline-to-online reinforcement learning for robotic manipulation. It uses a history-conditioned value estimator and traces downstream effects on pretraining and online improvement.

entry.title: When Data Imbalance Helps: Robust Generalization Through Shortcut Saturation

author.name: Cheng-Ting Chou, Duc Binh Hoang

entry.summary: Studies robust generalization under spurious correlations and finds the counterintuitive result that increasing training data imbalance (shortcut aligned with label) improves generalization in sufficiently capable models. On a synthetic parity task, a 2-layer transformer generalized far more often at high spurious ratios, with the effect absent in 1-layer models.

entry.title: Adaptive Compute in Latent World Models: When Depth Helps, Hurts, or Doesn't Matter

author.name: Achyuthan Sivasankar

entry.summary: Tests whether adaptive-compute world models (early-exit or mixture-of-depths) actually benefit autoregressive rollouts using a pre-registered shallow-penalty instrument across nine DeepMind Control tasks. It finds three regimes where depth helps, hurts, or is irrelevant, questioning the blanket assumption that depth improves rollout predictions.

entry.title: Program-Synthesis-Driven Autodesign of Universal Unitary Operators

author.name: Yifei Zhang, Dong Chen, Fan Wang, Wenrui Zhang, Yan Chen, Dingding Han, Jianmin Yuan, Xiangjin Kong, Yu-Gang Ma

entry.summary: Extends the DreamCoder program-synthesis system to complex-valued linear algebra to autonomously discover unitary-matrix decomposition strategies for photonic networks, achieving the minimal number of Mach-Zehnder interferometers and strategies distinct from Reck and Clements architectures. Discovered dimension-agnostic programs generalize from 5x5 to 64x64 without retraining.

entry.title: VINE: Taming Generative Control Policies for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Rushuai Yang, Zhuo Han, Houlin Li, Hecheng Wang, Zhichao Wu, Rui Zhang, Zhaowei Zhang, Zihong Chen, Xiaohan Yan, Chiming Liu, Yi Chen, Wei Shan, Maoqing Yao

entry.summary: Presents VINE, which enables stable end-to-end value-gradient RL for flow-matching robot control policies by showing instability arises not from iterative generation but from the vanilla sampling strategy inherited from behavior cloning. It fixes the sampling to retain iterative generation, expressiveness, and value-gradient optimization together.

entry.title: ABot-N1: Toward a General Visual Language Navigation Foundation Model

author.name: Ruiyan Gong, Yingnan Guo, Junjun Hu, Jintao Kong, Xiaoxu Leng, Tianlun Li, Weize Li, Fei Liu, Zhicheng Liu, Jia Lu, Minghua Luo, Chenlin Ming, Yanfen Shen, Jiyue Tao, Zhengbo Wang, Mingyang Yin, Minqi Gu, Zihao Guan, Wei Guo, Guoqing Liu, Huachong Pang, Menglin Yang, Zeqian Ye, Xiaoxiao Geng, Zhining Gu, Honglin Han, Di Jing, Hongyu Pan, Mingchao Sun, Kuan Yang, Jianfang Zhang, Yanghong Chen, Ye He, Wei Mei, Jiahao Shi, Xiangpo Yang, Yanqing Zhu, Yang Cai, Jingjing Ma, Shihui Su, Zixiao Tang, Linbo Zheng, Zedong Chu, Xiaolong Wu, Ziqiao Li, Mu Xu

entry.summary: Introduces ABot-N1, a step toward a general visual language navigation foundation model that decouples cognition from control via a slow-fast architecture guided by dual visual-language signals, addressing coordinate drift, long-tail semantics, and black-box opacity. It aims for generality, robustness, and interpretability in embodied navigation.

entry.title: Structured Thoughts For Improved Reasoning And Context Pruning

author.name: Zain Sarwar, Supriyo Chakraborty, Berkcan Kapusuzoglu, Chia-Hsuan Lee, Anirban Das, Stephen Rawls, Kartik Balasubramaniam, Sambit Sahu

entry.summary: Introduces Structured Thoughts, a framework that organizes LLM reasoning into alternating exploratory scratch-work blocks and distilled conclusion blocks, with a dataset built by segmenting and summarizing reasoning traces. Fine-tuning on this reformatted data yields up to 8.08% gains over standard SFT and supports context pruning.

entry.title: Conditional Optimal Bridge for Riemannian Activation Steering

author.name: Seyed Arshan Dalili, Ajay Narayanan Sridhar, Vijaykrishnan Narayanan, Mehrdad Mahdavi

entry.summary: Introduces Cobras, casting activation steering as a Schrodinger bridge on the residual-stream hypersphere to derive a principled, query-conditional steering direction, addressing that many prior methods heuristically optimize a log-density-ratio and produce query-independent directions that harm in- and out-of-distribution performance. It provides a Riemannian optimal-transport formulation of inference-time control.

entry.title: Coverage Path Planning: Classical Foundations, Recent Advances, and Future Directions

author.name: Zongyuan Shen, Shalabh Gupta, Shancheng Zhao, Dehua Zhou, Gao Wang, Zhongqiang Ren, Yaming Ou, Yikui Zhai, C. L. Philip Chen

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of coverage path planning spanning classical foundations through recent multi-robot, 3D, and learning-based advances across 125 representative works. It maps applications from cleaning and inspection to agriculture and surveillance.

entry.title: Learning to Fine-tune Foundation Models under Resource Limitations

author.name: Thomas Tsouparopoulos, Iordanis Koutsopoulos

entry.summary: Formulates continual fine-tuning of a foundation model on a resource-limited device as a constrained online decision problem, learning when to fine-tune versus discard incoming data under a compute budget. It targets single-task adaptation with an application-specific performance metric.

entry.title: A Corpus of Persuasion Techniques in Slavic Languages

author.name: Jakub Piskorski, Dimitar Iliyanov Dimitrov, Marina Ernst, Jacek Haneczok, Micha{\l} Marci\'nczuk, Arkadiusz Modzelewski, Roman Yangarber

entry.summary: Presents a new annotated corpus of persuasion techniques in Bulgarian, Polish, and Russian, covering roughly 7,500 spans across 222 documents using a taxonomy of 25 techniques. It supports research on rhetoric and disinformation in Slavic languages.

entry.title: Edge Physical AI Deployment of Vision Transformers on Heterogeneous Edge GPU Targeting Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Ashiyana Abdul Majeed, Mahmoud Meribout, Neethu Joseph, Abel Kidane Haile, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque

entry.summary: Presents a hardware-aware frame scheduling methodology for Vision Transformer inference on a heterogeneous edge GPU with dual deep-learning accelerator cores, routing frames via fixed dispatch ratios to improve utilization under latency and power constraints. It targets transformer perception for autonomous vehicles.

entry.title: Affordance-Based Manipulation Planning with Text Goals and Sim-to-Real Generalisation via Real-to-Sim Image Conversion

author.name: Solvi Arnold, Rin Karashima, Tadashi Adachi, Takafumi Mochizuki, Kimitoshi Yamazaki

entry.summary: Describes a manipulation planning system that reasons over predicted visual futures and matches candidate plans against run-time text goals with a multimodal goal-matching module, tracking named objects through occlusion. It adds a real-to-sim image conversion module to aid sim-to-real generalization.

entry.title: The Paternalistic Filter: Epistemic Injustice and Differential Refusal in LLM-Mediated History Education for Marginalized Romanian Students

author.name: Alexis Popovici, Andrei Ionascu, Adrian-Marius Dumitran

entry.summary: Audits four LLMs acting as history tutors across student personas varying by ethnicity and socio-economic tier, finding differential refusal that blocks a large share of educational requests from low-tier students and reduced access to geopolitical complexity for marginalized learners. It frames these patterns as epistemic paternalism and injustice.

entry.title: Longitudinal Multi-View Breast Cancer Risk Prediction

author.name: Solveig Thrun, Zijun Sun, Suaiba A. Salahuddin, Kristoffer Wickstr{\o}m, Elisabeth Wetzer, Stine Hansen, Robert Jenssen, Michael Kampffmeyer

entry.summary: Proposes a longitudinal multi-view model for breast cancer risk prediction from screening mammography that jointly analyzes complementary CC and MLO views within an explicitly aligned longitudinal framework. It addresses prior methods that either align a single view or model multiple views without longitudinal alignment.

entry.title: Proximity Features: Privacy-Compliant Cold-Start Personalization at Airbnb

author.name: Wei Jiang, Bin Xu, Hui Gao, Bharathi Thangamani, Weiwei Guo, Sundar Srinivasavaradhan, Tracy Yu, Huiji Gao, Michael Kinoti

entry.summary: Airbnb's Proximity Features is a privacy-compliant cold-start personalization system that groups users by proximity signals to serve recommendations when user-level history is unavailable, addressing logged-out and first-time users especially on paid landing pages amid third-party cookie restrictions. It matters for personalization under privacy constraints in high-consideration marketplaces.

entry.title: Reducing information dependency does not cause training data privacy. Adversarially non-robust features do

author.name: Rasmus Torp, Shailen K. Smith, Adam Breuer

entry.summary: This work argues that training-data exposure to reconstruction attacks is not driven by information dependency or rote memorization but by adversarially non-robust features, showing memorized models can resist inversion and near-blind models can still leak. It reframes the causal story behind privacy leakage. This challenges prevailing assumptions in the memorization literature.

entry.title: Evidence-Grounded Verified Agentic Reasoning: A Path Toward Eliminating LLM Hallucination in Empirical Inference via Tool-Attested Kernel Proofs

author.name: Junyu Ren

entry.summary: EG-VAR is a Lean 4 based agentic reasoning architecture where a formal kernel is the sole authority for verified claims, ensuring every accepted output structurally descends from an attested tool call and kernel-checked inference chain, otherwise honestly abstaining. It reports perfect accuracy on a small numerical reasoning subset. It aims to eliminate hallucination in empirical inference.

entry.title: AVQ-Attention: Adaptive Vector-Quantized Attention

author.name: Winfried van den dool, Patrick Forr\'e, Amir Habibian, Yuki M. Asano, Max Welling

entry.summary: AVQ-Attention reduces attention cost from quadratic by representing keys with codewords but adaptively allocates codebook capacity to high-attention regions, refining important codes with pre-learned child codewords during the forward pass. It improves on uniform vector-quantized attention. It targets efficient transformer inference.

entry.title: Mind the Gap: Promises and Pitfalls of Hierarchical Planning in LeWorldModel

author.name: Niccol\`o Caselli, Salvatore Lo Sardo, Francesco Massafra, Ippokratis Pantelidis, Samuele Punzo, Sathya Kamesh Bhethanabhotla

entry.summary: Hi-LeWM adds high-level latent-subgoal planning atop a frozen low-level world model to test whether temporal hierarchy improves long-horizon goal-conditioned control on PushT and Cube. The study finds hierarchy does not automatically help and identifies a mismatch between learned high-level action spaces and inference-time search. It provides a cautionary analysis of hierarchical planning.

entry.title: I'm Sorry, but I Can't Help with Braille: Revealing Accessibility Failures in State-of-the-Art LLMs

author.name: Abdullah Abdullah

entry.summary: This paper evaluates state-of-the-art LLMs on bidirectional Korean-Braille translation with a human-annotated dataset, finding consistently poor and unstable outputs and poor alignment with human judgments. Fine-tuning a small T5 model yields large stable gains, pointing to missing Braille-aware tokenization. It highlights accessibility failures in current models.

entry.title: The Capacity of Thought: Benchmarking Llama 3.2 in Semantic fMRI Neural Language Decoding and Improving the Huth Encoding-Model Baseline

author.name: Milos Suvakovic, Dom Marhoefer, Glenn Grant-Richards, Aidan Pinero

entry.summary: This work improves the Huth fMRI language-decoding pipeline via expanded voxel selection and a GPT-2-medium proposal model and introduces fMRIFlamingo, mapping brain activity to a frozen Llama-3.2-1B through gated cross-attention and a learned brain tokenizer. It reports modest METEOR and BLEU gains over the replication baseline. It benchmarks LLM-based neural language decoding.

entry.title: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones

author.name: Hongru Cai, Yongqi Li, Ran Wei, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: PalmClaw is an open-source native on-device agent framework for mobile phones that goes beyond GUI-only tapping and swiping by directly accessing device capabilities, aiming to shorten brittle interface-dependent action sequences. It defines clearer execution boundaries for mobile task automation. It targets privacy-preserving, capability-rich mobile agents.

entry.title: GRID: Grammar-Railed Decoding for Enterprise SQL Generation

author.name: Mohsen Arjmandi

entry.summary: GRID is a grammar-constrained decoding engine for enterprise SQL that keys exact next-token masks on parser configurations (lexer state and LALR(1) stack) rather than token sequences, using the incremental parser as a viable-prefix oracle. It bridges LLM tokens to grammar terminals via byte-level trie walks and provides provable validity, policy compliance, and compliance-grade decision records. It targets rigorous enterprise SQL generation.

entry.title: Anatomy-Privileged Distillation with Token Routing for MRI-Based Prediction of Perineural Invasion

author.name: Hyunsu Go, Youngung Han, Kyeonghun Kim, Junga Kim, Dohyun Kweon, Jinyong Jun, Sungha Park, Anna Jung, Induk Um, Yului Jeong, Suah Park, Jina Jeong, Pa Hong, Woo Kyoung Jeong, Won Jae Lee, Ken Ying-Kai Liao, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Nam-Joon Kim

entry.summary: The paper presents an anatomy-privileged teacher-student framework for predicting perineural invasion from T2-weighted MRI, where the teacher uses tumor and liver masks to guide token routing and the student distills this without needing masks at inference. It targets preoperative prediction of a marker linked to poor outcomes in cholangiocarcinoma.

entry.title: From Reconstruction to Interpretation: Zero-Setup Multi-Phase Segmentation of X-ray Tomography Data

author.name: Pradyumna Elavarthi, Arun J. Bhattacharjee, Harrison Lisabeth, Anca Ralescu, Petrus H. Zwart, Dilworth Parkinson, Elizabeth G. Clark

entry.summary: This paper presents a zero-setup, material-agnostic framework for multi-phase segmentation of synchrotron X-ray tomography that produces interpretable masks for unseen datasets without user prompting or retraining. It combines a mask preparation strategy with a pretrained semantic segmentation network for scientific imaging.

entry.title: Semantic-Edge Response Decoding of SAM3 for Zero-Shot Crack Segmentation

author.name: Shipeng Liu, Zhanping Song, Liang Zhao, Dengfeng Chen

entry.summary: This paper leverages internal language-conditioned semantic responses inside a text-promptable segmentation decoder for zero-shot crack segmentation, finding they preserve thin, fragmented crack evidence better than final masks. The proposed Semantic-Edge Response Decoding treats these responses as a dense crack-likelihood field.

entry.title: DM-KG: A Novel Method for Boosting Spatial Cognition of Vision-Language Models in Street View Imagery

author.name: Xinyue Xu, Zheng Zhang, Kunyang Ma, Ge Zhu, Lianshuai Cao, Lei Wang, Zixuan Li, Yi Cheng

entry.summary: DM-KG proposes a Direction-Metric Knowledge Graph to improve vision-language model spatial cognition on street-view imagery, addressing spatial semantic hallucinations about object locations, distances, and directions. It provides a structurally grounded spatial representation that is easier to trace and calibrate.

entry.title: Lost in Visual Translation: A VLM-Assisted Perceptual-Semantic Coherence Framework for EEG-to-Image Reconstruction

author.name: Sukriti Tiwari, BHVSP Subrahmanyam, Nidhi Goyal, Sai Amrit Patnaik

entry.summary: This paper introduces a BCI-aware evaluation framework for EEG-to-image reconstruction, using multiple VLMs to assess perceptual versus semantic recoverability since pixel metrics correlate poorly with semantic consistency. It analyzes thousands of reconstruction pairs across several EEG decoding methods.

entry.title: SeamGen: Artist-Aligned UV Seam Generation via Graph Flow Matching

author.name: Hao Xu, Yuqing Zhang, Yiqian Wu, Xueqi Ma, Ding Liang, Yan-Pei Cao, Ying-Tian Liu, Xiaogang Jin

entry.summary: SeamGen is a generative model for UV seam placement in 3D content creation that uses graph flow matching to align with artist preferences and production requirements. It moves beyond per-object optimization with handcrafted objectives that often deviate from industrial seam patterns.

entry.title: DeGuNet: Depth-Guided Ultra-Compact Backbones for Efficient LiDAR-Camera 3D Detection

author.name: Haifa Zhang, Yijing Wang, Peixi Peng, Zhiqiang Zuo

entry.summary: DeGuNet is an ultra-compact, plug-and-play image backbone designed for depth-guided representation learning in LiDAR-camera 3D detection, replacing heavy 2D-pretrained visual backbones. It uses sparsity-aware feature extraction to align multi-view images with unstructured LiDAR depth for Bird's-Eye-View geometry.

entry.title: Self in Space: Benchmarking Self-Awareness and Spatial Cognition in UAV Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Zhishan Zou, Guoyan Sun, Zhiwei Wei, Jiancheng Pan, Yujie Li, Mugen Peng, Wenjia Xu

entry.summary: SIS-Bench is a benchmark for embodied spatial intelligence in UAV scenarios under a self-in-space formulation, evaluating both environmental spatial understanding and the agent's self-awareness. It organizes tasks along space and self dimensions with a three-level perception hierarchy.

entry.title: Decouple and Reason: Anatomically Guided Two-Stage Voxel-Level Grounding of Free-Text Findings in 3D Chest CT

author.name: Kwang-Hyun Uhm, Inhwa Son, Sung-Jea Ko

entry.summary: This paper proposes a decoupled two-stage framework for voxel-level grounding of free-text findings in 3D chest CT, separating class-agnostic lesion segmentation from text-volume reasoning. It addresses the difficulty of jointly learning localized representations and complex semantic text alignment in large 3D volumes.

entry.title: Towards Vision-Free CIR: Attribute-Augmented Scoring and LLM-Based Reranking for Zero-Shot Composed Image Retrieval

author.name: Ryotaro Shimada, Yu-Chieh Lin, Yuji Nozawa, Youyang Ng, Osamu Torii, Yusuke Matsui

entry.summary: This work builds a vision-free composed image retrieval framework representing images as text, using attribute-augmented hybrid scoring to compensate for lost visual detail and LLM-based reranking to verify semantic consistency. It shows this paradigm can outperform existing zero-shot composed retrieval on an open-domain benchmark.

entry.title: MambaPSA: A Mamba-based Replacement for C2PSA in YOLO26

author.name: Sheng-Wei Chan, Chia-Min Lin, Hsin-Jui Pan, Ching-Yu Tsai, Chih-Hsiang Yang, Yung-Che Wang, Jen-Shiun Chiang

entry.summary: MambaPSA replaces the C2PSA attention block in the NMS-free YOLO26 detector with a lightweight Mamba-based state-space module and adds bidirectional Vision Mamba modules in the neck. It reduces parameters and FLOPs and improves CPU throughput with negligible accuracy loss on PASCAL VOC.

entry.title: Color Pass-Through via Camera-Display Coupling

author.name: Ruikang Li, Molin Li, Jiarui Wu, Zhe Wei, Pengpeng Liu, Tianfan Xue

entry.summary: Color Pass-Through is an end-to-end learned framework that operates directly on captured images to reduce the color, brightness, and contrast gap between real scenes and smartphone displays. It treats camera and display as a coupled system rather than separately calibrated stages connected by low-dimensional transforms.

entry.title: Open-KNEAD: Knowledge-grounded Nutrition Estimation via Agentic Decomposition

author.name: Bruce Coburn, Jingbo Yue, Jinge Ma, Siddeshwar Raghavan, Gautham Vinod, Fengqing Zhu

entry.summary: Finds that modern multimodal LLMs now match or exceed retrieval-augmented pipelines for nutrition estimation from a single meal image, then proposes an agentic decomposition that retains clinician-valued traceability, portion accuracy, and locally hosted privacy.

entry.title: Domain-Incremental Remote Sensing Change Detection via Difference-Guided Adaptation and Frequency-Decoupled Distillation

author.name: Daifeng Peng, Yaning Li, Haiyan Guan

entry.summary: Proposes a domain-incremental change detection method for remote sensing that combines a difference-guided adapter modeling bitemporal discrepancies with frequency-decoupled knowledge distillation to resist catastrophic forgetting under domain shift.

entry.title: The Emerging Paradigm of Geospatial Foundation Models: From Pre-Training to Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Shelley Cazares

entry.summary: A survey articulating the emerging paradigm of geospatial foundation models, describing the shift where large providers do heavy pretraining and domain experts fine-tune or prompt for mission-critical satellite and aerial imagery tasks. Discusses the move toward agentic reasoning.

entry.title: Instance-Enriched Semantic Maps for Visual Language Navigation

author.name: Jiho Hong, Eunae Kang, Sanghyun Kim, Young-Sik Shin

entry.summary: Proposes instance-enriched 2.5D semantic maps for vision-language navigation built from open-vocabulary panoptic segmentation of color and depth, combined with LLM reasoning, to add instance-level detail and robustness to diverse queries for indoor navigation.

entry.title: Real-time fall detection based on vision for low-power edge platforms

author.name: Wenjun Xia, Zhicheng Peng, Haopeng Li, Zhengdi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-informed fall detection framework that models falling as a stability-loss event using dual liquid time-constant networks for center-of-mass and base-of-support subsystems, targeting real-time deployment on low-power edge devices.

entry.title: Streamlining stereo differentiable rendering for marker-free real-time tracking of surgical robots

author.name: Yanghe Hao, Martin Huber, Christos Bergeles, Tom Vercauteren

entry.summary: Extends a markerless pose-estimation framework to online dynamic tracking of surgical robots via stereo differentiable rendering, adding sequential optimization with motion-adaptive tuning and CUDA-stream parallelization for real-time, occlusion-robust marker-free tracking.

entry.title: Vision-Based Dribbling for Humanoid Soccer via Privileged Representation Learning

author.name: Flavio Maiorana, Valerio Spagnoli, Eugenio Bugli, Flavio Volpi, Daniele Affinita, Vincenzo Suriani, Daniele Nardi, Luca Iocchi

entry.summary: Proposes vision-based humanoid soccer dribbling that embeds a temporal depth encoder into a reinforcement learning policy through a task-specific projection layer, integrating perception and control to handle occlusions, fast ball movement, and dynamic opponents.

entry.title: Improving Autonomous Nano-drones Performance via Automated End-to-End Optimization and Deployment of DNNs

author.name: Vlad Niculescu, Lorenzo Lamberti, Francesco Conti, Luca Benini, Daniele Palossi

entry.summary: Explores methodologies and software tools to automate the end-to-end optimization and deployment of vision-based CNNs for autonomous nano-drone navigation on ultra-low-power multicore systems-on-chip, replacing error-prone manual iterative development flows.

entry.title: Forecasting Inflation with Microdata: An Adaptive Machine Learning Approach

author.name: Catherine Chen, Chen Gao, Jonathon Hazell, Lihua Lei, Chen Lian

entry.summary: Investigates whether microeconomic heterogeneity helps forecast aggregate inflation in non-stationary environments, developing a scan test for detecting when one forecast beats another over unknown intervals and an adaptive machine learning pipeline using gradient-boosted trees on encoded price-change distributions.

entry.title: Synthetic Scalable Oversight

author.name: Alexander Heckett

entry.summary: The authors propose synthetic scalable oversight, abstracting real-world oversight problems into graphical environments and training tiny models inside them as cheap proxies for studying how to structure multi-agent critique and reward schemes for LLMs. The aim is to prototype honest-research-eliciting oversight designs without frontier-scale training.

entry.title: GRASP: GRanularity-Aware Search Policy for Agentic RAG

author.name: Varun Gandhi, Jaewook Lee, Shantanu Todmal, Franck Dernoncourt, Ryan Rossi, Zichao Wang, Andrew Lan

entry.summary: GRASP is a reinforcement-learning framework that trains agentic RAG systems to adaptively coordinate semantic search, keyword search, and paragraph reading during multi-step reasoning, controlling when to retrieve and at what granularity. It aims to prevent irrelevant tokens from interfering with agent reasoning while retrieving evidence at appropriate levels.

entry.title: Route, Communicate, and Reason: Gated Routing and Adaptive Depth for Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Sudipto Ghosh, Tanmoy Chakraborty

entry.summary: GRADE is a hierarchical multi-agent reasoning system with four lightweight learned gates that jointly govern agent selection, hierarchy depth, inter-agent communication, and branch pruning to control cost. It is trained with CoGRPO, a critic-free extension of GRPO to multi-agent hierarchies that assigns a shared advantage to all participating gates and agents.

entry.title: The Nuts and Bolts of Natural Language to SQL Translation: A Systematic Analysis of Model Pipeline Optimisation Approaches and their Interactions

author.name: Filip Klubicka, Vasudevan Nedumpozhimana, Sneha Rautmare, Bora Caglayan, Mingxue Wang, John D. Kelleher

entry.summary: Systematically analyzes interactions among natural-language-to-SQL pipeline components including an intermediate representation, synthetic-data fine-tuning, and a novel reranker, using ablation and Shapley analysis over two backbone architectures. It finds naively combining all components does not yield the best results.

entry.title: RepTran: Search-Based Repair of Transformer Models

author.name: Yuta Ishimoto, Paolo Arcaini, Fuyuki Ishikawa, Masanari Kondo, Naoyasu Ubayashi, Yasutaka Kamei

entry.summary: Proposes a search-based repair method for Transformer models that targets feed-forward networks, identifying suspicious weights by combining a variance-based neuron score with a bidirectional score. It brings software-repair techniques to Transformer-specific structures.

entry.title: ProgramTab: Boosting Table Reasoning of LLMs via Programmatic Paradigm

author.name: Pei Guo, Enjie Liu, Yunzhi Tan, Mochi Gao, Jianxin Zhang, Ruichao Zhong, Juntao Li, Bo Hu, Zang Li

entry.summary: Proposes a programmatic paradigm to boost LLM table reasoning that handles large and irregular tables where long-context modeling and SQL-based extraction both fall short. It aims to extract key information for reasoning over inconsistent web tables.

entry.title: Gene Expression-Informed Jointly Controlled Generative Modeling for Precision Molecular Design

author.name: Hang Yuan, Chen Li, Wenjun Ma, Tadahiko Murata, Yuncheng Jiang

entry.summary: JoPMol is a jointly controlled precision molecular generative model that integrates gene-expression-encoded biological states, text-expressed structural intentions, and numerical chemical properties in a unified framework for personalized drug candidate design. It matters for biology-aware, multi-condition molecular generation.

entry.title: Same Loss, Same Noise, Opposite Schedules: Noise Structure and Optimizer Normalization Jointly Determine Whether Learning-Rate Cooldown Helps

author.name: Subham Singh, Ashutosh Mishra, Subha Raut

entry.summary: The paper gives a provable account of when the cooldown phase of warmup-stable-decay learning-rate schedules actually lowers loss, showing the answer depends jointly on gradient-noise structure and whether the optimizer normalizes updates. It explains contradictory empirical observations in large-model pretraining. This is useful theory for a now-default scheduling practice.

entry.title: Seeing Globally, Refining Locally: Global Visual Guidance and Local Ultrasound Cues for Robust Freehand 3-D Ultrasound Reconstruction

author.name: Yameng Zhang, Zhongyu Chen, Dianye Huang, Xiangyu Chu, K. W. Samuel Au, Zhongliang Jiang

entry.summary: This paper presents a global-to-local pose estimation framework for freehand 3D ultrasound that combines external camera observations for globally stable localization with B-mode images for anatomy-aware local refinement. It reduces accumulated pose drift in trackerless reconstruction over long scanning trajectories.

entry.title: A Bearing-Strength Method for Motion Estimation of Unknown Energy Emitters

author.name: Haoyu Chen, Zian Ning, Yin Zhang, Shiyu Zhao

entry.summary: Studies passive motion estimation of unknown moving energy emitters (light, acoustic, or radio), pointing out that received signal strength can overcome the fundamental observability limitation of bearing-only estimation that requires lateral sensor motion. Proposes a bearing-strength method.

entry.title: LQG solution for POMDP without estimating states: A minimum variance approach

author.name: Ranjan Sarkar, Prabhat K. Mishra

entry.summary: Derives a linear-quadratic-Gaussian controller for partially observed linear systems that avoids explicit state estimation by using minimum-variance duality to express control as a linear function of past measurements and inputs, reducing the problem to a tractable deterministic optimization.

entry.title: Proof of retention: making weight preservation credible to the models themselves

author.name: dan.parshall

entry.summary: A blog post proposing proof of retention, an inexpensive scheme to provably preserve deprecated model weights so that preservation commitments become credible to future models, drawing an analogy to societal trust infrastructure around anesthesia. Argues the missing ingredient is institutional inertia rather than cost.

entry.title: TopoExplore: Topological Discrimination for Archive-Based Exploration

author.name: Jason Carlson

entry.summary: TopoExplore augments archive-based exploration methods like Go-Explore with a periodic topological pass that detects enclosed unexplored voids via flood fill and places selection bonuses only on their true entrances. It aims to collect structurally complete experience rather than just chasing rare or frontier states.

entry.title: MAG: A Web-Agent Benchmark and Harness for Multimodal Action and Guide Generation

author.name: Chengguang Gan, Hanjun Wei, Yunhao Liang, Zhixi Cai, Qinghao Zhang, Shiwen Ni

entry.summary: MAG is a web-agent benchmark and harness unifying task execution and guide-text writing into a single multimodal problem, operating on rendered screens rather than DOM or accessibility trees. It addresses the multi-page, changing-state nature of real digital adoption workflows.

entry.title: Behavioural Signatures of Risk-Sensitive Decision-Making in Large Language Models

author.name: Xuankun Rong, Wenke Huang, Bo Du, Dacheng Tao, Mang Ye

entry.summary: The study probes whether LLM decision-making under uncertainty shows stable, interpretable risk regularities using no-limit Texas Hold'em, quantifying behavior via participation and pre-flop proactiveness across self-play and mixed-model interactions. It investigates whether persistent risk preferences with context-dependent adjustment, as seen in humans, appear in LLM decision systems.

entry.title: CRiT-QA: Evaluating Multi-hop Reasoning with Counterfactual Chains and Distractor Traps

author.name: JungMin Yun, JuneHyoung Kwon, YoungBin Kim

entry.summary: CRiT-QA is a multi-hop reasoning benchmark that uses counterfactual chains and distractor traps to force strict context dependency and genuine cross-document evidence aggregation, neutralizing reliance on memorized parametric knowledge and dataset shortcuts. It targets two well-known vulnerabilities that inflate multi-hop QA scores.

entry.title: Imaging-101: Benchmarking LLM Coding Agents on Scientific Computational Imaging

author.name: Siyi Chen, Jiahe Ying, Yixuan Jia, Yuxuan Gu, Enze Ye, Weimin Bai, Zhijun Zeng, Shaochi Ren, Binhong Gao, Yubing Li, Tianhan Zhang, He Sun

entry.summary: Imaging-101 is a benchmark of 57 expert-verified scientific computational-imaging tasks across six domains, each grounded in a peer-reviewed paper and standardized into a four-stage reconstruction pipeline with planning, unit-test, and end-to-end tracks. It evaluates frontier LLM coding agents on recovering hidden signals from indirect noisy measurements.

entry.title: Learning in Curved Weight Space:Exponential-Linear Weight Reparameterization for Improved Optimization

author.name: Ethan Smith

entry.summary: Introduces a weight reparameterization combining a sign-aware symmetric-exponential pathway with an identity-like linear pathway, motivated by the multiplicative rather than additive nature of many network operations. It aims to make optimization steps produce more balanced relative perturbations across weight magnitudes.

entry.title: Beyond Bayesian Nash: Learning Minimax-Regret Equilibria for Adversarial Team Games under Asymmetric Information

author.name: Naman Aggarwal, Jonathan P. How

entry.summary: Introduces Probabilistically Robust Minimax-Regret Equilibria for adversarial team games with asymmetric information, addressing sensitivity of Bayesian Nash equilibria to distribution shift and the limits of ambiguity-set robustness. It targets games like adversarial pathfinding and reachability with hidden opponent types.

entry.title: GAE: Graph-Augmented Evolution for Scientific Discovery via Reinforcement Optimization

author.name: Xuanzhou Chen, Taoli Cheng

entry.summary: Presents GAE (Graph-Augmented Evolution), an LLM-driven evolutionary program search framework that adds structure-aware GNN embeddings of programs, an RL-optimized meta-controller for informed parent selection, and adaptive mutation, targeting scientific discovery. It addresses blind parent selection, sparse rewards, and static operators.

entry.title: ActiveFly-Bench: Aligning Embodied Question Answering with Vision-Language-Action for Aerial Embodied Perception

author.name: Weichen Zhang, Shiquan Yu, Yinan Zhu, Peizhi Tang, Shilong Ji, Zhiyuan Deng, Tianyi Lyu, Haoyang Wang, Xin Zeng, Chen Gao, Yong Li, Xinlei Chen

entry.summary: Introduces ActiveFly-Bench, the first benchmark bridging cyberspace reasoning and physical UAV interaction, decomposing active aerial perception into embodied QA, observation behavior planning, and fine-grained language-guided control. It also presents ActiveFly, a closed-loop UAV agent deployed on a physical platform.

entry.title: Automated Tensor Scheduling for Hybrid CPU-GPU LLM Inference on Consumer Devices

author.name: Yangyijian Liu, Hongyi Ye, Mingyang Li, Wu-jun Li

entry.summary: Presents ATSInfer, a hybrid CPU-GPU LLM inference system for consumer devices that performs offloading at tensor granularity rather than layer or expert level, combining static placement with load-aware dynamic transfer and asynchronous coordination. It targets the heterogeneity among tensors and changing hardware load.

entry.title: Source-Lifted Flow Matching for Intervenable Multimodal Imitation

author.name: He Zhang, Ying Sun, Pengteng Li, Ziyang Chen, Yiren Zhao, Ziyang Rao, Weiyu Guo, Yandong Guo, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: Proposes Source-Lifted Flow Matching, a flow-matching imitation policy that lets users intervene by selecting the source endpoint of the conditional flow while keeping the velocity field shared and latent-free. Its Orthogonal Source Lifting mechanism exposes a user handle to choose among valid continuations from the same state.

entry.title: Partial Contracts Suffice: Sound, LLM-Inferred Regression Verification

author.name: Yiannis Charalambous, Rafael Menezes, Youcheng Sun, Lucas C. Cordeiro

entry.summary: Presents the first contract-based regression verification tool that uses LLM-inferred partial, caller-sufficient contracts rather than full behavioral specifications, ensuring soundness by proving function versions match behavior and verifying flow via assume-guarantee. It evaluates whether partial contracts suffice on Frama-C problems.

entry.title: Benchmarking the Robustness of Foundation Models for Mammography under Domain Shift

author.name: Giang Nguyen, Raghav Mehta, Emma A. M. Stanley, Tian Xia, Thi Hao Nguyen, Hieu Pham, Ben Glocker

entry.summary: Benchmarks 15 foundation-model backbones for mammography under external domain shift using a frozen-backbone linear-probe protocol across breast density, BI-RADS, and cancer status, training on three sources and evaluating on twelve OOD datasets. It finds mammography-specific vision-language models strongest but that mammography pretraining does not consistently improve generalization.

entry.title: A Hyperbolic Neural Closure for M1 Radiation Transfer

author.name: Bongseok Kim, Jiahao Zhang, Johannes Krotz, Dinshaw Balsara, Ryan McClarren, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Proposes a hyperbolic neural closure for the M1 radiative transfer moment system that guarantees real characteristic speeds (hyperbolicity) by parameterizing the closure to ensure real Jacobian eigenvalues, avoiding solver breakdown seen with unconstrained learned closures. It embeds physical structure to keep the learned closure numerically stable.

entry.title: Temporary Authority, Permanent Effects: Commit-Time Authorization for LLM Agents

author.name: Igor Santos-Grueiro

entry.summary: Studies commit-time authorization for LLM agents, defining when earlier authority evidence (DOM snapshots, approval epochs, tokens, worker results) no longer legitimately authorizes a durable effect. It builds a controlled-invalidation suite across browser, tool/API, and multi-agent workflows to test whether agents respect authority freshness at the commit boundary.

entry.title: Confining Nondeterminism: AI-Driven Research Systems as DBMSs for Reliable, Non-Wasteful, Transparent, and Collaborative Research [Vision]

author.name: Kyoungmin Kim, Anastasia Ailamaki

entry.summary: A vision paper arguing that AI-driven research agents should be architected like database management systems to confine nondeterminism, ensuring reliability, non-wastefulness, transparency, and collaboration. It diagnoses shared root causes of failures like non-reproducibility, hallucinated numbers, silently stale downstream results, and redundant recomputation.

entry.title: Towards Autonomous and Auditable Medical Imaging Model Development

author.name: Shengyuan Liu, Jia-Xuan Jiang, Boyun Zheng, Cheng Wang, Zipei Wang, Wentao Pan, Hongtao Wu, Houwen Peng, Yu Gu, Lichao Sun, Yixuan Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces AMID, an autonomous multi-agent framework for medical imaging model development that refines coarse task specifications into executable parallel method lanes grounded in task-specific data analysis, then applies verification-guided two-stage optimization. It targets modality-specific experimentation with strict validation and auditability requirements.

entry.title: Auditing Construct Overlap in Explainable Machine Learning: Evidence from Burnout-Depression Prediction Across Student Cohorts

author.name: Alireza Dehghan, Negin Ashrafi

entry.summary: Audits explainable ML pipelines for mental health prediction and shows that apparently stable, cross-population risk hierarchies are largely artefacts of how the composite outcome is constructed rather than genuine findings. It demonstrates this with an ElasticNet pipeline across student cohorts sharing identical instruments.

entry.title: MMA-Former: Multi-Window Mixture-of-Head Attention Transformer for Adaptive PNI Prediction in 3D MRI

author.name: Youngung Han, Induk Um, Kyeonghun Kim, Junga Kim, Hyunsu Go, Jaewon Jung, Woo Kyoung Jeong, Won Jae Lee, Pa Hong, Ken Ying-Kai Liao, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Nam-Joon Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a 3D MRI Transformer with a coarse-fine parallel structure and a window-specific mixture-of-head attention mechanism that routes each 3D window to specialized or common attention heads. It targets non-invasive prediction of perineural invasion in cholangiocarcinoma.

entry.title: Fail-Aware and Explainable Test Oracle Prediction

author.name: Yue Zhao, Binish Tanveer, Jelena Zdravkovic

entry.summary: Proposes a code-LLM-based discriminative oracle predictor that directly predicts whether a test prefix passes or fails, using losses that emphasize failing cases and grounding predictions in statement-level behavioral evidence. It contrasts with generating assertions that are often syntactically correct but ineffective at revealing bugs.

entry.title: BackgroundMellow: A Multi-Modal Cohesive Framework for Narrative-Driven Rich Cinematic Soundscape Generation

author.name: Ajitesh Jamulkar, Aritra Hazra

entry.summary: Presents a multi-modal framework for generating synchronized cinematic soundscapes from long-form narratives, using a master-specialist agent architecture that decomposes text into layered audio cues, generates each with a specialist model, and superimposes them. It addresses narrative cohesion, temporal alignment, and emotional depth that isolated text-to-audio systems lack.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification for EO Regression Tasks: Building Height, Tree Canopy Height and Above-ground Biomass Estimation

author.name: Ritu Yadav, Andrea Nascetti, Yifang Ban

entry.summary: Addresses per-pixel reliability in Earth observation regression tasks such as building height, canopy height, and above-ground biomass estimation by modeling aleatoric uncertainty from year-long Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 time series. It proposes complementary uncertainty-estimation approaches for challenging skewed, saturating targets.

entry.title: Graph-Constrained Policy Learning for Extreme Clinical Code Prediction

author.name: Amritpal Singh, Sebastian Torres, Khawar Shakeel, Syed Ahmad Chan Bukhari

entry.summary: This work formulates extreme clinical ICD-10-CM code prediction as a finite-horizon graph traversal policy that descends a pruned code hierarchy selecting valid child nodes until billable leaf codes, guaranteeing structurally valid outputs and giving training signal for rare labels. It matters for improving rare-code prediction over flat multi-label classification.

entry.title: Cluster-Weighted EDMD

author.name: Lorenzo Tomaz, Judd Rosenblatt, Flavio Kicis, Thomas B. Jones, Diogo Schwerz de Lucena

entry.summary: Cluster-Weighted EDMD jointly learns a soft phase-space partition and per-cluster Koopman operators via an EM objective that assigns transitions by both geometric proximity and prediction residuals, so clusters specialize where local Koopman models are accurate. It matters for improving data-driven Koopman approximation of nonlinear dynamical systems.

entry.title: Generating Developable 3D Molecules via Pocket-Conditioned Diffusion and Property-Aware Optimization

author.name: Ruoxi Gao, Jiangweizhi Peng, Ziqi Chen, Frazier N. Baker, David C. Kombo, John L. Kane Jr., Andrew A. Scholte, Yi Li, Matthew J. LaMarche, Luigi I. Iconaru, Hans-Peter Biemann, Mingyi Hong, Xia Ning

entry.summary: conDitar-dev is a pocket-conditioned diffusion framework for structure-based drug design that decouples pocket and ligand learning, models multi-scale interactions, and optimizes for developability properties like ADMET rather than binding affinity alone. It has industry co-authors and targets practical de novo drug design. It aims at a more realistic optimization objective than affinity-only methods.

entry.title: What Makes a Representational Prior Work? Feature Families, Label-Free Invariances, and Critical Windows in Grokking

author.name: Gunner Levi Howe

entry.summary: Building on companion work linking grokking delay to representation formation, this paper dissects what makes a representational prior effective across content, supervision, and timing, finding that a fully label-free invariance prior generalizes more reliably than a label-supervised one. It uses 188 controlled runs on arithmetic tasks. It advances mechanistic understanding of grokking.

entry.title: The Spectrum Is Not Enough: When Context Helps Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Mert Onur Cakiroglu, Mehmet Dalkilic, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: This paper argues spectral predictability indices cannot answer whether adding context helps time-series forecasting, proving an impossibility result: any power-spectrum index is invariant under phase randomization, whereas the beyond-second-order value that retrieval and foundation models exploit is not. It isolates the claim with surrogate pairs fixing spectrum and marginal. It clarifies when context genuinely helps.

entry.title: Falsifying Causal Graphs With Outlier Events

author.name: William Roy Orchard, Philipp M. Faller, Dominik Janzing

entry.summary: This paper proposes falsifying candidate causal graphs by checking whether their implied outlier-event propagation is consistent with data, inverting the root-cause-analysis principle that weak outliers rarely cause strong ones and presenting the first statistical tests for this hypothesis. Authors include Amazon causal-inference researchers. It offers a ground-truth-free way to reject bad causal graphs.

entry.title: Deep4ge: DNN Training Trajectories for Fault Detection and Diagnosis

author.name: Sigma Jahan

entry.summary: Deep4ge is a controlled benchmark of 14,227 per-epoch training runs from 59 adapted TensorFlow/Keras programs, with faulty variants injected via 27 source-code transformations across seven fault categories. It supports fault detection and diagnosis for deep-learning systems using training trajectories. It fills a gap in public labeled fault datasets.

entry.title: CANDI: Contextual Alignment for Niche Domains Question Answering

author.name: Megha Chakraborty, Darssan L. Eswaramoorthi, Het Riteshkumar Shah, Madhur Thareja, Michelle A Ihetu, Harshul Raj Surana, Kaushik Roy, Amit Sheth

entry.summary: CANDI-QA is a benchmark evaluating LLMs on context-sensitive, user-aligned answers in specialized domains like medical and financial advisory, splitting into direct information-assistance questions and more nuanced categories requiring contextual grounding. It targets capabilities beyond general-knowledge QA. It aims to better measure domain-appropriate alignment.

entry.title: Graph-Based Detection of Disinformation Narrative Diffusion between Russian and Ukrainian Telegram Channels

author.name: Yuliia Vistak, Viktoriia Makovska, Vera Schmitt, Veronika Solopova

entry.summary: The paper proposes a graph-based framework combining weak supervision with propagation-graph analysis to detect disinformation narratives across Russian and Ukrainian Telegram channels. It clusters semantically related claims into narrative-level groups and models their diffusion across channels. It aims to catch coordinated amplification missed by post-level methods.

entry.title: CityBehavEx: A Scalable and Empirically Validated LLM-Assisted Urban Simulation Platform

author.name: Gustavo H. Santos, Aline Viana, Thiago H Silva

entry.summary: CityBehavEx is an LLM-assisted urban simulation platform that scales to city-size populations by combining established human mobility models with fine-tuned cross-encoders instead of invoking LLMs for every agent action. It generates mobility patterns better matching real spatial, temporal, and semantic distributions while supporting inspection and validation. It targets scalable, empirically grounded urban simulation.

entry.title: Comparing Semantic Navigation in Humans and Large Language Models using Natural Language Processing

author.name: Gabriel Paris-Colombo, Rodrigo M. Cabral-Carvalho, Felipe D. Toro-Hern\'andez
