It attributes this to aggressive teacher gradients at high-entropy decision forks and proposes mitigation via gradient masking.

entry.title: Can a Language Model Learn Facts Continually in Its Weights?

author.name: Charles O'Neill

entry.summary: Empirically studies whether a language model can accumulate facts written into its weights over sequences of tens to a hundred later writes, using invented facts on Qwen3 models. It finds that training data breadth determines whether the model merely recites versus can use knowledge, with diverse restatements sharply reducing the recitation-to-use gap.

entry.title: A Survey on LLM Watermarking: Theory and Deployment

author.name: Huy Phan, Kieu Dang, Ojaswi Dulal, Aiham AL Shukairi, Abby Shine, Chase Garner, Phung Lai

entry.summary: Provides a systematic, deployment-oriented survey of LLM watermarking, organizing methods by design choices and reasoning about their guarantees to bridge research and deployable attribution systems. It addresses provenance, auditing, and misuse concerns for machine-generated text.

entry.title: FlashBEV: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact BEV Transformation with IO-Awareness

author.name: Shunsuke Yokokawa, Hironori Kasahara

entry.summary: Introduces FlashBEV, an IO-aware, memory-efficient exact implementation of sampling-based bird's-eye-view view transformation that avoids materializing large height-dependent intermediate tensors. It reduces the systems-level memory and latency bottleneck for high-resolution, long-range multi-camera BEV perception.

entry.title: What Does Your Short-Answer VQA Score Actually Measure? Evaluator-Dependent Instability in Multimodal Short-Answer Benchmarks

author.name: Guanhua Ye, Niu Jingbin, Yan Li, Meiyu Liang, Zhe Xue, Yingxia Shao, Yawen Li

entry.summary: Audits short-answer VQA scoring across six vision-language models and six benchmarks, using a high-precision semantic judge to show that up to half of official errors on text-rich benchmarks are semantically correct answers penalized for surface-form mismatch. It reveals evaluator-dependent instability structured by answer type.

entry.title: LLM-PDESR: Robust PDE Discovery via Subdomain Weighted Residuals and LLM-Guided Symbolic Hypothesis Generation

author.name: Jinyang Du, Hao Ma, Xiaohu Shi, Bo Yang, Yanchun Liang, Heow Pueh Lee, Chunguo Wu

entry.summary: Proposes LLM-PDESR, which combines LLM-driven symbolic hypothesis generation with subdomain-weighted residual evaluation to discover governing PDEs from noisy data, mitigating high-frequency noise amplification and search-space explosion. It integrates domain priors into symbolic regression.

entry.title: Toward Stronger Code Watermarking: A Grammar-Driven Approach to Optimizing the Trade-off Between Quality and Detectability

author.name: Licheng Yu, Aiwei Liu, Songze Li

entry.summary: Introduces Grammar-Driven Watermark, a code-watermarking method that preserves syntactic validity via grammar-guided masking and modulates watermark strength by token structural role to balance code quality and detectability. It addresses the difficulty of watermarking low-entropy code.

entry.title: Detecting AI-Generated Video: A Vision-Language Dual-View Survey

author.name: Dylan Xinming Hou, Juntian Zhang, Xu Gu, Yichen Wu, Nils Lukas, Gus Xia, Xiuying Chen, Yuhan Liu

entry.summary: Surveys AI-generated video detection, reframing the task as factual fidelity verification and proposing a vision-language dual-view taxonomy spanning intrinsic cues, spatiotemporal consistency, cross-modal reasoning, and language-guided analysis. It responds to the fading effectiveness of low-level artifact detection as generated video grows more realistic.

entry.title: The VC dimension of partial concept classes via Radon's theorem

author.name: Grigory Ivanov, Attila Jung, M\'arton Nasz\'odi

entry.summary: Proposes a policy-driven CT-Agent that models phase-aware diagnostic control, deciding whether additional imaging phases are needed rather than assuming all phases are available, to mimic clinically consistent CT reasoning. It addresses radiation reduction and cross-hospital protocol variability.

entry.title: Bandit PCA with Minimax Optimal Regret

author.name: Mo\"ise Blanchard, Dmitrii Ostrovskii, Aadirupa Saha

entry.summary: Improves both upper and lower regret bounds for bandit-feedback online PCA, essentially establishing the minimax regret and closing the gap left by prior work. It advances the theory of online learning with bandit feedback over spectral objectives.

entry.title: TabPFN beyond Tabular Data: Calibration and Accuracy on Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Jingxiang Zhang, Lujia Zhong, Zijie Zhu, Shuo Huang, Yuang Xu

entry.summary: Evaluates TabPFN as a zero-gradient, plug-and-play classification head on frozen image, text, and audio encoders, showing it achieves the best mean rank on calibration and likelihood metrics across many datasets and encoders. It substantially reduces negative log-likelihood and calibration error versus common lightweight heads.

entry.title: Fundamental Limitations of Fixed-Budget Best-Arm Identification

author.name: Motti Goldberger

entry.summary: Resolves an open question in fixed-budget best-arm identification by characterizing fundamental limits, addressing whether any adaptive algorithm can match the static oracle's error-decay rate uniformly across all problem instances. It advances the theory of ranking and selection.

entry.title: Learning Partition Trees for Nearest Neighbor Search

author.name: Sanjeev Khanna, Ashwin Padaki, Erik Waingarten

entry.summary: Studies nearest neighbor search as data-driven algorithm design, learning a balanced halfspace tree optimized for a specific query distribution. It gives an efficient algorithm achieving sublinear query time under Gaussian-like conditions.

entry.title: NetInjectBench: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-Using Large Language Model Agents for Network Operations

author.name: Ruksat Khan Shayoni, Muhammad Faraz Shoaib, S M Asif Hossain, M. F. Mridha

entry.summary: Presents NetInjectBench, a 130-scenario benchmark for indirect prompt injection against tool-using LLM agents in network operations, separating untrusted artifact text from trusted policy metadata. Naive execution reaches high unsafe-action rates, which layered defenses like a two-pass judge substantially reduce.

entry.title: QwenPaw-Data: Bridging Facts, Methodology, and Execution for Autonomous Enterprise Data Analytics

author.name: Tianjing Zeng, Yuntao Hong, Zhongjun Ding, Dandan Liu, Yinan Mei, Yunxiang Su, Yiming Wang, Xiaojian Zhang, Jingyu Zhu, Junhao Zhu, Zhuowen Liang, Jiazhen Peng, Lianggui Weng, Zhihao Ding, Kerui Yi, Qifeng Wang, Rong Zhu, Bolin Ding, Liyu Mou, Jingren Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces QwenPaw-Data, an agentic system for autonomous enterprise data analytics that consolidates warehouses, dashboards, documents, and logs into reusable analysis assets and turns natural-language requests into end-to-end workflows. Aimed at open, evolving enterprise environments.

entry.title: NVAITC AI Scientist: A Governed End-to-End Research System -- A Hypertension GWAS Case Study

author.name: Eddie Huang (NVIDIA AI Technology Center, NVIDIA Corporation), Ken Liao (NVIDIA AI Technology Center, NVIDIA Corporation), Iven Fu (NVIDIA AI Technology Center, NVIDIA Corporation), Yang-Hsien Lin (NVIDIA AI Technology Center, NVIDIA Corporation), Chao-Shun Zhan (NVIDIA AI Technology Center, NVIDIA Corporation), Andy Liao (NVIDIA AI Technology Center, NVIDIA Corporation), Virginia Chen (NVIDIA AI Technology Center, NVIDIA Corporation), Johnson Sun (NVIDIA AI Technology Center, NVIDIA Corporation), Pika Wang (NVIDIA AI Technology Center, NVIDIA Corporation), Richard Huang (NVIDIA AI Technology Center, NVIDIA Corporation), Jiun-Cheng Jiang (NVIDIA AI Technology Center, NVIDIA Corporation), Ting-Yuan Liu (Department of Medical Research, China Medical University Hospital, Taichung, Taiwan, Master Program for Digital Health Innovation, China Medical University, Taichung, Taiwan), Hsing-Fang Lu (Department of Medical Research, China Medical University Hospital, Taichung, Taiwan, Laboratory for Statistical and Translational Genetics, RIKEN Center for Integrative Medical Sciences, Yokohama, Japan), Ray Y. Lee (AI-Driven Genomic Medicine and Drug Discovery Lab, China Medical University Hospital, Taichung, Taiwan), Chi-Chou Liao (Department of Medical Research, China Medical University Hospital, Taichung, Taiwan), Simon See (NVIDIA AI Technology Center, NVIDIA Corporation), Fuu-Jen Tsai (Department of Medical Research, China Medical University Hospital, Taichung, Taiwan, Department of Medical Laboratory Science and Biotechnology, Asia University, Taichung, Taiwan)

entry.summary: Presents NAIS, an NVIDIA-affiliated governed end-to-end agentic research system for biomedical workflows, integrating proposal review, governed data routing, reproducible orchestration, and human oversight, demonstrated on a hypertension GWAS case study. Emphasizes keeping protected data within institutional boundaries.

entry.title: What We Talk About When We Talk About LLM Planning: Evidence for Two Distinct Planning Abilities

author.name: Sukai Huang, Chenyuan Zhang, Fucai Ke, Zhixi Cai, Naim Rastgoo, Gholamreza Haffari, Hamid Rezatofighi

entry.summary: Argues that uneven LLM planning performance reflects two distinct latent competencies rather than one difficulty axis, using multidimensional item response theory on ACPBench-Hard. It identifies operational reasoning and structural enumeration as separable dimensions.

entry.title: The Differential Neural Tangent Kernel and Its Positivity

author.name: Bangti Jin, Longjun Wu

entry.summary: Introduces a Differential Neural Tangent Kernel framework to analyze physics-informed neural networks solving linear PDEs, and proves positivity of the infinite-width kernel despite the challenge posed by multiple differential operators. The result provides theoretical grounding for the training dynamics of a widely used class of neural PDE solvers.

entry.title: Hierarchical Bayesian Quadrature

author.name: Tim Weiland, Toni Karvonen, Philipp Hennig

entry.summary: Extends Bayesian Quadrature to nonstationary integrands via an adaptively growing tree partition of the domain into local stationary Gaussian-process models, recombined through a hierarchy of GP conditioning. It improves uncertainty-quantified numerical integration for probabilistic ML.

entry.title: FastTPS: An Optimized Method for LLM Token Phase for AI accelerators

author.name: Wenzong Yang, Danyang Zhang, Kun Cao, Tejus Siddagangaiah, Rajeev Patwari, Zhanxing Pu, Siyin Kong, Zijiang Yang, Hao Zhu, Varun Sharma, Yue Gao, Tianping Li, Fan Yang, Jicheng Chen, Yushan Chen, Fennian Zhao, Aaron Ng, Elliott Delaye, Ashish Sirasao, Sudip Nag

entry.summary: Presents FastTPS, a low-precision method with three components to accelerate the sequential token-decode phase of decoder-only LLM inference on AI accelerators, improving throughput and compute-unit utilization for long inputs. It targets the low-parallelism bottleneck of autoregressive decoding.

entry.title: An Exact Instrument for State Usage in Selective State-Space Models, and the Input-Driven Migration It Reveals

author.name: Raktim Bhattacharya

entry.summary: Introduces an exact per-mode measurement instrument for how trained selective state-space models like Mamba use their diagonal state modes, enabling offline prediction of pruning error at any budget. Validated to extremely small relative error against reference implementations.

entry.title: ShapKO: Shapley-Adaptive Modality Knockout for Robust Multimodal Learning

author.name: Nusrat Binta Nizam, Fengbei Liu, Sunwoo Kwak, Minh Nguyen, Ruining Deng, Mert R. Sabuncu

entry.summary: Proposes ShapKO, a dynamic training strategy that learns modality-specific knockout probabilities based on validation utility to improve robustness of multimodal medical models under missing inputs. It addresses modality dominance during training.

entry.title: Local Multimodal Music Alignment from Global Supervision

author.name: Irmak Bukey, Zachary Novack, Jongmin Jung, Dasaem Jeong, Chris Donahue

entry.summary: Introduces FuSiLi, a Sinkhorn-based soft-alignment similarity score for multimodal contrastive learning that learns local audio-to-score correspondences from only coarse global supervision. It retains global alignment ability while enabling fine-grained localization.

entry.title: Are We Ready for AI-Driven Discovery? AI Verification Before the Next Fundamental Physics Breakthrough

author.name: Gaia Grosso, Vinicius Mikuni, Lukas Heinrich

entry.summary: Reviews frameworks for rigorously verifying autonomous ML systems in fundamental physics across particle physics, astrophysics, and cosmology. It emphasizes fundamental limits like unavoidable inductive bias and sample complexity bounds on discovery.

entry.title: Integrating Background Knowledge for Scalable Causal Discovery

author.name: M\'aty\'as Schubert, Theofanis Aslanidis, Tom Claassen, Sara Magliacane

entry.summary: Develops a framework that integrates expert background knowledge directly during the causal discovery process rather than only as postprocessing, improving identifiability, accuracy, and search-space reduction. This helps scale causal discovery to larger variable sets.

entry.title: Diversify Diffusion with Temperature Sampling and Variance-Corrective Time Shifting

author.name: Peizhuo Li, Emre Aksan, Alexandru-Eugen Ichim, Thabo Beeler, Olga Sorkine-Hornung

entry.summary: Introduces variance-corrective time shifting, a training-free method to sample diffusion models at high temperature to reach rare or under-represented modes without inflating per-mode variance that would degrade quality. It queries the network at a shifted timestep and scales the score accordingly.

entry.title: Transferable Implicit Solvent Machine Learning Potential for Drugs and Proteins Approaching Ab Initio Accuracy

author.name: Jan Eckwert, Julija Zavadlav

entry.summary: Introduces TWIN, a transferable implicit-solvent machine learning potential for drugs and proteins parametrized entirely by an equivariant network to approach ab initio accuracy without empirical force-field data. It targets the slow inference of explicit MLPs for microsecond-scale biomolecular simulations.

entry.title: JobHop v2: A Large-Scale Career Trajectory Dataset from Unstructured Resumes

author.name: Iman Johary, Guillaume Bied, Alexandru C. Mara, Tijl De Bie

entry.summary: Presents JobHop v2, a large public dataset of about 355k career trajectories extracted end-to-end by LLMs from roughly 440k pseudonymized multilingual resumes, annotated with ESCO occupation codes and temporal information. It matters as authentic, richly annotated labor-market data for workforce planning and job recommendation research, addressing the scarcity of open resume-derived corpora.

entry.title: Hearing Like Humans? Sound Symbolism and Perceptual Alignment in Speech Language Models

author.name: Yun-Shao Tsai, Chun-Wei Chen, Chee-En Yu, Yi-Cheng Lin, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: Investigates whether speech language models exhibit human sound symbolism, using real speech recordings across auditory, crossmodal, and visual conditions. It finds that model auditory judgments align poorly with human perception and miss acoustic cues like spectral tilt that drive human intuitions.

entry.title: InterPet4D: A Multimodal 4D Human-Pet Interaction Dataset for Pet Motion Generation

author.name: Yichen Peng, Jyun-Ting Song, Chen-Chieh Liao, Kris Kitani, Hideki Koike, Erwin Wu

entry.summary: Presents InterPet4D, described as the first multimodal 4D dataset of natural human-dog interactions with 6.8M frames from 13 dogs and 23 participants, including multi-view and egocentric video, keypoints, meshes, and audio, plus an InterPetMoGen motion-generation framework. It fills a gap in human-pet interaction estimation and generation.

entry.title: Generalize LMMs to Versatile Visual Modalities via Fabricated Modality Synthesis

author.name: Shihao Yuan, Yuanze Li, Ruyi Zhang, Ming Liu, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: Introduces VVM-Tuning, a training framework that generalizes large multimodal models to unseen visual modalities by synthesizing appearance-varied images and using modality contexts to disentangle invariant scene semantics from modality-specific characteristics. It treats different modalities as distinct samplings of the same physical world.

entry.title: Self-supervised Automatic Matting

author.name: Xiaonan Hu, Zhiyuan Lu, Jingdong Zhao, Hao Lu

entry.summary: Introduces SSMatte, a self-supervised image-matting framework that trains using only RGB images with no manual annotation by decomposing the problem into semantic anchoring and detail matting. It reportedly reaches performance on par with fully supervised automatic matting.

entry.title: Grassmannian Splatting I: Moving rank-2 Spacetime Surfels for Dynamic Scene Rendering

author.name: Aaron Maurice Berman, Shantanu Dave

entry.summary: Introduces Grassmannian splatting, a dynamic scene representation whose primitives are Gaussians supported on 3-planes in 4D spacetime, encoded via a Grassmannian normal and an unconstrained factor that yield rank-2 surfels per frame with velocity and shape. It offers a mathematically principled alternative to native 4D Gaussian splatting.

entry.title: Spectral Heat Flow for Conservative Token Condensation in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhaoyang Li, Yanjun Li, Wangkai Li, Yujia Chen, Tianzhu Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes SpecFlow, a training-free framework that condenses rather than prunes visual tokens in vision-language models, using spectral heat flow for a stable importance field, adaptive spatial partitioning for coverage, and aggregation of discarded tokens for statistical conservation. It reduces the cost of processing long visual token sequences under high compression.

entry.title: EgoSteer: A Full-Stack System Towards Steerable Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos

author.name: Yifan Zhong, Zhang Chen, Tianrui Guan, Fanlian Zeng, Yuyao Ye, Tianjia He, Ka Nam Lui, Jiayi Li, Tingrui Zhang, Ruilin Yan, Xinhao Ji, Guangyu Zhao, Wenjie Lou, Jiayuan Zhang, Yuanpei Chen, Yaodong Yang

entry.summary: EgoSteer is a full-stack system that scales dexterous vision-language-action pretraining from 9.6K hours of curated egocentric human videos and enables data-efficient real-robot post-training, including a world-model-enhanced VLA and a teleoperation stack. It targets steerable, language-aligned dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: AutoNorm: Understanding Adaptive Normalization in Transformers through Differentiable Gating

author.name: Piyush Kaushik Bhattacharyya, Divyanshu Rai, Swastik Singh, Kumar Aakash, Ayush Ranjan, Krutika Verma

entry.summary: Investigates differentiable normalization gating in transformers, finding that Gumbel-Softmax gating's gradient variance hinders convergence on stationary vision tasks while sustained gating diversity helps on non-stationary language tasks. It proposes AutoNorm to adaptively select normalization strategies.

entry.title: LayerNorm as Implicit Gain Control in Looped Transformers

author.name: Matthias M. M. Buehlmaier

entry.summary: Shows that in pre-LayerNorm looped transformers, LayerNorm acts as an implicit gain controller, making the recurrence Jacobian non-normal and contractive at fixed points so the true stability budget is the spectral margin rather than the operator norm. It clarifies convergence conditions for looped transformer recurrences.

entry.title: Singular perturbations and hierarchical learning in two-layer neural networks

author.name: C\'edric Gerbelot, Jean-Christophe Mourrat

entry.summary: Proves that the constant and linear components of a misspecified single-index target are recovered within predicted timescales during joint gradient-flow training of an infinitely wide two-layer network, confirming a hierarchical-learning conjecture and analyzing quadratic-component onset. It advances rigorous understanding of feature learning dynamics.

entry.title: Velocity Scheduled Flow Matching

author.name: Vitalii Bondar

entry.summary: Introduces Velocity Scheduled Flow Matching, which replaces the constant-speed conditional target of flow matching with a time-varying nonnegative velocity profile integrating to one, allowing pretrained linear flow models to be resampled under different profiles. It explores six motion-planning-inspired polynomial profiles.

entry.title: Random Label Prediction Heads for Studying Memorization in Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Marlon Becker, Jonas Konrad, Luis Garcia Rodriguez, Benjamin Risse

entry.summary: Introduces random label prediction heads attachable at arbitrary network depths to empirically measure memorization and model capacity, interpreting head performance as an estimate of Rademacher complexity. It enables layer-wise analysis of how memorization evolves through a network.

entry.title: Bet on Features: Anytime-Valid and Feature-Aware Auditing of Conditional Quantile Forecasters

author.name: Ivane Antonov, Sohom Mukherjee, Richard Pibernik, Yo Joong Choe

entry.summary: Develops a distribution-free, game-theoretic, anytime-valid framework for continuously auditing black-box conditional quantile forecasters under non-i.i.d. losses, incorporating the information-dependence of calibration by allowing feature-aware auditors. It targets sequential monitoring under drift for decisions like inventory planning.

entry.title: Robustly Invertible Nonlinear Dynamics and the BiLipREN: From Inversion-Based Control to Generative Trajectory Modelling

author.name: Yurui Zhang, Ruigang Wang, Ian R. Manchester

entry.summary: Defines a notion of robust invertibility for nonlinear dynamical systems and constructs recurrent networks (BiLipREN) that are bi-Lipschitz invertible by design, guaranteeing robust forward prediction and input reconstruction. It applies this to inversion-based control and generative trajectory modeling.

entry.title: On the Efficiency of LoRA Fine-Tuning for Vision-Language-Action Models in Industrial Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Finn Ferchau, Daniel Pommer, Cristian Axenie

entry.summary: A systematic study of LoRA fine-tuning for the flow-matching VLA model on precision assembly tasks with a real robot, sweeping ranks and allocation strategies. It finds no significant advantage of full fine-tuning over well-configured LoRA, with performance saturating at moderate rank.

entry.title: Emergent Generalization by Representation Learning in Artificial Neural Networks

author.name: Hardik Rajpal, Dan Goodman

entry.summary: Shows that an explicit information bottleneck forcing a recurrent network to learn a low-dimensional representation is necessary for rotational and out-of-distribution generalization in time-series prediction. It uses information-theoretic causal emergence measures to argue such low-dimensional codes are functionally relevant.

entry.title: Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models Using Diversion Decoding

author.name: Basel Abdeen, S M Tahmid Siddiqui, Meah Tahmeed Ahmed, Anoop Singhal, Latifur Khan, Punya Parag Modi, Ehab Al-Shaer

entry.summary: Introduces diversion decoding, an uncertainty heuristic that detects LLM hallucinations by actively challenging model-generated responses during the decoding phase. It aims to be cheaper than existing probabilistic hallucination-detection methods.

entry.title: Edge Cluster Expansion with Radial Rotary Attention for Interatomic Potentials

author.name: Zemin Xu, Wenbo Xie, P. Hu

entry.summary: Investigates SO(2) equivariant architectures for machine learning interatomic potentials and proposes new interaction building blocks including an edge complex product basis and radial rotary complex attention. It addresses limitations of SO(2) linear layers relative to SO(3) tensor products.

entry.title: Implicit Neural Networks as Static Controllers: Certificates and Performance Separation

author.name: Giuseppe C. Calafiore, Laurent El Ghaoui

entry.summary: Proposes an implicit representation of neural network controllers as trainable linear interconnections closed through a static activation map, enabling tractable well-posedness and Lyapunov/IQC analysis. It provides certificates for exponential stability and quadratic performance for LTI plants.

entry.title: How Temperature Shapes Ideological Discourse in Retrieval-Augmented Generation?

author.name: Elmira Salari, Hazem Amamou, Jos\'e Victor de Souza, Shruti Kshirsagar, Maria Nunes Delfino, Anderson Avila

entry.summary: Studies how decoding temperature affects the transmission, amplification, or suppression of ideological positions in retrieval-augmented generation, using lexical multidimensional analysis over a corpus of COVID-19 treatment articles. It highlights an underexplored ideological-bias dimension of RAG robustness.

entry.title: ChartSync: A Benchmark for Visuo-Logical Cascading Chart Editing

author.name: Jiakang Yu, Yixuan Chai, Tianci Wang, Rihui Jin, Guangkai Xu, Hongtao Deng, Xun Zhu, Wang Gao, Xinrun Guo, Haipang Wu

entry.summary: Introduces ChartSync, an expert-validated benchmark of 870 triplets for visuo-logical cascading chart editing, where data changes require geometry-synchronized updates rather than localized text swaps. It exposes weaknesses of generative image editors on structured, dependency-aware chart modifications.

entry.title: LFD: Enabling Real-World Lensless Face Recognition with a Large-Scale Dataset

author.name: Junho Kim, Salman S. Khan, Sara Wan, Tomi Kuye, Ashok Veeraraghavan

entry.summary: Presents LFD, a large-scale dataset enabling real-world lensless face recognition, addressing artifacts and poor generalization of reconstruction-based lensless imaging pipelines. It supports privacy-friendly, compact camera designs for biometrics.

entry.title: Imperceptible and Reversible Adversarial Examples against Vision-Language Models for Privacy Protection

author.name: Qi Lu, Ziqi Zhou, Yufei Song, Zijing Li, Lulu Xue, Minghui Li, Shengshan Hu, Leo Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes CloakDiff, a reversible, high-fidelity privacy protection method that produces imperceptible adversarial examples against text-based query attacks on vision-language models by combining diffusion-based adversarial editing with an invertible network for lossless recovery. It addresses the visual-quality degradation of prior noise-based adversarial examples.

entry.title: On the Real-World Generalisability of Optical Flow Models

author.name: Petter Reijalt, Sander Gielisse, Rickard Karlsson, Jan van Gemert

entry.summary: Builds a real-world optical-flow evaluation benchmark of over 8k frame pairs across several sources and tests whether modern models trained on synthetic data actually generalize to real video. It questions whether accuracy on synthetic proxies predicts real-world optical-flow accuracy.

entry.title: Prism: Automating Science-of-Evals Research

author.name: LAThomson

entry.summary: Introduces Prism, a scaffold that gives Claude Code sub-agents and resources to autonomously conduct science-of-evals research, treating evaluations themselves as the object of study. A demonstration run shows minor prompt perturbations push GPT-4.1 toward indirect blackmail that the eval scorers fail to detect, revealing measurement gaps.

entry.title: AI agents create virtual playgrounds to help robots get crucial training data

author.name: Alex Shipps | MIT CSAIL

entry.summary: MIT CSAIL researchers, including Russ Tedrake, describe using AI agents to automatically generate rich, diverse simulated scenes so robots can obtain more varied training data without labor-intensive physical teaching. It addresses the data bottleneck in robot learning through scalable content generation for simulation.

entry.title: Are LLMs Ready for Scientific Discovery? A Capability-Oriented Benchmark for AI Scientists

author.name: Chuhan Shi, Xiaoquan Ren, Sicheng Song, Haobo Li, Rui Sheng, Yushi Sun

entry.summary: Introduces SDABench, a benchmark reorganizing evaluation of AI scientists around six analytical capabilities (descriptive to mechanistic) across five domains, with 527 real and 6000 synthetic instances. It moves beyond code-execution metrics toward scientific-claim validity.

entry.title: Efficient Test-Time Optimization for Multi-Agent Proof Autoformalization

author.name: Tian-Shuo Liu, Shiyuan Zhang, Zijie Geng, Haoyu Liu, Runjie Xu, Pengyuan Wang, Lei Yuan, Yang Yu

entry.summary: Introduces ToMap, a Decomposer-Formalizer-Prover multi-agent pipeline for full-proof autoformalization with test-time optimization guided by formal verification, avoiding costly training or unguided repair. Targets long-horizon coordination of claims and dependencies.

entry.title: When does distribution shift break graph neural networks calibration?

author.name: Abderaouf Bahi

entry.summary: Provides the first closed-form theoretical characterization of graph neural network calibration under distribution shift, showing calibration is governed by a single scalar depending on structural change and feature quality. It predicts when models become miscalibrated without deployment-distribution labels.

entry.title: When Classical Baselines Are Tuned as Carefully as the Quantum Model, Does Quantum Reservoir Computing Still Win?

author.name: Tushar Pandey

entry.summary: Tests whether quantum reservoir computing retains an advantage when classical baselines are given equal size and tuning effort. Using exact small-system simulations, it finds the claimed quantum advantage disappears under fair comparison.

entry.title: Tokenizing Numerical and Embedding Features for LLM RecSys

author.name: Zhe Xu, Ankit Peshin, Chiyu Zhang, Feng Qi, Johnson Lui, Anil Ramakrishna, Justin Johnson, Carl Hu, Kaushik Rangadurai, Luke Simon

entry.summary: Proposes a soft-token fusion framework that maps continuous numerical and dense embedding features into an LLM's embedding space so recommenders can use non-textual signals through the standard token interface. It addresses the mismatch between LLM text tokens and real recommendation pipelines.

entry.title: Vertical Fusion: Condensing Internal Representations for Robust ViT Classification

author.name: Francesco Di Salvo, Shyam Nandan Rai, Hamed Damirchi, Ignacio Meza De la Jara, Sebastian Doerrich, Marco Lents, Christian Ledig

entry.summary: Challenges using ViTs as black-box last-layer feature extractors by showing intermediate-layer probes can correctly classify many samples the last layer misses. It attributes this to a redundancy-correctness correspondence and proposes vertical fusion of internal representations for robustness.

entry.title: ZoRRO: A Zero-Weight Personalized Recommender System for Scalable News Recommendation

author.name: Johannes Kruse, Ryotaro Shimizu, Kasper Lindskow, Jon Tofteskov, Michael Riis Andersen, Julian McAuley, Jes Frellsen

entry.summary: Presents ZoRRO, a zero-weight training-free personalized news recommender that outperforms strong neural baselines offline and nearly matches a state-of-the-art deep model in online A/B testing while running over 600 times faster. It also reveals notable offline-online gaps and differing recommendation distributions.

entry.title: CoSAG: Compact Semantic Anchor Gaussians via Training-Free Rate-Distortion Coding

author.name: Yuang Jia, Jinlong Wang, Junhong Lin, Ruiting Dai, Wei Gao

entry.summary: Proposes CoSAG, a training-free rate-distortion coding method that decouples 3D Gaussian semantic field construction from storage, compressing the per-Gaussian feature assignment that dominates memory in CLIP-embedded Gaussian splatting scenes. It targets the gigabyte-scale storage bottleneck of open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding.

entry.title: Improving Sample Diversity in Autoregressive Text-to-Image Generation via Cluster Truncation

author.name: Trang Nguyen, Shuang Wu, Runyan Tan, Phillip Howard

entry.summary: Investigates whether autoregressive text-to-image models can improve the quality-diversity trade-off relative to diffusion models, which suffer diversity collapse, by adapting token-based decoding strategies and introducing a cluster truncation method. It leverages the sequential nature of AR generation for diversity control.

entry.title: Is Energy Guidance All You Need? Training-Free Norm Injection for Driving World Models

author.name: Xiyan Su, Frank Diermeyer, Markus Lienkamp

entry.summary: Investigates whether controllability of driving world models requires training, showing that a rectified-flow model jointly generating future video and planned ego trajectory can be steered at sampling time by differentiable energy functions encoding driving norms, without retraining the diffusion backbone. It demonstrates counterfactual behaviors like braking on an Open-Sora-based backbone.

entry.title: Prism: Automating Science-of-Evals Research

author.name: LAThomson

entry.summary: A duplicate cross-post of the Prism science-of-evals scaffold on the Alignment Forum, presenting a Claude Code based system that autonomously investigates evaluation dynamics and reveals scorer blind spots in the Agentic Misalignment setting. Content matches the earlier LessWrong version.

entry.title: Valid $\ne$ Necessary: Diagnosing Latent Inefficiency in Chain-of-Thought

author.name: Daeyeop Lee, Hwanjo Yu

entry.summary: Identifies a blind spot in reasoning-step evaluators that penalize logical or factual errors but ignore valid-yet-inefficient steps that inflate token usage. Introduces RIV-GSM8K, a diagnostic benchmark injecting five inefficiency types such as circular reasoning and excessive decomposition.

entry.title: Interpreting learning dynamics of autoencoders: Transient scaling and emerging concepts of the Ising model

author.name: Max Weinmann, Miriam Klopotek

entry.summary: Studies how unsupervised autoencoders trained on Ising-model spin configurations spontaneously learn macroscopic physical variables, revealing two distinct learning regimes governed by depth, width, and learning rate. It offers interpretability insight into how representations of theory-relevant quantities emerge during training.

entry.title: Pitfalls of Administrative Censoring in Survival Models with Time-Indexed Inputs

author.name: Yanqi Xu, Hui Dai, Carlos Fernandez-Granda, Krzysztof J. Geras, Yiqiu Shen

entry.summary: Identifies a failure mode in survival models with time-indexed inputs: administrative censoring combined with acquisition-time artifacts (device or protocol changes) can leak outcome information and bias predictions. It warns clinical prediction practitioners about a subtle but consequential pitfall.

entry.title: Scaffold splits hide structural-frontier failures in ADMET models

author.name: Jiacheng Zheng, Chang Guo, Zixuan Wang, Xinyu Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a label-free structural-frontier split for ADMET molecular property models that reserves the sparsest and most physicochemically remote scaffolds, showing standard scaffold splits substantially underestimate error on unfamiliar chemistry. It exposes evaluation optimism in drug-property prediction.

entry.title: The Spectral Structure of Latent Treatment Effects

author.name: Hamza Virk, Bijan Mazaheri, Yihren Wu

entry.summary: Shows that latent treatment effects under discrete unobserved confounding admit an exact compressed observable operator whose eigenvalues are the latent effects, generalizing prior synthetic-potential-outcome moment recovery. It provides a spectral characterization for identifying heterogeneous treatment effects.

entry.title: Neural Discovery of Memory and Nonlocal Kernels in Integro-Differential Equations with Constrained Kolmogorov--Arnold Networks

author.name: Aruzhan Tleubek, Salah A Faroughi

entry.summary: Proposes a differentiable-solver framework that discovers memory and nonlocal kernels in integro-differential equations from sparse noisy data using constrained Kolmogorov-Arnold Network parameterizations with imposed physical constraints. It addresses an ill-posed inverse problem across IDE classes.

entry.title: Rank-Conditioned Sample Reuse for the Plackett--Luce Best-of-$K$ Objective

author.name: Melveena Jolly, Midhun Xavier

entry.summary: Studies the Plackett-Luce best-of-K objective under sampling without replacement (the law of Gumbel-Top-K / stochastic beam search) and shows reusing i.i.d. Max@K weights is provably biased, then derives rank-conditioned Horvitz-Thompson estimators that add sample reuse to unbiased joint-score REINFORCE. It corrects estimator bias for coupled best-of-K decoding.

entry.title: SPARC-Net: A Spectral, Causality-Aware, and Hard-Constrained Physics-Informed Architecture for Stiff and Shock-Dominated Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Divyavardhan Singh, Dimple Sonone, Hammad Mohammad, Kishor Upla

entry.summary: Presents SPARC-Net, a physics-informed architecture combining an adaptive multi-scale spectral encoder, causality-aware training, and hard constraints to jointly address spectral bias, imbalanced loss weighting, temporal-causality violation, and under-resolved collocation in stiff and shock-dominated PDEs. It targets known failure modes of PINNs.

entry.title: Advancing Optimal Subset Oracle via Learning Relaxation of Neural Set Functions

author.name: Yongquan Shi, Zijing Ou, Shiping Wang, Yatao Bian

entry.summary: Reinterprets the evidence lower bound for optimal subset oracle learning as a continuous relaxation to avoid Monte Carlo gradient estimation of variational updates, reducing computational overhead and stochasticity in learning neural set functions. It targets applications like compound selection and recommendation.

entry.title: Manifold Constrained Conformal Prediction for Spatial Events

author.name: Collin Nill, Trevor Harris, Jason Adams

entry.summary: Introduces a conformal prediction method that builds calibrated prediction sets over collections of spatial events (like cyclone genesis or earthquakes) using sliced Wasserstein distance and manifold constraints. It derives a coverage lower bound for the intersected sets.

entry.title: Is Model Instability just Noise to be Tolerated or a Property that can be Managed?

author.name: Amirali Rayegan, Lunxiao Li, Tim Menzies

entry.summary: Argues that model instability in software analytics is a manageable property rather than mere noise, showing repeated runs of a state-of-the-art optimizer agree on only a small fraction of cases. By adjusting labeling, model complexity, and split scoring, it substantially increases run-to-run agreement.

entry.title: Observation-Level Watermarking and Detection for Tabular Data

author.name: Dongyu Cui, Xuan Bi

entry.summary: Introduces STAMP, a framework for watermarking tabular data at the single-observation level that accommodates numerical, categorical, and mixed distributions, plus a detection mechanism robust to small sample sizes. It addresses the under-explored problem of watermarking non-numerical tabular data.

entry.title: Fast Whole-Brain, Geometry-Aware Functional Alignment for Cross-Subject Decoding

author.name: Pierre-Louis Barbarant, Florent Meyniel, Bertrand Thirion

entry.summary: Introduces SpectralOT, a fast functional alignment method for fMRI that embeds cortical geometry into Laplace-Beltrami eigenmodes to regularize whole-brain alignment for cross-subject decoding. It balances functional feature alignment against anatomical preservation with computational efficiency.

entry.title: STEP: Career-Path Recommendation via Temporal and Educational Trajectory Modeling

author.name: Iman Johary, Guillaume Bied, Alexandru C. Mara, Tijl De Bie

entry.summary: Introduces STEP, a career-path recommendation approach that models temporal and educational trajectory signals extracted from unstructured resumes via LLMs. It aims to enable large-scale, sequence-aware job and skill recommendation grounded in authentic career histories.

entry.title: PC-Mix: Partial-Component Audio Spoofing Detection under Mixed Speech and Environmental Sound Conditions

author.name: Zhenshan Zhang, Xueping Zhang, Linxi Li, Yechen Wang, Ming Li

entry.summary: Presents PC-Mix, described as the first dataset for partial-component audio spoofing detection where speech and environmental-sound components can each be partly spoofed. It addresses realistic mixed-condition scenarios overlooked by prior studio-focused partial-spoof research.

entry.title: Low-Power License Plate Detection and Recognition on a RISC-V Multi-Core MCU-Based Vision System

author.name: Lorenzo Lamberti, Manuele Rusci, Marco Fariselli, Francesco Paci, Luca Benini

entry.summary: Demonstrates a low-power license-plate detection and recognition pipeline on a 9-core RISC-V microcontroller (GAP8) paired with an ultra-low-power greyscale imager, using MobileNet-based detection and LPRNet recognition. It achieves high recognition rates on tiny plate crops under strict energy and compute budgets.

entry.title: Detangled: A Framework for Creating, Editing, and Inferencing Feature Rich Hair Strands

author.name: Sarah Jobalia, Yitong Deng, Carolyn Smith, Ronald Fedkiw

entry.summary: Presents Detangled, a framework for creating, editing, and inferring feature-rich hair strands via a five-dimensional parameter space intended to bijectively map naturally occurring strand textures like curl and twist. It emphasizes inclusive coverage of diverse hair types independent of overall strand direction.

entry.title: WeaveEarth: Structured Evidence Construction and Reasoning for Training-Free UHR Remote Sensing Understanding

author.name: Xianzhi Ma, Shujun Wang, Xiaohan Li, Hao Liu, Changhua Pei, Jianhui li

entry.summary: Proposes WeaveEarth, a training-free framework for ultra-high-resolution remote sensing understanding that constructs structured evidence and reasons over it rather than expanding resolution or doing costly multi-round zoom search. It seeks better organization of visual information within limited compute budgets.

entry.title: REVA-PO: Stabilizing Reinforcement Learning for Chest X-ray Report Generation

author.name: Li Guo, Anas M. Tahir, Z. Jane Wang

entry.summary: Proposes REVA-PO, a reinforcement learning framework for chest X-ray report generation that stabilizes long training via response-weighted KL regularization and periodic validation-anchored policy resets. It addresses instability and limited exploration caused by fixed KL regularization and static reference policies.

entry.title: Benchmarking Dynamic Affective Reasoning: A Viewer-Centric Video Emotion Dataset

author.name: Zhiyan Zhang, Peipei Song, Jinpeng Hu, Jingyang Jia, Xun Yang, Xiaojun Chang

entry.summary: Introduces Dynamic Affective Reasoning (DAR), a large viewer-centric benchmark of over 15k videos and nearly 37k event-aligned affective segments across 27 emotion categories, capturing emotion transitions driven by cumulative causal events. It reframes video emotion analysis from static classification to dynamic causal reasoning.

entry.title: GNOCHI: Generative Neural mOdel for Close Human-Human Interactions

author.name: Gonzalo G\'omez-Nogales, Marc Comino-Trinidad, Andr\'es Casado-Elvira, Dan Casas

entry.summary: Introduces GNOCHI, a conditional variational autoencoder that generates poses for one person conditioned on another's pose to synthesize realistic close 3D human-human interactions with physically plausible, collision-free contact. It targets the shortcomings of prior generative methods in modeling close contact.

entry.title: Incremental Online Scene Reconstruction by 3D Gaussian Triangulation

author.name: Yanjin Zhu, Shaofan Liu, Jianke Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes an online framework that incrementally reconstructs and updates high-fidelity explicit meshes by directly triangulating a dense geometric Gaussian representation, avoiding offline conversion to an implicit field for mesh extraction. It supports both high-quality rendering and incremental surface reconstruction.

entry.title: Effective Synthetic Image Detection via Noise Residual Clustering

author.name: Caihui Yan, Gang Cao, Huawei Tian, Zhen Li, Yuhang Zhai

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free synthetic image detection method that extracts noise-residual fingerprints via a pretrained Noiseprint++ model, then derives multi-scale features from a frozen Vision Transformer with adaptive clustering. It aims to generalize to unknown generative models without costly labeled training.

entry.title: Traj-VLN: Learning Pixel-Space Interaction via Autoregressive Trajectory Generation

author.name: Changfei Fu, Guangcheng Chen, Wenjun Xu, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Traj-VLN, which decomposes vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments into sub-tasks and learns pixel-space interaction via autoregressive trajectory generation, leveraging VLM priors for sim-to-real and cross-scene generalization. It targets embodied navigation following natural language instructions.

entry.title: STAMP: Provenance-Guided Credit Assignment for Deep Search Agents

author.name: Ke Xu, Han Xu, Xinran Chen, Yuqian Wang, Zhixuan Li, Xiaojian Liu, Changwo Wu, Jianqiang Xia, Yuchen Li

entry.summary: Proposes STAMP, which assigns targeted credit in RL for deep-search agents by using a reference-based verifier to judge whether each cited document supports an evidence-graph entity, tracing citations to the action that first surfaced them. It modulates advantages while preserving trajectory-level rewards.

entry.title: Bringing Back Rule Induction to Fluid Intelligence Research? An Initial Validation of the ARC-AGI Benchmark in Humans

author.name: Jasmin Thelen, Oliver Wilhelm

entry.summary: Provides the first psychometric validation of the ARC-AGI benchmark in a human sample, examining its properties and nomological network relative to fluid-intelligence theories emphasizing rule induction over working memory. Bridges cognitive-science measurement and AI benchmarking.

entry.title: Inverse-IMPRESSION: A Graph-based Platform for Molecular Structure Elucidation from Experimental NMR Spectroscopic Properties

author.name: Zheqi Jin, Grace Armitage, Richard Cox, Ben Honor\'e, Mohammad Golbabaee, Craig Butts

entry.summary: Presents an inverted graph transformer platform that reconstructs molecular bonding directly from experimental NMR data through connectivity prediction, structure correction, and multi-shot ensemble ranking. It integrates multiple 1D and 2D NMR experiments.

entry.title: TOLiD: Bridging the Architecture Gap in Vision Foundation Model to LiDAR Pretraining via Token Lifting for Distillation

author.name: Sutharsan Mahendran, Darshana Priyasad, Kaushik Roy, Tharindu Fernando, Sridha Sridharan, Clinton Fookes, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: Proposes TOLiD, a self-supervised LiDAR pretraining method that couples a LiDAR backbone with a student ViT initialized from a frozen vision foundation model, using token lifting to bridge the architecture gap in cross-modal distillation. It reduces reliance on dense point-wise annotation for 3D scene understanding.

entry.title: Generative Chinese Statute Retrieval

author.name: Yiteng Tu, Zitao Su, Weihang Su, Xuanyi Chen, Yueyue Wu, Yiqun Liu, Min Zhang, Qingyao Ai

entry.summary: Proposes GCSR, a generative statute retrieval framework that recasts retrieval as sequence generation with a multi-granularity structured document identifier encoding legal hierarchy, trained with a multi-task strategy. It reports outperforming sparse, dense, and legal-domain baselines for Chinese statute retrieval.

entry.title: Navigating the Open-Source Model Ecosystem: An Empirical Study of Creator Practices in Artistic Image Generation

author.name: Yiluo Wei, Yupeng He, Qiming Ye, Gareth Tyson

entry.summary: Presents a large-scale empirical study of creator behavior in open-source image generation, using a dataset of 6 million images with embedded metadata linking 22.4K base models and 154K LoRA models to outputs. It illuminates emergent community model-mixing workflows contrasting with closed tools.

entry.title: Oversight of automated research via summarisation: a toy model

author.name: Aleksandr Bowkis

entry.summary: A toy study of research oversight via summarisation, where a strong model distills a synthetic language grammar into a token-capped summary that a weaker student uses to translate or verify. It finds translation competence does not imply summarisation competence, and that a good summary can equal many worked examples for the weak student.

entry.title: AdvNav: Behavior-Guided Black-Box Adversarial Attacks on Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Chenyang Li, Kaige Li, Zeyu Jiang, Changhao Chen

entry.summary: Proposes AdvNav, a gradient-free black-box adversarial attack against Vision-and-Language Navigation systems that disrupts the multistep perception-action loop using only observable inputs and outputs. Addresses the temporal dependencies that single-step black-box methods miss.

entry.title: Sharp Concentration Bounds for Bundle-Valued Statistics on Manifolds

author.name: Swagatam Das, Vaclav Snasel

entry.summary: Develops non-asymptotic, dimension-free Hoeffding- and Bernstein-type concentration bounds for empirical means of observations living in fibers over a base manifold, accounting for curvature and holonomy effects from parallel transport. It extends classical concentration theory to geometric statistics on manifolds.

entry.title: Lower Bound on the Cumulative Constrained Violation for the OGD+Projection algorithm for Constrained Online Convex Optimization (COCO)

author.name: Haricharan Balasundaram, Karthick Krishna Mahendran, Rahul Vaze

entry.summary: Establishes a lower bound on cumulative constraint violation for the OGD+Projection algorithm in constrained online convex optimization, complementing prior upper bounds on regret and violation. It sharpens theoretical understanding of the achievable trade-offs.

entry.title: Enhanced Byzantine-Robust Federated Learning Via Truncated-Quadratic Loss for Heterogeneous Data

author.name: Zhi-Yong Wang, Hao Nan Sheng, Werner Stefan, Hing Cheung So, Linqi Song, Weitao Xu

entry.summary: Shows centered clipping and Huber aggregators for Byzantine-robust federated learning are equivalent and can be biased under outliers and high heterogeneity, then proposes a truncated-quadratic-loss aggregation rule to reduce this bias. It aims for robustness under both attacks and non-IID data.

entry.title: Adapting Evidential Neural Networks to Test-Time Neighbor Fusion Improves Molecular Property Prediction

author.name: Cameron Gruich, Weichi Yao, Yixin Wang, Bryan Goldsmith

entry.summary: Introduces PG-EVIKAL, a retraining-free test-time correction that uses evidential neural networks' aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty for a Bayesian neighbor-fusion update, learning a property-distance metric to re-rank structurally similar neighbors before fusion. It improves molecular property prediction on most of 16 datasets.

entry.title: Event-based Neural Decoding for Neuroprosthetic Motor Control

author.name: Khaleelulla Khan Nazeer, Sirine Arfa, Matthias Jobst, Richard George, Christian Mayr

entry.summary: Develops event-based spiking neural network decoding for neuroprosthetic motor control to enable compressed communication and low-power on-device inference, addressing latency, energy, and connectivity constraints of current prostheses. It seeks to narrow the accuracy gap between spiking and standard deep models.

entry.title: Adversarially Guided Diffusion for LiDAR Range Image Synthesis

author.name: Stavros Bouras, Antonios Makris, Alexandros Gkillas, Aris S. Lalos, Konstantinos Tserpes

entry.summary: Presents the first diffusion-based unrestricted adversarial attack against 2D LiDAR range-image semantic segmentation, using segmentation-loss guidance during sampling. It stays within the manifold of natural range images.

entry.title: Generative Testing of Automated Speech Recognition Systems

author.name: Yanis Xabier Wilbrand Pe\~na, Oliver Wei{\ss}l, Andrea Stocco

entry.summary: Introduces GATAS, a black-box testing method that generates failure-inducing inputs for ASR systems by interpolating in the phoneme-level latent space of a TTS model. It preserves perceptual naturalness while inducing transcription errors.

entry.title: Gradient-Skipping Relevance Propagation for Efficient Explainability of Vision Transformers

author.name: Christopher Buratti, Michele Marchetti, Federica Parlapiano, Davide Traini, Domenico Ursino, Luca Virgili

entry.summary: Introduces GradSkip, a relevance propagation method for Vision Transformers that models uneven attention-head importance and dynamically distributes relevance across attention and residual paths. It improves attribution accuracy over methods that assume uniform heads and identity skips.

entry.title: Approximation of Analytic Functions by ReLU Neural Networks with Adjustable Depth and Width

author.name: Yanming Lai, Defeng Sun, Yang Wang

entry.summary: Establishes approximation-rate upper bounds for ReLU networks approximating analytic functions as a joint function of width and depth. In contrast to finite-smoothness classes where depth and width play symmetric roles, it derives distinct bounds for analytic functions.

entry.title: Learning Topological Quantum Phases from Limited Subsystems

author.name: Mehran Khosrojerdi, Sougato Bose, Alessandro Cuccoli, Paola Verrucchi, Abolfazl Bayat, Leonardo Banchi

entry.summary: Introduces a data-efficient supervised learning framework that classifies topological quantum phases from small subsystems using a quantum kernel built from reduced density matrices, avoiding non-local string order measurements. It achieves high accuracy on cluster-Ising and Haldane chain phase diagrams.

entry.title: Normative Alignment of Recommender Systems via Internal Label Shift

author.name: Johannes Kruse, Kasper Lindskow, Michael Riis Andersen, Ryotaro Shimizu, Julian McAuley, Pierre-Alexandre Mattei, Jes Frellsen

entry.summary: Introduces NAILS, a scalable method for aligning recommender outputs with target distributions over item attributes like categories without retraining, formulated as internal label shift in a hierarchical classification framework. It preserves learned preferences while inducing specified marginal attribute distributions for fairness and diversity.

entry.title: Time Imprint: Learning Time-Aware Representations in Multi-Modal Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Pengyu Zhang, Klim Zaporojets, Congfeng Cao, Jia-Hong Huang, Paul Groth

entry.summary: Proposes Time Imprint, a framework that treats time as an entity-level modality in multi-modal knowledge graphs and jointly aligns temporal, textual, and visual representations to disambiguate entities with similar features. It addresses sparse temporal semantics and noise from multiple timestamps.

entry.title: Compression Asymmetry and Trajectory Binding in Noise-Anchored Diffusion Inversion

author.name: Yongseong Park, Joeun Kim, HoEun Kim, Young-Sik Kim

entry.summary: Analyzes real-image diffusion inversion through the forward Gaussian noise anchor, identifying an element-wise compression asymmetry (full-dimensional int8 anchors reconstruct well while low-dimensional subspace summaries collapse) and showing inversion is trajectory-bound and score-prior coupled. It clarifies mechanisms behind efficient stored-noise inversion.

entry.title: Label-Free Target-Domain Adaptation for Unconstrained Event-Image Feature Matching via Dual-Stage Distillation

author.name: Zhonghua Yi, Hao Shi, Qi Jiang, Yufan Zhang, Kailun Yang, Kaiwei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage training paradigm for event-image feature matching that uses large-scale label-agnostic distillation pretraining followed by target-domain adaptation without matching labels or aligned hardware. It targets unconstrained real-world cross-modal correspondence between event cameras and images.

entry.title: Structured Evidence Selection for Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Chenglizhao Chen, Tianxiang Nan, Wen Li, Xinyu Liu, Guisheng Zhang, Mengke Song, Xiaomin Yu

entry.summary: Proposes SESAD, a structured evidence selection framework for weakly supervised video anomaly detection that reformulates the task as structured reasoning over clip-level visual evidence instead of directly mapping aggregated features to scores. It aims to reduce reliance on scene-related statistical shortcuts.

entry.title: Neural Motion Blending Across Arbitrary Character Topologies

author.name: Luca Cazzola, Giulia Martinelli, Nicola Conci

entry.summary: Presents a framework for motion blending across heterogeneous skeleton topologies using a semantic encoder for per-frame latent motion states and a diffusion-based decoder that reconstructs character-specific motion, blending via latent interpolation. It removes the usual requirement of identical skeletons across characters.

entry.title: NanoVSR: Towards Real-Time Video Super-Resolution on Edge Devices

author.name: Filip Pawlicki, Marcel Ka\'ndu{\l}a, Marcin Pucek, Kamil Dobies

entry.summary: Presents NanoVSR, a fully convolutional, transformer-free and optical-flow-free video super-resolution architecture that uses structural reparameterization to collapse into standard convolutions at inference for hardware-accelerator compatibility. It maintains competitive REDS4 quality while enabling real-time edge deployment.

entry.title: Spectral Consistent Flow for One-step 3D Medical Image Translation

author.name: Haoqing Li, Jun Shi, Mingchao Li, Zehua Zhu, Qiwei Jia, Jiong Shi, Hong An

entry.summary: Presents SC-Flow, a single-function-evaluation 3D medical image translation framework that formulates translation as a stochastic Brownian bridge predicting a mean velocity field, with a spectral consistency corrector regularizing power spectral density via learnable frequency-domain gain. It mitigates modality entanglement, over-smoothing, and artifacts.

entry.title: MonkeyOCRv2: A Visual-Text Foundation Model for Document AI

author.name: Yuliang Liu, Zhang Li, Ziyang Zhang, Shuo Zhang, Qiang Liu, Jiajun Song, Zidun Guo, Xinhan Wang, Handong Zheng, Yang Liu, Dongliang Luo, Zhiyin Ma, Jiarui Zhang, Xiang Bai

entry.summary: MonkeyOCRv2 is a visual-text pretrained document AI model trained on MonkeyDoc v2, described as the largest document-image pretraining corpus with 113 million images across 17 languages. It jointly learns image-to-text generation and pixel-level document reconstruction to preserve character strokes and layout while aligning visual and textual content.

entry.title: Towards Human-level Dexterous Teleoperation

author.name: Puhao Li, Zeyuan Chen, Yingying Wu, Pengkun Wei, Yuyang Li, Tianyu Wang, Jiaxiao Shi, Mingrui Yu, Baoxiong Jia, Song-chun Zhu, Tengyu Liu, Siyuan Huang

entry.summary: TeleDexter is a hand-object co-tracking controller for human-level dexterous teleoperation that maps operator intent into learned low-level contact execution, trained on consecutive co-tracking subgoals from human reference motions. It targets in-hand dexterity like tool wielding, grasp swapping, and finger gaiting via dynamic contact control.

entry.title: It’s 2030 and we fucked up. How did it happen?

author.name: Boaz Barak

entry.summary: Boaz Barak, writing personally, imagines a future where the AGI transition goes badly and works backward to diagnose plausible failure modes, contrasting optimistic visions like Machines of Loving Grace with a glass-half-empty scenario. It is an opinionated essay on AI risk pathways.

entry.title: Neural Posterior Estimation for Inferring Weak Lensing Shear

author.name: Tim White, Dingrui Tao, Camille Avestruz, Jeffrey Regier, the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration

entry.summary: Applies neural posterior estimation, a form of simulation-based inference, to infer weak gravitational lensing shear directly from multiband images, folding detection, deblending, and calibration into one learned pipeline. Backed by the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration.

entry.title: The Path to Self-Evolving Clinical Systems: Scaling Medical Agents from Assistance to Autonomy

author.name: Chunzheng Zhu, Lei Tian, Bohan Tan, Ziqi Zhou, Yuxuan Sun, Yijun Wang, Chengchao Lv, Yilin Wen, Yijun He, Jinghao Lin, Yihang Chen, Cheewei Tan, Qianshan Wei, Lei Zhao, Bin Pu, Kenli Li, Yuan Xue, Jianxin Lin

entry.summary: Reframes medical agents from a deployment-first perspective, formalizing them as sequential decision systems under partial observability with a three-level autonomy taxonomy from assisted to autonomous. Focuses on contamination-resistant benchmarks and interactive training environments needed for clinical trust.

entry.title: Calibrated e-CUSUM Decoding for Quantized Reasoning Models: Why Token Log-Probability Is the Wrong Observable for Decoding Monitors

author.name: El Hassane Ettifouri (Novelis Research, Paris, France), Ayoub Belfatmi (Novelis Research, Paris, France), Mahaman Sanoussi Yahaya Alassan (Novelis Research, Paris, France), Walid Dahhane (Novelis Research, Paris, France)

entry.summary: Argues that centered token log-probability is the wrong observable for monitoring quantized reasoning models because it is a mean-zero martingale that measures sampling self-consistency, not trajectory health. Introduces a training-free decoding controller fusing token uncertainty with explicit repetition detection.

entry.title: Learning from Noise: Effective-Rank Collapse and Out-of-Distribution Rejection in Restricted Boltzmann Machines

author.name: Oshada Rathnayake, Nikhil Shukla

entry.summary: Analyzes out-of-distribution rejection failures in restricted Boltzmann machines through the spectrum of the visible-visible interaction matrix, showing training spreads spectral weight and increases effective rank. Assigning random binary images to a rejection label improves OOD rejection.

entry.title: Multi-dimensional training-priority weighting based on physical information propagation paths: a unified residual-weighting framework for physics-informed neural networks

author.name: Zhangyi Lian, Xinda Dong, Wenxuan Huo, Weifeng Huang, Gang Zhu, Qiang He

entry.summary: Proposes a unified residual-weighting framework for physics-informed neural networks that prioritizes training based on physical information propagation paths (temporal, spatial, and boundary), generalizing prior temporal-only causal training. It aims to improve PINN stability and accuracy.

entry.title: HiFi-LLP: High-Fidelity, Low-Cost Latency Predictors with Confidence for Robust HW-NAS

author.name: Shambhavi Balamuthu Sampath, Behzad Shomali, Nael Fasfous, Moritz Thoma, Judeson Anthony Fernando, Lukas Frickenstein, Pierpaolo Mori, Manoj Rohit Vemparala, Alexander Frickenstein, Walter Stechele

entry.summary: Presents HiFi-LLP, high-fidelity low-cost latency predictors with confidence estimates to replace slow hardware-in-the-loop measurements in hardware-aware neural architecture search, reducing sample requirements and guarding against misleading inaccurate predictions. It targets efficient edge-device deployment.

entry.title: Q-Score: A Quantum-Native Scoring Function for Molecular Docking

author.name: Kangyu Zheng, Yidong Zhou, Ruihao Li, Zixin Ding, Zhiding Liang, Shaohua Li

entry.summary: Introduces Q-Score, a quantum-native molecular docking scoring function that encodes GNN-predicted orbital donor-acceptor energies and solves a clique problem via a quantum optimization algorithm. It is orthogonal to classical scoring functions.

entry.title: How much Data do We Need? Sequential Data Collection for Stochastic Programming

author.name: Xin Li, Juergen Branke, Xuan Vinh Doan

entry.summary: Studies an optimal stopping problem for sequential data collection in stochastic optimization under parameter uncertainty, proposing a benefit-driven framework that balances information gain against sampling cost. It uses Bayesian belief updating to decide when to stop gathering data.

entry.title: MeloBottleneck: Self-Supervised Melody Skeleton Extraction with a Latent Subsequence Bottleneck

author.name: Fan Bu, Rongfeng Li, Linfeng Fan

entry.summary: Introduces MeloBottleneck, a self-supervised framework that extracts melody skeletons as length-controlled order-preserving latent subsequences via a hard bottleneck and re-ornamentation decoder. It avoids reliance on hand-crafted rules or biased pseudo-labels.

entry.title: Byzantine Accountability Without Consensus: Strong Eventual Consistency for Non-Associative, Stochastic, Robust Aggregation

author.name: Ryan Gillespie

entry.summary: Presents ACFA, a coordinator-free replication scheme for Byzantine-robust aggregation rules like multi-Krum, achieving strong eventual consistency and accountability without consensus. It replicates a content-addressed set of signed contributions and self-authenticating equivocation proofs.

entry.title: Representation Learning for Semiparametric Causal Mediation Analysis under No Essential Heterogeneity

author.name: Roberto Faleh, Sofia Morelli, Holger Brandt

entry.summary: Proposes UNIT, a two-stage estimator combining deep representation learning (TARNet) with G-estimation for structural causal mediation parameters under a no-essential-heterogeneity assumption. It identifies structural parameters even with unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding.

entry.title: BucketKD: A Safety-Aware Bucket-Based Knowledge Distillation Framework for End-to-End Motion Planning

author.name: Md Nahidul Islam, Mohd Hasan Ali, Dipankar Dasgupta, Myounggyu Won

entry.summary: Presents BucketKD, a knowledge distillation framework for compact end-to-end motion planners that discretizes critical environmental variables into adaptive buckets and uses a safety-aware waypoint attention mechanism. It aims for deployable safety-aware planners on resource-constrained platforms.

entry.title: Demixing Sparse Signals from Nonlinear Observations using Generalized Non-convex Regularization

author.name: Raziyeh Takbiri

entry.summary: Studies recovery of two sparse vectors from nonlinear observations of their superposition using Huberized fidelity with generalized folded-concave penalties and a two-block proximal alternating algorithm. It proves convergence to critical points and establishes restricted strong convexity guarantees.

entry.title: When cheap gradients fail: the measurement cost of attacking quantum classifiers

author.name: Bacui Li, Chandra Thapa, Tansu Alpcan, Udaya Parampalli

entry.summary: Shows that finite quantum measurement statistics (shot noise) act as a built-in defense against gradient-based attacks on variational quantum classifiers, imposing a dimension-dependent measurement budget on attackers. Single-step attacks provably require at least quadratically many shots in the input dimension.

entry.title: Does YOLO26 Truly Offer Advantages Over Its Predecessors for Edge Deployment? A Benchmark Study in Aquaculture

author.name: Rakesh Ranjan, Gajanan S. Kothawade, Kata Sharrer, Scott Tsukuda, Christopher Good

entry.summary: Benchmarks the YOLO26 detector with NMS-free end-to-end inference against YOLOv5u, YOLOv8, and YOLO11 across model scales for fish-mortality detection in aquaculture edge scenarios. It systematically evaluates accuracy, training efficiency, and deployment suitability to test whether the newer architecture truly helps.

entry.title: Bridging the Catalog-to-Real Gap: Scalable Product Recognition via Multi-Stage Contrastive Learning

author.name: Anyi Zhang, Joy Mazumder, Kiril Lomakin

entry.summary: Reformulates large-scale product recognition as embedding-based cross-domain retrieval and introduces a multi-stage contrastive learning pipeline to bridge the gap between pristine catalog packshots and noisy in-store images. It targets scalable matching against extensive corporate catalogs for retail intelligence.

entry.title: TextGaze: Prompting Gaze Target Estimation with Textual Scene Cues

author.name: Junhui She, Fei Wang, Kun Li, Yiqi Nie, Yuxin Liu, Zhangling Duan, Xun Yang

entry.summary: Introduces TextGaze, a cross-modal architecture that uses a large vision-language model to produce gaze-aligned textual cues that guide gaze target estimation, balancing multi-branch supervision-heavy methods against saliency-driven ones. It aims to align predicted attention with actual gaze intent without heavy annotation.

entry.title: Physics-inspired Pseudo Anomaly Generation and Prototype Feature Guidance for 3D Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jian Ning, Qin Zou, Linchun Wu, Yuanhao Yue, Kunmo Li, Shoubin Chen, Zhongyuan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes PA3AD, a 3D point-cloud anomaly detection framework that generates physically plausible pseudo-anomalies from normal data and uses weight-shared prototype features to capture normal-versus-abnormal distribution shifts. It addresses the scarcity and cost of real anomalous samples in industrial inspection.

entry.title: Why Domain Matters: Domain-Aware Benchmarking of Underwater Object Detection and Annotation Quality

author.name: Melanie Wille, Dimity Miller, Tobias Fischer, Scarlett Raine

entry.summary: Introduces a framework that labels underwater images by appearance, scene composition, and acquisition geometry to enable domain-aware benchmarking, then systematically studies how domain factors affect both annotation quality and detector performance. It reveals failures hidden by aggregate metrics and by synthetic domain-generalization benchmarks.

entry.title: HyperBank: A Differentiable Bank of Classical Priors for Few-Shot Spheroid Microscopy Segmentation

author.name: M. Pr\r{u}\v{s}ek, A. Novoz\'amsk\'y, F. \v{S}roubek, T. Volfov\'a, V. Svobodov\'a Pavl\'i\v{c}kov\'a, S. Rimpelov\'a

entry.summary: Introduces HyperBank, a differentiable bank of classical image-processing operators (Frangi vesselness, Sauvola thresholds, structure tensors, gradients, Laplacian-of-Gaussian) fitted on few support images for interpretable few-shot spheroid microscopy segmentation. It emphasizes understanding which visual cues drive success versus opaque foundation segmenters.

entry.title: TriCons-Pose: Triangle-Invariant Geometric Consistency Learning for Category-Level Object Pose Estimation

author.name: Zuzhi Yang, Shuai Wang, Mounir Kaaniche, Ziwei Li, Zhiming Cheng, Zhidong Zhao, Chenggang Yan

entry.summary: Proposes TriCons-Pose, a triangle-invariant geometric consistency learning method for category-level object pose estimation that anchors stable keypoints and aggregates pose-invariant cues for reliable canonical mapping. It aims to improve robustness under intra-class shape variation and occlusion where correspondence-based methods are fragile.

entry.title: RED-Sphere: Hyperspherical Residual Edge Debiasing for Cross-Population Fundus Disease Domain Generalization

author.name: Yan Lin, Ziheng Wang, Shuang Chen, Amir Atapour-Abarghouei, Stephen McGough

entry.summary: Proposes RED-Sphere, a plug-and-play hyperspherical residual edge-debiasing framework for cross-population fundus disease domain generalization under a strict source-only setting where external populations are unseen even for validation and model selection. It disentangles population-correlated low-level cues from lesion evidence that share edge and texture structure.

entry.title: OmniX: Any-view and Any-time 4D Reconstruction via Feed-forward Trajectory Fields

author.name: Yanqin Jiang, Tengfei Wang, Zhengwei Wang, Chenjie Cao, Junta Wu, Wenhan Luo, Weiming Hu, Jin Gao, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: OmniX is a feed-forward 4D reconstruction framework that predicts dense 3D point trajectories per pixel from videos with large camera motion, decoupling dynamic motion from static geometry using compact dynamic tokens. It exploits the sparse, low-rank structure of 3D motion to reconstruct complete dynamic scenes under large viewpoint changes.

entry.title: LATO.2: Factorized 3D Mesh Generation with Vertex and Topology Flow

author.name: Hang Long, Tianhao Zhao, Junkai Lin, Youjia Zhang, Huipeng Guo, Rendong Liang, Jiale Xu, Jozef Hladk\'y, Matthias Nie{\ss}ner, Wei Yang

entry.summary: LATO.2 factorizes 3D mesh generation into a vertex flow followed by a connectivity flow conditioned on realized vertices, both anchored to a shared voxel scaffold, to avoid entangling continuous geometry with discrete topology. This reduces drifting vertices and broken surfaces in flow-based mesh generation.

entry.title: 3D Scene Graph Prediction: Generating Hierarchical Models from Partially Observed Environments

author.name: Siyi H, Jared Strade, Hyungtae Lim, Luca Carlone

entry.summary: Proposes a top-down framework to predict hierarchical 3D scene graphs, including room-level layout and traversability, from partially observed indoor environments to support robot exploration and object search. Focuses on high-level structure prediction beyond single-room object layout.

entry.title: Artificial Foveated Perception for Mitigating Shortcut Learning in Robotic Foundation Models

author.name: Xiatao Sun, Yuan Zhuang, Mateo Sanchez Lopez Negrete, Matei-Victor Coldea, Chen Liang, Haoyang Zhang, Che Liu, Ziyao Zeng, Shawn Li, Qian Wang, Fei Miao, Daniel Rakita

entry.summary: Identifies shortcut learning in robotic foundation models, where policies exploit spurious scene correlations, and proposes artificial foveated perception to focus on causally relevant visual structure. It aims to improve robust deployment across diverse real-world settings.

entry.title: A Single Diffusion-Policy Controller for Multi-Task Block Pushing with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer

author.name: Haitong Ma, Haldun Balim, Yang Hu, Bo Dai, Na Li

entry.summary: Trains a single diffusion policy from scratch with reinforcement learning for multi-shape block-pushing manipulation, using a reweighted ELBO policy loss compatible with RL and reverse curriculum generation to overcome exploration without demonstrations. It shows zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

entry.title: WALA Learning Executable Latent Actions from Action-Labeled Demonstrations and Action-Free Videos

author.name: Jiahao Liu, Zhongpu Xia, Shuai Tian, Huangrui Li, Yuhang Zheng, Ning Ma, Xin Fu, Xiaotian Liu, Jing Li, Yixian Li, ShangQing Zhou, Zebin Xing, Linbo Wang, Chaoyue Li, Haoran Li, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: WALA learns executable latent actions from both action-labeled demonstrations and action-free videos by pretraining a semantic-geometric latent action model that predicts future deltas in DINOv3 feature space and dense depth rather than raw pixels. This preserves task-relevant structure to scale robot learning beyond labeled data.

entry.title: Robust bipedal locomotion on flowable slopes via foot-driven terrain manipulation

author.name: Deniz Kerimoglu, Junnosuke Kamohara, Jiyeon Maeng, Ziwon Yoon, Seth Hutchinson, Ye Zhao, Daniel I. Goldman

entry.summary: Investigates bipedal locomotion on flowable granular slopes by actively controlling terrain response through foot-driven manipulation, addressing the fragility of walking robots where foot contact induces large surface deformations. The work links terrain physics with robot control to improve stability on deformable ground.

entry.title: Narrix: Remixing Narrative Strategies from Examples for Story Writing

author.name: Chao Zhang, Shunan Guo, Abe Davis, Eunyee Koh

entry.summary: Presents Narrix, a writing-support tool that identifies narrative strategies in example stories, highlights them with lexical cues, and lets novice writers remix these strategies along an interactive story arc. It targets the creativity-support gap for less experienced storytellers.

entry.title: ABot-3DWorld 0: A Universal World Model to Explore Any 3D Space

author.name: Mingchao Sun, Luyang Tang, Yu Liu, Xu Yan, Zhan Li, Yunwei Zhang, Fei Yu, Zengye Ge, Yumin Liu, Jiacheng Zhang, Yongchang Zhang, Jiawei Zhang, Zhicheng Liu, Zhongxu Sun, Tianjian Ouyang, Wenzheng Chen, Shixing Yang, Nianfei Fan, Guodong Sun, Huan Li, Zheng Zhou, Yongze Li, Yingliang Peng, Mengmeng Du, Yuan Liu, Haozhe Shi, Chunnuo Gong, Chengzhen Yu, Chunxue Jia, Yang Liu, Shiying Zeng, Junnan Lai, Hang Zhang, Ning Guo, Baoquan Chen, Mu Xu, Hongyu Pan

entry.summary: ABot-3DWorld 0 is a universal multimodal 3D world model that turns text, image, and video inputs into high-fidelity explorable 3D worlds using a Spatial Generative Primitive combining a panorama and a spatial point cloud. A 3D-consistent panoramic video generator explores the primitive along a planned trajectory before reconstructing a photorealistic 3D Gaussian Splatting world.

entry.title: Markov Chain Monte Carlo with Diffusion Paths

author.name: Han Chen, Sifan Liu, Jun Yang

entry.summary: Proposes running MCMC by interpolating along a diffusion (noising) path toward a Gaussian rather than classical tempering, arguing this preserves relative mode weights and improves mixing for multimodal distributions. It supports the claim with a spectral-gap analysis of the ideal transition kernel.

entry.title: [AI 2040] Transparency Plan

author.name: Thomas Larsen

entry.summary: A cross-posted AI 2040 supplement laying out transparency proposals for AGI projects, including a trustless US-China verification deal and a favored total research transparency regime where algorithmic secrets, experiments, and training runs would be broadly visible. It analyzes desiderata and possible transparency regimes.

entry.title: Linear Probes add little for Verifiable Reward Hacking

author.name: Chandram Dutta

entry.summary: An empirical alignment study testing whether linear probes on model activations can give early warning of reward hacking during GRPO training on a small model with a planted reward-checker bug. It finds probes detect the hack near-perfectly but add little over simply inspecting the output, since only obvious lazy hacks emerged.

entry.title: Compile, Then Page: Executable SOP Programs and a Capability-Gated Runtime for Procedural LLM Agents

author.name: Chenglin Yu, Li Yin, Ying Yu, Hongxia Yang, Ming Li

entry.summary: Compiles machine-readable standard-operating-procedure constraints into executable pseudo-code run by a program-guided stack machine that pages the active frame while an LLM performs semantic execution. A three-arm SOPBench study shows compiled text helps and runtime guidance is capability-gated, helping strong models but harming weak ones.

entry.title: From Neural Network Decisions to Training Cases: An Exact Account via Case-Based Decision Theory

author.name: Manli Yan, Yuebin Lin, Yaowen Yu, Yong Zhao

entry.summary: Shows that an OLS action readout on a fixed neural representation admits an exact case-based decomposition, expressing each action score as a weighted sum of training-case returns via Gram geometry. Grounds neural decisions in case-based decision theory for auditability.

entry.title: CA-DGCL: Dynamic Graph Continual Learning via Condensation and Attachment

author.name: Tingxu Yan Ye Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces CA-DGCL for dynamic graph continual learning that condenses historical snapshots into compact representations and uses Tucker decomposition over cross-timestamp node chains to obtain stable features encoding historical knowledge. It aims to reduce catastrophic forgetting while exploiting temporal information.

entry.title: CatRetriever: Contrastive Representation Learning for Slab-to-Bulk Retrieval in Generative Catalyst Discovery
